This Game is good. It isn't the best rpg, or the greatest game of all time. Many fans hype it up to be THE GREATEST THING EVER, but I can't really agree with it. I love games like Earthbound. I love Mother 3 as well. I find those two games to be better than this one. This game has a strong beginning, but it gets worse as it goes on. After Waterfall (which is the best area in the game IMO) the games slowly gets worse. Once the character Alphys gets introduced the game feels like it has to talk to you nonstop to remind you "IM FUNNY RIGHT?” It gets a little irritating.  The game also gets more linear and boring. The combat in Undertale is... all right. The bullet hell inspired selections are really fun, but have huge difficulty spikes. But combat is repetitive and boring, and when you’re doing a genocide run it’s SO bad. The pixel art in Undertale is a little ugly at times too. The over world sprites are bad, showing little to no detail. The battle sprites all much better, but in a weird design choice aren't in color. It does give the game some style however. I know some people might not enjoy the lack of color, but I don’t mind it too much. It may seem like I hate this game, but I don’t. I might not feel like it's the greatest game of all time, but it’s still good, and DEFINIETLY WORTH PLAYING! It’s an experience. By the way I don’t find Ocarina of Time the best game either so I’m not just saying it isn’t the best game because of that. I can’t get into why I don’t like Ocarina of Time in this review however.

This game has the funniest reviews I've ever read on Steam so I don't know if I can match them.
If this is really what the world would be like if the zombie holocaust happened I don't know how long I would last before I drank the bottle of bleach. This game can be really brutal. You can spend hours wandering around the woods with nothing, then the second you find a bottle of water someone breaks open your skull with a bat and you have to start all over. Repeat this sequence for a couple days (or weeks) before you really break through to satisfying gameplay.
The world is enormous and beautiful. The hyperrealism (having to know your blood type for blood packs, etc...) is pretty neat but makes the game that much more difficult. Having skill or previous experience in other MMORPGS and first person shooters will help you emmensely with the skills you need for this game.
I like the realism the most. The isolating, soul-crushing gameplay does have its own charm too. It is a lesson in patience and persistance, good training for real life I suppose.
The zombies are the monsters, but they are nowhere near as dangerous as your fellow players. Trust no one, and approach all situations with caution.
All in all, I think it's a great game and worth the frustration.

This is literally the greatest bloody game I've ever played.. And it's not even a game!
Euro Truck Simulator 2 really knows how to involve the 'player', and make him or her feel like they're actually driving a truck across Europe. The driving mechanics are mostly simple and easy to use, as is the management of the business, and buying/upgrading trucks and garages, hiring and firing drivers, and even receiving emails about income/outcome, making the game easy to use, whilst providing features that make it so much more realistic.
Though it focuses on the roads, the atmosphere and surroundings in Euro Truck Simulator 2 are ASTONISHING! With everything from aeroplanes to hot air balloons decorating the skies, and hills, farms and wind turbines seasoning the land, it's impossible not to appreciate the beauty of the world as you go through yet another long day of work. As if this wasn't enough, the "game" world is HUGE, and takes literally hours to cross, as well as perpetuating the realism (after all, it is supposed to be a large chunk of Europe) this makes it much more interesting, as there are so many diverse places to see you'll just have to spend the hours it takes to see them all!
The presence of things such as tiredness and reducing fuel levels make the game even more real, and can add a nice amount of tension at the right (or wrong) times. When I found myself driving in the dark in Belgium one night, and all of a sudden the word "Drifting" polluted my screen I was hectic! I was desperately checking my map for the nearest place I could stop to rest, while simultaneously ensuring that I'd finish the job on time if I did so. These moments really do make what may be considered a dull and boring job as exciting as it is, and can take at least a few hours for the 'player' to begin to adjust and remember to keep an eye on when they sleep and how much fuel they have.
As a whole, many will see this as a 'game' in which you merely "drive a truck", but it's so much more than that. In a similar way to improving a character on an RPG, the expansion of your company in Euro Truck Simulator 2 is incredibly rewarding, allowing you to deliver more dangerous things or do longer jobs. These produce intense motivation in the 'player', and you'll find yourself striving to expand even when away from the "game".
Euro Truck Simulator 2 is truly amazing, it provides endless unforgettable experiences, not all good, but none at all that you won't think back on and smile about your first day, when you held up traffic for almost 30 minutes because you got stuck on that sharp turn, seems almost like yesterday. And that's exactly what this "game" aims to do, to give you something you'll both enjoy and feel good about, and it not only acheives that, but goes a step further and pulls at your heartstrings.
If you haven't bought this game already, why not? You will not be disappointed.

I played this game back when it came out, and I recently picked it back up again, and holy heck... This game... If you have not bought or seen this game before, play it right now. Don't watch any videos about it, just play it blind.
This is probably one of my favourite games of all time, and I don't see that changing any time soon. Everything about this game is absolutely astonishingly amazing. The characters, the interesting and fun combat system, the self-awareness, the side-splittingly funny moments, the horrifyingly disturbing moments, the soundtrack, the feels (oh god the feels), and the fact that it makes you rethink the way you traditionally play games.
It is just so ingrained into our minds that when we encounter something in a game like this, you just have to fight. This game makes you think twice. Right from the beginning, the game tells you that you don't have to fight an enemy, and in fact, it discourages this. Every single monster you come across feels like it's own character; it's own person. No wonder people feel so bad when they kill something. The way that the characters act towards you can change completely depending on how you treat them and the world around you, causing for a ton of replayability.
Anyways, I could ramble for hours about everything that this game has done right, but I don't want this review to be too long. Overall, I give it a 10/10, without a single doubt. This is my number one most recommended game. Toby Fox is a genius.

This game is one of the most fascinating games I've ever played. If you told me a year ago one of my favorite games would be a semi-truck driving simulator, I would have called you insane, and here we are. The game is really self explanatory: you are a truck driver who started your own business and you build an empire. You'll drive across all of Europe, having to take note of the different driving restrictions everywhere, hire more drivers to work under you, and upgrade your truck to be beautiful. I recommend Scanias. You can put your own music into the game, or in my case, listen to a bunch of podcasts. It's a pretty relaxing, peaceful game, with fantastic controls and something that just keeps calling you back.
Note: After playing this game, you will become fascinated by semis on the road and become acutely aware of the different companies and types. Don't worry. That's normal.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is a truck simulation game created by SCS Software, using OpenGL. It is the sequel to Euro Truck Simulator, with a redone physics and game engine. The player can drive across a significant part of Europe.
Player should pick up a variety of cargoes, and delivering them to the desired destination.
The game features 8 different trucks, includes: DAF, Volvo, Man, Scania, Renault, M. Benz and Iveco. 4 of them are licensed already.
Gameplay
You can start your game in one of the following countries: Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, Slovakia, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. You will be asked to select your desired city in one of them. Your garage will be located there. So the journey will be begin. In the beginning, you wont have enough money and experience to buy a truck, so you will start with quick deliveries. You also can get loans. You can open your own company, hiring drivers from all over the map. What you need is to have enough money to afford their trucks purchase and a free slot in a garage. You can buy a garage in every city you tend, Then you should upgrade it.
The gameplay is so sweet and handy. Its obvious how the developers have worked on it. and they have done it nicely. Riding trucks seems so realistic with a great system of handling. So after delivering any cargo, you will be given an amount of money and EXP will be gained. EXP is needed to unlock trucks and items. As you gain an amount of EXP, you earn a level as well. You also will be estimated as your level in the game. The system of opening of company makes a motivation for the player. Its almost the goal of the game. AI of the vehicles in ETS 2 is actually OK. its average, but they are making it better with every patch to make the game an awesome experience for the player. Accidents are not so realistic. Plus you wont get any physical damage. After any accident your truck will be damaged, but not physically. actually nothing happens to your truck. Its a defect. The game physic is good and its being improved by every patch.
You wont see any police in the game. But there are traffic lights, speed limit, toll stops and accident penalty. if you violate any mentioned things [except toll], you should pay an specific amount of fine. This systems made without any defect. The driver will become tired, so you should pull over in an specific place to get rest. Gas stations, repair stations, drivers agencies, Truck showplaces and resting stations are available in the game. For buying a truck, you need to visit its shop [which are in its own particular city] or you can use online purchasing. Any truck needs a slot in your garage. The limitation of slots is 5 in per garage. Also drivers you can hire are limited at 116 at the moment. Overall, this part of the game is decent. except some defects like lack of physical damages. Also the map is so much big. thats a fantastic point. so much to explore with a great system of running company that let you enjoy the title for many days.
Graphic
The graphics are stunning. Lighting system and shadows are awesome. Vegetables, trees and environments made perfectly. Designing of trucks is amazing. Into the cabin has very good details with a perfect designing. But designing cities are kinda average. You also can see humans in the cities. There are also some famous places made in the game. Cargoes have a good variety. Weather system is great. Raining seems so realistic. You can enjoy the darkness of the night, the sunset, the sunrise and the sunlight in the middle of the noon. Also Other vehicles seem average.
This part is one of the most important factors that makes this simulator so special, and puts it as the best truck simulator ever made.
Sound
Well, the sound effects part is nothing special. I cant really talk about this. The sound seems so low when you are into the cabin camera. You should switch to another camera mode to hear it better. Its overall made well. There is also online radio streaming. Its decent. Also you can make your customized track list from your own music library.

Do you like big trucks? Do you like Europe? Are you willing to eat sleep and♥♥♥♥♥♥behind a wheel of 10 tonne road monster? Are you willing to deliver a giant tank of gasoline from Paris to Glasgow? If the answer is yes, this game is just for you. A beatiful environment, active community and an actual developers who listen to the fans, this game have all the things a car simulation game has to offer. Be sure to turn off that damn parking brake.

If you have either seen or played earthbound, this is in a sense a homage to that game, which in my book is a plus considering I loved that game on the SNES.
~The story is one of the best things about this game, without spoiling much, long ago in this world, monsters waged war against humanity, but in the end, the monsters were sealed underground by a magic barrier, one day a child fell down a hole and into the underground and now you play as this child trying to find a way out of the underground while also coming face to face with the monsters that were sealed down there.
*Warning: If you don't like reading or you just skip text and dialogue in games, then this game probably isn't for you as their is quite a bit of dialogue to read throughout the game.
~The tones this game can give are quite interesting as it depends on your play style and route             chosen as their are in a way 3 to chose: Pacifist, Neutral, and Genocide.
~The humour was usually fitting and actually made me laugh or at least chuckle.
~The battle system is akin to a bullet hell game, where you dodge incoming attacks except unlike conventional bullet hell games you don't have to fight back. Instead after each attack they throw at you, a dialogue box pops up and you get to chose a course of action through it.
~The boss battles are what make the battle system so good as each boss is unique and has a completely different play style and quirk. On a somewhat related note, each enemy in the game also have a unique battle pattern and way to deal with it depending on the story route chosen.
~Then the music fits very well with each area and battle you come across, but it may get a bit repetitive at times especially if you're in an area for a extended amount of time. Albeit some of the best music is played during boss battles as each boss has their own theme.
This is an amazing game all around. 9/10

Word of the Experienced

Pros: Great graphics quality and the scenery is nice too, even the best GPUs are currently stressed on this one. It's really noob friendly in terms of UI, gearing and even driving. Haven't seen any bugs of any kind yet, although through research, apparently they're out there somewhere and there's mods available which fixes them, just be careful as some mods are impossible to remove without losing your save files. Gameplay is very addictive and staying within the lanes while using just a keyboard is much easier than 18WoS was, though ppl recommend a joystick or wheel to play as apparently it's even better than keyboard. The career path is far better than 18WoS was, although it's pretty much the same, it's much more polished (like Porsches and their stubborness to keep their engines at the back but eventually made it work properly). I like the level up system where you can improve on skills and abilities to haul different / more valuable cargos and also improve on fuel efficiency.
Cons: AI traffic are both intelligent and stupid at the same time: they sometimes behave like typical bad drivers do (they cut you off and then slow down faster than you can brake, stuff like that), but they also do really dumb things like drive right into you or put you in a situation where you have no choice but to cause an accident which will happen a lot if you're not careful enough and experienced. Realistic lights mod is almost a necessity to have because otherwise you can't really see AI in the mirrors and you can't see oncoming traffic until they're close (might of been fixed by now, I'm stuck with the mod though so I don't know). GPS is not that great, though definitely needed (slightly improved with v1.11), but that's for the most part realistic since most GPS's are terrible. The infractions are very strict with no leniency at all and you WILL get a lot of them no matter how much you try to obey the rules of the road. Truck dealerships start off as hidden in the cities until you discover them which is difficult to do since you don't start off with your own truck to explore with, so you kind of need to become a rebel and use the employer's truck to explore with and hope to still be able to deliver the cargo in time. Analog controllers are definitely not something I'd recommend ppl to use for this game... way too twitchy and unpredictable. While taking damage can affect the truck, it takes a lot of crashes in order for it to need those repairs, also, no matter what condition the trucks are in, no damage is ever seen on the trucks, that also includes AI cars. The world feels really flat (even though it isn't), there really isn't any major hills other than in the quarry.
Even though I listed way more Cons than Pros, I very much highly recommend this game if you're a fan of simulation games or driving games of almost any kind as it really is a fantastic game in many ways. It's far better than 18WoS and any other trucking game I've played. It's a game I keep coming back to.
EDIT: With the 1.9 update which apparently improves the AI system... well, it doesn't improve the AI system, it only made them worse. Still doesn't stop me from playing and enjoying the game though, just keeps me more on my toes when around them.
RE-EDIT: Some cons removed with 1.11 update. AI is still very stupid (but not bad for AI limitations)

Especially for someone who has been Molested. But that's not what we are here to talk about. I think that there should be rules and regulations on names. Rust is a survival PVE/PVP online multiplayer game. As one of my favorite Youtuber's (VERTiiGO) would say "The Butt Naked World That Is Rust" (VERTiiGO says it in all his Rust gameplay Commentaries.) It is true. You start as a fresh spawn butt naked with only a rock and a torch. You use your rock to hit trees for wood, rock nodes for sulfur ore/stones/metal ore/high-quality metal ore, to try to kill animals like boar's, bear's, wolves, chicken, horses and stag's for leather/cloth/bone fragments/wolf skulls and pork/bear meat/chicken and wolf meat. You have to gather materials to build a base or home to keep yourself and your stuff safe and nothing is safe on rust.
Raids on rust are always a given unless you are on a modded PVE only server. You will be raided and or killed. Raids tend to happen with c4 and rockets (with rocket launchers). But sometimes people will use flamethrowers, the bean can grenades (not really reliable), f1 grenades, satchel charges (kind of like c4 but less damage and less reliable), pickaxes and axes (which neither of those really do much unless you have a ton of them and a ton of time).
The old blueprint system required you to use blueprint fragments, pages, books or library's to get a blueprint (which was random on what you would get) which you would then use and be able to craft that item with the required materials. Or using a research table and the item you wanted the blueprint for (getting them from either points of interest like Radtown, Military Tunnel, Trainyard, Airfield, Satellite Dish, Water Treatment Plant, Powerplant, Sphere Tank, Warehouse's or from Airdrops.
The new experience system requires you to level up by doing the above or giving players crafted items you made and having them do all the work which would give you XP to level up. Every level up to level 30 you unlock different items that you can craft.
They have added blueprints back in a way of research papers. You use an item and research paper you received in the above way to us at the research table to get a limited number of crafting uses for that item which you need the required materials for.
You survive on food and water. Not all water sources are drinkable, only the running water sources are drinkable, water catchers or you have to use a water carrier like a bottle or bota bag to use in any water then using the water purifier to purify the water so you can drink it. You can get water bottles the above ways. For food, you have to hunt and then cook or by running rivers you can get pumpkins and corn, mushrooms that are all over in un-grassy patches that look like dirt. You can also get food from the above ways.
There are also many guns in the game. Use guns to protect yourself, kill animals or to kill people. Some guns are Pump Shotgun, Assault Rifle, Custom SMG and Pistols.
Tools are also in the game and you use them just like the rock. But certain tools work better for certain things. For instance, pickaxes would be best to use on the rock nodes and an axe for trees and chopping up animals or humans which you can get skulls, cloth, raw human meat (not really good for food, even after cooking).

~The story is one of the best things about this game, without spoiling much, long ago in this world, monsters waged war against humanity, but in the end, the monsters were sealed underground by a magic barrier, one day a child fell down a hole and into the underground and now you play as this child trying to find a way out of the underground while also coming face to face with the monsters that were sealed down there.
*Warning: If you don't like reading or you just skip text and dialogue in games, then this game probably isn't for you as their is quite a bit of dialogue to read throughout the game.
~The tones this game can give are quite interesting as it depends on your play style and route             chosen as their are in a way 3 to chose: Pacifist, Neutral, and Genocide.
~The humour was usually fitting and actually made me laugh or at least chuckle.
~The battle system is akin to a bullet hell game, where you dodge incoming attacks except unlike conventional bullet hell games you don't have to fight back. Instead after each attack they throw at you, a dialogue box pops up and you get to chose a course of action through it.
~The boss battles are what make the battle system so good as each boss is unique and has a completely different play style and quirk. On a somewhat related note, each enemy in the game also have a unique battle pattern and way to deal with it depending on the story route chosen.
~Then the music fits very well with each area and battle you come across, but it may get a bit repetitive at times especially if you're in an area for a extended amount of time. Albeit some of the best music is played during boss battles as each boss has their own theme.

Rust is a survival PVE/PVP online multiplayer game. As one of my favorite Youtuber's (VERTiiGO) would say "The Butt Naked World That Is Rust" (VERTiiGO says it in all his Rust gameplay Commentaries.) It is true. You start as a fresh spawn butt naked with only a rock and a torch. You use your rock to hit trees for wood, rock nodes for sulfur ore/stones/metal ore/high-quality metal ore, to try to kill animals like boar's, bear's, wolves, chicken, horses and stag's for leather/cloth/bone fragments/wolf skulls and pork/bear meat/chicken and wolf meat. You have to gather materials to build a base or home to keep yourself and your stuff safe and nothing is safe on rust.
Raids on rust are always a given unless you are on a modded PVE only server. You will be raided and or killed. Raids tend to happen with c4 and rockets (with rocket launchers). But sometimes people will use flamethrowers, the bean can grenades (not really reliable), f1 grenades, satchel charges (kind of like c4 but less damage and less reliable), pickaxes and axes (which neither of those really do much unless you have a ton of them and a ton of time).
The old blueprint system required you to use blueprint fragments, pages, books or library's to get a blueprint (which was random on what you would get) which you would then use and be able to craft that item with the required materials. Or using a research table and the item you wanted the blueprint for (getting them from either points of interest like Radtown, Military Tunnel, Trainyard, Airfield, Satellite Dish, Water Treatment Plant, Powerplant, Sphere Tank, Warehouse's or from Airdrops.
The new experience system requires you to level up by doing the above or giving players crafted items you made and having them do all the work which would give you XP to level up. Every level up to level 30 you unlock different items that you can craft.
They have added blueprints back in a way of research papers. You use an item and research paper you received in the above way to us at the research table to get a limited number of crafting uses for that item which you need the required materials for.
You survive on food and water. Not all water sources are drinkable, only the running water sources are drinkable, water catchers or you have to use a water carrier like a bottle or bota bag to use in any water then using the water purifier to purify the water so you can drink it. You can get water bottles the above ways. For food, you have to hunt and then cook or by running rivers you can get pumpkins and corn, mushrooms that are all over in un-grassy patches that look like dirt. You can also get food from the above ways.
There are also many guns in the game. Use guns to protect yourself, kill animals or to kill people. Some guns are Pump Shotgun, Assault Rifle, Custom SMG and Pistols.
Tools are also in the game and you use them just like the rock. But certain tools work better for certain things. For instance, pickaxes would be best to use on the rock nodes and an axe for trees and chopping up animals or humans which you can get skulls, cloth, raw human meat (not really good for food, even after cooking).
I probably could go on and write a book but I believe I left you with enough information as of right now. If you have any questions please feel free to comment and I will get back to you or if you got to this blog from ifttt posting my blog on my twitter or facebook you can message me on those.

This game is awesome. In way that are rather difficult to describe, this game keeps you entertained for a very long time. I spent hours just cruising around the highways, at times going for so long without a rest stop that my character began falling asleep.
There's something oddly intoxicating about Euro Truck Simulator 2. Visually, it's an impressive game. You'd expect the environments to be boring and repetitive, but they're not. Everything has a unique vibe and you can clearly distinguish industrial districts from the more rural ones.
There's really not much else to it. You need to play it to understand why it's entertaining. I suggest getting some of the mods that make the map bigger, though, since after a while driving from Dijon to Paris gets tedious.
Fun simulator game :)

Now don't be fooled by the 'simulator' part. This is actually a really, really solid experience.
On the one hand you've got a driving simulator, shipping stuff all across Europe on the big road listening to the radio or what have you, which is all well and good on it's own, but the game also has a tycoon bit in it, where you buy garages, hire drivers and equip them with trucks to drive.
Leveling up is fast enough that it doesn't feel like too much of a chore to get bigger and better, but slow enough to give the game a good lifetime. Couple that with the tycoon aspect and you've got a long game in front of you, potentially endless if you really like cruising the French countryside on the way to England to drop off a shipment of forklifts while managing a hundred drivers across the continent.
The physics are very solid and well-rounded, there's a lot of difference between driving with no trailer, driving with a few tons of corrosive acid or driving with sawdust panels. Try not to go too fast around corners with too much weight, you'll regret it. Turned into a highway into mainland France like 15 minutes away from my drop-off point and I had to call for assistance because I ended up on the side.
If you're skeptical, give the demo a try. If you find that you like it, I wholeheartedly recommend purchasing it and getting to work on your truck empire.

I have games like 7 Days to Die, that came out around the same time as this, made by a small team The Fun Pimps, Vs. a bigger company like BI. Pretty sure the Fun Pimps have made much less on 7 days to die and sold less copies than DayZ.

Where to start with this?
As you can see, I've played this game a lot. Unfortunately, this game, a game I once poured hours into, is broken. Back when it was released (yes, I was sad enough  to buy this on the day of release) it had great potential. The engine was clunky and the content was lacking but the environment it provided as an open world survival game was unmatched. Despite the lack of content, myself and about 4 friends would play this nearly everyday, forming a squad and roaming around the map and frankly, enjoying ourselves more than playing a lot of full build games.
It seemed odd that a pre-alpha game could give me more pleasure than games I'd paid £50 for, that were out of developement, yet slowly but surely the developers destroyed everything that was fun about it. It started with them neglicting the core problems and with Dayz and instead focusing on minor content addition, which sound great given what I have just stated above about the lack of content. But when said content doesn't even spawn into the game or fails to work entirely just as you're about to engage in a fire fight, it starts to dampen the spirits and begs the question, was this content even added? They were focusing more on adding more guns/armor when most players were struggling to run this busted engine on pretty solid hardware (or were starving to death before reachign the nearest town).
Without getting into a hardware tin helmet war, I run on a 7970 Ghz Edition (Yep that's 5 year old hardware), FX8350 (@4.2Ghz), 8GB 2133Mhz and a 256GB SSD. A pretty average gaming system from what I can gather even by todays standards. Yet the game ran better 3 years ago than it has done for the last 18 months. I am right in thinking that the idea of pre-alpha is to optimise and streamline the game to better run on a larger percentage of the community's hardware? So why is my reasonably spec'd PC struggling to run this game on LOW preset OUTSIDE of major cities? I struggle to push 50FPS nowadays and around 17FPS in Elektro, averaging about 25FPS the rest of the time. When the game was released I got around 35FPS in cities and 70/80FPS out in the open (West of NW Airfield) at approximately  HIGH settings (Rotational Blur off but Alpha to Coverage on All Trees and Grass) with my average around 45FPS.
Fundamentally the game is broken, it isn't built on an engine fit for the mass market. If you don't have £1500 to burn on the latest hardware then you won't even have the game playable  never mind it being remotely pleasing to the eye.
That's just the graphical part of the problem though, let's assume you have endless amounts of money and I'm only one step up from the infamous console peasant. You still are unlikely to have any success with this game.
As of writing this, we are on patch 0.61 (maybe 0.60, I care little to check tbh), the game is 3 years old, the player base has disintegrated and newer, more developed (and dare I say better games?) have been released. The is no stability, there is no content and there is no interest in this frankenstein corpse of a game. It has been easily hacked, exploited and left to die in the box that is labelled "early access". The points most boasted are the integration of animals into the engine and the utopian idea that "it isn't quite as buggy anymore". I mean, what do we really have to work with there? OH FANTASTIC, WE HAVE EVEN MORE HOSTILES TO LAG THROUGH WALLS AND ONE TAP US AFTER SPENDING 4 HOURS WALKING AROUND THE MAP FINDING OUR FRIENDS AND NOT STARVING TO DEATH. Yeah, god save this glorious developer, right? No.
There is nothing to do, nothing to strive for. There is no progression or goal that you can aim to complete. You spawn, you starve (Nice loot spawns guys), you die, you respawn. If you do somehow manage to break this cycle once or twice I'm sure you'll find a nice ladder or doorway that will break your legs and ruin all the gear you've collected over the last 72 hours. If you're lucky enough the glitch will have despawned the morphene and bandages you've been carryign too, at least then you can rage quit the game instead of proving your insanity.
For the sake of the integrity of the gaming comminity and showing developers that we won't back games which are taking money from us without any reward, don't buy this game. Take your money and bet it on Elvis still being alive, you can die knowing you spent your money on the wisest option of the two. GL & HF friends.

Now don't be fooled by the 'simulator' part. This is actually a really, really solid experience.
On the one hand you've got a driving simulator, shipping stuff all across Europe on the big road listening to the radio or what have you, which is all well and good on it's own, but the game also has a tycoon bit in it, where you buy garages, hire drivers and equip them with trucks to drive.
Leveling up is fast enough that it doesn't feel like too much of a chore to get bigger and better, but slow enough to give the game a good lifetime. Couple that with the tycoon aspect and you've got a long game in front of you, potentially endless if you really like cruising the French countryside on the way to England to drop off a shipment of forklifts while managing a hundred drivers across the continent.
The physics are very solid and well-rounded, there's a lot of difference between driving with no trailer, driving with a few tons of corrosive acid or driving with sawdust panels. Try not to go too fast around corners with too much weight, you'll regret it. Turned into a highway into mainland France like 15 minutes away from my drop-off point and I had to call for assistance because I ended up on the side.
If you're skeptical, give the demo a try. If you find that you like it, I wholeheartedly recommend purchasing it and getting to work on your truck empire.

Undertale is possibly my favorite game ever, and I don't say that lightly. The gameplay is good, but not amazing. In combat, it's turn based with a simple timing mechanic for attacking, and you dodge attacks similar in style to a SHMUP (Shoot'em Up). The other option is talking to the monsters that attacked you, and you have to figure out what to say or do to pacify them and press on, meaning you can finish the entire game without ever killing a monster. The sprites are well done with some special sprites that are rarely used again, showing a special attention to detail. The music is fantastic with VERY few bad songs if any, and the world is interesting. What makes Undertale my favorite game is all the little touches, and most importantly, how it made me feel.

From a longtime DayZ player since 2013:
I am thumbing this game up solely because I like looting and the sporadic gunfights.
The mechanics, after 4 years of development leave a lot to be desired. Invisible zombies, framerate drops, poor vehicle performance, game crashes, among other issues, are still prevalent and have not been resolved. Some bugs, like breaking your legs by walking down a flight of stairs too fast, have been resolved, but too many bugs still remain for 4 years' worth of development.
The long-awaited .63 beta release is up next, and if all that is promised with it so far makes it to the release, the game will see a revival of it's playerbase once again and perhaps will no longer be viewed so negatively. Everyone has the right to write scathing reviews of DayZ, because it could be so much better if the devs fixed the core mechanics, performance, and physics of the game rather than implement a new gun and shirt with every patch, or something like that. For those with little patience, this game would be a complete waste of your money in its current state. Players like me, who have tolerance for the bugs and hours of running from building to building, will continue enjoying the game quietly. I do believe that this game has produced too much revenue for Bohemia for them to abandon their efforts; DayZ WILL become great in the future. Right now it's just...meh with all things taken into consideration.
P.S:
Bohemia, if you're listening, focus on the core framework of the game before adding random things like farming that nobody cares about right now. You'll take less heat from the community if you do that.

Undertale is possibly my favorite game ever, and I don't say that lightly. The gameplay is good, but not amazing. In combat, it's turn based with a simple timing mechanic for attacking, and you dodge attacks similar in style to a SHMUP (Shoot'em Up). The other option is talking to the monsters that attacked you, and you have to figure out what to say or do to pacify them and press on, meaning you can finish the entire game without ever killing a monster. The sprites are well done with some special sprites that are rarely used again, showing a special attention to detail. The music is fantastic with VERY few bad songs if any, and the world is interesting. What makes Undertale my favorite game is all the little touches, and most importantly, how it made me feel.
When Toriel guides you through a dangerous area and grabs your hand, it's a unique sprite and animation, and you can see how her expression is a loving one. Her eye looks back at you, and she has a small smile. The annoying dog that continues to pop up throughout the game, constantly causing laughs. The soundtrack that has a song that is never used in the game, with a title specifically used to mess with your head. Finding the truth of the main antagonist. This game made me happy, sad, joyful, scared, thoughtful, and empty. I can't remember the last time a game has made me feel like this one did, and for that, I have to recommend playing Undertale. It has flaws, it doesn't have the greatest or most unique combat system, but it is my favorite game.
PS - If possible, PLAY THIS BLIND! Part of the fun of the game is experiencing everything for the first time and seeing everything unfold before you.

ETS2 is an impressive game, as on the surface it just looks like an average simulator, but is well detailed and actually portrays driving a truck as accurately as it can. The European environments are beautiful and varied, making every delivery feel unique. The early game can feel a little taxing, as you're forced to use mostly terrible trucks for random employers in order to make money. This isn't all bad, as it allows you to test drive almost every truck in the game before you eventually save up to purchase your own truck.
From there the game gets more open as you can explore and do deliveries at your leisure, eventually building enough capital to hire new drivers to make money for your business as well, or take your money and customize your truck to look more impressive. Ultimately, ETS2 is built to be a relaxing game that's mostly stress-free, yet remains incredibly fun.
My only problem with the game is when driving in towns I would have to frequently save and reload in order to despawn cars--the game will attempt populating towns with an infinite number of cars which never leave due to their close proximity to the player, and with civilian AI being very unintelligent and traffic lights lasting all of five seconds, traffic becomes congested within minutes. Other than that, the game is fantastic and is a great time killer.
I play this using a g27 steering wheel and it's such a wonderful and immsersive experience. Highly recommended.

Undertale is possibly my favorite game ever, and I don't say that lightly. The gameplay is good, but not amazing. In combat, it's turn based with a simple timing mechanic for attacking, and you dodge attacks similar in style to a SHMUP (Shoot'em Up). The other option is talking to the monsters that attacked you, and you have to figure out what to say or do to pacify them and press on, meaning you can finish the entire game without ever killing a monster. The sprites are well done with some special sprites that are rarely used again, showing a special attention to detail. The music is fantastic with VERY few bad songs if any, and the world is interesting. What makes Undertale my favorite game is all the little touches, and most importantly, how it made me feel.
When Toriel guides you through a dangerous area and grabs your hand, it's a unique sprite and animation, and you can see how her expression is a loving one. Her eye looks back at you, and she has a small smile. The annoying dog that continues to pop up throughout the game, constantly causing laughs. The soundtrack that has a song that is never used in the game, with a title specifically used to mess with your head. Finding the truth of the main antagonist. This game made me happy, sad, joyful, scared, thoughtful, and empty. I can't remember the last time a game has made me feel like this one did, and for that, I have to recommend playing Undertale. It has flaws, it doesn't have the greatest or most unique combat system, but it is my favorite game.
PS - If possible, PLAY THIS BLIND! Part of the fun of the game is experiencing everything for the first time and seeing everything unfold before you.

First of all - I own Borderlands 1 & 2. And even though I had some fun times I can not wholeheartly recommend this game.
Lets just leave Borderlands' unique feature, the randomly constructed weapons, aside for a moment and look at the rest of this game: BL2 is fun for a playthrough. The game unfolds most of its potential when you play it with good friends. Lots of laughter ensured of the sometimes hilarious babbles about ponies made of diamonds. Later you will cheer at the treasures you find and show off to your friends. The back-side, though? The further we progressed through the game the duller it got.
Borderlands 2 just never really delivered anything new. New Mobs and Bosses appeared, of course, but for the most part they are just "more of the same". Upscaled enemies or often, not always, just the same with a slightly altered look and a different Prefix.
The Handling of the game isnt flawless either, in my humble opinion. I am okay with the cartoonish-look about BL and its heavily arcade-like playstyle. Especially with my Sniper I couldnt help but feel hindered by the Crosshairs/Laserdots - they felt like huge blots of paint on my ocular and made it difficult to place headshots on far-away enemies. Dropped Loot then isnt player-locked either, meaning that if you stay back to snipe from behind, you will only get the trash your teammates didnt bother to pick up.
Regarding the Loot - I kinda like the Idea of the endless rain of randomly constructed weapons - at some point it got on my nerves, though. Theres a constant flood of mostly garbage-weapons that just clog up your inventory. Tossing a few worthless pistols away is, thanks to the unwieldy Inventory, cumbersome. You can easily see its meant for consoles and not the PC. I would either prefer weapons to be much less dropped, but also much better in terms of stats, so you can actually look forward to a weapondrop - or improve the UI so you can sift through your 24-tons-backpack of (mostly) garbage quicker.
And finally: Borderlands' huge selling-argument - the endless possibilities with randomly constructed weapons: Back when I first heard of the series I actually envisioned endless posibilities: Rocket-launchers with lock-on, mortar-like, with warheads that explode into a radial blast of toilet-bowls. Snipers that would make up for incredible reload-times by firing head-sized fireballs, leaving burning trails or more simple stuff like Machineguns featuring Sniper-oculars, making them suitable for Covering mates over larger distances.
Yes there is some hilriousity like that in the game: Rocketlaunchers firing chainsaws and talking shotguns for example, but those are rather rare. Most of the loot is - like mentioned - just differently colored garbage with slightly shifted stats and a different elemental-type.
All in all the game isnt bad, but unless you really like grinding for stuff, I dont think this game is worth its money. Especially since this is another candidate for the DLC-joyride. If I wanted to keep up with everyone online I would have had to spend maybe another 50 bucks for all the DLCs - one of them even ups the Levelcap from 50 to 60. Having only the basic game I kind of feel like I bought only half of the title back then.

Everyone speaks of the gamebreaking issues DayZ has nowadays, but they forget the most important thing...A while back, I spawned in at the shores near cherno and decided to run towards Balota to try and score some left overs until I seen two figures in the distance standing in the open field outside Balota airfield's walls. These two figures were armed, so I accepted my fate and ran towards them yelling the notorious "F" word, or friendly for the slower folks, and then their attention was on me. One of them looked at me, the other remained seated. Keep in mind, I also had a revolver stuffed inside my sweater incase of an emergency... I ran upclose so that I can hear what they were saying and it was scary at first when I thought they were going to stuff me with lead at any second but it turns out one of the strangers weren't infected with the vibe of shooting people on sight. His name was Jacob... Jacob oh Jacob..His friend was a silent one, well he was afk for several minutes and so we left him alone and ran off towards the Pavlovo military base. Jacob is by far the most intriguing person I have met in DayZ. We had our conversations on our way and I felt we started a thing...A bond..Not brokeback mountain type of bond but something I haven't experienced in DayZ in a while with a stranger.. As we arrived at the military base to gear up, we had no luck at finding what were were looking for. Jacob still had his trusty MP5 with no mag and Skorpian with no mag in hand, and I still had my concealed magnum, not so very concealed after I told Jacob about it but you get the point (I hope). However, it all became dead when me and Jacob heard two foreign footsteps outside the barracks were were in...It was a different person, this one with no gun but a baseball bat to defend himself. Jacob scared him off with a couple bullets from his ferocious Skorpian but he didn't kill him...If only he'd had...So we ran off to Zeleno to check out that military base and once we came up to the outskirts of pavlovo town, my world shattered. Jacob...My only friend...He always ran ahead...He..We still had so much to live for and to see but it all ended in less than a minute. As Jacob was talking about our arrival to Zeleno, a man walked out from cover of a wall and looked at us. His clown mask, his jacket...I have encountered another infected thing, not different to those who lie at Kamy or Cherno shooting innocent fresh spawns. My poor Jacob didn't have enough time to react and the clown started spraying at Jacob..His last fighting words were an incomplete sentence and the last bullet from his Skorpian. I watched in cover as my companion...A friend dropped to the ground dead..No last words to each other, just plain dead. It took me a second to register what happened, and then I looked at the culprit and started unloading .357 rounds on him. I broke his legs and put some more into him but the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ was still kicking. By then, I ran out of ammo and was left to avenging Jacob with my slegehammer..So I ran outside of cover, past Jacob's body to end this menace with my slegehammer. I swung and hit him several times on the back while trying to aim for his head but then it all connected. The clown had managed to shoot off my toe and so I slowly dropped to the ground, envisioning all that happend between me and Jacob recording back in my head, all the jokes and laughs and encounters we had going back to the point where I first him him, and last. I died not feeling awful (even though I did) but knowing that even if I had killed the clown, I would still not have my Jacob by my side..And so I died knowing that I was still together with Jacob in the afterlife.This is the thing about DayZ, you make your stories with people to enrich YOUR EXPERIENCE. ALSO, Jacob If you do see this, end my agony and add me on steam..

This title manages to strike a good balance between simulation and gaming. I enjoy most of the time I spend with it. the scenery is pretty, driving feels realistic but the controls are well thought out. It is good enough in terms of simulation and at the same time, it contains many interesting traditional video game mechanics. That said, you will not regret purchasing this if you feel like taking long drives in realistically modelled trucks, taking a wide range of goods from A to B. There is also the company management side where you buy garages and trucks and hire drivers. Making profit isn't a challenge, but it's nice to grow and expand your assets.
There are a few slight disappointments, however. First off, I don't like how every city is almost exactly the same in terms of scale and scenery. Only the map will tell that you are in London or Paris, they look the same as any other town or city. A couple of unique landmarks would definitely spruce things up. Second, for a game in which driving around is the main objective, I find that the road network is quite coarse. There aren't many turns to make, some parts made unavailable by virtual walls and then road markers that just contain red X's because you can't go where it points to. It's mostly highways and other open roads, no small streets or off-roads to lose your way on.
Overall though, I do recommend this game and special credit must be given to SCS software for being great developers that listen to their players. A dozen patches and improvements have come out since I bought this and they just keep coming. Again, you won't regret your purchase.

ETS2 is an impressive game, as on the surface it just looks like an average simulator, but is well detailed and actually portrays driving a truck as accurately as it can. The European environments are beautiful and varied, making every delivery feel unique. The early game can feel a little taxing, as you're forced to use mostly terrible trucks for random employers in order to make money. This isn't all bad, as it allows you to test drive almost every truck in the game before you eventually save up to purchase your own truck.
From there the game gets more open as you can explore and do deliveries at your leisure, eventually building enough capital to hire new drivers to make money for your business as well, or take your money and customize your truck to look more impressive. Ultimately, ETS2 is built to be a relaxing game that's mostly stress-free, yet remains incredibly fun.
My only problem with the game is when driving in towns I would have to frequently save and reload in order to despawn cars--the game will attempt populating towns with an infinite number of cars which never leave due to their close proximity to the player, and with civilian AI being very unintelligent and traffic lights lasting all of five seconds, traffic becomes congested within minutes. Other than that, the game is fantastic and is a great time killer.
I play this using a g27 steering wheel and it's such a wonderful and immsersive experience. Highly recommended.

When this game first came out, it was quasi-revolutionary, especially given the *way* that it looked, the feel of it, the gameplay, the loot, and, oh yes, the zombies.  Here we are almost three years later, and what has the journey looked like?
--No persistence, loot hard to find
--No persistence, loot explosions
--Finally persistence!  No more loot.
--Hmm, game is laggy, let's take out zombies for six months.
--OK, zombies are back in, but vehicles are no longer persistent.
--Look!  We're working on wolves.
--Vehicles are back!  But, they will randomly despawn.
Get the idea?  This entire development "process" has been one disaster after another.  The game is still plagued by the problems that it had from the beginning--lag, desync, rubber-banding, etc.  PVP firefights are a joke.  As others have mentioned, the game engine that this thing is built on is broken, and there is no fixing it.
I refuse to believe that regular game development works this way.  Do yourself a favor and save your money.  I wish I had.

First of all - I own Borderlands 1 & 2. And even though I had some fun times I can not wholeheartly recommend this game.
Lets just leave Borderlands' unique feature, the randomly constructed weapons, aside for a moment and look at the rest of this game: BL2 is fun for a playthrough. The game unfolds most of its potential when you play it with good friends. Lots of laughter ensured of the sometimes hilarious babbles about ponies made of diamonds. Later you will cheer at the treasures you find and show off to your friends. The back-side, though? The further we progressed through the game the duller it got.
Borderlands 2 just never really delivered anything new. New Mobs and Bosses appeared, of course, but for the most part they are just "more of the same". Upscaled enemies or often, not always, just the same with a slightly altered look and a different Prefix.
The Handling of the game isnt flawless either, in my humble opinion. I am okay with the cartoonish-look about BL and its heavily arcade-like playstyle. Especially with my Sniper I couldnt help but feel hindered by the Crosshairs/Laserdots - they felt like huge blots of paint on my ocular and made it difficult to place headshots on far-away enemies. Dropped Loot then isnt player-locked either, meaning that if you stay back to snipe from behind, you will only get the trash your teammates didnt bother to pick up.
Regarding the Loot - I kinda like the Idea of the endless rain of randomly constructed weapons - at some point it got on my nerves, though. Theres a constant flood of mostly garbage-weapons that just clog up your inventory. Tossing a few worthless pistols away is, thanks to the unwieldy Inventory, cumbersome. You can easily see its meant for consoles and not the PC. I would either prefer weapons to be much less dropped, but also much better in terms of stats, so you can actually look forward to a weapondrop - or improve the UI so you can sift through your 24-tons-backpack of (mostly) garbage quicker.
And finally: Borderlands' huge selling-argument - the endless possibilities with randomly constructed weapons: Back when I first heard of the series I actually envisioned endless posibilities: Rocket-launchers with lock-on, mortar-like, with warheads that explode into a radial blast of toilet-bowls. Snipers that would make up for incredible reload-times by firing head-sized fireballs, leaving burning trails or more simple stuff like Machineguns featuring Sniper-oculars, making them suitable for Covering mates over larger distances.
Yes there is some hilriousity like that in the game: Rocketlaunchers firing chainsaws and talking shotguns for example, but those are rather rare. Most of the loot is - like mentioned - just differently colored garbage with slightly shifted stats and a different elemental-type.
All in all the game isnt bad, but unless you really like grinding for stuff, I dont think this game is worth its money. Especially since this is another candidate for the DLC-joyride. If I wanted to keep up with everyone online I would have had to spend maybe another 50 bucks for all the DLCs - one of them even ups the Levelcap from 50 to 60. Having only the basic game I kind of feel like I bought only half of the title back then.

For some reason, I keep coming back to this one periodically. I was originally addicted to the 18 Wheels of Steel series, but this one is MUCH better. Many improvements in gameplay and graphics make this take on the 'big hauler' types of games refreshing and entertaining. There is something about just leisurely driving along miles of roads that makes for entertaining and relaxing gameplay. There's no pulse pounding intense shooting matches or scoreboards to keep an eye on. Instead it's you, your truck (once you can afford one) and the open road for miles, along with some stupid drivers you have to keep an eye out for. This game is well balanced and allows you to from a penniless trucker, having to drive company trucks for a small profit per mile, to owning your own truck for greater profits, with plenty of upgradeability choices and brands to choose from, all the way to a mogul with a garage full of hard-working drivers and trucks, and further to a chain of garages across europe. ETS2 is an impressive game, as on the surface it just looks like an average simulator, but is well detailed and actually portrays driving a truck as accurately as it can. The European environments are beautiful and varied, making every delivery feel unique. The early game can feel a little taxing, as you're forced to use mostly terrible trucks for random employers in order to make money. This isn't all bad, as it allows you to test drive almost every truck in the game before you eventually save up to purchase your own truck.
From there the game gets more open as you can explore and do deliveries at your leisure, eventually building enough capital to hire new drivers to make money for your business as well, or take your money and customize your truck to look more impressive. Ultimately, ETS2 is built to be a relaxing game that's mostly stress-free, yet remains incredibly fun.
My only problem with the game is when driving in towns I would have to frequently save and reload in order to despawn cars--the game will attempt populating towns with an infinite number of cars which never leave due to their close proximity to the player, and with civilian AI being very unintelligent and traffic lights lasting all of five seconds, traffic becomes congested within minutes. Other than that, the game is fantastic and is a great time killer.

When this game first came out, it was quasi-revolutionary, especially given the *way* that it looked, the feel of it, the gameplay, the loot, and, oh yes, the zombies.  Here we are almost three years later, and what has the journey looked like?
--No persistence, loot hard to find
--No persistence, loot explosions
--Finally persistence!  No more loot.
--Hmm, game is laggy, let's take out zombies for six months.
--OK, zombies are back in, but vehicles are no longer persistent.
--Look!  We're working on wolves.
--Vehicles are back!  But, they will randomly despawn.
Get the idea?  This entire development "process" has been one disaster after another.  The game is still plagued by the problems that it had from the beginning--lag, desync, rubber-banding, etc.  PVP firefights are a joke.  As others have mentioned, the game engine that this thing is built on is broken, and there is no fixing it.
I refuse to believe that regular game development works this way.  Do yourself a favor and save your money.  I wish I had.

Borderlands 2 is an open world First Person Shooter with obscene amounts of weapons, variety and personality developed by Gearbox known for such greats such as Duke Nukem Forever and Aliens: Colonial Marines... OK don't let that put you off this game as if you did you would be missing out on one of the greatest First Person Shooters of all time.
[THE GOOD]:
This game has a fantastic art style that fits perfectly with the humor and the world around it, a simple detail that is a breath of fresh air in compatison to all the games trying to be as photo realistic as possible. The absurdity of the world of pandora allows for extreme amounts of guns, ind by this i mean that this game doesn't lie when it says it has a bazillion guns, and the legendary guns feel very fun to use plus some of them are extremely creative.
The classes (Gunzerker, Siren, Commando, Assassin, Psycho and Mechromancer) are all very unique and fit very well with different playstyles allowing everyone playing to have fun for example, the gunzerker is good for the run and gun players, the psycho is the melee driven tank, the commando is for the people who somehow like every game to be a bloody cover shooter the siren for locking  enemies into place and working with teammates etc. this can make for very diverse gameplay and in turn is incredibly fun, the skill trees are also incredibly well balanced and is is clear that a lot of effort went in to the more interesting skills and even some of the passives making effective skill builds take a lot of thought, this is further boosted by the class mods buffing skills and adding unique passives to help improve your build.
The story is simple but effective and the characters (particularly the primary antagonist Handsime Jack) with comical, consistent personalities. This makes the plot much more engaging, as Handsome Jack is a genuinely horrible person with understandable yet incorrect morals, this allows plot points to be fantastic and unpredictable.
[THE BAD]:
I probably missed a lot from the good, however the fact that the game's quality drains significantly if you play the game alone, although it remains fun, the game is centred around the multiplayer campaign and the singleplayer is unbalanced as a direct result.
Another problem i have with the game is the menus are slightly irritating, the port is poor in this respect (this is the only area in which i believe this to be true) and you spend too much time looking at the menus asking yourself 'which gun is better?' which can get annoying if you just want to shoot things
[FINAL VERDICT]:
buy this game... just... buy this game.

This game has been in development for quite some time now and I have been basically waiting for this "sweet spot" in development. A spot where enough of the end game features are present, to make the game enjoyable on its own, when those features interact with one another.
I think we may have reached this point at 0.61. Besides many obvious bug fixings, starting off from the coast and just wandering into the map blindly, without taking your old pre-0.61 routes, is now actually enjoyable enough. There are enough zombies present to make it a little bit better at mood setting. There are weird new noises from deer and wolves (who also attack you). The loot system no longer is completely broken in either directions (not too little and not too much). Most buildings can now be entered and pretty much all coastal spawn points now have enough loot spots on the road, or around them, away from major settlements to give you good enough surviving odds.
Quite simply, I think this game has nearly matured and is getting closer to be consider out of beta. Not quite there yet, but if you were to start playing now, you may even keep on playing it, if their rate of development continues on at the same pace.

The best thing about this game is the experience.
I have not spent a lot of time in Europe, but I feel like I have after driving from Scotland to Hungary. You've probably read all the other reviews here and in publications talk about the experience of just slipping into some kind of "groove". You will be cruising down the autobahn with a load of potatoes at 3:00 AM with the radio on to some Dutch station and just lose yourself in that moment, almost as if you can roll down the window and feel the wind blow in. Those moments create immersion in a way few games can and this game will creep up on you with them. When you do make it to Milan with those potatoes you will feel like you've accomplished something.
The experience is the best part about this game, and while it's great I find myself wishing that the whole "company management" aspect of this game was done just a bit better. It has the bare bones there, you buy trucks, hire guys, buy garages, make money, but I wish it had more depth and strategy than it does. There's enough there to make you care about hitting the road with that load of tractors or upgrading your engine, but it's not quite what it could be to make this a truly killer game.
But what is here, those "on the road moments", is worth it.

This title manages to strike a good balance between simulation and gaming. I enjoy most of the time I spend with it. the scenery is pretty, driving feels realistic but the controls are well thought out. It is good enough in terms of simulation and at the same time, it contains many interesting traditional video game mechanics. That said, you will not regret purchasing this if you feel like taking long drives in realistically modelled trucks, taking a wide range of goods from A to B. There is also the company management side where you buy garages and trucks and hire drivers. Making profit isn't a challenge, but it's nice to grow and expand your assets.
There are a few slight disappointments, however. First off, I don't like how every city is almost exactly the same in terms of scale and scenery. Only the map will tell that you are in London or Paris, they look the same as any other town or city. A couple of unique landmarks would definitely spruce things up. Second, for a game in which driving around is the main objective, I find that the road network is quite coarse. There aren't many turns to make, some parts made unavailable by virtual walls and then road markers that just contain red X's because you can't go where it points to. It's mostly highways and other open roads, no small streets or off-roads to lose your way on.
Overall though, I do recommend this game and special credit must be given to SCS software for being great developers that listen to their players. A dozen patches and improvements have come out since I bought this and they just keep coming. Again, you won't regret your purchase.

This game has been in development for quite some time now and I have been basically waiting for this "sweet spot" in development. A spot where enough of the end game features are present, to make the game enjoyable on its own, when those features interact with one another.
I think we may have reached this point at 0.61. Besides many obvious bug fixings, starting off from the coast and just wandering into the map blindly, without taking your old pre-0.61 routes, is now actually enjoyable enough. There are enough zombies present to make it a little bit better at mood setting. There are weird new noises from deer and wolves (who also attack you). The loot system no longer is completely broken in either directions (not too little and not too much). Most buildings can now be entered and pretty much all coastal spawn points now have enough loot spots on the road, or around them, away from major settlements to give you good enough surviving odds.
Quite simply, I think this game has nearly matured and is getting closer to be consider out of beta. Not quite there yet, but if you were to start playing now, you may even keep on playing it, if their rate of development continues on at the same pace.

Really relaxing game. Pure fun after playing all those intense games like Battlefield, etc.
Driving is very fun, though it feels that you need a gamepad at the very least to fully enjoy this game. Analogue triggers help when needing to maintain a certain speed at short bursts (aka inbetween traffic lights). Driving long distances can be tiring (just like real life >.<), and Euro Truck Simulator fixes this authentically by providing a radio feature that allows you to connect to real radio stations (of your choice too), lightening up the mood. Crashes, speeding, accidents do occur if you are not careful, so no space for much dilly-dallying (though I might say the game isn't terribly unforgiving).
Vehicle customisation allows for very varied trucks. Even if you purchase an entry level truck, depending on the brand, it could be very powerful through upgrading, eliminating the need to buy another truck (unless it is for your company of course). You can spray paint your truck to look much better than just plain-red or white, and designs are more-or-less varied.
A business model is incorporated into this game. You can purchase garages, which after upgrading allow you to purchase multiple trucks (at least 3 trucks can fit in a garage). To maximise the use of these garages and trucks, you can also hire workers who will be happy to work for you. Through this, you can eventually start earning huge amounts of money (or even lose money). It is quite engaging, but takes quite a while (I have so far hired one driver only after 14 hours of playing [without any bank loans]) to really start kicking, which requires quite a bit of dedication.
Graphics are pretty, with nearly every road having distinct features and landmarks. In terms of realism, the game doesn't really do much to push even the weakest of computers, even at high settings. Road textures could be better, some cities look uninspired and lighting is a hit-or-miss, sometimes there is too much bloom and sometimes there is too little.
AI in this game falls-back a little when compared to the quality of the other mechanics in this game. The AI is a little shoddy, and is exuded in narrow junctions or turning points and lane converging points, where you can have cars or trucks crashing right into you while you make a turn or suddenly switch to your lane, completely ignoring the fact that you are right next to them. They usually never acknowledge blinkers or horns, rendering them useless 80% of the time, detracting the immersion you get from this game. However, the impact is only prevalent in tight-corners or narrow areas such as cites. In highways, they are less of a nuisance.
Pros-
Great driving, fun especially with music
Very relaxing
Sufficient vehicular customisation
Engaging business mechanic
Wider range of unique places to explore
Cons-
Poor AI
Graphics not too great when it comes to realism (which sort of coincides with simulation)

For some reason, I keep coming back to this one periodically. I was originally addicted to the 18 Wheels of Steel series, but this one is MUCH better. Many improvements in gameplay and graphics make this take on the 'big hauler' types of games refreshing and entertaining. There is something about just leisurely driving along miles of roads that makes for entertaining and relaxing gameplay. There's no pulse pounding intense shooting matches or scoreboards to keep an eye on. Instead it's you, your truck (once you can afford one) and the open road for miles, along with some stupid drivers you have to keep an eye out for. This game is well balanced and allows you to from a penniless trucker, having to drive company trucks for a small profit per mile, to owning your own truck for greater profits, with plenty of upgradeability choices and brands to choose from, all the way to a mogul with a garage full of hard-working drivers and trucks, and further to a chain of garages across europe. The environments are nice to look at, and the weather effects are well done. The driving physics are detailed and it sounds like they're going to keep improving and upgrading this game. A definite buy if your'e looking for something without constant pulse-pounding action you can sit back and relax to for hours of calm gentle driving with the periodic (realistic) traffic jam or crazy driver.

On June 12, 2016, Omar Mateen, a 29-year-old security guard, killed 49 people and wounded 53 others in a terrorist attack/hate crime inside Pulse, a gay nightclub in Orlando, Florida, United States. He was shot and killed by Orlando Police Department (OPD) officers after a three-hour standoff. Pulse was hosting Latin Night and most of the victims were Latino. It was both the deadliest mass shooting by a single shooter and the deadliest incident of violence against LGBT people in United States history. It was also the deadliest terrorist attack in the United States since the September 11 attacks in 2001.
In a 9-1-1 call shortly after the shooting began, Mateen swore allegiance to the leader of the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL), Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, and said the shooting was "triggered" by the U.S. killing of Abu Waheeb in Iraq the previous month. He later told a negotiator he was "out here right now" because of the American-led interventions in Iraq and in Syria, and that the negotiator should tell the United States to stop bombing.
Initial reports said Mateen may have been a patron of the nightclub and used gay dating websites and apps, but Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) officials said they have not found any credible evidence to substantiate these claims. The Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) also conducted an investigation and said it found no links between ISIL and Mateen.

This game is far more fun than it should be.  It's relaxing, driving around in your big rig to music from the many online radio stations from around the world.  It's challenging, trying to park your rig to earn that extra money and XP.  It's got a very nice progression system, earning experience to improve your skills.  Customizing your trucks with better equipment and paint styles.  It's deep, in that you can buy your own garages, hire drivers, buy trucks for them to drive and grow your business.  It's beautiful, the scenery is sometimes breathtaking as you drive across farming fields, through cities, over mountain roads, through the rain and fog and night time.  It's one of my favorite games of the year, and although I find that surprising to say out loud, it honestly is.  It's like the Elite or Privateer of driving simulation games.  Very much recommended if you want a relaxing but fun and challenging driving game.

"Borderlands 2 builds upon the gameplay elements introduced in its predecessor. It is a first-person shooter that includes character-building elements found in role-playing games, leading Gearbox to call the game a "role-playing shooter." At the start of the game, players select one of four new characters, each with a unique special skill and with proficiencies with certain weapons. From then on, players take on quests assigned through non-player characters or from bounty boards, each typically rewarding the player with experience points, money, and sometimes a reward item. Players earn experience by killing foes and completing in-game challenges (such as getting a certain number of kills using a specific type of weapon). As they gain levels from experience growth, players can then allocate skill points into a skill tree that features three distinct specializations of the base character."
"Borderlands 2 begins with the player fighting to the death to win a priceless cache of loot in a gladiatorial tournament run by Handsome Jack for his personal amusement. The player succeeds and gains notoriety, but Handsome Jack sees this as a threat to his popularity with the people. At the tournament's end he denies the reward and leaves the player for dead in a tundra. The mysterious Guardian Angel from the first game then contacts the player and explains that Handsome Jack must be killed, directing the player to rescue the four original vault hunters from Hyperion's clutches to accomplish this. Although Jack's full intentions are unknown, part of his plan involves finding an ancient evil named "The Warrior" that is located somewhere on Pandora."

EARLY ACCESS REVIEW
So, this is the game that stared the survival hype.
After many years in development (original ArmA 2 mod released back in 2012!) it's far from being finished. Question is: is it worth buying in it's current state and was the hype around DayZ justified?
DayZ 's been entertaining since the original mod released, the standalone is entertaining since it's early pre-alpha as well.
It's one of those games where bugs might infuriate you but still can be forgiven because the game sucks you in.
Even after years of playing DayZ, every encounter with an other player raises my pulse an gets me on the edge. I'm not the kill on sight guy, but oh lord, I had to kill many and have been killed even more times. And I remember most of those encounters. That's what makes DayZ special: you'll remember those moments after years. DayZ can be frightening, ecstatic, tense.
DayZ is still the good old "run away from the coast-loot as much as you can grab-die to a ridiculous reason-rinse&repeat" sim:
That will never change. Even if they add flying saucers to the release version. But it's astonishingly entertaining in beind that.
Most of all, it's very immersive. Dev's did you an outstanding job in converting the old Chernarus map, and they still keep on adding stuff and transforming the environment into the most believable and largest explorable post apocalyptic landscape that you'll see out there.
DayZ is a game with actual content to be discovered, not a fraud. How broken and unfinished it may be there's ton of fun to be discovered. No matter if you're playing the lone wolf, socializer or take the bandit path. Every new life is like a new story to be told. (There's so much more to discover in Chernarus then just the NE Airfield, lol)
So: yes. It's good. And it's shaping up to be even better, it's getting more unforgiving with every patch. Soon as we're forced to live from the land, harassed by hordes, preadators, weather, nature and illness with scarce loot- it might be one of my all-time favourite games.
P.S. Don't trust reviews that state "omg ♥♥♥♥ is broken don't buy!!11! fraud" from ppl having played ~800 hours and more. DayZ is still in alpha, but there's been a ton of new features and improvements esp. to the core engine during the last year. It will be finished.
