The game has come a long way over the past 2 years. Their patches are getting more and more indepth as well as provoding more content and working features per patch rather than just adding things and hoping they work.
-Since 0.60, the game has been massivly optimised and in 0.61 it's even better.
-The camera is less jagged and moves smoothly.
-The gun sounds have been inproved as well as gunshot sounds from a distance.
-Zombies, oh man, they are back with force. They jump over gates, fences, crawl on the floor, aggro to sound, stealth is actually viable now since you can use it to sneak past zombies to not be seen. Oh and all of their new models have been added.
-Loot. It has become a mission to find it, as it should be. You may be forced to find some seeds and hoe to start farming as a way to get food. Or you could setup camp near an apple tree and pick apples from it to slowly fill you up.
-Wolves....Running at night has never been scarier. On top of the Zombie threat that exists once again, wolves have been added as predators. You may come across a lone wolf or a pack of them. Just let it be known, if they see you, run.
Overall, I'm very happy with the progess they have made off 2 patches. The 0.60 and 0.61 patches have added over 4gb of content to the game alone. I def recommend this game, especially if you have friends that play it or are interested in playing it.
*EDIT*
Though I dont have nearly the hours that some people have in this game, I have been playing it for two years. I've seen the changes of NE Airfield (RIP) and additions of cities. This game has def come a long way since patch 0.39. And the hackers, havent seen any since 0.59.
If you dont want to spend the money to get the game, then don't. No one is twisting your arm to get it. You are paying for a game that is still in development and will probably still be in it another year or so. You are paying to watch the game grow and maybe find a community that you can hang with. You're paying for a incomplete game that has bugs, glitches, and is on the road to something amazing. But like I said, if you don't want to pay the money for the game, believe the rage reviews, or are looking for a complete game, then don't buy it. All I can say is that I got my money's worth out of it.

I never knew anything about UNDERTALE and didn't watch any videos on it but I was told about it by some friends of mine, and one of them gave it to me for my birthday, so I didn't have any expectations apart from knowing it was an RPG.
I think what makes the game so unique and entertaining is the fact that is has entertaining and intriguing characters. Normally in RPG games you just have to kill bosses without any thought, because that's how progression works in RPG games, but in UNDERTALE you have the choice of deciding whether or not to kill or save the enemies in this game, which gives you time to think because in the game, the actions actually matter.
UNDERTALE is one of those unexpected games that can make you cry, because the story is so well done to an extent, no matter what your choice is. Giving the characters backstories really benefitted the game because it made it feel more realistic and more "life-like" whereas in most RPG games it just feels like an endless grind or just mindlessly killing just to progress further, but this game defeats that purpose... almost.
The grinding in the game isn't a huge flaw, but sometimes it feels like a chore to do. However it does feel worth it though considering the consequences of what you do in the game and how it can deeply effect the story of the game entirely.
The game has many endings but three main endings. One if you choose to be pacifist, one if you choose to kill everyone and one if you do a mixture of both killing and sparing. Both versions of the story are well-thoughtout and impactful and very entertaining and managed to keep me playing even just after a boring part (not like there is any in this game) happened.
Another huge pro to this game is the soundtrack. The soundtrack may just be one of the highlights of this game. It is so well crafted and fits the respective characters very well and is definitely worth buying / listening to.
Overall, UNDERTALE is a really good game which changed how RPG games worked and managed to make a captivating and entertaining storyline.

If you are looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an Peanut Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
1/2 cup butter,
softened 1/2 cup peanut butter
1 cup packed brown sugar
1/2 cup white sugar
2 eggs
2 tablespoons light corn syrup
2 tablespoons water
2 teaspoons vanilla extract
2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon baking soda
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 cups chopped semisweet chocolate
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
In a large bowl, cream together the butter, peanut butter, brown sugar, and white sugar until smooth. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the corn syrup, water, and vanilla. Combine the flour, baking soda, and salt; stir into the peanut butter mixture. Fold in chocolate chunks. Drop by 1/4 cupfuls 3 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes in the preheated oven, or until edges are golden. Allow cookies to cool for 1 minute on the cookie sheet before removing to wire racks to cool completely.
And eat it!

Mesmerizing game, the career progression is spot-on and makes it really addictive. You only need to drive a few short trips before you can buy your own rig & build a company employing other drivers. The real joy comes from completing jobs driving across Europe. There's quite a variety of scenery that varies with the location - more pine trees in the North for example - and plenty of variety in the road network - you'll drive both on multi-lane divided freeways as well as unmarked rural roads and brief inner-city encounters. The distances & time scaling work well - a trip can take between one minute and several hours of real time depending on the distance - although starting out you'll only get short trips of less than an hour. Time slows down when manually parking a trailer - close to real time - so you don't have to panic to get a job parked in time (or just press Enter in range of the drop-off point to avoid the hassle). I could play this game for hours - it's mostly a relaxing experience after you get accustomed to your inputs (eg. steering with a mouse) but still has its moments of tension when close to the deadline on a rush delivery or overtaking another truck at midnight on a winding two-lane rural road.

Story and characterization are the biggest draws of this title. There are no deep mechanical systems to work with to build up your character, nor is the combat (conflict?) system something that will satisfy someone looking for a challenge. The quirky environment and its cast of strange creatures are where the richness of the game lies, as they help propel you along the game's central plot. Although the game is fairly minimalist, little details and bits of dialog can be found all over for those inclined to exploration.
There are a few branches in the plot that have a fairly large impact; barring spoilers, you may have to play the game twice or thrice to see all that you want to see.
If you are someone who can get attached to the characters and story (possibly two or three times), you should find Undertale a satisfying, emotional ride well deserving of its reputation.  If that isn't really your thing and you are looking for more "game" in your game, or for a more serious and nuanced storyline, this may not be the best choice.

This game is easily one of my all-time favorites. A couple of friends had gotten really hyped up about it and convinced me to get it, and I was glad they did. Borderlands 2 is a healthy mix of RPG, story, Co-op, and picking up 87 bajillion guns and shooting them only to find another 87 bajillion guns 10 minutes later. The story on the game is amazing. I've read other reviews and that's the most criticized part. Many said it was shallow, didn't make sense, and was just pointless. You're allowed to disagree, but in my opinion they couldn't be more wrong. The story was interesting, engaging, funny, and had it's share of plot twists. I personally enjoyed the story and have yet to get sick of it. The drop-in drop-out co-op is really nice when playing with friends. My only criticism is that farming/grinding can be tedious and sometimes boring. I've had my fair share of times where I want a Legendary weapon and have farmed a boss for over 3 hours and have gotten nothing. Leveling up can be difficult once finishing a playthrough where you're stuck mobbing/killing raid bosses over and over. I still find that kind of fun, but others don't, so be aware of that. All in all, Borderlands 2 is a fantastic game, with nearly unlimited replay value, a great story, rewarding gameplay, and a quirky sense of humor. I highly recommend this game to anyone, RPG fans or not.

This game is amazing. But calling it a game would be too low for this masterpiece. Euro Truck Simulator 2 can run on a dinosaur pc, intel graphics, or you can have it devour all the power your PC can push, and it LOOKS AMAZING! It's a great way to wind down after a long day at class or work.

Best Simulator!!!

Mesmerizing game, the career progression is spot-on and makes it really addictive. You only need to drive a few short trips before you can buy your own rig & build a company employing other drivers. The real joy comes from completing jobs driving across Europe. There's quite a variety of scenery that varies with the location - more pine trees in the North for example - and plenty of variety in the road network - you'll drive both on multi-lane divided freeways as well as unmarked rural roads and brief inner-city encounters. The distances & time scaling work well - a trip can take between one minute and several hours of real time depending on the distance - although starting out you'll only get short trips of less than an hour. Time slows down when manually parking a trailer - close to real time - so you don't have to panic to get a job parked in time (or just press Enter in range of the drop-off point to avoid the hassle). I could play this game for hours - it's mostly a relaxing experience after you get accustomed to your inputs (eg. steering with a mouse) but still has its moments of tension when close to the deadline on a rush delivery or overtaking another truck at midnight on a winding two-lane rural road.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is one of the premier titles of all the big simulators, and it deserves that praise. The game features a good, all though not perfect, driving mechanic, easy to navigate menus, a good selection of trucks standard (not to mention the ones you can download as mods), a variety of cargo to haul (again, you can download more as mods), and a huge map. Oh, did I mention mods? There is a slew of good mods out there ranging of custom trucks, accessories for trucks, and extensions to the map adding places such as Scandinavia.
The career mode is the real meat of this game. You'll start out taking deliveries for other companies in trucks provided for you. Before long, you can start your own business with a garage and start building your trucking empire. The business management side of this game isn't too deep, but it a nice addition none the less. You can buy and upgrade garages located in the major cities across Europe, as well as buy additional trucks and hire drivers to drive those trucks for you. Other drivers can be levelled up, as can your own personal driver. These upgrades range from better fuel economy to the ability to drive ADR class hazardeous materials. Hired drivers won't bring in much money from the start, but once you get a few of them upgraded you'll find yourself with more money than you'll be able to spend.
The scenery in ETS2 is a real strong point, but there is room for improvement. Much of the back roads are indistinguishable from one another. There is little to tell you that you're driving through southern France instead of eastern Poland. The actual cities themselves are very simplified, consisting of only a few roads to travel. There is a picture of the city in the background that does feature accurate buildings found in the real city (the Gurken in London for example), but you can't actually drive to those locations. Nevertheless, it's a really enjoyable experience to carry a load from the north of Hungary to Glasgow in Great Britian, passing across thousands of miles and a ferry trip. Driving in the early morning and watching the sun rise, or late in the evening and watching it set, is a great part of the game that really brings out the best of the the graphics.
The game itself plays pretty smoothly. I have an older system running a Radeon HD5800 and I can max this game out and still have a stable framerate. There are rain effects in the game, all though there isn't any seasonal changes (you can get a snow mod however). The weather effects look fantastic, all though it would be nice to get a seasonal cycle where you can get snow. Perhaps we'll see this in a future installment. There is also radio stations to listen to, and these are actual, live internet radio stations. It's a very little detail that really contributes to the overall experience. Driving through Germany listening to Star FM Berlin really makes the game feel real and authentic.
The controls are a real strong point. If you're feeling brave and want to use a keyboard and mouse, you can do that. Have a gamepad and want to use that? Go for it. But the real fun is with a wheel and pedals. I have a Fanatec 911 Turbo S wheel with a 6 speed H pattern shifter, and it really makes the game come alive. You can even use the real 12 speed split gear pattern that the real Scania R Line trucks use. You simply won't find that it another sim.
Overall, ETS2 is a ridiculously good deal. There is lot's of replay value here, even if you're not looking to get into it all the way with a wheel and pedals. I would highly recommend this title to anyone considering it, you won't be disappointed.

So this game sounds really stupid, right? Sounds like just driving trucks around? Well, that's totally what it is. However, its a lot more fun than it originally sounds, and for some reason, it's kept me coming back for more.
When you first start the game, you are asked to create a company for your trucking business. When you start, you don't have enough capital or credit to take out a loan, so you just take "quick missions" running freight from European city to city. This serves as a pretty good introduction to the game, and allows you to get a good feel for how the game plays. This is what drew me in. I had a lot more fun than you'd expect attaching the back of the trailer to the truck and driving it around the roads. There's not much actual city driving, as the cities themselves are pretty small. But that's okay. As I found out one day, I really am not playing this game to sit in traffic, so if there was just a bunch of city with cars, I don't think I'd like it very much. Sure, it would be more "real", but sometimes you should sacrifice reality for fun.
After you get the trailer hitched up, you roll out of the industrial park you picked it up in and get on the road. This game doesn't work with a controller, as there are too many buttons to push to fit on a controller. You need to use you turn indicators, check your mirrors and change your views. You need to drive inside the lines, not hit other cars, and generally just obey all traffic laws. Again, this sounds really boring, but when you finally get to your destination, and you haven't hit anyone, its pretty rewarding. It also helps most cars drive faster than you, so you don’t have to play that annoying weaving game of trying to pass cars because they drive 20 MPH below the speed limit.
When you get enough capital, you can take out a loan and buy your own truck. The trucks they have for sale are all real trucks, and all have different stats and strengths. You then can take missions for your business and every mission has advantages and disadvantages (eg, the dangerous cargo gives you the most money). Every mission your complete (quick job or company mission) gives you experience and level up various stats, such as levels of dangerous cargo, increased fuel efficiency, and increased money for each mission. I haven’t got too far into the business side of the game, but I hear you can hire other drivers to work for you.
Overall, I enjoy this game thoroughly. For some reason, it’s compelling to come back just drive by the trees and fields of Europe, even if they're not the real thing.

This game is an abomination. More than anything else I've played recently, it's atrociously designed, moronic and utterly without redeeming features. I barely know where to start. How about with this? Half the time it's more expedient to let people kill you. Why? Because a feature called 'second wind' gives you a generous period after 'death' in which to finish an enemy off, rewarding you with all your shield and some health back. Fighting enemies is so laborious and repetitive, with so little opportunity to reduce the damage you take, that the best tactic is to repeatedly 'die' and then miraculously come back to life using second wind.
How about this? The game supposedly lets you play a sniper character. But can you infiltrate enemy camps stealthily, picking them off from a distance? No, you cannot. The rifles are so weak, and most of the enemies so preposterously over-armoured, that a direct headshot has little effect - except to alert every enemy in the area to your presence, causing them to immediately charge at you, screeching irritatingly.
But that's not even the worst of it - you can't infiltrate or snipe principally because most enemy camps are almost empty ... until, that is, you're inside them, whereupon they spawn waves of enemies out of black holes. You can wearily gun your way through them, but there's no real way to dodge, hide or retreat. You just have to weather their firepower and mow them down. Tedious. Extremely so. Here's a very common thing that happens when I play: "Right, that's the last of them dead. Wait, I can still hear the faint rat-tat-tat of gunfire and my shield appears to be being chipped away at. Looks like I'll have to perform a careful 360-degree turn to try to work out which of these many black holes all around me has belatedly decided to spawn one more bandit. Oh, there also appears to be someone repeatedly hitting me. I'd better sort that out."
How about this? The way ammo is dispensed/used up is unforgiveably stupid. Glowing green boxes, lockers, crates, barrels and toilets are littered everywhere, all containing guns and ammo, but since you have to empty about four clips of any gun into a single enemy, you soon run out. So a huge portion of the game is spent foraging and reloading, foraging and reloading. Opening lockers. Opening bins. Opening toilets. Why not just have less of this nonsense and have the enemies go down much more quickly? Do I really have to shoot twelve rounds from a high-powered sniper rifle into someone (three rounds at a time, with annoying reloading intervals) to get them to stop harassing me?
And that word, 'harrassing'? That's what it feels like. Nothing in this game feels particularly dangerous or testing. It's all just harrassment. They filled the world with hundreds and hundreds of fireamrs, but they might as well be spud guns. Enemies defeat you by mobbing you and filling you with hundreds of bullets while you reload every few seconds and gradually work your way through them. It's a war of attrition. An incredibly boring one.
The collision detection for melee combat is obviously woeful - it always is in games like this. I made the mistake of picking a character whose special talent is to project a hologram, them go invisible, allowing them to perform an assassination strike. A fat lot of good it is against any enemy who attacks with fists, since you can't actually come up behind them without getting hit by a punching animation that's directed the other way.
Why is there so much utter faffery around choosing which weapons to use? Each gun has about twelve statistics, plus additional bonuses and defects, which you're supposed to compare and contrast in order to find your favourites. And the game spits weapons at you at a rate of about one every minute. Enemies drop them. Enemy camps are flooded with them. Vending machines sell them.
Want to upgrade your character? Grind through dozens of boring encounters to level up and enjoy adding 0.6% to dozens of achingly dull statistics, like accuracy, reload time and zoom level. You will never notice a difference in how the game plays. It's still grinding, grinding, grinding, through the same braindead goons who roll up, absorb five clips' worth of ammo, then fall down slowly, only to be replaced by another identical enemy emerging from the same ♥♥♥♥ing bivouac.

If you are looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an Peanut Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
1/2 cup butter,
softened 1/2 cup peanut butter
1 cup packed brown sugar
1/2 cup white sugar
2 eggs
2 tablespoons light corn syrup
2 tablespoons water
2 teaspoons vanilla extract
2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon baking soda
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 cups chopped semisweet chocolate
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
In a large bowl, cream together the butter, peanut butter, brown sugar, and white sugar until smooth. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the corn syrup, water, and vanilla. Combine the flour, baking soda, and salt; stir into the peanut butter mixture. Fold in chocolate chunks. Drop by 1/4 cupfuls 3 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes in the preheated oven, or until edges are golden. Allow cookies to cool for 1 minute on the cookie sheet before removing to wire racks to cool completely.
And eat it!

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is one of the premier titles of all the big simulators, and it deserves that praise. The game features a good, all though not perfect, driving mechanic, easy to navigate menus, a good selection of trucks standard (not to mention the ones you can download as mods), a variety of cargo to haul (again, you can download more as mods), and a huge map. Oh, did I mention mods? There is a slew of good mods out there ranging of custom trucks, accessories for trucks, and extensions to the map adding places such as Scandinavia.
The career mode is the real meat of this game. You'll start out taking deliveries for other companies in trucks provided for you. Before long, you can start your own business with a garage and start building your trucking empire. The business management side of this game isn't too deep, but it a nice addition none the less. You can buy and upgrade garages located in the major cities across Europe, as well as buy additional trucks and hire drivers to drive those trucks for you. Other drivers can be levelled up, as can your own personal driver. These upgrades range from better fuel economy to the ability to drive ADR class hazardeous materials. Hired drivers won't bring in much money from the start, but once you get a few of them upgraded you'll find yourself with more money than you'll be able to spend.
The scenery in ETS2 is a real strong point, but there is room for improvement. Much of the back roads are indistinguishable from one another. There is little to tell you that you're driving through southern France instead of eastern Poland. The actual cities themselves are very simplified, consisting of only a few roads to travel. There is a picture of the city in the background that does feature accurate buildings found in the real city (the Gurken in London for example), but you can't actually drive to those locations. Nevertheless, it's a really enjoyable experience to carry a load from the north of Hungary to Glasgow in Great Britian, passing across thousands of miles and a ferry trip. Driving in the early morning and watching the sun rise, or late in the evening and watching it set, is a great part of the game that really brings out the best of the the graphics.
The game itself plays pretty smoothly. I have an older system running a Radeon HD5800 and I can max this game out and still have a stable framerate. There are rain effects in the game, all though there isn't any seasonal changes (you can get a snow mod however). The weather effects look fantastic, all though it would be nice to get a seasonal cycle where you can get snow. Perhaps we'll see this in a future installment. There is also radio stations to listen to, and these are actual, live internet radio stations. It's a very little detail that really contributes to the overall experience. Driving through Germany listening to Star FM Berlin really makes the game feel real and authentic.
The controls are a real strong point. If you're feeling brave and want to use a keyboard and mouse, you can do that. Have a gamepad and want to use that? Go for it. But the real fun is with a wheel and pedals. I have a Fanatec 911 Turbo S wheel with a 6 speed H pattern shifter, and it really makes the game come alive. My thoughts and review of Borderlands 2:
First to start off it is an improvement over Borderlands 1 and it is a very good port with many graphic options to choose from, which every PC game loves.
Borderlands 2 has improved in a few areas such as more interesting characters, better NPCS and an overall better story compared to Borderlands 1.
Something that it has not improved on from the first game is the classes, each class has their own special ability and than passive upgrades you get while you level up. The problem is the passives are soooo boring. Examples would be "Do 10% more damage with melee, do 10% more damage with certain guns, Recharge shield and health 10% faster... And so on.
And the so called "87 bazillion weapons" is obviously exaggerated. While their are a ton of guns you'll constantly find yourself finding the same guns over and over with a slight change to their stats. ALTHOUGH their is also a great variety of crazy and cool weapons that you'll have a blast with. No matter what, you will find a gun that suits you and you like.
As for the story, it's far better than Borderlands 1, I can see some people not getting into it but for me I actually wanted to pay attention to the story and try to find all the audio logs to find more bits to the story.
Inclusion this an awesome FPS and it deserved the praise that it got.
(On a side note) A lot of people say to play this Coop because it's "impossible" to beat by yourself. That's just not true, I beat it fairly easy on solo and I also prefer solo because any weapon/shield I find is mine! In coop it's kind of like a rat race trying to grab the best loot before everyone else.
I don't like giving games scores so I'll just say this is a must have game and you'll end up sinking hours on end into it,
Borderlands 2 has and will always be one of those games that never get boring. With the DLC and other options that are avalible it makes the game a never ending game.

A sequel that completely eclipses its predecessor.
Tons of varied environments ranging from icy mountains to futuristic cities and volcanic canyons and guns that are not just simple reskins of each other but also feel different for the most part with diverse and "funky" modifiers; they scream while firing, they may explode on reload, etc.
The PC version is also really well done this time arround with lots of options including FoV tweaking and UI placement/ resizement.
Matchmaking is handled throught Steam so dropping in and out of a game is a breeze.
Story and characters are also emphasized in comparison to the 1st one, with a likeable yet truly evil main bad guy, a completely insane little girl and characters from the 1st title making a triumphant return, with the game taking more time to showcase each one's personality a little bit better.
This doesn't mean however that BL2 has become a story or character driven game.
It's still the same gun-toting, over the top violent loot fest as it was before, with quests just being an excuse for you to go buck wild on your enemies.
There are also raid bosses and tweaks since the game's release have made soloing them more difficult than before, just as it should be.
DLCs have also rebalanced the game's economy, especially Eridium that has other uses now than just inventory upgrades and Raid Boss fees.
The season pass is also highly recommended as it adds hours upon hours of new content to the game.
Recommended for solo, HIGHLY recommended for co-op.

This game is an abomination. More than anything else I've played recently, it's atrociously designed, moronic and utterly without redeeming features. I barely know where to start. How about with this? Half the time it's more expedient to let people kill you. Why? Because a feature called 'second wind' gives you a generous period after 'death' in which to finish an enemy off, rewarding you with all your shield and some health back. Fighting enemies is so laborious and repetitive, with so little opportunity to reduce the damage you take, that the best tactic is to repeatedly 'die' and then miraculously come back to life using second wind.
How about this? The game supposedly lets you play a sniper character. But can you infiltrate enemy camps stealthily, picking them off from a distance? No, you cannot. The rifles are so weak, and most of the enemies so preposterously over-armoured, that a direct headshot has little effect - except to alert every enemy in the area to your presence, causing them to immediately charge at you, screeching irritatingly.
But that's not even the worst of it - you can't infiltrate or snipe principally because most enemy camps are almost empty ... until, that is, you're inside them, whereupon they spawn waves of enemies out of black holes. You can wearily gun your way through them, but there's no real way to dodge, hide or retreat. You just have to weather their firepower and mow them down. Tedious. Extremely so. Here's a very common thing that happens when I play: "Right, that's the last of them dead. Wait, I can still hear the faint rat-tat-tat of gunfire and my shield appears to be being chipped away at. Looks like I'll have to perform a careful 360-degree turn to try to work out which of these many black holes all around me has belatedly decided to spawn one more bandit. Oh, there also appears to be someone repeatedly hitting me. I'd better sort that out."
How about this? The way ammo is dispensed/used up is unforgiveably stupid. Glowing green boxes, lockers, crates, barrels and toilets are littered everywhere, all containing guns and ammo, but since you have to empty about four clips of any gun into a single enemy, you soon run out. So a huge portion of the game is spent foraging and reloading, foraging and reloading. Opening lockers. Opening bins. Opening toilets. Why not just have less of this nonsense and have the enemies go down much more quickly? Do I really have to shoot twelve rounds from a high-powered sniper rifle into someone (three rounds at a time, with annoying reloading intervals) to get them to stop harassing me?
And that word, 'harrassing'? That's what it feels like. Nothing in this game feels particularly dangerous or testing. It's all just harrassment. They filled the world with hundreds and hundreds of fireamrs, but they might as well be spud guns. Enemies defeat you by mobbing you and filling you with hundreds of bullets while you reload every few seconds and gradually work your way through them. It's a war of attrition. An incredibly boring one.
The collision detection for melee combat is obviously woeful - it always is in games like this. I made the mistake of picking a character whose special talent is to project a hologram, them go invisible, allowing them to perform an assassination strike. A fat lot of good it is against any enemy who attacks with fists, since you can't actually come up behind them without getting hit by a punching animation that's directed the other way.
Why is there so much utter faffery around choosing which weapons to use? Each gun has about twelve statistics, plus additional bonuses and defects, which you're supposed to compare and contrast in order to find your favourites. And the game spits weapons at you at a rate of about one every minute. Enemies drop them. Enemy camps are flooded with them. Vending machines sell them.
Want to upgrade your character? Grind through dozens of boring encounters to level up and enjoy adding 0.6% to dozens of achingly dull statistics, like accuracy, reload time and zoom level. You will never notice a difference in how the game plays. It's still grinding, grinding, grinding, through the same braindead goons who roll up, absorb five clips' worth of ammo, then fall down slowly, only to be replaced by another identical enemy emerging from the same ♥♥♥♥ing bivouac.
What a load of♥♥♥♥♥♥ Seriously.

DayZ is only getting better and .60 showed us that. The EA development could've been faster but we're getting there. Still, buy at your own risk, this game is not for everyone.
Been playing DayZ SA since its release and I have to say that I was very frustrated for over 2 years (as most people were) with the development progress of this game. I get why people hate DayZ that much but I'm not one of them.
After the biggest patch thus far, 0.60, the game is completely playable and fun. I rarely drop below 50fps with High+ settings. The renderer did work wonders and I cannot wait for the new player controller and dynamic lighting and infected spawning in the upcoming patch.
Most nasty bugs have been fixed, the game runs smooth, tons of things are still getting added to the game, servers are most stable than ever, and the community is less toxic now.
This is not a finished game by any means, but in my opinion, DayZ right now, is far better than it ever was. We still have at least a year or more until the finish line, but at this point, why give up? It's already been 3 years since the EA release...might as well stick with it till the end.
This game is not for everyone! Not that much because of its technical state, but because it's unforgiving, slow, semi-realistic, clunky and requires a lot of patience. It's not a run 'n gun game. Go play something else if you are looking for a fast-paced game.
Last thing is the modding community. When BI will release modding/server tools, the game will only get better and all kinds of servers will be up, ranging from full-on PVP to hardcore survival RP servers. People will play the DayZ they want to, resulting in a (hopefully) better experience for everyone.
Overall, I'd say that DayZ is still the King of zombie/post-apocalyptic survival games. The atmosphere and suspence is something that only this game has truly captured, while its competitors seem too casual and joyful for me. And it's only getting better...slowly though.

Undertale is a game that teaches you how people who seem bad or evil, may be more than just bad.
I'm aware that this game's been out for over a year now, but I'll still keep spoilers to a low here.
This game encourages you to SPARE monsters that you encounter on your quest, but you don't have to follow that rule. The game remembers pretty much all the things that you do, and because of that, it has over 20 different endings depending on what you do.
If you're a fan of bullet-hells, then you'll like the game's unique way of how the battle-system works. You have two options when it comes to fighting an enemy; FIGHT, or MERCY. (Although, you'll have to ACT to the monster before you can SPARE them) Both options are solutions to ending a battle. When an enemy attacks, it becomes a bullet-hell, but if you are used to bullet-hells, then you'll find this game too easy. Yes, it does get harder as you progress, but as stated before, if you're used to playing bullet-hells, than this will be a cake-walk for you.
Honestly, this game focusses more on Story and characters rather than Gameplay. That's not to say that the Gameplay is bad. Gameplay is a bit simple, and that's about it. If you play games only, and I mean ONLY, for gameplay, your experience may not be as great as others. If you are into Stories and Character Development, you'll most likely love this game.
Basically, UNDERTALE is more of an Interactive Story that has Gameplay Elements, so if your up for a good Story that you can control, then go ahead and buy it!

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is the sequel to the lesser-known Euro Truck Simulator, if the titles didn't tip it off, and does exactly as it suggests: you drive a long-haul truck across much of Europe for many hours. Now, it's probably coming across as slightly... boring. And, yeah, it is a little bit. The scenery isn't always spectacular, and the highways don't generally differ in design and traffic.
But, like the award-winning Papers, Please, which was just about working a tedious desk job, or Cook, Serve, Delicious, ETS2 is one of those simple games where, if you're not always on guard, you're going to mess up.
For real-life drivers, it's known that the road has a sort of lull, where between the hum of tires, vibration of the engine, and stock sights, you find it easy to doze off. Now, behind the wheel of a huge semi-truck, it becomes a much larger issue. And this game simulates it, not to mention the things like gas and money.
There's also the hazards of speed cameras and sudden changes in limit, cars cutting you off, and sudden death at the hands of merging buses. It's always a good idea to remap the turn signals to Q and E, if you're on keyboard, which the game is against, just so they're easy to use. You'll need them.
While rather... empty, what scenery does exist of Europe's classical countryside is attractive, and some of the urban areas are actually very pretty to look at. Don't expect a full city to explore, though, we're simulating, we're not stealing cars and taking peyote, here.
Some other features of ETS2 are the managment section, where the player might develop an armada of trucks and build a real business out of the shambles you start in, a working internet radio you can listen to while driving, and multiplayer is in progress, though in a separate mod.
The main draw, I think, is just the simple idea that you can drive a huge, gas-guzzling, speed-limit busting truck without too much consequence. There's no police, most places are sparse on traffic, and you get the cargo to Strasbourg on time. With so many cities and a shrunk-down map of Europe available to explore, ETS2 is also a good sight-seeing game. Makes me want to visit Warsaw.
All in all, ETS2 is a good game for an easy, but not relaxing, ride around Europe while making a pretty digital penny.
Also, if North American trucking is more your thing, SCS software is working on that for their next game. All of the U.S. I, for one, am going to crash into my house multiple times.

I have played DayZ since the beginning of the Arma 2 mod, I have been through the ups and downs over the years of development.
At the time of this review, the graphics are phenomenal and after one of the previous major updates it drastically improved frame rates as well. Sometimes there are some issues with shadows, or stretched texture, but it is much less common than ever before.
I remember the first day the standalone went into alpha. Basically nothing worked and I mean
The DayZ mod had more features. But over the years more and more features are being added. Now there are vehicles and to get them to run you have to have a certain degree of knowledge on how combustion engines work, which I think is awesome. You can handcuff someone, put a bag over their head and lock them in a room. Hell, you can force someone to eat your old rotten fruit.
Each time you die, you respawn in a random location with no gear. This is unlike every game nowadays that has virtually done away with any penalties for dying. Not only does this provide a more meaningful gameplay experience, but also drastically improves the replayability as well. The adrenaline rush you get when you get into a firefight with another survivor will keep you coming back for more.
Many people may disagree about this, but the fact of the matter is the alpha has been out for 3 years and the developers are still adding new content to the game. There are very few indie devs that commited to their game (the only other one I can think of off the top of my head is Space Engineers
Personally I have (at the time of this review) 190 hours into the game, which is a 6.3 value, which means I got 63x more entertainment than going to a movie, a GREAT deal in my book.

I think this game will never be finished, was a good source of income off an idea of a good game.
-Good day.

I love game like this, and have Euro Truck Sim and UK Truck Sim already.
This isn't a blending of the two, it's much more.
They've really impressed me with this game...with all the extra stuff they've added.
It took me a while to get the hang of the new steering system, but once I did I found it to be much easier and less jerky than before.
It's much more realistic, and I've even seen pedestrians in this game.  I just saw a jumbo jet land as I was driving down the motorway.
They've added many more ferry services, toll roads and even level crossings.  I thought they were just decoration but nope, I saw a train earier with the barrier and lights and everything.
Customisation is a great addition, although the extra lights don't really help unless you have high beams on, and the other drivers don't like that...flashing me when I'm using them.
The AI has been improved too.  For example, in Euro Truck SIm 1, if there was a blockage of any kind, the AI cars just sat there with their hazard lights flashing.  If you were behind them, you had to find an alternate route, ot barge through...bad idea.
This time, the AI doesn't just sit there.
I'll give you a quick example.  I was coming up to a junction, and saw a lot of stationary traffic.  Yep, blockage.  There was a bus trying to turn left, but a truck was trying to turn right and they'd kinda blocked each other.  The other road had cars trying to go but this bus was stopping things.
I thought I was gonna have to drive round, but nope...I was shocked to see the bus actually reversing into a better turning position, turn then drive on it's way.  The truck then did the same, turning into the right road...end of blockage and all was well.
The AI even wait at the on-ramps for it to become clear, and even go into the petrol stations now.  It's much more realistic and enjoyable.
Although, the AI isn't perfect.  Right of way is still a mystery to them.  I was driving down a main street, and the cars on either side of the junction should've waited for me to pass before driving out, but nope...at the last moment a truck came out and I couldn't avoid it.
That's the only bad thing I can say about this game...but if you know about it, you can avoid it.
9/10 rating from me because of the little flaws (lights and AI), but other than that I'm really enjoying this game.

Borderlands 1 was a revolutionary game that thrusted the player into a ficticious world of aliens, monsters, bandits, and of course, weapons. The playable characters all had their own unique strengths and weaknesses, as well as their own niches. The boss fights were great, the loot system was well though-out, and in general, it was a great game.
Borderlands 2, took all these qualities, and built upon them ten fold. The story was jacked up by so much by giving the player an actual, physical antagonist, Handsome Jack. The character designs were well-made, and the gun designs were ramped up and were also given a much more wide variety of quirks that a gun could have about it. The characters were also more balanced, allowing for anyone wishing to play any of the four playable characters to freely choose who they wanted and have the same level of importance as that of any other character.
In general, if you enjoy gun-toting action coupled along with an RPG-style game and crude humor, then this game is for you.

There aren't many realistic simulators on the market which is quite strange to say. There's an abundance of games such as Farming Simulator 2013 but these can't be called realistic considering the physics engine. ETS2 does not suffer from these problems. The graphics are ridiculous and the level of detail is mind numbing. Also theres no Farming Simulator physics found here; whether you're using a keyboard or a controller the acceleration is slow and the steering weighty it therefore feels like you are driving a truck.
Not only is ETS2 a good simulator but it is also a good game and it is likely you will spend hours trying to build up your truck business from just one truck to a massive empire.
And not to mention the large amount of mods available, making it so you can adjust the gameplay to suit your style of driving.
If you are going to buy any simulator, do yourselves a favour and make it this one.

I'm kind of in awe as to how much fun can be had with Euro Truck Simulator 2. In many ways it feels like an RPG: You create your character, start off by taking random jobs, until eventually building yourself up enough to start a company of your own. You can hire other drivers, buy a fleet of vehicles, take out loans to expand, basically what you'd expect to go along with owning and operating a trucking business. It's a pretty deep system and surprisingly fun to mess around with.
If you don't want to deal with the management aspects, though, you can simply take quick jobs and focus on the fantastic driving portion of the game. It's hard to explain, but there's something that's simply relaxing and soothing about driving an 18-wheeler across European highways, soaking in the atmosphere, listening to the radio, and trying to get to your destination on time and with your cargo in tact. Along your trip you'll have to deal with things like speed traps, traffic, sleep deprivation, inclement weather, and perhaps worst of all... parking (which in RPG terms would be considered the dungeon boss fight at the end of your long quest).
To make things better, there's a devoted modding community that has helped produce hundreds of downloads that add realism to various aspects of the game. Some are as simple as new skins, while others completely overhaul the physics and add enhanced sound effects.
In all, ETS 2 was a big surprise for me, a game that I never really took seriously until I finally decided to give it a shot. A truly fresh and interesting experience that had me engrossed from the start. It's very accessible even for newcomers to the genre (such as myself), so if you have any interest in driving/management games at all, I'd recommend at the very least giving the free demo a try. You might just get hooked like I did.

Yes, this is not for everyone.  I bought this game after seeing a few streams online and began enjoying myself the second I started it up.
Surprisingly immersive, don't go bunching this game with all of the other, crappy sim games.  In a time where games are all about explosions, flashy graphics and shooting, it's surprisingly refreshing to drive a big rig for two hours en route from Edinburgh to Amsterdam while obeying traffic laws and listening to some european radio (yes, the game supports radio station streams from accross Europe out of the box).
The trucking company sim also seems decently in-depth, allowing you to buy garages your operations are based out of, hire drivers, buy trucks and slowly dominate the european shipping economy!
Give it a try if you can get your hands on it for a decent price and enjoy driving.  Analog controller or USB steering wheel highly recommended.

DayZ Standalone was easily my most anticipated game to be released back when it first came out in early access. Now, it is the biggest disappointment I have ever had. In a review for  this game I wrote awhile ago, I went on about how the game has barely progressed in the several years it had been in early access and that if you want a more developed, while not as good looking, version, buy Arma 2 Combined Operations and install the Epoch mod. It is likely that you will have a better experience doing so at a cheaper price. All of this still holds true, each development cycle furthering the time it takes for them to work on their game changing updates, which generally involve a few new coats and backpacks. DayZ standalone is just a prime example of how not to do early access. They took people’s money far before they should have and promised them a game that would never come to be. At one point I would have said that the game was a cash grab, which now has been proven wrong. It isn’t a cash grab, it’s just a game, that could have been amazing, that is being developed at an extremely slow pace. They are focusing on the wrong things and getting ahead of themselves. Rather than work on the still atrocious performance and lack of meaningful gameplay mechanics, they continue to pump out more clothing and weapons that you will likely never find. Back when the game was first released in early access in late 2013, it was a free for all where you found a gun and clothes and then proceeded to kill everyone in sight. Almost three years later it is the exact same thing, just now you can decide how fashionable you want to be while doing so. All of this having hours of mostly uneventful walking between it. Like I said at the start of this review, I wanted to love this game, I still do. I have yet to find another game that gives me an adrenaline rush when I see another player like it did and it saddens me to have to write this review for what was such a promising game, but as it stands there just isn’t enough in it to warrant a purchase and the development team is likely to give up on it before it’s anywhere near finished. If you want to play this kind of game I would look to Arma 2 Combined Operations with the epoch mod installed for a proper experience, not just a walking sim with rinse and repeat gameplay.

I bought DayZ SA the day it came out. I had played the Arma 2 mod in the past and was excited to try the game in a newer form.
I loved it. I played it all the time, hence my 200ish hours in it. I'd spawn, head north, die and repeat over and over again.
Eventually I got tired of doing the same thing over and over again and took a break, probably sometime mid 2014.
Since then, I've come back to play it about 3 or 4 times. Usually I play it for a week to see what they added, realize they added nothing, then leave.
They haven't updated the game since July of 2016, which was their first update of the year. Their current experimental version has been out for around 2 months or so.
The point of this story? I feel my views reflect the views of the community. I'm sick and tired of doing the same thing every time I play. I'm tired of the trash community that get ghillie suits and snipers and sit for hours on end waiting for victims to show up. I'm tired of waiting 6 months for 3 new items and a "change" in the engine (when nothing's actually changed.)
I'm pretty sure I wrote an old review as a meme but now I'm being serious: don't buy it. Maybe consider it when the devs are done wiping their asses with our money and decide to use it for this "early access" game.
Edit: A few months and one major update later, there have been minor improvements. The game runs smoother, looks better, etc. The bi-weekly status reports are nice as well, even if there aren't any new updates. It shows the dev team is at least involved to some extent. Still not enough to get a thumbs up, but it's a start.

Where should I begin? A simulation game that to drive a truck and deliver goods would be any good or exciting things to do? Hell no....at least that what my though before I bought it. See it pops up on steam sale and with over 3000 recommendations is really make me curious, so I'm like "whatever, if it's not that good, at least I can get to visit many Europe places that I probably won't visit in my life time."
BUT, I got totally blown away. This, is by far the best simluation game I ever played. Yeah, I know my "game protfolio" doesn't seem to convince any one. But my first sim goes way back, it's the monochrom Inday Car racing sim on a 5.25 floppy disk. I've played tons of sim games, fighter jet(most of Microprose releases), racing(from arcade to realistic ones), tanks(yeah, not COD ones, actual tank sim that you have to do a lot to kill another tank, but I forgot the game name, it's really old), MS Flight Sim. And dropped this genre because there is nothing new to revisit. So, to back my credibility a bit. Back to topic.
Euro truck simulator 2 is really good. The sound effects, environment, and sense of speed is all there. I don't have a wheel here, and don't have fancy paddles and shift sticks. Even playing with button mapped gamepad, this game is a joy to play with. You have to manage a lot of stuff for sure, just like in real life. Like put on signals, turn on/off wiper when it's raining( if you go under a over pass, rain will actually stops and then continue, talking about details), putting lights on when it's dark, lean out of driver side window when you are reversing into cargo bay, and yeah honk as well as cruise control !! And there are many body type to choose from and the internal view is actually different from truck to truck.
Of course it's not perfect, some of the truck is like ninja truck that change lane and off ramp like it's a mini cooper, or the fact that you eat ticket if your body( not including cargo) does not cross stop line when traffic light turns red. Or say you expect they have entire Europe, but in fact they only have most western EU and limited city area that you can explore. Or the fact that some of the road in a city is actually blocked by virtual hologram huds( this is by far I think the worst part of this sim, they could've just use road blocks or construction sites wtih detour signs to make it more realistic. )
But, when you put on signals to left turn, cars on coming traffic would actually yield and let you turn left in no traffic light controlled area. When you are on highway, road construction will generate those familiar noise you heard in real life and AI will merge to the lane still open just like in real life. If you drive too much off the side, the vibration sound of your tire hitting those side marking lines will remind you to correct your course. There are so many details that I have yet to discover with my roughly 2 hour play time so far. There is career mode, emergency delivery, managing a comany and so on. And after all, supporting Mods from the community.
I rarely write recommendation for a game on Steam, but if you are anywhere like to drive or just wanna do some relaxing stuff to kill sometime without stress, Euro Truck Simulator 2 is highly recommended. :happymeat:

Borderlands 1 was a revolutionary game that thrusted the player into a ficticious world of aliens, monsters, bandits, and of course, weapons. The playable characters all had their own unique strengths and weaknesses, as well as their own niches. The boss fights were great, the loot system was well though-out, and in general, it was a great game.
Borderlands 2, took all these qualities, and built upon them ten fold. The story was jacked up by so much by giving the player an actual, physical antagonist, Handsome Jack. The character designs were well-made, and the gun designs were ramped up and were also given a much more wide variety of quirks that a gun could have about it. The characters were also more balanced, allowing for anyone wishing to play any of the four playable characters to freely choose who they wanted and have the same level of importance as that of any other character.
In general, if you enjoy gun-toting action coupled along with an RPG-style game and crude humor, then this game is for you.

DayZ Standalone was easily my most anticipated game to be released back when it first came out in early access. Now, it is the biggest disappointment I have ever had. In a review for  this game I wrote awhile ago, I went on about how the game has barely progressed in the several years it had been in early access and that if you want a more developed, while not as good looking, version, buy Arma 2 Combined Operations and install the Epoch mod. It is likely that you will have a better experience doing so at a cheaper price. All of this still holds true, each development cycle furthering the time it takes for them to work on their game changing updates, which generally involve a few new coats and backpacks. DayZ standalone is just a prime example of how not to do early access. They took people’s money far before they should have and promised them a game that would never come to be. At one point I would have said that the game was a cash grab, which now has been proven wrong. It isn’t a cash grab, it’s just a game, that could have been amazing, that is being developed at an extremely slow pace. They are focusing on the wrong things and getting ahead of themselves. Rather than work on the still atrocious performance and lack of meaningful gameplay mechanics, they continue to pump out more clothing and weapons that you will likely never find. Back when the game was first released in early access in late 2013, it was a free for all where you found a gun and clothes and then proceeded to kill everyone in sight. Almost three years later it is the exact same thing, just now you can decide how fashionable you want to be while doing so. All of this having hours of mostly uneventful walking between it. Like I said at the start of this review, I wanted to love this game, I still do. I have yet to find another game that gives me an adrenaline rush when I see another player like it did and it saddens me to have to write this review for what was such a promising game, but as it stands there just isn’t enough in it to warrant a purchase and the development team is likely to give up on it before it’s anywhere near finished. If you want to play this kind of game I would look to Arma 2 Combined Operations with the epoch mod installed for a proper experience, not just a walking sim with rinse and repeat gameplay.

I'm pretty sure I wrote an old review as a meme but now I'm being serious: don't buy it. Maybe consider it when the devs are done wiping their asses with our money and decide to use it for this "early access" game.

I know what you're thinking: "A truck driving simulation? Is this a joke?" Believe it or not, it's no joke. I can't explain why it's as fun as it is, but driving around Europe while hauling fertilizer or a load of brand new cars is very interesting and slightly addictive!
You start out taking small jobs where you use a company's truck and cargo, but eventually you'll find a nice place to start your own business. You'll get your own truck, and then drive around picking up jobs, attaching to loads, and even getting the manual parking bonus! After you get comfortable with that, it's time to hire other drivers! As long as they do a good job, the money will start rolling in and you'll be able to trick your truck.
I always like to relax by taking a load on a long haul, listening to the streaming internet radio built into the game, and enjoying the scenery. It really gives you an appreciation for what real truckers deal with, not just with controlling their rig, but things like weather and traffic are VERY different in a huge truck vs a normal passenger car.
The title may sound like some sort of joke, a fake game title, but I assure you it is very real and a definite sleeper hit!

I'm kind of in awe as to how much fun can be had with Euro Truck Simulator 2. In many ways it feels like an RPG: You create your character, start off by taking random jobs, until eventually building yourself up enough to start a company of your own. You can hire other drivers, buy a fleet of vehicles, take out loans to expand, basically what you'd expect to go along with owning and operating a trucking business. It's a pretty deep system and surprisingly fun to mess around with.
If you don't want to deal with the management aspects, though, you can simply take quick jobs and focus on the fantastic driving portion of the game. It's hard to explain, but there's something that's simply relaxing and soothing about driving an 18-wheeler across European highways, soaking in the atmosphere, listening to the radio, and trying to get to your destination on time and with your cargo in tact. Along your trip you'll have to deal with things like speed traps, traffic, sleep deprivation, inclement weather, and perhaps worst of all... parking (which in RPG terms would be considered the dungeon boss fight at the end of your long quest).
To make things better, there's a devoted modding community that has helped produce hundreds of downloads that add realism to various aspects of the game. Some are as simple as new skins, while others completely overhaul the physics and add enhanced sound effects.
In all, ETS 2 was a big surprise for me, a game that I never really took seriously until I finally decided to give it a shot. A truly fresh and interesting experience that had me engrossed from the start. It's very accessible even for newcomers to the genre (such as myself), so if you have any interest in driving/management games at all, I'd recommend at the very least giving the free demo a try. You might just get hooked like I did.

Right now, the component system gives all players a chance to be on equal footing, avoiding being bulldozed by veteran players and the occasional server admin abuse. Axton the Commando, is very similar to Roland. Axton was not exactly a repeat but had a lot of simularities to the previous commando, so he will feel familiar to players of the original commando.
Zero the Assassin, Zero is can either be similar to mordecai or the complete opposite. He has three trees one focuses on sniping and getting huge criticals. His second is called cunning and does exactly what it says. It has benefits for guns and also melee so it is a nice balance of the inbetween. His last focuses on pure melee and lifesteal, he deals massive amount of melee damage to everyone and everything, he is also able to recloak after killing an enemy.
Maya the Siren, is similar and different to Lillith. She focuses on elements as the same as Lillith, but her real difference is her ability. Phaselock, essentially removes the target from the battle lifting them up in the air and freezing them. This can be changed depending on the skill tree that has been chosen. If the target is to large or heavy (usually bosses) it deals significant damage to the bus as a trade off.
Gaige the Mechromancer is very unique. Her ability releases a robot called Deathtrap that wrecks house, he can be upgraded throughout all three trees. She can rebound bullets off walls which is very interesting and entertaining. Anarchy is what one tree focuses on. For every kill and magazine reloaded fdue to no bullets in combat adds 1.75% damage and subtracts the same amount in accuracy. This a source of nearly endless entertainment as you can use whole clip and not hit anyone.
Kreig the Psycho. He is essentially a controllable psycho, thats all that needs to be said.

Bought the game a long time ago. I have spent playing more than 400 hours on this game with a bunch of friends and sometimes solo.
The game changed quite alot from the simple Blueprint Era to the Experience Age to the current Component era. Right now, the component system gives all players a chance to be on equal footing, avoiding being bulldozed by veteran players and the occasional server admin abuse. However, this current system can be grindy and therefore unpopular to some players since components are needed for base construction to guns and buns to explosives.
But hey, it's a PVP game, you have two choices:
1. Raid players for resources and items to build your ultimate raider base (Very satisfying)
2. Grind your way to making the ultimate base and then raid the other poor SOBs (still satisfying)
One thing that new players must know is that it is very easy to die after a few minutes running around in a server.
My advice is that you either play with a couple of friends (especially long time Rust players) or check how things work in a  less crowded modded server. Because you WILL rage quit at some point, unless your still calm enough to find the raider's base and take back what's yours.
Microtransactions? Mainly for skins for various items from clothing to guns. Personally, I find it useless and it's better to steal the items from other players.
The player community in Rust is very diverse. From minecraft kids to veteran players to griefers and whatever kinds of people there are. One thing you must remember though is DON'T TRUST ANYONE. The only genuine Friendly people are the ones with guns who decided to leave you alone with your rock, even then that's debatable.
Oh and be smart where and how you build your base. The fun part is in how to prevent others from getting your loot. Or  how to lure people in if that's your thing.

DayZ is sorta like crack. It feels great when things are going well, but eventually you die and everything sucks.
I have spent countless nights running from town to town, trying to find matching ammunition for the weapon I found after 2 hours of looting, only to be shot by someone who server hopped to find an M4. I've played since the Mosin was a decent rifle and the chance of finding a group of "Heroes" was higher. Since those days, DayZ has dramatically declined in its playability. Things continually become more buggy and more difficult to use. Ammunition, food, clothing, and anything else you might find is becoming more and more scarce. While some may argue that this is the right direction for the developer to follow, it changes the game so that the group of people willing to play this "Early Access" game is becoming exponentially smaller.
With that being said, I love DayZ. I love the combat and the idea of the game. My only grievance is that the developers will pull their heads out of their butts and focus on making improvements to the quality of the game, rather than merely adding features and increasing the difficulty of an almost unplayable game.

In short:
Recommended for: people who love to grief others, steal, murder, and ruin others' days.
NOT Recommended for: people who want to keep their hard work in survival worlds (like minecrafters) & enjoy a minimal stress game
In long:
This is a great core game and still to this day one of the best survival games around.  I've had plenty of moments where I've truely enjoyed this game but in the end it has one thing that will keep me from playing it again.
Simply it requires a TON of time devotion and in the end when servers wipe it will leave you feeling like "oh good i have to start all over AGAIN".  The fact is unless you start right after a server wipe you will be the naked dude running around a pond of big F***ing fishes; if you don't devote constanly large sums of time you will be destroyed.  You will die ALOT and I mean ALOT, it will give you paranoia like you've never known, and you will want to throw your keyboard when you log back in to that cool little base you spent hours on to find that its blown to hell and raided, or someones broken in and murdered you then reset the locks and stolen all you've worked hard for.
Its a game where its super fun TILL you lose everything 500 times then you get tired of restarting, getting killed when you have nothing, ganged up on by a mob, losing your base, raided, or hunted down repeatedly till you quit.
But I still feel the need to state that this is what the game was meant to offer.  It does what its designed for very very well, but i wanted to lay out the warning for anyone who was looking for a good survival with a few thrills and being able to look back at your accomplishments in enjoyment.  You won't get that here, you'll get some great moments, a small brain aneurysm, tons of anger, and a load of paranoia.
Still the game is phenominal for what its for so I recommend it if this is what you're looking for.  And highly discourage you from getting it if you want a relaxing survival game.  I will doubtfully play much more of this only as it isn't what I was looking for in the end.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is one of the very few succeful games of its genre.
Advantages -
+Nice graphics
+Smooth controls
+Large map
+Hours upon hours of gameplay
+The trucks have a heavy feel to them, unlike in a game such as Farming Simulator.
+An in game radio
+When it rains, it will effect the way your truck drives
+Good selection of trucks and upgrades
+A solid modding community
Disadvantages -
-Like many other simulators, driving slowly while obeying rules for an hour may become dull to an extent.
-No driver in your truck (sort of). While in first person mode, you cannot see the drivers hands. But, while in third person, you are able to see a driver.
In conclusion, this game is a fantastic simulator. I myself have put many hours into Euro Truck and I plan to add more to that number. If you are looking for a good driving simulator then this is definately one of the best choices on the market.

Bought the game when it was in EA, and now I'm definitely placing myself in the "I doubt this will ever get out of EA" camp.
That being said, I can't help but love this game.
(Or maybe I've invested too much of what little playing time I have into this game that I now don't want to admit that I'm dissapointed...)
Anyway, I still find DayZ enjoyable because:
1. The realism. As in, you can't dig metal ores and then craft an assault rifle. This also extends to other gameplay aspects, from the hunger/thirst mechanism, ambient temperature, ballistics, etc., etc. So, playing DayZ mostly feels logical (for lack of a better word... at least it does for me.)
2. The multiplayer. As in, playing with other people can be enjoyable but adventuring solo is viable as well. Which is a big bonus for people like me who can't play on a regular basis.
3. Tension. Approaching an empty-looking village in broad daylight and still having to be careful in case there's somebody with a shotgun also looking around for food; looking at rolling hills carresed by a light summer breeze and worrying about snipers hiding in the forest; etc., etc. These never really get old for me.
Sure, there are a ton of problems, from bugs to glitches and cheaters etc., but I somehow still enjoy loading up the game once in a while to see how far I can make it and what new experiences I can find.
