This game is awesome! A unique comic-book-style world with lots of colorful characters, crazy wildlife, sarcasm and satire, action skills, epic loot, crazy weapons, and plenty of opportunities to use them in over-the-top ways. I felt immersed in the imaginative (and fairly expansive) world and my character(s), and finding a good, rare, or legendary item continues to excite.
Overall, I definitely recommend it. Like any game, though, it's not without its flaws. I found the hard limits on backpack and bank size (even after all upgrades) to be much too strict, leaving me to have to spend lots of time managing my inventory - something that the game devs ironically said they were trying to avoid by imposing the limits in the first place. This was by far the biggest issue for me.
Also at times during the campaign I found myself stuck without ammo due to several spots with multiple bosses in a row and no chance to properly load up on ammo. Finally, sometimes if I had to backtrack a bit, bosses that I already took major effort to kill would sometimes respawn so that I had to kill them again. These issues are fairly minor in the scheme of things.
After I got tired of always running out of backpack space and the hassle of maintaining loot mules, I quit the game for a while. I recently discovered a method that kinda sorta lets me fit more loot, and I am back to enjoying the brilliance of the rest of the game. Maybe future Borderlands successors will address this issue.

Before I start, let me just say, I enjoy Rust, but I write reviews to help people decide whether they will invest their money in a game or not. I will list the pros and cons, with a nuetral approach (as nuetral as I can get). With that said, here is the review:
Rust is a great game with barely any bugs/glitches. The main "issue" is the playerbase. Most people who play Rust will only befriend you when you are fresh spawns, and 75% of the time, they will betray you later on. If you find yourself in a situation where you are a fresh spawn, and they other person had a gun, they will shoot you because they like wasting bullets for rocks and a torch. Also, 50% of the fresh spawns that you will encounter that won't betray you later on, are the ones that charge at you with a rock without saying anything.
Aside from SoS PvP, there is your base. If you don't want to get raided, you must spend the first 3 hours collecting supplies so you can get 1 layer of honeycombing so you don't get raided, and don't even think about using a standard key lock, because if you forget to make a spare and don't have 100 wood lying around, when you die you are trapped in your base with no key to unlock your door and escape your own home. On your first day of Rust, you will be excited if you made a base. If you did your research on base building, you might have a nice home to come back to the next day. If you did not do your research, chances are you left the game with your base made of twigs, which can get knocked down in 5 swings from a stone hatchet.
In conclusion, you won't have a problem with rust if you are patient enough to get supplies before interacting with other players, or you could take a chance at befriending a freshie, and maybe he won't betray you!

There's already been so much said about this game that I don't think there's much more I can add. However, what I found most endearing about it, besides the soundtrack and general quirkiness that everyone loves, is how it engages with the player ethically. Not only does it provide a creative narrative with fulfilling moral consequences, but it forces the player to come to terms with the morality of the medium itself, with the ethics of playing video games. For this reason, I think Undertale has the potential to provoke more potent responces than any other game out there, simply because it engages with the player directly, forcing them think through the process of making choices as an omnipotent being standing outside of the game's world, normally able to restart at any time without repercussions if they are ever unsatisfied or uncomfortable with their decisions. This alone makes
one of my favorite video game antagonists, because he antagonizes both the protagonist and the player, and seems to be prepared for any excuse we might make to justify our actions.
The two moments that hit me the hardest were
. On both of these occasions,
made me aware of these decisions and made me think about what they entailed and why I made them. The first may have just been an accident, but does that justify doing what I did without first trying other options? And does the fact that I could just reload the game make it any less troublesome? As for the second, I may have avoided killing all the characters I came to love by watching someone else go down the evil path, but does this make me any better? Of course, it's only a video game, so it's easy to distance oneself from the narrative and its characters for the sake of completionism or curiousity, but what does the fact that we are so easily able to distance ourselves say about us? Whatever it says, this game certainly provoked thoughtful questions about the ethics of gaming and I would definitely recommend it. Also, the music and characters are awesome! ;)

TL;DR - Just got Rust. Got manipulated and betrayed as a Slave by preteens. Raided by Koreans. Foundation wiped. Hosted by experience player. Proceeded to rekt entire server including preteens and Koreans with new group of friends that I've never met in real life.

I come from over 1k hours of CS:GO and I have to say there is a ton of variable gameplay in Rust then CS:GO. I'm pretty sure there are people that argue this but for me peeking corners and triggering game sense can only get so entertaining after a while.
I started out getting a lot of lag and almost impossible to win PVP's because of my fps but after roaming and letting my 16GB ram pre render most of the map, it became viable for me to become confident in defending myself.
That's when I started voice talking to people.
I ended up being a "helper" for a group that was gathering resources to build their new base in exchange for a small room in their old one. I get near the new base and I get shot and killed instantly by one of the group members. Ok, maybe he didn't know it was me.
I steam message, no response. I try to quietly head over again and use game voice to identify myself so I don't get shot again. They respond by telling me they changed the codes because they thought they were going to get code raided and that they'll come out to give the codes. That's when they shoot me wounded, and told me to "Take a hint. Don't come back here again"
#So you can imagine my crushed self esteem by getting betrayed by these preteens who I've spend a lot of grind time in gathering their resources. I'm talking like 40+ hours and 15k wood, stone, components, and guns. So what do I do?
I change the code lock to my room in the old base, gather enough resources fueled by hate and revenge to make satchel charges (had no idea how to find long pipes for rockets) for the old base front door to get access to cupboard. (This was a 2x3x3). The take over was complete, now to gather resources to raid their new base. It was unrealistic seeing how I was now solo and their base was hexagonal, metal, and huge but I had all month and was a noob fueled by passionate revenge.
The next day I find another noob (we'll call him Player 1) which I cautiously trusted him to be my helper (not slave) by giving him the room I had in the old base while building 2 more bases next to it.
This is when things pick up for me exponentially for next 2 weeks.
Player 1 proceeds to farm and be friendly with anyone who passes by our area which resulted in bringing 2 more people who play from Sweden into our bases. So now we have a total of 4 people in our group.

I don't know how Gary and Facepunch did it, but they've created a game where I experienced politics, social economics, and structural engineering all in one game. The fact that I was able to build random relationships through a video game is beyond me. I've never played a game for 200 hours in one month for $20. So a huge thanks to them and this wonderful ALPHA (not even finished) NON DLC ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥T game.
For anyone who is having trouble playing solo or finding a fun group, choose people wisely. Here are some key points to look for in a potential teammate:
1. Humility: they're willing to sacrifice time for objectives they don't necessarily agree with but understand it's for the betterment of the group.
2. Contribution: Understanding that losing something creates responsibility in gaining that value back on their own. We all know that one person who only pvps, loses, then takes from the group chest just to lost it all again.
3. Respect and Optimism: Give the only AK to the guy who has best shot/most hours and not to the 11 year old who has his mom buy skins. Don't grill the teammate who accidentally killed you while trying to get air drop but let him know you had med pens and that you hear other people nearby that might kill him.
Usually you have better chance of finding these qualities in 18+ although there are exceptions. There are also smart, objective players who are great at pvp because they come from CSGO that have less than 100 hours. This is why I find LFG kind of challenging. But what's interesting is that you have an equal chance of finding a group in game using voice chat.
I may be just stating the obvious here but I learned a ton from this game than I have from others. I never felt the kind of satisfaction I had when the preteen group knew of my group and knowledge the fact that their slave ended up being a master of the server (muahahhaha). The fact that I was able to raid the Koreans who raided my bases.
I hope this game continues to develop into Beta even though I feel like it's ready for retail. You have my full support Gary and I hope the community continues to enjoy this game that dares to reach a new kind of open world flexible game play.

I became curious about 'Undertale' after numerous coverage of this cultural phenomenon. After receiving it as a gift, I decided to give it a go. I definitely see merit in the game, with its modern take on turn-based RPG and a twist to its levelling system. The graphics are a miss for me at times given some inconsistency in the style department. The combat is based on "bullet hell" shooting games, thus requiring some sharp reflexes on the player's part. Unfortunately, I am neither partial to bullet hell games nor possess sharp enough reflexes, so I found combat in 'Undertale' a nuisance. By mid-game, I got so frustrated that I don't find the game interesting or enjoyable anymore. However, for those who do well with bullet hell games or can tolerate it more than I, I will recommend 'Undertale' for its interesting take on turn-based RPG and its tropes; else, I would say stay away.

This game is awesome! A unique comic-book-style world with lots of colorful characters, crazy wildlife, sarcasm and satire, action skills, epic loot, crazy weapons, and plenty of opportunities to use them in over-the-top ways. I felt immersed in the imaginative (and fairly expansive) world and my character(s), and finding a good, rare, or legendary item continues to excite.
Overall, I definitely recommend it. Like any game, though, it's not without its flaws. I found the hard limits on backpack and bank size (even after all upgrades) to be much too strict, leaving me to have to spend lots of time managing my inventory - something that the game devs ironically said they were trying to avoid by imposing the limits in the first place. This was by far the biggest issue for me.
Also at times during the campaign I found myself stuck without ammo due to several spots with multiple bosses in a row and no chance to properly load up on ammo. Finally, sometimes if I had to backtrack a bit, bosses that I already took major effort to kill would sometimes respawn so that I had to kill them again. These issues are fairly minor in the scheme of things.
After I got tired of always running out of backpack space and the hassle of maintaining loot mules, I quit the game for a while. I recently discovered a method that kinda sorta lets me fit more loot, and I am back to enjoying the brilliance of the rest of the game. Maybe future Borderlands successors will address this issue.

TL;DR - Just got Rust. Got manipulated and betrayed as a Slave by preteens. Raided by Koreans. Foundation wiped. Hosted by experience player. Proceeded to rekt entire server including preteens and Koreans with new group of friends that I've never met in real life.

I come from over 1k hours of CS:GO and I have to say there is a ton of variable gameplay in Rust then CS:GO. I'm pretty sure there are people that argue this but for me peeking corners and triggering game sense can only get so entertaining after a while.
I started out getting a lot of lag and almost impossible to win PVP's because of my fps but after roaming and letting my 16GB ram pre render most of the map, it became viable for me to become confident in defending myself.
That's when I started voice talking to people.
I ended up being a "helper" for a group that was gathering resources to build their new base in exchange for a small room in their old one. This was going on for a week until I found a dead hazmat body that was trying to climb dome and had a bunch of great loot on him including an LR and loot from the top of the dome. The day after, the old base is completely empty including my small room so I thought my group was done transitioning to their new base which had a room for me as well.
I get near the new base and I get shot and killed instantly by one of the group members. Ok, maybe he didn't know it was me.
I steam message, no response. I try to quietly head over again and use game voice to identify myself so I don't get shot again. They respond by telling me they changed the codes because they thought they were going to get code raided and that they'll come out to give the codes. That's when they shoot me wounded, and told me to "Take a hint. Don't come back here again"
#So you can imagine my crushed self esteem by getting betrayed by these preteens who I've spend a lot of grind time in gathering their resources. I'm talking like 40+ hours and 15k wood, stone, components, and guns. So what do I do?
I change the code lock to my room in the old base, gather enough resources fueled by hate and revenge to make satchel charges (had no idea how to find long pipes for rockets) for the old base front door to get access to cupboard. (This was a 2x3x3). The take over was complete, now to gather resources to raid their new base. It was unrealistic seeing how I was now solo and their base was hexagonal, metal, and huge but I had all month and was a noob fueled by passionate revenge.
The next day I find another noob (we'll call him Player 1) which I cautiously trusted him to be my helper (not slave) by giving him the room I had in the old base while building 2 more bases next to it.
This is when things pick up for me exponentially for next 2 weeks.
Player 1 proceeds to farm and be friendly with anyone who passes by our area which resulted in bringing 2 more people who play from Sweden into our bases. So now we have a total of 4 people in our group.
During the next three weeks we've
1. demolished doors to build a cave base.

4. Brought in 2 more group members (1 is actually from lfg!)

I don't know how Gary and Facepunch did it, but they've created a game where I experienced politics, social economics, and structural engineering all in one game. The fact that I was able to build random relationships through a video game is beyond me. I've never played a game for 200 hours in one month for $20. So a huge thanks to them and this wonderful ALPHA (not even finished) NON DLC ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥T game.
For anyone who is having trouble playing solo or finding a fun group, choose people wisely. Here are some key points to look for in a potential teammate:
1. Humility: they're willing to sacrifice time for objectives they don't necessarily agree with but understand it's for the betterment of the group.
2. Contribution: Understanding that losing something creates responsibility in gaining that value back on their own. We all know that one person who only pvps, loses, then takes from the group chest just to lost it all again.
3. Respect and Optimism: Give the only AK to the guy who has best shot/most hours and not to the 11 year old who has his mom buy skins. Don't grill the teammate who accidentally killed you while trying to get air drop but let him know you had med pens and that you hear other people nearby that might kill him.
Usually you have better chance of finding these qualities in 18+ although there are exceptions. There are also smart, objective players who are great at pvp because they come from CSGO that have less than 100 hours. This is why I find LFG kind of challenging. But what's interesting is that you have an equal chance of finding a group in game using voice chat.
I may be just stating the obvious here but I learned a ton from this game than I have from others. I never felt the kind of satisfaction I had when the preteen group knew of my group and knowledge the fact that their slave ended up being a master of the server (muahahhaha). The fact that I was able to raid the Koreans who raided my bases.
I hope this game continues to develop into Beta even though I feel like it's ready for retail. You have my full support Gary and I hope the community continues to enjoy this game that dares to reach a new kind of open world flexible game play.

I've been playing Rust since it was first released back in December of 2013, and I must say that this game has changed quite a bit from then until now. Even so, the game has been an alpha release for about 3+ years now.
Pros:
-Fun and engaging combat, but is still enough of a challenge to not make it all that easy to master
-Amazing visuals that have been greatly overhauled from previous Rust Legacy
-A cancerous community that makes any person want to kill themselves (everyone needs a little bit of cancer in their life)
-Day/night cycle + weather (i.e Rain... yeah that's basically it)
-Different biomes (i.e: Plains, forest, desert, beach, etc...)
-Crafting system that has been reworked several times (and will possibly be reworked again since the devs love doing that)
-Tons of weapons to craft, ranging from stone-age weaponry to military grade weaponry
-Animals to hunt and kill (or be killed by)
-Simplistic base building mechanic that allows you to build and upgrade a home to live in
-Several different monuments to explore and loot (i.e: airport, water treatment plant, power plant, etc...)
-Great in game audio FX and soundtrack
-Weekly updates/monthly server wipes
-Official servers, community servers, and modded servers
-DX9, DX11, and DX12 support (DX12 experimental at the moment)
-Steam Workshop support (players can make different weapon/clothing skins and put them on the workshop to be voted on)
Cons:
-Poorly optimized, even for high end PC's
-Poor animal AI/animals faze through objects (i.e: rocks, trees, houses)
-A lot of bugs other than what I had just mentioned
-Has a memory leak that often leads to lag or using too much computer resources
-The community for this game is beyond cancerous in fact. About 97% of the player you meet in this game will kill on sight, even if you're a naked
Final Verdict (ATM)
6.5/10
Despite my cons, I'd still recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun game to play with friends or by themselves. Though the community is terrible, about 3-4% of the players in this game are actually pretty cool and you might even make some new friends while playing.
The game is still in alpha, so it has quite a ways to go before everything is finalized and is in a more stable state.

Alright, after all the time I've sunk into this game, I've decided to give my opinions on it.  Let's start off with a simple description.
So, this game is a First Person Shooter that was made around the mechanic of playing in a premade group of people, and is relatively iterave of it's predacessor.  The mechanics that are meant to set this apart from other shooters are the focus on cooperative play, it's class/skill system (mostly based around a single activatable skill specific to each class) and a random weapon generator.  All the gameplay is through a single campaign in an open world situation with many optional quests and small areas to discover scattered around the different regions.
So let's talk about the things that make this game stand out.  First off let's talk about the available weapons.  The game uses a system of random weapon generation that assigns statistics to a pre rendered gun model, with many variants on each different model, I'd say enough to be sufficient to give a real random weapon feel to the game.  There are some pre made weapons and equipment, but they are all considered "very rare" and are generally related to a character or situation.  This can actually add replayability, because one playthrough can focus on the use of a weapon with a very different playstyle of the weapon you would get at that same point in another playthrough.  Aside from the usual pitfalls that come in with all random situations in games, being that you can get screwed by luck and no forms of skill.
The gunplay is a step up from the first one, each weapon handles well, and the random generation adds some interesting weapon types, one of the more interesting things I've personally found run from swarm rockets to long range shotguns to burst snipers to grenades that fire bullets in a circling pattern instead of the standard explosion.  The elemental types in the game add a good overlay to each weapon and make for interesting synergy.
Now let's move on to the class system, there are 4 basic classes and two added via DLC (we'll talk about the DLC later) each one is actually fairly varied and plays around his action skill.  While it's possible to play characters out of their class, the bonuses and their skill trees make it in such a way that it is impossible to optimize for anything other than what your class is built for i.e. the soldier builds around using his turrets while he lays down fire using mainly Assault weapons, the Siren plays around shorter range weapons and her ability to lock an enemy and deal extra damage to that same enemy, and the Assassin is based around his stealth skill and keeping safe while he either uses melee damage and/or Sniper damage, building on critical hits.
Each class can build in different ways allowing for wiggle room in each class, the fact that you can change your specs easily can help a lot if you're playing a solo game and some fights require a different style than what you're currently playing.  On the subject, one catch of the action skill system is that the Action skill system is based around one action per character, but the thing that people need to realize is that this game is still a shooter first, and since the upgrades are level based, and the scaling of the enemies is fairly rapid, having multiple underpowered abilities would be contrary to the rest of the style of the game.
The most difficult thing to review about this game is the humor, it's honestly kind of purile, but there is still the occasional clever joke, and especially when you're with a group of friends, even the simple stuff can warrant a chuckle or two, but humor's relative, so I wont judge people for finding certain things funny and other things not.
One of the big downs of the game is it's focus on cooperative play, it's difficult to find a balance as the game does not add enemies based on number of players but simply increases the health of the pre existing ones, making enemies unessessarily frustrating with a full party.  On the flip side a single player experience is frustrating because many enemies are designed to be fought while one pulls aggro and the other attacks from behind.  The campaign almost demands teamwork which makes classes such as the gunzerker and the siren even more difficult to play solo, because they cannot use anything to distract enemies.
Finally, the my biggest personal problem is the (and this is putting it lightly) abhorrant DLC whoring that gearbox is famous for.  Not even the GOTY edition has all the dlc, and they're actually releasing even more DLC as i write this review, even though they've announced the next in the series.  Of course, the beauty is the base game is still a full game, and some of the major DLC is considered top notch and comes with glowing recommendations of those who've played it.  And the best thing is that because it's still a satisfying experience with no DLC, so you simply dont need to buy it if you feel it's not worth the money.

There's not a lot about Undertale that hasn't already been said by so many others at this point. The quality of the writing, the characters, combining bullet hells with puzzles and timing-based strikes all in the same combat... the game making a STORY MECHANIC out of you reloading an earlier save if you made a mistake or died...  The only downside to the entire game is it's far too short and leaves you wanting more no matter how many times you "reset" and play from the beginning.
As someone who's been gaming since I was four, never having an issue playing the good/evil sides of every game, the highest complement I can give Undertale is that I had to FORCE myself to kill these characters in order to take on the infamous final boss of the genocide route.  And even then I couldn't complete the genocide run, I had to reset to the start as soon as I beat him because I flat-out couldn't make myself continue that save.
I'm saying goodbye to Undertale now, because to go back and start again after this last True Pacifist run, would be a disservice to the characters I've quickly come to love and enjoy.  If the maker of Undertale ever creates another game, they have my support and backing 100%.

The puzzles are boring. This fact is lampshaded, however, and that makes it cool, right?
The graphics are bland and uninspired. Just stop it with the crappy pixel art, game developers. Games of the 8-bit and 16-bit era were dealing with a lack of technology, not a lack of talent. Then again, retro-inspired art, no matter how bad, is cool, right?
Being so vague one cannot get invested in any real way without reading loads of signs on the walls that all say essentially the same thing is cool, right?
I don't care if it "gets better" later on, my first impressions were not favourable at all. I have no desire to go back to this game. I gave it the time of day, and I was very disappointed. I even went in with an open mind, ignoring the hype surrounding it and trying to judge the game by it's own merits. I found almost nothing redeeming about this game, and I don't care if the hipsters who treat this game like a beached whale that will die if not constantly moistened by their collective tongues descend upon me in a rabid frenzy because I didn't like their favourite piece of flavour-of-the-month entertainment.
In short, I don't like Undertale, which is a shame because I was looking for a new RPG to get invested in that isn't Final Piggin' Fantasy (I don't like Final Fantasy either, go figure). If only it had a better start than it does, and gave me a reason to be invested, then I would have been more forgiving. As it stands, however, this is one game that I will be putting back in the ground and burying again.

Alright, after all the time I've sunk into this game, I've decided to give my opinions on it.  Let's start off with a simple description.
So, this game is a First Person Shooter that was made around the mechanic of playing in a premade group of people, and is relatively iterave of it's predacessor.  The mechanics that are meant to set this apart from other shooters are the focus on cooperative play, it's class/skill system (mostly based around a single activatable skill specific to each class) and a random weapon generator.  All the gameplay is through a single campaign in an open world situation with many optional quests and small areas to discover scattered around the different regions.
So let's talk about the things that make this game stand out.  First off let's talk about the available weapons.  The game uses a system of random weapon generation that assigns statistics to a pre rendered gun model, with many variants on each different model, I'd say enough to be sufficient to give a real random weapon feel to the game.  There are some pre made weapons and equipment, but they are all considered "very rare" and are generally related to a character or situation.  This can actually add replayability, because one playthrough can focus on the use of a weapon with a very different playstyle of the weapon you would get at that same point in another playthrough.  Aside from the usual pitfalls that come in with all random situations in games, being that you can get screwed by luck and no forms of skill.
The gunplay is a step up from the first one, each weapon handles well, and the random generation adds some interesting weapon types, one of the more interesting things I've personally found run from swarm rockets to long range shotguns to burst snipers to grenades that fire bullets in a circling pattern instead of the standard explosion.  The elemental types in the game add a good overlay to each weapon and make for interesting synergy.
Now let's move on to the class system, there are 4 basic classes and two added via DLC (we'll talk about the DLC later) each one is actually fairly varied and plays around his action skill.  While it's possible to play characters out of their class, the bonuses and their skill trees make it in such a way that it is impossible to optimize for anything other than what your class is built for i.e. the soldier builds around using his turrets while he lays down fire using mainly Assault weapons, the Siren plays around shorter range weapons and her ability to lock an enemy and deal extra damage to that same enemy, and the Assassin is based around his stealth skill and keeping safe while he either uses melee damage and/or Sniper damage, building on critical hits.
Each class can build in different ways allowing for wiggle room in each class, the fact that you can change your specs easily can help a lot if you're playing a solo game and some fights require a different style than what you're currently playing.  On the subject, one catch of the action skill system is that the Action skill system is based around one action per character, but the thing that people need to realize is that this game is still a shooter first, and since the upgrades are level based, and the scaling of the enemies is fairly rapid, having multiple underpowered abilities would be contrary to the rest of the style of the game.
The most difficult thing to review about this game is the humor, it's honestly kind of purile, but there is still the occasional clever joke, and especially when you're with a group of friends, even the simple stuff can warrant a chuckle or two, but humor's relative, so I wont judge people for finding certain things funny and other things not.
One of the big downs of the game is it's focus on cooperative play, it's difficult to find a balance as the game does not add enemies based on number of players but simply increases the health of the pre existing ones, making enemies unessessarily frustrating with a full party.  On the flip side a single player experience is frustrating because many enemies are designed to be fought while one pulls aggro and the other attacks from behind.  The campaign almost demands teamwork which makes classes such as the gunzerker and the siren even more difficult to play solo, because they cannot use anything to distract enemies.
Finally, the my biggest personal problem is the (and this is putting it lightly) abhorrant DLC whoring that gearbox is famous for.  Not even the GOTY edition has all the dlc, and they're actually releasing even more DLC as i write this review, even though they've announced the next in the series.  Of course, the beauty is the base game is still a full game, and some of the major DLC is considered top notch and comes with glowing recommendations of those who've played it.  And the best thing is that because it's still a satisfying experience with no DLC, so you simply dont need to buy it if you feel it's not worth the money.

I've been playing Rust since it was first released back in December of 2013, and I must say that this game has changed quite a bit from then until now. Even so, the game has been an alpha release for about 3+ years now.
Pros:
-Fun and engaging combat, but is still enough of a challenge to not make it all that easy to master
-Amazing visuals that have been greatly overhauled from previous Rust Legacy
-A cancerous community that makes any person want to kill themselves (everyone needs a little bit of cancer in their life)
-Day/night cycle + weather (i.e Rain... yeah that's basically it)
-Different biomes (i.e: Plains, forest, desert, beach, etc...)
-Crafting system that has been reworked several times (and will possibly be reworked again since the devs love doing that)
-Tons of weapons to craft, ranging from stone-age weaponry to military grade weaponry
-Animals to hunt and kill (or be killed by)
-Simplistic base building mechanic that allows you to build and upgrade a home to live in
-Several different monuments to explore and loot (i.e: airport, water treatment plant, power plant, etc...)
-Great in game audio FX and soundtrack
-Weekly updates/monthly server wipes
-Official servers, community servers, and modded servers
-DX9, DX11, and DX12 support (DX12 experimental at the moment)
-Steam Workshop support (players can make different weapon/clothing skins and put them on the workshop to be voted on)
Cons:
-Poorly optimized, even for high end PC's
-Poor animal AI/animals faze through objects (i.e: rocks, trees, houses)
-A lot of bugs other than what I had just mentioned
-Has a memory leak that often leads to lag or using too much computer resources
-The community for this game is beyond cancerous in fact. About 97% of the player you meet in this game will kill on sight, even if you're a naked
Final Verdict (ATM)
6.5/10
Despite my cons, I'd still recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun game to play with friends or by themselves. Though the community is terrible, about 3-4% of the players in this game are actually pretty cool and you might even make some new friends while playing.
The game is still in alpha, so it has quite a ways to go before everything is finalized and is in a more stable state.
(Review is subject to change throughout the lifespan of alpha/beta)

I started playing DayZ a long time ago, back through the mod. The early (ish) days of DayZ Mod were amazing, you could meet players that would help you and you could exchange gear and supplies. As the DayZ Mod grew older many saw "Vanilla" DayZ as boring as it gets old after a while. Then Mods like Overwatch and Epoch were born, a huge boom happened where everyone came back to DayZ Mod as there where many more things that you could do now. However with the new mods players attitude changed, you no longer have to search for guns for large amounts of time, For example Overwatch, There were ACRs EVERYWHERE. You could not search one building without finding an ACR. So people thought "Well I dont need to try anymore because everything is easy to find, guns, supplies, meds. I will just kill people to make things interesting." Therefor everyone immedeatly thinks about killing the first player they find because everything is easy to find.
DayZ Standalone is announced, everyone gets hyped. It looks like it's going to be great, I couldnt wait.
DayZ Standalone is released, It is a little difficult to run and there are alot of bugs. This was expected.
A year passes, Not much has changed.
Current Day, DayZ standalone is starting to get it's act together bringing out the new enfusion engine which greatly improbed FPS in some areas, the game is active with around 3000-6000 players at one time. The game is enjoyable to diehard fans however it is lacking to draw in new players as DayZ Standalone had a very shaky start.
Now, I do recommend this game because it has so much potential. If modding comes out for DayZ Standalone it would be f***ing amazing, however it may still be some time before the game is really on it's feet. This game for me has been really good, however I have been with the game from the very start, therefor my opinion is based of knowing what DayZ used to be. I know that the creater of Namalsk is working on the map for the DayZ Standalone, Namalsk was one of my most favourite maps for the mod as I live in Scotland and I like the cold, also frames were really good.
If this game dies, Im not sure what I would do. It has been such a large influence on me it is unreal...
I hope that you enjoyed reading about my views and expereance with DayZ and Bohemia Interactive, Thanks for reading and I hope that you found my review helpful.

After years in development this game is in a Early Release stage and I don't mean just nominally. Although my overpowered video card can now run this game with a decent FPS (thank dog for small mercies) it is full of glitches.
Consider this scenario:
You spent a day gearing up by running to the farthest point on the map, because that's how loot works in this game nowadays. You ran back to where the action is and finally you are in a firefight. Your heart is pounding: finally you'll be able to kill somebody and then sing Neverending Story song on top of their corpses. You shoot off a few bullets then you get in a safe place and try to reload. You have no space in your inventory so your character can't take out the empty mag and then place in there. You put the empty mag on the floor around you.
You put in the second, full mag into your gun. It disappears. It now shows up as lying around you with the empty mag. The enemies are closing in on you. You try to put the full mag back into your inventory. It disappears completely. You can not now see it at all through you inventory, though it looks like it's still lying in front of you on the floor near the empty mag. You try to pick it up by using F button. Instead you receive bullets out of the mag with it remaining on the ground. The enemies are now within shouting distance and are promising to do unspeakable things to your corpse.
You put the empty mag back in your inventory to refill it with bullets. Perhaps the full mag is just glitched. The empty mag refuses to go into the empty slot in your inventory. You now have two mags lying in front of you on the ground. You now have an empty looking gun. You panic and fire to test if the mag is invisible. It works, but you just fired your last bullet that was in the gun barrel. The enemies now know where you are.
The enemy runs in with a pistol. He shoots you long time. You see darkness. You hear Neverending Story being sung very badly.
Despite bugs, I like this game. I am really fan of dayz. Just dont stop and keep  updating it.

Even with all the issues this game has, I gotta say its a great game. i know its not finished and its going to be a while till they release the final product, but I do recommend this game. Once its complete then this game will be the best out there.

After some recent playtime, I’ve decided to write another review.
TLDR;
This game had so much potential, but too bad that potential has been squandered because of lazy money hungry developers (Dean Hall). It’s a mess, and the only reason why 5,000 people play it sometimes is because we all got tricked into buying a lemon.
My positive thoughts:
In its current state, the game is very atmospheric and beautiful. I’ve found myself playing this game a little bit here and there over the past couple of days. I must say, this game has the setting to be an amazing survival experience. Personally, hiking your way around the map looking for better loot and food is quite fun (especially if you craft the bow and use it to take out zombies and such).
My negative thoughts:
Well, since 2013 the game has improved, I will say that much. It doesn’t change the fact however, that the game is a complete and utter disaster still. The U.I. feels stupid, and clunky. It amazes me that PUBG has a better inventory management system than this game does and PUBG has been out for what, four months now? The game is just buggy in general still, yesterday I was hiding in a small shack trying to apply bandages when my character just teleported outside of it. No part of this game is streamlined, nothing.
Ending thoughts:
There’s no way in hell this game is worth 34.99, I might be able to recommend it if it were 20.00 bucks.
for that state the game is in, it isnt worth the current price. I cant wait to see where it goes but right now it isnt going very far.

Still waiting for the BETA, after all this time. WHEN WILL THIS GAME EVER RELEASE!? I feel like a total sucker for buying this game. I knew it was early access, but the original DayZ mod and it's newer iterations have far surpassed the standalone from what I've seen. By the time it comes out, we might all be zombies for real.
It's time to stop.

The graphics are a matter of taste; either you love retro or you hate it. Personally, I don't mind. When it comes to game length, it's about 7 hours, which is quite long for an indie game.
Bottom line, play this game. It's worth the money.

Lets start off by being honest, I REALLY want to give this game a good rating because when I have been able to play it, it's fantastic, probably one of the best survival games on the market today. But alas, the game is broken, in a way in which it is literally unplayable and is currently just a waste of space on my hard drive.
Memory leaks my friends, memory leaks out the wazoo, now before you say "ho ho ho your PC is probably s**t" it isn't and my specs are well over the recommended, but out of 16gb RAM, this game uses, well, tries to use all of it and causes my PC to literally give up on life. I have tried every fix under the sun that normally resolves pc related memory leaks I even went and bought larger ram, it still used all of it. It's not drivers or graphic settings or resolutions or private servers or registry issues that's causing the problem, the game is broken and it has been this way for the last 2 years. Do we see a fix from the devs? No we don't just more cosmetic stuff being thrown in, if it was just a handful of us players I'd understand, but there is a large population of us on the forums screaming about this issue and yet nothing is done, even the people who can play the game smoothly experience these leaks.
So right now can I recommend this game? Absolutely not, maybe one day in the future when the issue is fixed, but now it's potentially just a waste of your money.

Borderlands 2: Probably the best game I've ever gotten from a friend. (Thanks [A.C.E] ACEALEC︻デ═一 for getting me this game) It combines the good parts of shooters, with an impressive, dark story, and also some amazing characters. I usually keep this stuff towards the end, but I'm gonna be honest with you: This is probably one of the finest games of last generation. To the review!
The visuals were annoying at first and still are, but I began to grow into the comic styled visuals and then thought it looked great. However, some enemies had poor textures along with lots of the environment. The characters look great, the buildings look awesome, but the environments, many of the enemies (Not all, though. Some look great) have odd textures or look poorly done. When it comes to comic graphics, it's either a hit or a miss. I say Borderlands 2 was successful, but I can't say that it was out of the park good. Overall though, I like it.
The gameplay, which is tied for first as Borderlands 2's (BL2 for short) strong point, takes the "good parts of shooters" and along with countless loot, class combinations, several RPG elements, etc, and makes some strong gameplay. The gunplay is heated along with the special ability each class has, the fights are even more intense. All of the characters are pretty balanced, heck, even Axton (The Commando) is pretty balanced for a guy who has a sentry who does the work. However, since I used to play quite a bit of Salvador (The Gunzerker) seems a bit weak, His ability is good, but it isn't as useful as the Siren's, the Assassin's, and the others. He could use a small buff. Ironic, too. He actually did lots of steroids. Must be karma or something. Don't do drugs, kids! Oh wait, I'm getting off topic. Excuse me for that. Anyway, the vehicles in BL2 are good enough, but maybe a few more different vehicles would've been better. Either way, going around and running over Psychos is good fun. The world is large and there's lots to explore, too. I love this game's gameplay.
The story was done right and makes most shooters look bad. It isn't top notch like Spec Ops: The Line (Which was also released in 2012) or Mass Effect (When a game has a better story than Mass Effect, you KNOW it's good) but it's able to satisfy me. The writing has a dark tone to it, but at the same time, there is some funny moments that try to cheer you up in the hostile world of Pandora. I'm not going to spoil it, but if you've played Borderlands 1, there will be a moment towards the end of the game where your heart will just break. There are some strong plot twists that greatly affect the story greatly and make the huge 90 degree turns worth it. The humor is a bit rushed, but I still laughed out loud many times. Claptrap and Handsome Jack are the two guys who basically lead the whole story. Claptrap is always funny, and even Handsome Jack is humorous a lot. However, Handsome Jack starts to show that this "loving to hate him" thing is really starting to kick in at a certain point in the game. He goes flat-out revenge and really makes him a strong character and also one of the best villains I've ever encountered in a video game, rivaling GLaDOS and others. The four main characters (and DLC characters, making it six) are all good, but again, Salvador is a bit one dimensional. Either way, don't underrestimate this game's story.
The audio is great, and the voice actors did an outstanding job. Handsome Jack is definitely the strong point and is able to prove that he is a terrifying (yet awesome) villain. The music is great and fits in with the atmosphere perfectly. Not much to say other than Handsome Jack played his role well.
The replayability, if it isn't obvious enough, is tied with the gameplay for the #1 strong point of the game. I'll try not to make this part too long, so yeah. Here we go: There are TONS of DLCs to buy, you can try to beat the game with another class, try another playstyle, help a few friends, get some new customizable skins, get the legendary weapons, find all the easter eggs, and lots, lots, lots, lots more. Should I say anything else to back up the fact this game has some pretty strong replayability? No? Good.
In the end, Borderlands 2 proves that it is one of the best shooters of last generation and is one of my personal favorite shooters now. It does something few shooters actually do, which is have a strong story. The great gameplay, amazing replayability, detailed characters, and funny writing all make this game a true masterpiece any shooter fan should have in their library.
So, newbie Vault Hunters. Are you ready to go shoot, loot, and loot some more?

Let me lay it down for you guys, Borderlands 2 is one of my new favorite games in my library.
Borderlands 2 is a hybrid FPS RPG 4 player Co-Op game. Now, when I say RPG, I don't mean something like Final Fantasy, Skyrim, or Dragon Age. Those games need you to be fully invested in the RPG elements of the game, and while I do like that sometimes, other times it gets boring for me. Borderlands 2's system feels very unobtrusive and can produce some good results even if you are randomly picking things in the skill tree. But if you do put some thought into your character's skills and how you play the game, you could be rewarded with a character that is perfect just for you. A good thing to mention is that there is only 4 (now 6 with DLC) classes to choose. While that doesn't seem like many to some people, each charcter is unique in skillset and apperance.
I must say, even though it didn't feel like then, the first 1 to 2 hours are slow. You don't even unlock skills untill lvl 5. That goes away once you hit the "hub" city of Sanctuary. This is where the story picks up and the one of my favorite parts of the game shines, the side quests. These missions never take themselves too seriously and sometimes are quite inventive, more than the standard fetch quests other games make you do. And everyonce in a while you start a quest that turns into a large chain of quests, building this little mini story (A good example of this is Ellie's Clan War quest). The main story is okay, much better than the orignial's, but it isn't close to the amount of depth some other shooters have. However the writing is great and is very funny. All of the NPCs have their own personality and some you can really begin to love after a while. Except Claptrap. I can love him in short bursts.
For the FPS element, it comes down to the guns. Remember when I said the RPG system was unobtrusive? I kinda lied, as I have spent lots of time just sitting and comparing the stats of guns, shields, class mods, relics, and grenades to each other. Guns can be pistols, shotguns, assault rifles, snipers, SMGs, and rocket launchers. All equipment has a manufacturer which decides for guns what it's strenght has. So Jacobs guns are usually high damage, low capcity, semi-auto guns, but the fire as fast as you can pull the trigger. Hyperion guns actually get more accurate the more shots the fire. And there are more brands with more effects. Then there is elemental types that do more damage to certain types of enemies, like fire doing more damge to biological enemies, corriosive doing more to armored enemies, ect. So when ever you pick up a gun you have a lot of things to consider.
Speaking of guns and loot there is a serious issue when it come to Co-Op. When an enemy drops a gun, it only drops one. Not a problem in single player. But with 4 people that causes issues, especially on bosses who drop really valuable loot. For me that is my only serious issue with the game, and I play by myself mostly anyway.
I've had lot's of fun playing this game, and if you don't own it, I suggest you do. I also suggest you get the Game of the Year edition which is a great value. And remember in the words of Markus the gunsalesman, "No Refunds!"

Superior to its predecessor in many ways, notably the writing and story.
Verdict: What Gearbox did here in roughly 2 years is impressive, and it's a proper sequel with some great writing, but its not anything "revolutionary" over the original's concept and gameplay. Even if you hadn't played the first title, I'd recommend this one. The ending hints that BL3 will be on a bigger scope than previous titles, I'm interested to see what they do.
+ The 2nd 1/2 of the main campaign has some great moments and the finale feels epic. Some parts of the DLCs are great too.
+ Character build and customization is pretty good.
+Tons to do, although not quite enough variation to stay interesting.
+ Playing with friends or with people online can be pretty fun.
-The level system still has problems. When you're in the sweet spot though, its fluid.
- Ninja class is arguably underpowered, especially if you go solo. The other 3 starters are great and easy enough to learn.
- Traveling can still be a big pain in the butt. And the areas/enemies become a bit repetitive. This is saved by the writing though.
NOTE: Once you finish the content once and just want to try other classes without grinding, Google: "Borderlands 2 Gibbed"

Bottom line, play this game. It's worth the money.

I'm a simple woodcutter in real life so I was looking for a game where I can fulfill myself.
After 250+ hours of woodcutting I am still blasted.
The environment is beautiful, not much detailed but isn't so bad either.
Models of the wood are well made. There aren't too many different ones so after some time it is too repetitive.
The mechanism of woodcutting is simple yet rewarding and spectacular at same time.
There are multiple things you can use to reach your goal. The most base tool is a giant chunk'o rock. Big, sturdy, slow but it gets the job done.
If you want an upgrade, you can duck tape some rock shards with a stick and you get a basic axe. This is a fine weapon of tree destruction.
Lastly, if you don't want to look like a caveman, you can make your own, real hatchet. Badass.
The technique to get logs is easy. You go to a tree and swing your flobby. You swing it and ding it for a few seconds and then poof, tree is gone.
BEWARE FELLOW WOODCUTTERS
I experienced a large number of strange events while was only trying to do my job.
I was kidnapped numerous times or got killed in action.
One time a guy named PssyDstroyer aproached me in a frindly manner. I ended up being locked into his basement and he fed me nothing else raw human meat.
BEST WOODCUTTING GAME 10/10

Borderlands 2 is a Cell-shaded FPS with RPG elements. As you kill enemies or complete challenges you gain exp towards levelling up and gaining skills or "Bad♥♥♥♥♥Points" that add stats to ALL characters on your gamer-profile. The game has humour which works on many levels - Cult/Pop references, Story based humour, even some potty-humour but never over the top or too offensive.
The actual game play is stanrd FPS "see it? Shoot it!" style with random loot drops of new weapons/character customisation options. With up to 6 playable charcters (depending on your version 4 in basic, 6 in Game Of The Year Edition or with all DLC) with seprerate skills to aid combat or totally change play styles there is plenty of replay value. Plus LOADS of character customisation options - new heads and skins both unlockable in game or purchasable for cash (cheaply 79p per head).
Online play is mainly Co-Op with PvP duels and trading as an option. Co-op boosts loot, experience and enemy difficulty depending on how many players are playing (up to 4 per host). The other online option are the SHIFT KEY CODES which unlock new heads/guns/or usually grant players KEYS used to gain special rare items. These codes are findable online via various websites.
The game even has loads of graphic options so low-end PC's can run it too.
All in all I'd have to give this game a 9 out of 10. Only losing 1 pointasI like to create my own character from scratch but appreciate how much they have fleshed the various characters ith backgrounds and personality

So, after ~206 hours of playing this game, I have alot to say. This game is wonderful. Ignore those who have -100 hours and speak of so-called "Graphical limitations." While the game's graphics are sub-par, don't be too quick to judge, as you should any game. It does take alot to run, but I'm running on a crap-top right now and it's perfect. The game is obviously a survival multiplayer zombie game, which relies heavily on looting. There are few things I have to scold the game for, it's an experience that changes every single time, whether you spawn North in a large town, or SoutWest on the coast of Balota, you really never know what you're going to experience. Between the mix of infected and human players, this game always has me on my toes, and it has but one simple goal, survive. The aspect of survival comes from managing hunger/thirst (obviously), temperature, health, and whether or not you're bleeding. The game is very buggy, but that is nothing to be worried about because those bugs make the fun 50% of the time. This game rarely comes out with updates because Bohemia Int. is working on other projects and it's a small team that runs the development of this game, and I respect them for doing all of this with such a little team. Only one thing to carp about, is the updates, while promising for this game, seek to include new content amongst major bug fixes, while not a bad thing, the game isn't fully optomized yet, which should be a higher prioirty of major changes/introdutions. Other than that, its a fun game to play as it shapes itself into a full game.

So, after ~206 hours of playing this game, I have alot to say. This game is wonderful. Ignore those who have -100 hours and speak of so-called "Graphical limitations." While the game's graphics are sub-par, don't be too quick to judge, as you should any game. It does take alot to run, but I'm running on a crap-top right now and it's perfect. The game is obviously a survival multiplayer zombie game, which relies heavily on looting. There are few things I have to scold the game for, it's an experience that changes every single time, whether you spawn North in a large town, or SoutWest on the coast of Balota, you really never know what you're going to experience. Between the mix of infected and human players, this game always has me on my toes, and it has but one simple goal, survive. The aspect of survival comes from managing hunger/thirst (obviously), temperature, health, and whether or not you're bleeding. The game is very buggy, but that is nothing to be worried about because those bugs make the fun 50% of the time. This game rarely comes out with updates because Bohemia Int. is working on other projects and it's a small team that runs the development of this game, and I respect them for doing all of this with such a little team. Only one thing to carp about, is the updates, while promising for this game, seek to include new content amongst major bug fixes, while not a bad thing, the game isn't fully optomized yet, which should be a higher prioirty of major changes/introdutions. Other than that, its a fun game to play as it shapes itself into a full game.

Borderlands 2=High quality

Let me lay it down for you guys, Borderlands 2 is one of my new favorite games in my library.
Borderlands 2 is a hybrid FPS RPG 4 player Co-Op game. Now, when I say RPG, I don't mean something like Final Fantasy, Skyrim, or Dragon Age. Those games need you to be fully invested in the RPG elements of the game, and while I do like that sometimes, other times it gets boring for me. Borderlands 2's system feels very unobtrusive and can produce some good results even if you are randomly picking things in the skill tree. But if you do put some thought into your character's skills and how you play the game, you could be rewarded with a character that is perfect just for you. A good thing to mention is that there is only 4 (now 6 with DLC) classes to choose. While that doesn't seem like many to some people, each charcter is unique in skillset and apperance.
I must say, even though it didn't feel like then, the first 1 to 2 hours are slow. You don't even unlock skills untill lvl 5. That goes away once you hit the "hub" city of Sanctuary. This is where the story picks up and the one of my favorite parts of the game shines, the side quests. These missions never take themselves too seriously and sometimes are quite inventive, more than the standard fetch quests other games make you do. And everyonce in a while you start a quest that turns into a large chain of quests, building this little mini story (A good example of this is Ellie's Clan War quest). The main story is okay, much better than the orignial's, but it isn't close to the amount of depth some other shooters have. However the writing is great and is very funny. All of the NPCs have their own personality and some you can really begin to love after a while. Except Claptrap. I can love him in short bursts.
For the FPS element, it comes down to the guns. Remember when I said the RPG system was unobtrusive? I kinda lied, as I have spent lots of time just sitting and comparing the stats of guns, shields, class mods, relics, and grenades to each other. Guns can be pistols, shotguns, assault rifles, snipers, SMGs, and rocket launchers. All equipment has a manufacturer which decides for guns what it's strenght has. So Jacobs guns are usually high damage, low capcity, semi-auto guns, but the fire as fast as you can pull the trigger. Hyperion guns actually get more accurate the more shots the fire. And there are more brands with more effects. Then there is elemental types that do more damage to certain types of enemies, like fire doing more damge to biological enemies, corriosive doing more to armored enemies, ect. So when ever you pick up a gun you have a lot of things to consider.
Speaking of guns and loot there is a serious issue when it come to Co-Op. When an enemy drops a gun, it only drops one. Not a problem in single player. But with 4 people that causes issues, especially on bosses who drop really valuable loot. For me that is my only serious issue with the game, and I play by myself mostly anyway.
I've had lot's of fun playing this game, and if you don't own it, I suggest you do. I also suggest you get the Game of the Year edition which is a great value. And remember in the words of Markus the gunsalesman, "No Refunds!"

We're talking about:
-2 more playable characters
-4 more campaigns which includes more loot and UNIQUE weapons to be found.
-Max level cap at 72, meaning more skill points to wreck your enemies
-Level 72 not enough? Get overpower levels (up to 8) to make your enemies scale up to level 80+ and find level 80 weapons in the process. (Also a DLC)
-5 Head hunterpacks, optional if you're willing to spend some cash to spice up a little more missions.
If you love open world games with a mixture of RPG values AND coop features to play with your friends, would definately recommend this game.
-Ranks to increase stats that apply to ALL characters by completing tasks
As for storyline, has many aspects in it, of course, definitely humour
The only cons i see in the game is tedious farm for EXP towards end-game ONLY if you are playing multiple characters. Its a pain to level each one of them to level 72 (Only if you have both vault hunter packs) if you really felt like doing that in the first place, unless of ocurse you have the patience to do so.
Overall, in my opinion, i enjoyed the game and i do still have plans to continue here and there.

I have removed my recommendation from DayZ because my opinion of this game and the development team behind it have changed dramatically. No doubt this review will have the "Early Access Review" sticker hanging over it but don't kid yourself because this title will never leave Early Access.
The sad truth is, the first major flaw with this game is the clunky engine. They can add as many new models as they like, add more guns, vehicles, farming, shelters and whatever else you can think of. However, it all comes down to the engine that they are piling all of this on to and that's not going to go away.
Movement feels unresponsive, the animations are god awful, the melee combat is a joke not to mention pointless. The only thing you'll ever go up against are other players with rifles, lying in a treeline a couple of miles away.
There was so much potential for this to be great, I even raved about it to my friends until they bought it and joined up with me online. Now I feel like I owe them money,like I talked them into investing in a pipe dream. On top of that, the number of other, more respectable developers that have jumped on the bandwagon, rushing out sub par titles to "beat" this mess have left a dark cloud hanging over the entire genre.
As much as it pains me to say, this is just not an acceptable game.

DO NOT BUY THIS GAME! I have seen games come out of alpha and become beautiful works of entertaining art, however, DayZ is not one of those games. After all these years this game has not only remained in terrible quality, but it has actually gotten worse. The loot table has become impossible, the glitches unbearable, and the physics unremarkable. There has been little to no progress, and the devs are simply not putting in the effort that 70 million dollars should merit. After all these years the only progress they've managed is a broken vehicle system. The engine is simply too shoddy to live up to the expectations this game previously promised, and it will likely never leave alpha. If you're interested in a survival shooter, I suggest going back to Arma, at least the modders there can balance a loot system.

Millions upon millions of guns, a variety of different enemies, six unique classes, and up to three friends make one of the best games ever.
No game is without its flaws however.  Character customization is limited to only head and body selection.  Well, perhaps no game is without its flaw.

As you kill enemies or complete challenges you gain exp towards levelling up and gaining skills or "Bad♥♥♥♥♥Points" that add stats to ALL characters on your gamer-profile. The game has humour which works on many levels - Cult/Pop references, Story based humour, even some potty-humour but never over the top or too offensive.
The actual game play is stanrd FPS "see it? Shoot it!" style with random loot drops of new weapons/character customisation options. With up to 6 playable charcters (depending on your version 4 in basic, 6 in Game Of The Year Edition or with all DLC) with seprerate skills to aid combat or totally change play styles there is plenty of replay value. Plus LOADS of character customisation options - new heads and skins both unlockable in game or purchasable for cash (cheaply 79p per head).
Online play is mainly Co-Op with PvP duels and trading as an option. Co-op boosts loot, experience and enemy difficulty depending on how many players are playing (up to 4 per host). The other online option are the SHIFT KEY CODES which unlock new heads/guns/or usually grant players KEYS used to gain special rare items. These codes are findable online via various websites.
The game even has loads of graphic options so low-end PC's can run it too.
All in all I'd have to give this game a 9 out of 10. Only losing 1 pointasI like to create my own character from scratch but appreciate how much they have fleshed the various characters ith backgrounds and personality

So Undertale. Let me get this out of the way first. I do recommend the game, but I feel I can only do so with several notes.
Now to the point. You've probably noticed I've put a large number of hours into this game. I would not recommend doing this. Almost everything about the game will be pleasing the first time you experience it (thus the recommendation), however very little of Undertale is enjoyable after you start replaying it for extra endings multiple times.
First of all while the characters are entertaining, most of them are very static. I feel that the game does a good job at fleshing out the characters, but doesn't actually do much with them, which is disappointing because the games plot relies almost entirely on the characters. In most cases you'll meet a character in an area, most or all of your interactions will be confined to said area, and once the area ends there are a few possibilities depending on what actions take. My problem is that most of the optional interactions serve to show you more of what you will see regardless of what you do. Specifically, most characters rely heavily on a single trait. Some are overly intense, some are intended to bond with the player, and some are just weird. But In most cases every character will fall back on these traits no matter what happens or what you do. Once again, the first time around the limits that these traits are pushed to make up for the lack of depth, but the second or third time around it seems monotonous. Once you know the character's behavior you'll quickly search for what you can do to make him or her do something different, and even if you stumble upon different dialogue, it will probably only be slightly different from what you have seen before. The same thing extends to the enemies, the enviroments, and even the items to an extent. The first time around it all seems very unique, but once you start to sense a pattern it gets bland.
Granted on the second and third playthroughs this isn't immediately apparent as you'll likely encounter portions of the game that you didn't on your first and second playthroughs. My problem with this is that alot of this content can be almost impossible to find without a guide, and since most of the fun of Undertale comes from going in blind, you risk devastating spoilers if you consult one. Most of my playtime of undertale came from trying to trigger certain events I knew existed (primarily due to screenshots) but had know Idea how to initiate. I played through the game so many times that once or twice I was able to finish it in two and a half hours or less (Note: my first playthrough took me ten hours). If I could say that throughout all the time I put in I was able to complete, or even consistently experience new parts of game , I wouldn't be complaining; but at the time of this review there are still multiple areas and bosses I've never seen on my file. Several of my playthroughs were nigh indentical due to the fact that you're only allowed to to use one save file. There were several times when I thought my actions would make a difference, but in the end did little to nothing, and I would've been better of restarting instead of continuing in vain hope.
Furthermore, the game often tries to subvert certain tropes in gaming, sometimes to the point of dialogue that blatantly condemns certain elements. However at some points this can be overbearing and unnecessary. There are multiple points in game that a certain action will be encouraged just so the game can subvert a trope associated with said action. The worst part for me is that some portions simply don't work well even with this in mind. There are several times when the intended effect of a certain portion is missed due to the fact that the player probably only triggered said event because he or she wanted to see something new, and not because of any persistent pattern in gaming culture or game design.
Although the aesthetics are a special case. With most of the other elements I feel they get old quickly, in the case of the visuals and sound I feel they are somewhat lopsided. To elaborate, there are some tracks that I could listen to on loop for hours, but there are others that I forgot existed by the time I bought the soundtrack. There are some objects that look very detailed for pixel art, but in the same area the floor might be a solid color with a black border or outline. At the end of the day I feel like the good far outweighs bad, but this inconsistency is worth mentioning. Furthermore the titles of the tracks include rather specific story spoilers, so I wouldn't recommend the soundtrack until you have seen most of the endings.
In Conclusion I feel that undertale is a game very much worth your time and money, however the latter moreso than the former. As aforementioned Undertale relies heavily on your initial experiences, however I don't really think I can adequately describe how potent the initial effect of almost every element is. If you can go in mostly blind (like I did) your first playthrough will undoubtedly be a positive experience, and if you don't get carried away with replaying the game (like I did) your experience as a whole will be almost entirely positive.

In a gaming market overflowing with brooding, dark, serious shooters and RPGs, a game like Borderlands 2 is a breath of fresh air.
This game is fun and funny, a great combination. The characters are wonderfully unique, and the dialogue makes me chuckle all the time. The gameplay is very much centered around the loot: guns, guns, and more guns. There are TONS of weapons to choose from, with 5 different classes including Assualt Rifles, SMGs, Snipers, Shotguns, and Launchers. You'll get them by completeing quests or looting crates and bodies, both of which you fill find a lot of.
I do have some mechanics issues...driving doesn't always feel smooth to me and can be annoying. The enemy AI is often bafflingly bad, specifically when they seemed to lose awareness of you if you step back a few feet. Even when I have a clear sight line to an enemy, they will leave combat mdoe and return to patrolling. Once I had a gun pinned behind cover, and after a few seconds he just stood straight up and started casually walking away, saying something like "you better run!". Finally, the save system is terrible. There are no manual saves that I'm aware of, and quiting mid play will often send you back several checkpoints. This can be very frustrating.
Despite those small flaws the game is loads of fun to play, and I've enjoyed every hour so far. If you like shooters and RPGs, this is for you!

This game has inspired me to improve my music composing skills. And I'm not kidding when saying the music is one of the biggest parts of this game. Sure, some tracks are definitely "borrowed" from other places, like the "Once upon a time" is a rehashed intro from Mother series, and the "Spookytune" is a "Puzzle" from Sonic Rush Adventure, but you need to be familiar with a ton of stuff to notice that.
When I see people complaining about the graphics, I can't help but sigh - every sprite is crafted with love and passion, it's a stylistic choice, don't attack it.
Story-wise, the game brings back something that has been forgotten for quite some time - a feeling of an Adventure, covered in a sparkling pile of humour and likeable characters.
Of course, there's a lot of things that got me disappointed at times - about 8 unused audio tracks (5 of which were not even included into official OST), the butterfly catching mini-game IS NOT THERE, DESPITE BEING FEATURED RIGHT ON THE COVER IMAGE! Oh, and... should I mention characters that were "cut off"? Can we expect more development for them in the possible updates? Toby, please..?

Undertale is a unique experience for story/rpg fans, the graphics may not be the best ever but after a while you get used to it. The replay time is very long and sometimes lasting 60+ hours, yet you can finish the game in 6hours if you really want too. It's very story indulging and the choices do matter and whatever you do affects the story of the game.
You should probably do all runs blind to get the full experience out of this masterpiece of a game, but if you haven't played it blind it's still amazingly fun!

The plot is that you are a human that has fallen down to the underground and the goal is to escape.
You meet many quirky monsters that all have different personalities and feel like real people (Ex: Toriel,Flowey,) and the Pacifist route story is very tear inducing, yet you have to kill them all to see everything, which can be very sad depending on how tied to the characters you are.
Cons:
-No different run speeds
-No difficuilty slider, which can be bad, especially if you're struggling on a boss. (I am aware of hard mode)
-Graphics, it's just terrible.
Overall, i rate it a 7.7/10, Highly recommended but poorly recommended for people who are only in for competition and blood.

Undertale...I don't even know where to start with this game.
It's a Role Playing Game where you play as a human child who fell down a deep hole on a mountain.
One of the first things you'll notice about this game is it's presentation. It is heavily stylized, valuing a deep immersive experience over modern day graphics or function. It is crude and simplistic in its design, but incredibly robust and full of charm.
One thing worth mentioning of the bat is the games soundtrack. The soundtracks has a lot of variation in style and is used heavily as a staple part with in the game to create a specific mood. There are many charming, memorable melodies within this soundtrack in my opinion.
The controls are simple, intuitive and few (there's only like 3 buttons you have to remember, minus movement keys), making it easy to remember.
The game follows a linear but ever evolving storyline full of weird and wonderful monsters, humor, dogs and spaghetti. Your choices matter, and you don't ever have to slay a single NPC.
Speaking of which, one of things that got me interested in this game in the first place is that the encounters with monsters never feel shallow.
The player has different things they can do in the "Act" tab which change depending on the monster(s) encountered. If an opponent ever loses the interest to fight with the player there is the option to spare them to end the battle.
Alternatively you can hit them with a stick (or a book or ballet shoes or a frying pan or...) by timing your attack to deal damage. If you defeat them this way you get traditional experience points to increase your survivability.
When the enemy gets a chance to attack, you get the chance to control a heart shaped object to avoid a series of stylized projectiles to avoid taking damage, probably one of the most engaging things about this game for me.
There's a lot this game has to offer. whether you enjoy the fast paced action of the 'bullet hell' system, or an engaging storyline, this might be the game for you.

So i decided to write a serious review
I've played a lot of Steam Games. A lot, a lot, a lot of games. But one of the games that stood out for me was UnderTale.
At first, it looks like a simple, childish game that you can finish in a few hours, but it is one of the best games i've played in a while. It fits in a huge 100 song soundtrack, (That I still listen to) some of the best music i've ever heard in a game, and one of the most memorable boss fights.
What makes UnderTale such as great game (no exagerration) is that each of the monsters are all amazing and you care about them, whereas in other games you do not care if they all suddenly died in a plane crash (xd 9/11 jokes). It also adds an ingenious system that allows you to spare or kill a monster, which leads to many different endings. It may look like i do not play this game often, but I usually play this game without internet when travelling, and my total hours would probably be around 50-60.
UnderTale is a cheap game that you may not clock hundreds of hours into, but says more about a game in a few hours than some games do in a thousand.
TL;DR it's good buy it ok?

I'm a skinny geek and totally out of condition, not a well trained soldier. I can easily get over a wall that's taller than me as long as I can jump and reach the top - and I can leap over obstacles much taller than them tiny DayZ fences without coming to a complete halt >.<
Bohemia, please, use me for mocapping and I'll show you the way of a true soldier!
ARMA 2 is based on Real Virtuality 3, released in 2009 and it will barely play properly on a modern and decent gaming rig in 2017.
DayZ is based on a variation of RV3 so it shares most if not all of the issues. Baaaaah!!!!

Give it a chance. I think you'll be pleasantly surprised.
