A deconstruction, by its nature, can't be particuarly innovative. A deconstruction can be clever, which Undertale certainly is at many points. The way shopkeepers question you when you try to sell things, "What is this, a pawn shop?"; and the way you gain EXP is all very clever, and points out much of the flaws through gamefication that we see in JRPGs and games in general.
While Undertale is a clever deconstruction, the basic elements of the game are a bit lacking. There's too much walking around in boring environment, repetitive and sometimes annoying battles or gameplay, and narratives that are forced or just dumb.
The world, despite a lot of effort being injected into the writing and natural sense of humour, wasn’t that engaging and offered nothing interesting visually. The sprites looked they were from a NES or old Atari game, which I wasn’t a fan of, but I can forgive on the basis that the graphics aren’t the focus of the game and that I’m pretty sure this has been developed by one dude.
While the purpose and point of the game was interesting, I didn’t overly enjoy my time playing it. I felt that the six and half hour game could have been done in two, and still got the same message across without a lot of the tedium.
But I should say hats off to the developer for trying something different and purposeful, even if it didn’t tickle my buttons.

I feel like too many people give this game a bad rap for it's community. Don't get me wrong, the community is pretty trash, but not recommending a game based on that alone feels a bit unfair. My strong suggestion is that Facepunch adds a singleplayer option, as many dislike the mpPvP aspect of it, especially beginners. This game is total hell for about 30h after purchase, while you learn the basics of the PvP system, base building, trustworthiness, etc. After those 30h it becomes a hell of a lot more fun. There's ups, downs, adrenaline kicks, pretty much everything that makes a game fun.
Another suggestion is that you only buy this game if you have friends that would play it with you, as playing solo ruins the fun of it, especially on multiplayer servers. It also makes it easier to build a base and gather materials.
If you get this game, you will be sad when your base gets raided, you'll be sad when you get destroyed by a guy with 1000 hours with an AK-47, but you will also be happy when you raid your first base, are getting raided and fend off the attackers. This game, as I said, is an up-down game, and you will definitely feel like♥♥♥♥♥♥sometimes, and like you're on top of the world at other times.
And trust me, although you may think it would suck having to start over again after spending 10 hours on a base, it actually is a good thing, because you usually start to get bored of your base within a few hours and just end up roaming around and PvP'ing. For people that like a grinding game that has a lot of fun, ups and downs, adrenaline kicks, etc. This is for you.

Overall, great game. Takes the things from its predecessor Borderlands and runs with them; some of the things are a bit overdone, such as the comedy, but for the most part they're well done. The story is decent yet solid, and (obviously) Gearbox provides no end of side missions and DLC for the game--if available, purchase the Game of the Year version. I never played multiplayer because of a lack of friends, but it's no doubt a huge plus to the game, so if you have the friends to play with, make this a group venture.
One criticism: the aerial AI programming is absolutely horrible. Most vehicles in the game are fast, making them difficult to attack with slow-acting rockets, but flying vehicles and enemies make this much, much worse by being 100% unpredictable and changing their flight paths constantly due to "collisions" they see. If you're fighting a flying enemy in this game, you're going to have a bad time.
Aside from that, this is a great game! Especially for sale value! Highly recommended for a full 40-hour game experience.

This game has a lot of longevity, it is an FPS/RPG that is based around looting weapons and4 person coop (though it isn't required).

In terms of story this game is phenominal. It takes a very serious story and wraps it in a very unique brand of humor that is unique to borderlands. Though it is a sequel you don't need to have played Borderlands 1 to enjoy this game, though it may do you well to learn the basic plot and main characters. This game also features my all time favorite videogame villain, Handsome Jack, who you will no doubt love to hate. All combined, this game has a hillarious and somewhat moving story.

As for gameplay, The game does an incredible job of adding variety to the many quests you recieve. Unlike Borderlands 1, which was plagued by fetch quests, the quests in this game feature many different objectives ranging from killing minibosses to blowing up bandit cars. A key component to this game is looting new and exciting weapons and leveling up your character. You will constantly be finding new and exciting loot to power up your character. That being said, Some of the enemies are very repetitive and at times fighting them can be tedious.

DLC. This game contains a wide variety of DLC which includes 4 story addons, 2 new playable characters, and 5 short "headhunter" DLC (Headhunter DLC is not included in the game of the year edition but can be bought seperatly). I won't review each peice of DLC individually, however, I will say that "Tiny Tina's Assult on Dragon Keep" is now one of my favorite DLC's of all time. It is absolutely worth bying the Game of the Year edition.
While the developers did a great job with the game, They had a few short cominhs. I will say that the game does not center on teamwork (Skill trees will buff your character but don't provide ways to help others) and The level cap (which was raised through DLC to 72) is tedious to reach and will require 2-3 playthroughs of the game, each playthrough more difficult than the last, limmits how unique your character is by providing access to most of the abilities by the time you're done. Some people may like having the higher level cap, I personally do not.
All in all, this is a phenominal game and if you havn't played it yet, you are doing your self a disservice. i give this game a 9/10. It is a good point to jump into the franchise.

Solid RPG Gameplay Wrapped in Emotion
I admit, when I first launched this game, I did not understand what catapulted it to cult status. The look of the game was a little offputting, given the NES/SNES/Gameboy hybrid art style. The gameplay, though unique in its shoot ’em up style dodging system, felt cumbersome to me. I felt all this as I dredged through the opening, hanging on by a single thread: The characters. And boy, am I glad I stuck around.
The game’s quirky characters take many pages from the Earthbound/Mother series of games as well as little sprinkles from the various RPG series starring Mario. They are full of wit and charm, never knowing what situation you are going to find yourself in next. As funny and odd as they can be, they all seem to be held back by various quirks of their personality or the situation of the monsters underground, delving into some rather dark subplots and events. This is what pulled me through the game. The sprite work itself is beautiful, recalling images of Earthbound as even the most insignificant mob has its own unique sprite bursting with personality. And the best part of the combat system? I don’t have to hurt anyone if choose not to.
The game turns the RPG genre on its head by allowing you to spare all of your foes, largely affecting the  game’s ending depending on how you go about it. As tempting as it can be to just crush all the mobs in front of you, the game pulls at your heartstrings and tempts you to run as a pacifist. This is a game best enjoyed multiple times, though I would recommend the most violent of runs as the last, for maximum effect and other reasons I do not plan on disclosing. As quickly as I fell in love with the characters and plot, the unique dodging system also drew me in despite my initial dislike and dread. The game also contains a gorgeous soundtrack, especially considering that it was all made by a single developer. No single track felt out of place and the boss themes are fantastic. Give it a try beyond the Ruins, and I assure you that you won’t be disappointed by this emotional rollercoaster.

A deconstruction, by its nature, can't be particuarly innovative. A deconstruction can be clever, which Undertale certainly is at many points. The way shopkeepers question you when you try to sell things, "What is this, a pawn shop?"; and the way you gain EXP is all very clever, and points out much of the flaws through gamefication that we see in JRPGs and games in general.
While Undertale is a clever deconstruction, the basic elements of the game are a bit lacking. There's too much walking around in boring environment, repetitive and sometimes annoying battles or gameplay, and narratives that are forced or just dumb.
The world, despite a lot of effort being injected into the writing and natural sense of humour, wasn’t that engaging and offered nothing interesting visually. The sprites looked they were from a NES or old Atari game, which I wasn’t a fan of, but I can forgive on the basis that the graphics aren’t the focus of the game and that I’m pretty sure this has been developed by one dude.
While the purpose and point of the game was interesting, I didn’t overly enjoy my time playing it. I felt that the six and half hour game could have been done in two, and still got the same message across without a lot of the tedium.
But I should say hats off to the developer for trying something different and purposeful, even if it didn’t tickle my buttons.

This game is essentially the most challenging PVO (Player Versus Offline) game I have played. I honestly stopped liking this game a while ago but I would definetly give it another try if I have friends who want to play. I recommend this game's  mechanics and beauty but not the community and overall experience. I haven't played in the last month but I played this game religiously previously. If you are looking for a game that is raw survival involving food management, construction, and scavenging then this game is for you. If you want to play with a community then that is a different story.
This games is designed to essentially live life as a raider. You start out naked and work your way up to gain the most resources while huge mass of other players are also competing. You start out only with a rock and eventually you will have a gun to defend your stuff. If you do happen to make friends that won't actually steal from you then this game will be consume your time with fun and friendly banter but it can also destroy your faith in humanity as you login to find your property pillaged.
As time goes on the game gets slow, it's fun for a while but you eventually get tired of having to either own enough stuff to build something solid enough to stop most attacks (concrete for example) or hide. The people who play this game devolve into three types; the raiders, the desperate survivors, and then the players who came with friends who also liked the game but wanted friends to both help and be able to log off without worrying. The raiding players are ones who played long enough or cheated (which happened a long time ago but not recently to me) who hunt new players for sport and steal your stuff just out of entertainment or to cement their power. The desperate are players who spend their time playing to survive and hide until they are powerful enough to be a raider themselves. The friends group are the rarest but the best players to play with as they rotate online and are able to render help to players.
What really spoiled the game is the server wiping, hacking, and community. Unless you play with friends or happen to find some online then be prepared to play the entire time with a hightened heart rate and fits of rage while also being anxious offline wondering if someone has found your base yet. After spending hours uppon hours of playing to become powerful enough to ward off the raiders and other hostiles (zombies) then the worst happens, you encounter a hacker. You spent all the time making a machine gun, ammo, and scavenging materials to be able to play without fear just to have your bullets do nothing and have a teleporting troll blink into your fortress and raid everything. If you finally do wait for the hacker to be kicked or get bored there is the worst thing that happens; a server wipe.
As it should be expected of early access games, server wipes are devestating for players who have sunk more than a couple of hours into a server. You finally find your friend, build a base, and crafted some decent items only to find that everyone is running around like they have nothing to lose after the admins gift everyone with rocket launchers, guns, and other weapons only seen after at least a day of mining, crafting, and scavenging schematics.
All in all I would highly recommend this game to someone who wants a SURVIVAL GAME. Suvival does not always mean friends, given things, and expecting everyone to be reasonable. I would also recommend it to someone who wants a challenge in online multiplaying.

8/10 would (and will) suffer paranoia and PTSD again.

While I love my console version for split-screen multiplayer (teaming up with my 9-year-old son against bandits and Hyperion alike is awesome), I find the Steam version of Borderlands 2 amazing for a couple of reasons. One, cloud saving just saved my♥♥♥♥♥when it came to this game! Having had to reboot from scratch earlier this week, finding out that my save file was intact on the cloud was a HUGE relief to me, something that I can't say would be done on consoles without paying for it. Second, something about the looks of it on my PC, even at the lower settings, that makes it look better than the console just tickles me. And lastly, it was very easy to transition from controller to mouse/keyboard setup for me. My son...not so much.
My advice is simple--get the GOTY version if and when you can. The only content it doesn't have that you might need would be the Headhunter series, and even that's more optional than anything. Everything else is there in all its glory to behold. And anyone who doesn't go through Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep without laughing at least once has no sense of humor.

A game that knows it's a game and wants to have fun with that self-awareness but still wants you to play it as a game and take it seriously. At every turn, the game is winking at you (figuratively and literally) and constantly challenges expectations and conventions. In a word: incredible.
My progress through Undertale was slow and, admittedly, interrupted by other games (once i started DOOM, there was no stopping). I found myself frustrated at parts, as i was playing the "True Pacifist" route and some of the bullethell boss battles are very difficult when playing this way. There are times that i wanted to stop, but i'm glad i didn't.
I often feel that a game is only as good as the impression it leaves behind, and this has left a monstrously-sized impression on me. Character relationships (with both the player and each other) is nailed in a way that gives these simple but lovingly-drawn figures life in a most convincing sense. Frustrations forgotten, all i'm left with is a fondness for the time i spent with this story.
Other games i would recommend to fans of Undertale: To The Moon and The Sea Will Claim Everything.

Undertale is a fantastic game.  One of the coolest features about it is that it is not necessary to kill anyone, unlike the more old-style RPGs. Undertale is super funny, has a great soundtrack and brillant characters you won't soon forget.  Both the characters and the soundtrack sometimes require a bit of thought to decide which is your favorite.  Undertale is definitely in my top three favorite games and even though I've played through each route multiple times, I never get tired of it.

I have played this game fully on console and recently bought it on pc for the summer sale, and I can easily say this is my all time favorite game. There are no cons in this game for me, although some people arent too keen on the graphics. In my opinion the graphics are awesome ad truely define the game and make it Borderlands. I also like how there is 2 playthrough modes (3 with dlc included) that get increasingly harder each time with higher level characters and weapons. The bosses and weapon legendary (rarest weapon) system is awesome too. It feels so satisfying to defeat a supposedly invincible raid boss and then get a rare weapon drop from him. This also adds more play value to the game and gives you the task of collecting them all if you choose. Characters are detailed and have thier own personalities. The game is humour rich and very detailed. Story is pretty long (I would say about 8 - 10 hours of gameplay) but with ample side missions and there is never a dull moment. Overall there is no question. This game, even though been out for quite a while, is a must buy, even to players that havent played the original game.

Points Review - Undertale (2015)
13 points must be achieved to get a recommended.
This review will go through Graphics, Gameplay, Story, Music and other less important details.
Gameplay - 3/5
Undertale uses a combination of a roaming environment and a battle system which involves random encounters with enemies which must either by defeated by force or through other means in a dodge-bullet and deal damage system. An addition to the play-it-your-way kind of games, it involves 3 main storylines with 2 of them having to meet different but obvious criteria. All these routes involve a different kind of gameplay; however, in order to see the rest of the game the player must play through at least 3 times which can take 9 hours (at least for me). A lot of the random encounters can become quite a bore in a mainly story-based game and if you are unfortunate enough to make a mistake and have to backtrack it can take a long time (this can be cut down if the transport between "worlds" is found).
Side note: There is no way or go back to the main menu in the game, so if you want to change the controller settings for example, you will have to restart. I also found that if you remove the controller you were using and re-insert it, it crashes the game.
Graphics - 4/5
Undertale's graphics are a joint between retro cartoony graphics when in the overworld and Sin City-esque black and white when in battle. This is also prominent when
, which I personally found to be a nice touch. The overworld graphics are usually quite minimal whilst the battle system has much more detailed characters albeit black and white.
The game's base resolution when in windowed mode is 640x480, and there is no way to change this in windowed. However a keystroke will take you to fullscreen mode with no compromise in the graphics quality.
Story - 5/5
This is where everybody knows what Undertale is about. Often heralded for its highly engrossing story, Undertale's story involves a human child falling down a hole into the underground and must make its way back to the surface and possibly making some new friends (or enemies) along the way. The backstory when you start the game every time gives a fine idea of what happened and how it happened before the game starts.
The neutral route (which is the only one that can be done first time) rather emotionally sets up characters that will be used later in other run-throughs (
). This can definitely been seen when
. Every single main character has a great personality and shows a sense of humanity (no pun intended) which can bring out real feelings and add to the emotion of the story.
Personally, I found the genocide route to be
because of the radical difference. It seemed like a completely different game and almost every single character reacted differently to you which was a great touch.
Side note: The game is short. This can please or annoy you depending on who you are but it being short will help if you wish to do mutliple runthroughs.
Music - 3/5
There are
of pieces of music in Undertale's soundtrack and there seems to be some effort put into it and made with love. However, although a lot of them are related in some way, the same melodies and songs get extremely tiresome by the end of the game. The soundtrack involves a lot of music genres, including retro-inspired battle music, rock, chiptune and even Touhou-inspired melodies and instruments. This can add a lot of variety in the game if you are like me and enjoy many different genres. Some of the music is amazing and I love, but some just simply don't hit for me and I detest hearing.
Other details:
- The game is far too easy. A basic runthrough is shockingly easy to beat without dying once. However, on the subsequent runthroughs there will be changes that will challenge you more. Controllers generally give the game a challenge because they really aren't good for this game.
- The game's size when downloading is around 115 MB, which is easy to shove on to a PC if you're bored.
- Changing the music files for your pleasing is incredibly bizarre. The speeds of some of the songs have to be adjusted so specifcally it seems trivial (for example, for the track "Undertale" the speed has to be increased by 17.5% and the Barrier SFX is 25% faster). Not really a changing factor, just very strange. They can all be found here if you wish to do it yourself
- Fanbase generally doesn't keep it to themselves. Many young players who have been watching too much YouTube have been stapling it everywhere they go (mainly YouTube and Steam), which is another annoying factor but not determining.
It's not a perfect game by any means, but it's a great way to find a new or interesting story and to kill some time (9-10 hours to speedrun the whole game with all routes). Recommending with caution because of the less-than-reserved fanbase. On an individual basis, try it for yourself and see what you think, it's a game with a divided viewpoint so your mileage may vary.

I bought this game after overwhelming reviews from friends.
After buying it, I decided to play it, like any self-respecting person would do.
12 minutes later, I quit it and stopped playing it. It was a good and well-developed game, but it bored me. The story really hadn't taken hold yet, and the game seemed repetitive. Walk around, find enemy, fight enemy, rinse and repeat.
It sat untouched in my library for 5 months.
I picked it up again at a friend's request, and played through to the boss battle with Undyne. I couldn't get through it (my keyboard was broken), but I still thought it was a bit repetitive.
So I put it away again, and moved on.
I guess my review for this game is, not everybody likes Undertale. The game is well-made, the music is captivating, the storyline is well thought out and beautifully executed, the characters are very life-like and engaging, and the combat system is a refreshing take on classic combat system from old RPGs. I like the game, but for me, I just can't get into it.
I give this game a 9/10, but it really isn't for everyone.

I can not think of a more memorable video game narrative that I've experienced recently. Depending on the player's approach, there are multiple ways to play Undertale due to the battle system that turn the typical RPG battle on their head. By giving the player the option to spare their "enemies" instead of fight, it offers more perspective on the entire point of the encounters. Battles can be used to learn about "enemies" as opposed to purely aggress against them and vice versa.
What appears as a simple indie RPG on the surface ends up being deep and humane in its story, tugging on heart strings and providing some lighthearted and funny fare, yet having no issue going to really dark places as well. A player will always wonder what may happen based on their actions.
For an RPG, it's not much of a time commitment either. Some may finish it in 5 hours. Some, 10-15. This depends on additional playthroughs as well, since Undertale sports multiple endings depending on what course you take. You can experience the bulk of the story possibilities in as little as two playthroughs if you are dedicated enough to following a single path at a time.

Having sold over 3 million copies as of January 2015 and grossing over $105 million dollars with development beginning in 2012, Early Access beginning in late 2013 and having been in Early Access for nearly 3 years with what was initially a delay due to some fundamental changes but has now manifested into a complete 'overhaul' it leads one to ponder about the future of this game and the integrity of the development team considering the initial mods are far more feature rich while working with little to no funding aside from small donations. The Epoch and Exile mod development teams were able to accomplish more in 3 months than Bohemia Interactive and DayZ Standalone development team could in 3 years.
There's no longer any incentive for this game to be completed aside from porting it to the console market for more sales and a much more handsomely lucrative market as the PC market is already exhausted and consumed up not to mention heavily saturated there's little to no profit to be made from PC. One look at the changelogs for patches and you'll notice a pattern of repeated abstract fixes and little bits and bobs that are imported from Arma 2, other mod work or can be modelled in under an hour by an amateur on YouTube who give free video demonstrations.
If you can get this game on sale for $20 or less, it may be worthwhile but in the current standing there's better survival games out there more feature rich with a better development schedule than this at or below the price of this game. I always put off writing a review for this game but it's important potential buyers are aware of the development history of this game and don't think for a moment that DayZ is some new and exciting Early Access title.
2017 UPDATE:
This is still a shadow of it's former self when it was just a mod. DayZ standalone AI pathing is still the same rudimentary pathing system used in Arma 2 and Arma 3, the zombies still run through walls as well as hit you when you're three floor levels above them, the animals they've added are still simulated by the default arma 2 AI, the map is still Chernarus from Arma 2 with a few more buildings added, the buildings you can enter are more or less copied from a players mod for Arma 2 that begun in 2011/2012 and eventually became the Open Chernarus Project.
The loot table is still awful and the only reason there isn't much loot is due to the loot holder needs to be simulated which impacts server peformance significantly which is why in Arma 2 and Arma 3 DayZ/Epoch/Overwatch/Origins/Exile etc. mods servers are restarted every 2 hours generally. DayZ Standalone is fundamentally still Arma 2 but at least with Arma 2 you had more than one game mode.
So why would you buy DayZ Standalone? All you're paying for is a shallow experience of the DayZ Experience™ and can only truly be experienced in Arma 2 OA mods. Just buy Arma 3 on sale for $14 USD  and get A3Launcher and go play DayZ Chernarus there, less than half the price with a much fuller experience.

When I first saw Undertale, I was really put off by the graphics. I thought the sprite for the main character looked really odd, and it didn't really interest me. What did catch my interest though, was the combat. The combat was very different, and not your run of the mill rpg combat. I dropped $15, picked it up, and was not disappointed.
Undertale is a strange game, through and through. It's sense of humor might not be for everyone, which is understandable. It's just a story about how a girl falls into a mountain full of demons. In her quest to be free from the mountain, she comes across many different many different demons, with a variety of personalities to suit them. Without saying too much plot wise, you get out what you put in. If you only beat the game once, you'll still get a decent story. If you want more of your favorite characters, and to experience the different endings, then go for it, you'll only get more enjoyment out of the game. You will probably not get the full story the first time through, which is why I recommend doing a blind run, and then doing one afterwards where you get some guidance from the internet.
The game is only a few hours long, which means if you go for a normal run, it'll take between 3-5 hours. It's a very good, short story.
The combat is a lot more active, since you have to dodge attacks from the enemies, and every attack from different enemies is really varied. You have to have quick fingers if you want to do well on some of the harder bosses.
The music is nothing short of perfect. Some of the music for the more dramatic parts of the game do a fantastic job of making you feel like a hero, a villian, or something in between. They set the mood perfectly, and the music is definitely what brought the game together overall. I still listen to some tracks off and on and it brings it all back. The music is just that well done.
Biggest complaint, no steam cloud save. I have a laptop and a desktop, I'd like to be able to swap between them easily, but not a huge deal.
If you like good music, zany characters, 8 bit art style, and well developed characters, I'd recommend this game.

It used to be, that this game was centered around player interaction, that a lot of encounters with another player would start somewhere around "yelling at eachother" and eventually escalate into a shootout.  This is no longer the case. With the advent of extremely arrogant and tryhard streamers with their own not-so-little cult following of kids and immature mankids, what was once a wacky wild naked adventure is now an exercise in reclusion. The "meta" now is to hide yourself in as remote a corner as possible, and to exterminate anyone who poses any threat (by virtue of existing).
The community sometimes attempts to justify this with frankly petty reasoning. "Oh, the bolt action rifles are too rare, so the people who own them will only roof camp with them. If they were made more common, the playing field could be leveled." "If only people showed their hotbar weapons on their backs, then I could see who is a faker threat and who is actually a fresh spawn." It's all lies and shoddy justification for a petulant behavior. A man with no weapons could be justified in being shot in that he may have had weapons not on his hot bar, but in his inventory, and so on and so forth.

When I first saw Undertale, I was really put off by the graphics. I thought the sprite for the main character looked really odd, and it didn't really interest me. What did catch my interest though, was the combat. The combat was very different, and not your run of the mill rpg combat. I dropped $15, picked it up, and was not disappointed.
Undertale is a strange game, through and through. It's sense of humor might not be for everyone, which is understandable. It's just a story about how a girl falls into a mountain full of demons. In her quest to be free from the mountain, she comes across many different many different demons, with a variety of personalities to suit them. Without saying too much plot wise, you get out what you put in. If you only beat the game once, you'll still get a decent story. If you want more of your favorite characters, and to experience the different endings, then go for it, you'll only get more enjoyment out of the game. You will probably not get the full story the first time through, which is why I recommend doing a blind run, and then doing one afterwards where you get some guidance from the internet.
The game is only a few hours long, which means if you go for a normal run, it'll take between 3-5 hours. It's a very good, short story.
The combat is a lot more active, since you have to dodge attacks from the enemies, and every attack from different enemies is really varied. You have to have quick fingers if you want to do well on some of the harder bosses.
The music is nothing short of perfect. Some of the music for the more dramatic parts of the game do a fantastic job of making you feel like a hero, a villian, or something in between. They set the mood perfectly, and the music is definitely what brought the game together overall. I still listen to some tracks off and on and it brings it all back. The music is just that well done.
Biggest complaint, no steam cloud save. I have a laptop and a desktop, I'd like to be able to swap between them easily, but not a huge deal.
If you like good music, zany characters, 8 bit art style, and well developed characters, I'd recommend this game.

Undertale undertale undertale.........
So what do I *personaly* think of undertale as a game first and foremost
So before I go on I would like to make a number of things clear. 1: this is MY OPPINION, if you like or hate this game im fine with it :). 2: im gonna review undertale as a game first and foremost, so none of the fandom and stuff will be mentioned (dont get me wrong its still toxic as hell and im not walking near it ever again). 3: im gonna try and look this game fairly criticly on top of my oppinion (aka anything i mention will be based unbiasedly unless I specify that its my oppinion)
So what are some of undertale's stronger points?
- The combat system is a very unique mix of and RPG and a Bullet hell styled game..... but is pretty flawed
- The locations in the game are honestly pretty original, despite the area themes being cliche
- (general opinion by many, as a heads up) the soundtrack is considered very good my most people who listen to it
- The difficulty balance is good for the most part (ill go on about this in a bit) and is generaly accessable by most people
So as you can see undertale is rounding up to look like a pretty cool experience, with stuff like a unique rpg combat system, some varity in its locations, a great soundtrack by most and some pretty fair diffculty...... however  there are some problems the game has that I feel no one really talks about.......
So what are the weaker points in undertale?
-The combat system is very unique and a nice idea, but its execution is something to be desired......
- Going off of before, the combat's problem is its very simple and can get quite boring after a while, Your hitbox in the     doging sections is huge for a game with precesion movements (however the game is built around it and it works about 95% of the time) and in the case of the Pacifist run there is no progress gained through battles and can feel unsatifying to some players.
- some of the games charm (its characters being the best example of this) is generaly subjective and some people will not enjoy it, while others will
-  The difficulty in the Genocide run is almost entirely broken, where all but 2 encounters will be complete pushovers and those 2 exeptions are massive spikes in challange
- Hotland as a whole is such a dumb area just for the sole reason that the *entire area* is just constant interuptions from a characters unending dialoge, a characters random wacky interuptions (that may or may not appeal to some), and a miniboss thats there because..... why not? (its never explained why you fight that midboss, you just do)
So with both sides in mind how is undertale in reality? as you can tell its the same kind of game that someone who likes games like Firewatch or Journey, games that are based on immersion (and maybe plot) over the actual game, im which undertale does good with.... at the same time these kinds of games arn't very accessable to the common consumer.
So would i personaly recommend undertale? as an immersive styled game I can recommended it. but as a game thats ment for the gameplay i think you should look past undertale. I think the spark is there for a good game (gameplay wise) here because the ideas it brings to the table are pretty smart and could be expanded into something very fun and immersive. but as it stands, undertale feels like its plot first, game later. and ill leave it at that......

This game is a ton of fun and I have had a good time, but I currently (as of version 0.60) do not recommend this game. DayZ is stuck in the well known "Development Hell", where the devs are either moving really slowly (like the team is made up of 3 indie devs), or the game has been promised but nothing has been shown. Diablo III is a good example of a Development Hell gone right, but some games never turn up, swept under the rug hoping no one will remember it. While I feel DayZ will be complete, I only recommend it at this state if you are looking for a fun experience with friends, and are wanting to participate in the journey of this development.
Another problem with the game is the community. It has sunken down into just KOSers and backstabbers. Many people say that the game sucks because the devs are rarely releasing new content, but I disagree. Bandits aren't bad, but there are too many of them and the reason is because in a game we often lack morals, especially if it is just other people who can't lose something IRL. This leads us to be like
where we always make decisions that are easiest and best suite ourselves and our group. Hate to burst your bubble, but it is much easier and better for myself if I just one-tappa kappa you and take your gear, and I don't care because this is just a videogame. With no encouragement to save others, why not just kill them? This is where the "Hero" system worked out in the mod. Bandits used to just take your beans and run off, but killing you is much easier, and the damaging gear thing where if you shot someone's pants they and its contents would be damaged didn't help really.
In conclusion, wait to buy this game. It is only for those who wish to take a ride on the development rollercoaster. The outlasting problem is the poor community, who just want to take your stuff rather than have fun by handcuffing you and "arresting" you. This is fixed somewhat by RP servers, but those have too many rules, and people just rob you of everything and run off, which is worse to me, as I would rather them kill me. Thank you for reading my review and please vote it helpful if you thought it was informative. Good luck if you make this purchase!

Rust is a good game. The community, however, sucks nuts. Imagine DayZ with 100x more KoS nonsense. No interaction, no positivity. Just mindless murder. You can sometimes have fun with a group, but even that gets boring when the only thing to do is kill everyone you meet (because they don't want to talk). The game's systems have been constantly iterated and improved upon, but there's one thing that Facepunch Studios cannot fix: the community.
It used to be, that this game was centered around player interaction, that a lot of encounters with another player would start somewhere around "yelling at eachother" and eventually escalate into a shootout.  This is no longer the case. With the advent of extremely arrogant and tryhard streamers with their own not-so-little cult following of kids and immature mankids, what was once a wacky wild naked adventure is now an exercise in reclusion. The "meta" now is to hide yourself in as remote a corner as possible, and to exterminate anyone who poses any threat (by virtue of existing).
The community sometimes attempts to justify this with frankly petty reasoning. "Oh, the bolt action rifles are too rare, so the people who own them will only roof camp with them. If they were made more common, the playing field could be leveled." "If only people showed their hotbar weapons on their backs, then I could see who is a faker threat and who is actually a fresh spawn." It's all lies and shoddy justification for a petulant behavior. A man with no weapons could be justified in being shot in that he may have had weapons not on his hot bar, but in his inventory, and so on and so forth.

Short version:
Game 7/10
Community 0.5/10
Long one:
As many other reviews have mentioned, the community around this game is incredibly toxic. On two separate servers I was mocked for not knowing how to begin, when there is no in-game tutorial (even a single pop-up with the basics of hit trees to get wood, hit dark grey rocks to get stone, and pick up hemp or hit cacti to get cloth would have been enough; though the map and sleeping bags could really use an explanation as well). And so after visiting a few extra-game websites to figure out how to start playing what's really a pretty simple game, I finally began.
After waking up naked, I ran up to a tree and started hitting it only to hear someone whisper "Hey, buddy" behind me. I turned around and he killed me with a gun. I woke up naked somewhere else and arrows immediately started flying past my head. I jumped around a bit until the other fellow finally pulled out a gun and killed me. Third time's the charm, right? Nope. After waking up naked, I started running away from the spawn area, only to get sniped at and finally killed by a couple of guys who were quite some distance away.
Finally on the fourth try, I was able to functionally start playing. After a couple of hours, I had a reasonably functioning base; cue a guy trying to sneak up and kill me with a silenced rifle. Luckily he was a terrible shot and I got lucky; I killed him first. I took all his gear and started exploring to see if I could find some of the stuff I couldn't craft myself. About 10 minutes later, I was dead and being looted by a guy with a machine gun.
After restarting again and getting a friend involved (who also was new to the game, but strength in numbers), I got a reasonable base and plenty of supplies. Had high quality metal bars smelted and could craft most of the stuff in the build menu. That was when I realized why everyone sat around killing other players: Unless you're really interested in just exploring the island, there's really only about 10 hours of gameplay here. By that time you'll have a fully functioning base, good armor, and at least a semi-automatic rifle. At that point, might as well just hunt new players as there's not really anything else left to do.

Bought this game on a whim, after seeing how much it had exploded over the internet. After hearing about how much the game made you question your choices and how much you would come to care for the characters, I expected exactly that.
However, the game I played was far, far different from that. Before I begin, let me be clear by saying that I have not completed the genocide/pacifist runs, nor do i intend on attempting them. This review is purely based on a 'standard' playthrough.
On a visual level, the game is in sore need of improvement. Many of the environments (especially the opening environment) felt bland and unfinished. Some of the character design is, admittedly, good, but the main character just looks bland and uninteresting.
On a technical level, the game has some serious head-scratching decisions. Why can I not use keyboard-and-mouse? I got stuck on the opening menu due to some quite horrific menu layout and key-binding, accidentally quitting the game and having to restart it (which is quick, so kudos to Toby Fox). Fortunately though, I did not encounter any game-breaking bugs or glitches.
On a gameplay and story level, however, Undertale is just overwhelmingly 'meh'. Let me start by getting some of the positives out of the way. The boss fights felt interesting and dynamic, with their accompanying theme perfectly suited for each fight. Undertale also has some interesting puzzles. Not head-banging levels of difficulty, but challenging enough to remain fun and not feel like filler.
However, apart from that, Undertale lets you down whenever it can. All the characters felt like crude archetypes, with barely enough characterisation to make their saving by your hand in the inevitable bossfight with them feel warranted.  The game itself is laughably easy. I only died once or twice. The game is over way too quickly. I felt constantly teased, thinking that the game was about to have some kind of revelation, only for it to never come to pass. The game's attempts at 'breaking game conventions' felt too much like it was a desperate kid saying: 'look at me, look at what I can do!'.
Please, only buy this game if you're curious about the game, but prepare for disappointment. Apart from that, your money is best off spent elsewhere.

I tried to resist raving about the game but I just couldn't because I ended up loving this game so much. I am with the hype!
The first few moments alone gave me that nostalgic feel to a game that I haven't quite felt since the PS1 days. As much as other games out there try to capture that retro vibe, Undertale went an extra mile and I would say it's all how it plays out at the start. A gameplay style that you wouldn't see everyday, an engaging storyline, lovable and memorable characters and one hell of a soundtrack which all together make this a game you simply cannot ignore. Months after I played through the whole of this game, I am still buzzing about it and even still listen to the soundtrack loads.
Whether you love it or hate it, one has to admit that Undertale has established itself as a game and made itself stood out of the crowd. This to me is the game the industry needs. For those that have yet to play it, I say go for it and see for yourself what the fuss is all about.

TL;DR - Enjoyable game with a predictable narrative that has made a huge impact on the current video game market.
This game gives the illusion of greatness. Launching the game, the player recieves some lore dialogue similar to a Legend of Zelda game. The game tricks its players into thinking they are playing an epic RPG, when it's really just a generic RPG (with some interesting twists) with a story and moral like that of an after school special. "Friendship is Magic" appears to be the mantra of this game, and the sapieness can be overwhelming sometime. It can also be fairly intriguing at times, and some of the writing in this game is humurous and interesting.
For a video game, the writing is fairly good, but the key phrase is "for a video game." The gameplay is nothing to write home about, it mostly involves dodging other characters atacks, and taking the pacifist or genocide route. You can either attack and kill your enemies, or talk them down. This is the games primary mechanic, and its tagline "the RPG where you don't have to kill anyone." And that is unique for about the first hour of the game, and then it gets tiring. If you want the "good" ending, then you can't kill anyone.
This is my biggest issue with the game; it creates a safe space for players, in which there is no real danger, there is no real challenge. Some bosses can can even be beaten by just letting them beat you severall times. Papyrus comes to mind, and that fight was very upsetting for me. Just as I thought I was learning his tactics, and getting better at fighting him, he surendered to me, and asked me to be his friend.
Overall, I don't think the game is terrible, I enjoyed bits of it. I just believe the game is overrated, and what I recieved compared to what I was expecting, I was underwhelmed. That is an issue with a lot of game media coverage nowadays, reviews and community impressions can impact a players impression of a game. Had I gone into this experience without any sort of background knowledge of the game, I believe I would have enjoyed it a lot more.
All-in-all, this game has character, it has charm and it has strength. It creates a world for the player to interact with, and seamlessly incorporates player choice into the story. It has also impacted expectations for Indie games, and showed developers that they can be creative and still be sucessful. It also shows the same thing to AAA developers, that small games can be equally as sucessful on todays video game market.

Rust isn't perfect, and while it is just the first survival game I've ever tried - it also gave me a good enough impression that it broadened my horizons and I now want to try other survival games. I've poured several hundred hours of my life into this game, had many sleepless nights, and it has brought me joy, happiness, rage, frustration, sadness, and feelings of hope which are eventually doused over and over and over again.
In my opinion, Rust is a game best played with friends. It is difficult to lone wolf - but its doable and quite enjoyable (and intense). The community is a bit toxic, but if you aren't a sensitive little♥♥♥♥♥♥there's some fun to be had. Remember, its just a game - and while the emotional rollercoaster that this game will take you on can be intense, you will most likely find yourself coming back for more.
The new updates with the component system are okay in my opinion. It makes it a bit harder to come up with the gear you want to craft, but in a way I suppose that it ensures that even early/low level equipment will be more visible in the game, which is good in my opinion.
However, there is one problem in this game, and its the large amount of hackers present on Official servers that have slowly started to invade Community servers as well. Lots of aimbots and other hacks make this game very frustrating if you play fairly. Facepunch has been working double time to solve this issue but at present the problem still persists. In Community servers at least the Admins can ban hackers, but then there are those hackers who have no problem with DDOSing the server until its unplayable for everyone else.
I recommend this game, despite the hacker issue - and I recommend that you buy a pack that allows you to gift it to your friends. I believe its worth the full price, but of course sales are the best times to purchase this.

Borderlands 2 is definitely a step-up from the original. The visuals have been improved by making them sharper and brighter. There is more of a story in this sequel, the company Hyperion has invaded Pandora to search for a new Vault, led by one of the best (and my personal favorite) villain Handsome Jack. There are a lot of characters who make a return such as: Moxxi, Marcus, Scooter and Claptrap. But of course there are new characters like Sir Hammerfell and Handsome Jack. There are four new Vault Hunters who (in my opinion) are better than the original four and there can be two more if you buy the Mechromancer and Psycho DLC. There is more variety in enemies but a lot of fan favorites like Psychos and Midgets return and adding new enemies like Goliaths and Nomads. The writing is very similar to the first and has the same type of humor, but there is more of it and there are loads of laugh out loud moments, especially with Handsome Jack. Borderlands 2 is without a doubt my favorite first-person shooter and one of the funniest games. Definitely my game of the year.

Overall definetly would recommend to anybody who likes  hardcore survival and pvp. Anyway... here is my DayZ story which might get you into the game :)
So i had freshly spawned in berezino and had found basic clothing and an axe, long story short i wasn't very geared. Down the road i saw another survivor looting a building so i thought to myself "well im fresh spawned with nothing good who cares if he kills me?" and approached him while saying i was friendly, he agreed and we had a brief conversation, none of us needed food or water so we went our seperate ways but we still saw eachother in the town every now and then, eventually i thought "maybe i could kill him for his rifle" so i had a zombie chasing me and decided to hit him with my axe, he then responded with "why would you do that man" i felt really bad so i apologised and he forgave me, i was looting very close to him inbetween a bunch of garages when i found another survivor, i was hit by a zombie and was bleeding but i had no bandages. This guy who i just found had a gun and offered me a leather sewing kit to stich up my wounds, when i was stitching up my wounds he continued to handcuff me and say "hahaha bet you didn't see that coming :D" so there i stood handcuffed while i had a casual conversation with my captor. He didn't want to kill me and was going to set me free when the friendly guy from earlier came around the corner and he tried saving me when he misunderstood the story of what had happened, long story short he was shot and killed and i was set free. My captor had left the original friendly man's loot for me and there was a rifle and some ammo... A man who i considered backstabbing for a gun had sacrificed his life for me... there was only one choice left, i picked up his rifle and loaded a shot into it and then continued to crouch down and put the barrel to my throat, i killed myself as i couldn't live with the guilt of what this man had done for me when i had considered killing him...
Overall this game could be extremely fun for you if you enjoy making your own story like i did.
Don't buy this game unless you want to actively support inactive development.

I have seen it all, from the days where you had to design
your base with a SEPERATE door for each friend that lived
there, and watched sunsets from the coast at resource valley
all the way to where we are today.
I have raided many a base, and have in turn been raided
many times, and asked myself many times: "Am I playing
Rust or is Rust playing me?"
Rust was born a child of a zombie/survival era and it very
actively tried to distance itself from that for a very long time
and how successful it was in that endevour im not sure, I'm
not even sure if that's a good or a bad thing, but it's a big
part of Rust's genetics since it formed it's early player base.
Is it worth the 20$? I think that is a daft question, because I
would argue it's worth more, but being a subjective question
I don't think, like with everything in rust, that it's a thing you
could get people to agree on, hell once I played a bit I baught
two more copies for two of my friends to join me, no regrets.
In MY opinion, Facpunch has been WAY to good to us, the
playerbase. A classic example of "give them the hand, they
rip off the whole arm".
Gary and Co are a tenacious bunch and in the grand scheme
of things the product they created is amazing for the size
of the team they have, they keep us up to date with clock
work devblogs every week.
Get electricity in, Get transport in, and remove the
early access badge, then spend some time optimizing
and bug hunting, and decide from there.
so hows the game? well gather up your friends and
bend over, Rust wants some love.
Cheers.

Played about 50 hours so far.  Its an open world game with little to no story line.  It is a great intriguing game with a relatively initial steep learning curve.  I think it the game had a tiny bit more structure with a bit of a storyline or competition, almost making it somewhat RPG/MMO  it would really steer this game in an even better direction.  That being said, the game is awesome - loads of fun, make friends VERY quickly.
Pretty realistic combat elements such as damage everyone is pretty squishy.
There are a few PVP trolls, but you'll find that in every game to think their isn't is being naive.  This game makes you use a bit of intellect as well when structuring and designing your compound.
Gear structure is pretty good, and it is, like I said more of a skills based thinking MMO than a gear driven MMO which I find VERY appealing for people who cannot put the necessary time into the game.
To make the game a little bit more interesting I would like to see a zone/providence (similar to battlefield and conquest - but continuous) control structure forcing people to make alliances and dominate the world - I think this would add an interesting competitive twist. Maybe even incorporate allowing people to align with NPCs which currently do not exist.
Overall this game is very fun but lacks a tiny bit of structure which I believe deters people from continuously playing this game similar to that of WoW.
My biggest advice to new players: Watch a few youtube tutorials before you play, take the 10 minutes to avoid the frustration of trying to figure things out yourself although it is very possible.

A very overrated game.
That's basically my review in a nutshell. I really hate to give this a negative review, but lemme still talk about it honestly. After all, this is a debated thing, and I do want to share my honest opinion.
First things first: THIS IS NOT RECOMMENDED FOR THOSE WHO ARE BORED EASILY!
Basically, what i'm trying to get here, is that this isn't your typical rpg game. In a positive and a negative way.
First, this game is awesome. It really is. It's story, its world, it's unique gameplay, it's characters, Papyrus being my favorite... it has everything an rpg needs to be an RPG
The story is of course essential to an RPG-type game, and it's strong in this game. It might not be as fleshed out as others are, but its strong. The world is very engaging and you want to know more about it as you go on. However, you don't get as much information from this world as you would want. After awhile, you want to know more about it, and you just don't get the info you want to make it more interesting and loveable. And as of course when its a story-driven game, it's pretty linear, so that's another setback to its engagement. Also, the story will get boring after awhile as well. Not terribly, but in a way that you will feel a bit unsatisfied.
Fortunately, the characters in this game are amazing. All of them feel unique and exciting, and some you will definitely love. Buuut, again, after some time, they get pretty old, jokes included. Not saying all of them would, opinion is an opinion of course, but I'm sure even you will get those vibes that you just dont want to hear his or hers talking, perhaps you even want to skip some dialoque. But, that isn't saying they are poorly executed. The character development is so good my brains we're filled with hopes and ideas like waterfalls.
Gameplay is definitely the most unique part in the whole game. The gameplay in Undertale is centered around talking and negotiating battles rather than fighting, with an option of fighting. These battles can be ended with 3 ways in total: Kill, spare or flee. Killing of course gives you gold and xp, but also can trigger either the neutral ending or genocide ending (which we will get to a in a few moments). Sparing is the hardest thing to do basically. In battles you can negotiate the enemy with talking, cheering, flirting, or even threatening. These of course are based on the enemy. You can achieve sparing or fleeing with doing some of these options. Either the enemy is influenced by some kind of hatred or sadness etc., you can respond to these emotions with these kind of options, but some are effective, and some are not. Then, when enemy is ready to end the battle, you can spare the enemy. Then you can also flee battles, which aren't that easy. You still have to do these things in order to leave a battle.At first, you get the hang of it, but it gets gradually harder and harder, and you even might have to look up ways to do these with some enemies.
Oh yeah, the fighting. Now the enemy attacks you usually with projectiles, that can induce a lot of damage. Some enemies are really easy, but some are hard as hell. How you respond to these projectiles is this little box on top of the option bars and below the enemy avatar, where you control a heart-looking object. This is your soul, and once a projectile hits it, you lose health (duh). How you fight back, is with this timing system. You have to hit the right spot in the right time with a straight line going side to side. If you hit the right spot, you deal a significant amount of damage to the enemy. A perfect hit might even kill enemies with one shot. This is a bit dissapointing for me atleast. I just wished they would've put more effort into fighting as much as in negotiating.
But then, theres the endings. And there's not just 2 endings, but 3. These endings can be triggered with some of the options in battles or befriending some of the characters. It's amazing to see how much devotion was put into making these kind of endings. 3 ways to end a great game. 3 ways to see the story come into a end. 3 ways to say goodbye in a satisfying fashion. (I dont really want to talk about the endings, cuz spoilers :P)
All in all, its a great game. I liked the majority of it, but towards halfway to the end, it became a bit dull and boring. Thats why, I'm recommending this to those who enjoy story-driven games, rather than full-action games.
7/10 Characters and Story (I would've given it a 6/10, but I loved the characters so much that I decided to give it a 7).
9/10 Gameplay and Endings (Same category because the gameplay influnced so much into the endings).
Overall rating: 8/10 ( Again, I would've given it a 7/10, but because of the sheer devotion to this game work put into developing the characters, I would gladly give it a 8/10).

Synopsis
Born in Austria in 1889, Adolf Hitler rose to power in German politics as leader of the National Socialist German Workers Party, also known as the Nazi Party. Hitler was chancellor of Germany from 1933 to 1945, and served as dictator from 1934 to 1945. His policies precipitated World War II and the Holocaust. Hitler committed suicide with wife Eva Braun on April 30, 1945, in his Berlin bunker.
Early Years
Dictator Adolf Hitler was born in Braunau am Inn, Austria, on April 20, 1889, and was the fourth of six children born to Alois Hitler and Klara Polzl. When Hitler was 3 years old, the family moved from Austria to Germany. As a child, Hitler clashed frequently with his father. Following the death of his younger brother, Edmund, in 1900, he became detached and introverted. His father did not approve of his interest in fine art rather than business. In addition to art, Hitler showed an early interest in German nationalism, rejecting the authority of Austria-Hungary. This nationalism would become the motivating force of Hitler's life.
Alois died suddenly in 1903. Two years later, Adolf's mother allowed her son to drop out of school. He moved to Vienna and worked as a casual laborer and a watercolor painter. Hitler applied to the Academy of Fine Arts twice, and was rejected both times. Out of money, he moved into a homeless shelter, where he remained for several years. Hitler later pointed to these years as the time when he first cultivated his anti-Semitism, though there is some debate about this account.
At the outbreak of World War I, Hitler applied to serve in the German army. He was accepted in August 1914, though he was still an Austrian citizen. Although he spent much of his time away from the front lines, Hitler was present at a number of significant battles and was wounded at the Somme. He was decorated for bravery, receiving the Iron Cross First Class and the Black Wound Badge.
3
GALLERY
3 Images
Hitler became embittered over the collapse of the war effort. The experience reinforced his passionate German patriotism, and he was shocked by Germany's surrender in 1918. Like other German nationalists, he believed that the German army had been betrayed by civilian leaders and Marxists. He found the Treaty of Versailles degrading, particularly the demilitarization of the Rhineland and the stipulation that Germany accept responsibility for starting the war.
After World War I, Hitler returned to Munich and continued to work for the military as an intelligence officer. While monitoring the activities of the German Workers’ Party (DAP), Hitler adopted many of the anti-Semitic, nationalist and anti-Marxist ideas of DAP founder Anton Drexler. Drexler invited Hitler to join the DAP, which he did in 1919.
To increase its appeal, the DAP changed its name to the Nationalsozialistische Deutsche Arbeiterpartei (NSDAP). Hitler personally designed the party banner, featuring a swastika in a white circle on a red background. Hitler soon gained notoriety for his vitriolic speeches against the Treaty of Versailles, rival politicians, Marxists and Jews. In 1921, Hitler replaced Drexler as NSDAP party chairman.
Hitler's vitriolic beer-hall speeches began attracting regular audiences. Early followers included army captain Ernst Rohm, the head of the Nazi paramilitary organization, the Sturmabteilung (SA), which protected meetings and frequently attacked political opponents.
On November 8, 1923, Hitler and the SA stormed a public meeting of 3,000 people at a large beer hall in Munich. Hitler announced that the national revolution had begun and declared the formation of a new government. After a short struggle including 20 deaths, the coup, known as the "Beer Hall Putsch," failed.
Hitler was arrested three days later and tried for high treason. He served a year in prison, during which time he dictated most of the first volume of Mein Kampf ("My Struggle") to his deputy, Rudolf Hess. The book laid out Hitler's plans for transforming German society into one based on race.
Rise to Power
The Great Depression in Germany provided a political opportunity for Hitler. Germans were ambivalent to the parliamentary republic and increasingly open to extremist options. In 1932, Hitler ran against Paul von Hindenburg for the presidency. Hitler came in second in both rounds of the election, garnering more than 35 percent of the vote in the final election. The election established Hitler as a strong force in German politics. Hindenburg reluctantly agreed to appoint Hitler as chancellor in order to promote political balance.
Hitler used his position as chancellor to form a de facto legal dictatorship. The Reichstag Fire Decree, announced after a suspicious fire at the Reichstag, suspended basic rights and allowed detention without trial. Hitler also engineered the passage of the Enabling Act, which gave his cabinet full legislative powers for a period of four years and allowed deviations from the constitution.
Having achieved full control over the legislative and executive branches of government, Hitler and his political allies embarked on a systematic suppression of the remaining political opposition. By the end of June, the other parties had been intimidated into disbanding. On July 14, 1933, Hitler's Nazi Party was declared the only legal political party in Germany.
Military opposition was also punished. The demands of the SA for more political and military power led to the Night of the Long Knives, which took place from June 30 to July 2, 1934. Ernst Röhm and other SA leaders, along with a number of Hitler's political enemies, were rounded up and shot.
The day before Hindenburg's death in August 1934, the cabinet had enacted a law abolishing the office of president and combining its powers with those of the chancellor. Hitler thus became head of state as well as head of government, and was formally named as leader and chancellor. As head of state, Hitler became supreme commander of the armed forces. He began to mobilize for war. Germany withdrew from the League of Nations, and Hitler announced a massive expansion of Germany’s armed forces.
The Nazi regime also included social reform measures. Hitler promoted anti-smoking campaigns across the country. These campaigns stemmed from Hitler's self-imposed dietary restrictions, which included abstinence from alcohol and meat. At dinners, Hitler sometimes told graphic stories about the slaughter of animals in an effort to shame his fellow diners. He encouraged all Germans to keep their bodies pure of any intoxicating or unclean substance.
A main Nazi concept was the notion of racial hygiene. New laws banned marriage between non-Jewish and Jewish Germans, and deprived "non-Aryans" of the benefits of German citizenship. Hitler's early eugenic policies targeted children with physical and developmental disabilities, and later authorized a euthanasia program for disabled adults.
The Holocaust was also conducted under the auspices of racial hygiene. Between 1939 and 1945, Nazis and their collaborators were responsible for the deaths of 11 million to 14 million people, including about 6 million Jews, representing two-thirds of the Jewish population in Europe. Deaths took place in concentration and extermination camps and through mass executions. Other persecuted groups included Poles, communists, homosexuals, Jehovah's Witnesses and trade unionists, among others. Hitler probably never visited the concentration camps and did not speak publicly about the killings.
World War II
In 1938Hitler, along with several other European leaders, signed the Munich Agreement. The treaty ceded the Sudetenland districts to Germany, reversing part of the Versailles Treaty. As a result of the summit, Hitler was named Time magazine's Man of the Year for 1938. This diplomatic win only whetted his appetite for a renewed German dominance. On September 1, Germany invaded Poland. In response, Britain and France declared war on Germany

A very overrated game.
That's basically my review in a nutshell. I really hate to give this a negative review, but lemme still talk about it honestly. After all, this is a debated thing, and I do want to share my honest opinion.
First things first: THIS IS NOT RECOMMENDED FOR THOSE WHO ARE BORED EASILY!
Basically, what i'm trying to get here, is that this isn't your typical rpg game. In a positive and a negative way.
First, this game is awesome. It really is. It's story, its world, it's unique gameplay, it's characters, Papyrus being my favorite... it has everything an rpg needs to be an RPG
The story is of course essential to an RPG-type game, and it's strong in this game. It might not be as fleshed out as others are, but its strong. The world is very engaging and you want to know more about it as you go on. However, you don't get as much information from this world as you would want. After awhile, you want to know more about it, and you just don't get the info you want to make it more interesting and loveable. And as of course when its a story-driven game, it's pretty linear, so that's another setback to its engagement. Also, the story will get boring after awhile as well. Not terribly, but in a way that you will feel a bit unsatisfied.
Fortunately, the characters in this game are amazing. All of them feel unique and exciting, and some you will definitely love. Buuut, again, after some time, they get pretty old, jokes included. Not saying all of them would, opinion is an opinion of course, but I'm sure even you will get those vibes that you just dont want to hear his or hers talking, perhaps you even want to skip some dialoque. But, that isn't saying they are poorly executed. The character development is so good my brains we're filled with hopes and ideas like waterfalls.
Gameplay is definitely the most unique part in the whole game. The gameplay in Undertale is centered around talking and negotiating battles rather than fighting, with an option of fighting. These battles can be ended with 3 ways in total: Kill, spare or flee. Killing of course gives you gold and xp, but also can trigger either the neutral ending or genocide ending (which we will get to a in a few moments). Sparing is the hardest thing to do basically. In battles you can negotiate the enemy with talking, cheering, flirting, or even threatening. These of course are based on the enemy. You can achieve sparing or fleeing with doing some of these options. Either the enemy is influenced by some kind of hatred or sadness etc., you can respond to these emotions with these kind of options, but some are effective, and some are not. Then, when enemy is ready to end the battle, you can spare the enemy. Then you can also flee battles, which aren't that easy. You still have to do these things in order to leave a battle.At first, you get the hang of it, but it gets gradually harder and harder, and you even might have to look up ways to do these with some enemies.
Oh yeah, the fighting. Now the enemy attacks you usually with projectiles, that can induce a lot of damage. Some enemies are really easy, but some are hard as hell. How you respond to these projectiles is this little box on top of the option bars and below the enemy avatar, where you control a heart-looking object. This is your soul, and once a projectile hits it, you lose health (duh). How you fight back, is with this timing system. You have to hit the right spot in the right time with a straight line going side to side. If you hit the right spot, you deal a significant amount of damage to the enemy. A perfect hit might even kill enemies with one shot. This is a bit dissapointing for me atleast. I just wished they would've put more effort into fighting as much as in negotiating.
But then, theres the endings. And there's not just 2 endings, but 3. These endings can be triggered with some of the options in battles or befriending some of the characters. It's amazing to see how much devotion was put into making these kind of endings. 3 ways to end a great game. 3 ways to see the story come into a end. 3 ways to say goodbye in a satisfying fashion. (I dont really want to talk about the endings, cuz spoilers :P)
All in all, its a great game. I liked the majority of it, but towards halfway to the end, it became a bit dull and boring. Thats why, I'm recommending this to those who enjoy story-driven games, rather than full-action games.
7/10 Characters and Story (I would've given it a 6/10, but I loved the characters so much that I decided to give it a 7).
9/10 Gameplay and Endings (Same category because the gameplay influnced so much into the endings).
Overall rating: 8/10 ( Again, I would've given it a 7/10, but because of the sheer devotion to this game work put into developing the characters, I would gladly give it a 8/10).

Okay, now that that's settled, let's get started.
Undertale is a 'friendly RPG where NO ONE has to die!' Yeaah. Sure. I'll get to that later.
It provides an excellent soundtrack, ranging from those that can pull at your heartstrings - like His Theme - to silly/fun ones - in themes such as Bonetrousle - to one that really get you pumped for battle, like Spear of Justice! With such a wonderful range of songs in the OST to choose from, I guarantee ('scuse spelling lmao) that you'll be listening for hours, if you enjoy the game!
If you DO join the game, however, I wouldn't exactly recommend getting too involved in the nastier side of the fanbase. In all honesty, this - and that GOD AWFUL BOSS FIGHT I'M STUCK ON [*raging intesifies*] - is the only downside of the game. Avoid misspelling the game - Ie. Undertail - and don't use keywords such as 'sin', unless, you know, you WANT to...
There's such a loveable cast in Undertale, ranging from: the lovely Goat Mama; the adorable, friendly flower *wink wonk*; the wacky Skele-duo; Alphy and Undyne (sitting in a tree, K-I-S-S-I-N-G.); and the L E G R O B O T. Not to mention, my personal favorite, the dark and not-at-all fluffy ASGORE! I'm sure that the characters in the game are one of the best parts.
The battle system in Undertale is a love letter to retero-style, bullet-hell RPGs. I think it's really smart how Toby builds up rules upon the fighting system and TOTALLY DOESN'T BREAK THEM A QUATER OF THE WAY THROUGH THE GAME. But, yeah, the whole way you battle in this gem of an RPG really hits you with some good ol' nostalgia.
Overall, I believe Undertale is an excellent game, and I highly reccommed it to you!

This game is a loot hunter's dream. You see a good gun and take it and test it on Pandora's residents just to find out an hour later that there is an even better gun waiting for you to shoot up some Hyperion Loaders which you then find a Rocket Launcher that's perfect to help you with that boss you are stuck on. I think you get the point.
The game is basicly a FPS Diablo. There are four Vault Hunters to choose from (6 with the DLC) and they are all different and fill different rolls. The Siren can be built as a support that can take an ability that allows her to revive downed allies. Her ability allows her to stun a target, allowing your team to take it down easily. The Assassian can be built as a sniper or a melee character that has the ability to go invisible. He is used to take out high priority targets without taking much damage. The Gunzerker is tanky and his special ability allows him to wield two guns and keep the lead coming.
The story is nothing to write home about but the funny characters that you meet along the way and the witty dialouge kept me enjoying every moment of the story. The antagonist is Handsome Jack, the sarcastic leader of Hyperion bent on stoping the Vault Hunters from reaching The Vault.
Now let's talk about the world of Pandora. Along the story you will go through all sorts of environments. There are tundras, grasslands, wrecked environments, urban environments, building interiors, etc etc... The loot that you find through out the game are all made by companies in the game.
The different gun companies all have unique attributes to their guns that make them different from the others. You can also find guns in different elements. These elements are Explosive, Incendiary, Shock, Corrosive, and Slag. The new one in this game is Slag which when an enemy is slagged, they take increased damage from other elemental and non-elemental guns.
I would recommend this game to people who like loot hunting, unique classes, shooting things in the face, cooperating with friends, whoring all the loot from your friends, and funny dialogue.

The only problem I had with the music is that quite often it would warn you that you're gonna be attacked, by playing action music before hand. The cinematics in Borderlands 2 are very good, they have comical bits and high detail, as well as being changed by what you did in the room (Eg, see corpses in the background), which is a nice touch. The story is fun, with lots of comedy and action with a fast but understandable pace. The idea is very fun and there is even a mode to repeat with higher leveled enemies for better loot, although the story doesn't change, which is slightly dissapointing. The controls are easy enough but feel smoother on a controler than a keyboard/mouse. The gameplay is fun, with chaos happening all around you and very small amount of time out of action. You will probably have your favourite character and play them the most, but all of them are very cool. You quite often find yourself laughing along or really enjoying a fight, there usually isn't a dull moment.
