i wrote a very silly review of this game shortly after it came out, but now that the anniversary has passed by i feel like writing a more serious one!
undertale is far and away one of my favorite games of all time. i went into the game blind (save for having played the demo) and i had an incredible time exploring the world and meeting all the interesting and quirky characters it had to offer. the ending(s) were incredibly emotional, and very few games have given me a stronger feeling of accomplishment than i felt while finishing this game's pacifist route. in essence, it's a very sweet game that makes you feel like your choices matter!
PROS:
- plenty of replay value, with several endings, variations on those endings, and lots of hidden content that you're unlikely to find in just one playthrough, despite its shortness. the game will reference even your most insignificant choices more than you expect!
- pretty, well-designed areas and characters with a simple but appealing style
- all the monsters you'll encounter in the game have lots of personality, and each has their own unique battle style. there are multiple ways to interact with and pacify them during combat, making battles interesting and fun. non-boss monster encounters happen randomly much like in pokemon games, but because the game is short this mechanic never felt like it had overstayed its welcome when i played it (unlike in pokemon where i inevitably resort to using repels because i'm tired of getting attacked every five seconds)
- awesome music! i highly suggest buying it with the soundtrack if you're into that sorta thing, it's real good. each area's music suits its aesthetic extremely well, and you may find yourself lingering in a place for several minutes just to listen to it. the music definitely makes the game what it is.
- puzzles that are fun and interesting but not too difficult to get through (excluding the infamous piano puzzle which is optional anyway)
- it's a game where you can be friends with everyone! when playing rpgs i often feel sad that i can't make friends with all the cool monsters i encounter, but with this game that is not a problem. they are all potential friends, and it is wonderful.
- Good Joke's
CONS:
- its overwhelming popularity and rather overzealous fandom can be pretty offputting - i admit that i lost some interest in the game after being bombarded with fan content for an extended period of time, though thankfully i had already played it in full before this happened. it's true that the game has the most emotional impact when you go into it blind, but with the game's prevalence this is now difficult to accomplish. that's fine, though! even if you've been spoiled for some stuff, you should still try out the game if you have any interest in it - i'm sure you'll still have fun. try not to pay attention to the hype and form your own opinions about it as you play!
- the game remembers your previous playthroughs and will sometimes reference them, which can be unsettling to some and makes it difficult to replay at times. fair warning that if you decide to do the "kill everybody" route and fully complete it, it will taint any other playthroughs you attempt afterwards. however, if you don't beat the final boss in that route you can still safely reset the game and play a more pacifistic run with no bad consequences.
- some of the solutions to boss battles can be difficult to figure out, making you use mechanics that you may have otherwise ignored in the game and may not realize are the only way to get a peaceful solution

Oh Borderlands 2 your sarcasim and crap ton of weapons has kept me playing on my PS3 for 90 hours and my computer 40 hours. This Game in just 1 word, GUNS and on the topic of GUNS this game a has geometric craptonne of guns some people go for the best they can find but rascals like me farm for the Legendaries,Seraphs AND Pearlescents. This game took me around 40 hours to complete but I stuffed around and did sidequests and other stuff along the way so you could probably finish it a lot quicker I'm also not that good so that's also probably why it took so long. But I didn't even mention the 6 playable characters or Vault Hunters. They are all very unique so I'll go over my favourites in short detail. The Siren is a character that controls the field of battle she uses her action skill Phaselock to trap enemies in a big purple ball thing. She has amazing skills (mostly found in the motion tree) like Subsequence which after you have killed an enemy in Phaselock it moves to another target or the final skill of the Cataclysim tree Ruin which causes enemies to get slagged, zapped, corroded and lit on fire while in your Phaselock, these 2 skills paired up with converge (suck nearby enemies in into the Phaselock) can be a deadly combination of skills. She is probably my 2nd favourite. My favourite vault hunter is the Assasin, Zer0. He is a stealthy warrior and with the action skill and skill trees this shows through. Zer0 has 3 skill trees (obviously) Sniping, Cunning and Bloodshed. So basically you can be a Sniper a Ninja or a Samurai. My favourite skill tree is the Cunning skill tree (Ninja skill tree) It revolves heavily around his action skill Deception. Deception is when you lay out a decoy of yourself while you become invisible. The enemies can not see you while you're in Deception so they will shoot your decoy. You become visible after you shoot an enemy or the 5 second timer on your Deception runs out. Anyhow back to the skill tree the middle skill of cunning is really amazing it is called Death Mark. After you stab or melee an enemy they will have a little Zero above their head notifying you that you've marked them. If you mark a target then all damage is 20% stronger to that enemy. The final skill of Cunning is Death Bl0ss0m which when you're in Deception if you press F on your keyboard you throw a handfull of Kunai (Little Sharp Knifes). This does so much damage it's insane but one of the best parts of this skill is that doesn't stop your Deception and it can apply Death Mark. Which means that if you don't want to get up close and stab them to get that Death Mark you can throw your Kunai instead. Borderlands 2 is a great game and I highly recommend it to anyone who is a fan of FPS or Shoot and Loot games.(By the way my favourite weapon is the Pitchfork sniper rifle)

Rust in my humble opinion is the best fps survival game out there! It has come a long way since its early beginnings and has been transformed into a beautiful experience. The switch from legacy Rust was absolutely the right decision, and as the hacks and exploits have been fixed or removed, more weapons and crafting added and the experience point experiment coming full circle, the game is quickly nearing completion.
There are still a few things that I hear people whine about:
1. The community is a bunch of KOS freaks.
A. You play serious PVP and that's what it's all about - also everyone goes through the same thing.
B. How about play some PVE first?
C. There are also plenty of no KOS servers so try a bit harder and go find one...
D. I have made many friends on RUST from all over the country (and the Great White North too)
2. The changes that have been made ruined the game:
A. Game play has dramatically improved.
B. Explioits and hacks are being cleaned up so the cheating♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥bags have to play by the rules.
C. The component system is more realistic than any other "crafting" system out there.
(using a pipe, some gears and a gun receiver is still a bit far-fetched but better than crafting magic!!!)
D. Radiation is plausible in post-apocalyptic scenarios and although a drag it does add to the gameplay.
(Plus if you don't like it there are plenty of non-radioactive servers.
E. The overall look / feel / sound has been polished by developers that clearly understand this game genre.
This is one of those games that has tons of replay-abilty for years to come. I trust the developers and applaud them for what they have created, and excited to see where it goes from here!

UNDERTALE.
Where do I start? (DONT WORRY THIS IS SPOILER FREE =) )
This game went from a regular kickstarter-backed RPG to one of the greatest gaming experiences I have ever had. And i think 30% of EVERYBODY ON YOUTUBE AGREES.
Dont be fooled by the simple 8-bit art style, this game is more story-driven than even Ocarina of Time and Final Fantasy 7 onwards. This game lets you KNOW when you mess up, and plays at your gamer instincts like gaining EXP, resetting, and even WANTING TO PLAY THE GAME TWICE. But that is what amkesit glorious (The FEEEEEELS).
This is one of the only game i have ever seen that lets you, you know, NOT BE A MURDEROUS JERK. This game rewards you for taking the harder and less obvious routes that you actually need to be A GOOD PERSON TO THE CHARACTERS or work your butt off to kill EVERYONE (if youre that kind of person). just killing everyone you encounter is something the game...dislikes (is that the right word?) and doesnt give a good ending, but being a pacifist (even to the bosses) gives you the most satisfying ending to a game i have probably ever seen and ever will see, with a battle that is ABSOLUTELY BRILLIANT.
I am not being overexcited, this game is a true work of art. loveable characters, the ability to spare, bullet hell/rpg elements, action, mystery, lots of spoilers and a BRILLIANT SOUNDTRACK. If you need proof of the soundtracks brilliance, google (of spotify, or Itunes, etc.) the soundtrack. youll thank me later.
The final thing i have to say is GO. IN. BLIND. UNDERTALE is best experienced without prior knowledge (like a spoiler free review ;) ), so don't youtube it, dont wikipedia it, dont google it, just buy this game (its a measly 10 bucks) and play it. Even if you hate the genre (like i DID), this game is something you wont regret. UNDERTALE is probably the best $10 i have ever spent, and I think this game is better than most $60-70 regular games. This game KNOWS when you save, what youve done before in the game (even if you reset or quit without saving. spooky) and the characters are 4th wall-breaking, hilarious, diverse and can all be befrended and spared.
PLAY THIS GAME. I HAVE NEVER RECCOMMENDED A GAME HIGHER AND NEVER WILL.

Undertale. Where do I begin? I can't formulate into words how good of a game this is. I have been playing for almost a year and the story gets me everytime.
I remember back when I first got the game. I had originally watched a playthrough of the Ruins, so I went into the game knowing a little of what to expect. That, I think, was my only regret. After I got through the Ruins, I thought, being a young developer, anyone could develop the game. The graphics were simple, the mechanics were pretty straightforward, and concept was just boring. That was before I left the Ruins.
Afterwards, I was a little less certain about my previous notion, but I still thought the game simple. After I had finished a pacifist run, my world was turned upside-down. I could never make a game like this; no one could.
Toby Fox is a genius. Remember the expression "don't judge a book by its cover"? That applies to Undertale too. On the surface, it looks like one of those retro games modeled after Pokemon with a unique fighting system. Once you peel back the layers, the game gets a lot more complicated. Undertale is a game that subtly drives you towards getting a "happy" ending, while a character WHO KNOWS THAT HE LIVES IN A GAME drives you to do the exact opposite. Do you become a good-doer who makes friends with everyone, or someone who tears apart the world, murdering everyone in their path? It is personal choice that drives the game. Undertale doesn't choose how the story will progress, like other RPGs. Instead, you choose what to do, and the game goes along with you, with no way to go back.
Undertale isn't anything like a modern game. These games rely on their graphics, reputation, and repetitive tasks ingame to get audiences attention. They run on a budget of tens of millions of dollars and still don't come CLOSE to Undertale, which was made on donations from people who wanted the game to be made. Undertale helps show that you don't need fancy graphics for a game to be popular; instead, what matters most is the characters and the storyline that are the core of the game.
The companies of the big games, whose franchises stretch across 5 or 6 titles asked the question, "What does the public want?" Toby Fox asked the question, "What does the public NEED?" They didn't need another franchise game. They needed a game that told a story, that was driven by the gamer, that gave a lesson to everyone. They needed a game that catered to everyone, from hardcore gamers to non-gamers. They needed a game that could take a step back and take a look at what happens if a character is gone forever. Erased. Forgotten. What happens then?
Undertale taught us all a lesson: Your choices matter. It taught us that people have different layers, that the "monsters" in our world are just like us, with dreams and ambitions. It gave us a way to reflect on why we still play video games. What is the point of a video game? Is it just to entertain? Or should it teach? Video games should be art, a specially, handcrafted piece of art that leaves a mark on each and every gamer. Undertale does that.
Undertale is not just a game. It's a story. It's a piece of art. It's a metaphor of the modern world and how we are all alike in our beliefs and choices. It's a journey. But it isn't a journey of the character making their way out of the underground. It is a journey through our choices, how one tiny instance like a question could turn the world upside down.
Undertale turns our own world upside down. I can never look at video games the same way.
Enjoy Undertale, and above all:
STAY DETERMINED...
-Jake
P.S. I hope my tears from writing this don't mess up my keyboard.

UNDERTALE.
Where do I start? (DONT WORRY THIS IS SPOILER FREE =) )
This game went from a regular kickstarter-backed RPG to one of the greatest gaming experiences I have ever had. And i think 30% of EVERYBODY ON YOUTUBE AGREES.
Dont be fooled by the simple 8-bit art style, this game is more story-driven than even Ocarina of Time and Final Fantasy 7 onwards. This game lets you KNOW when you mess up, and plays at your gamer instincts like gaining EXP, resetting, and even WANTING TO PLAY THE GAME TWICE. But that is what amkesit glorious (The FEEEEEELS).
This is one of the only game i have ever seen that lets you, you know, NOT BE A MURDEROUS JERK. This game rewards you for taking the harder and less obvious routes that you actually need to be A GOOD PERSON TO THE CHARACTERS or work your butt off to kill EVERYONE (if youre that kind of person). just killing everyone you encounter is something the game...dislikes (is that the right word?) and doesnt give a good ending, but being a pacifist (even to the bosses) gives you the most satisfying ending to a game i have probably ever seen and ever will see, with a battle that is ABSOLUTELY BRILLIANT.
I am not being overexcited, this game is a true work of art. loveable characters, the ability to spare, bullet hell/rpg elements, action, mystery, lots of spoilers and a BRILLIANT SOUNDTRACK. If you need proof of the soundtracks brilliance, google (of spotify, or Itunes, etc.) the soundtrack. youll thank me later.
The final thing i have to say is GO. IN. BLIND. UNDERTALE is best experienced without prior knowledge (like a spoiler free review ;) ), so don't youtube it, dont wikipedia it, dont google it, just buy this game (its a measly 10 bucks) and play it. Even if you hate the genre (like i DID), this game is something you wont regret. UNDERTALE is probably the best $10 i have ever spent, and I think this game is better than most $60-70 regular games. This game KNOWS when you save, what youve done before in the game (even if you reset or quit without saving. spooky) and the characters are 4th wall-breaking, hilarious, diverse and can all be befrended and spared.
PLAY THIS GAME. I HAVE NEVER RECCOMMENDED A GAME HIGHER AND NEVER WILL.

I played this a while back but I figure I'll leave a postive review because I do think highly of the game.  The thing is, Toby Fox is right.  He made a game that's probably a 7 or 8.  The reason it has the popularity it does isn't because of particularly well-written characters or a highly compelling story, or even a few experimental ideas.  No, UNDERTALE is great because of what it is compared to everything else around it.  The ideas it has are pretty small, the GAME is pretty small, and yet those flourishes stand out amongst the frankly grey and brown world of the games that surround it.
Most people write reviews like this for the game and that should be telling.  It's a mediocre niche-RPG with more heart than any game you've ever played and it might just challenge not just how you look at games, but the world around you.  Personally I came to regret the monsters I killed as I realized it's less a world of monsters attacking me and more a case of me invading their homes.  I wanted those deaths to disappear from my record, but they never did.  And I completed the game with an interesting feeling: guilt.  I didn't know!  It wasn't on purpose!  Yet, why should anyone forgive me?  Some did, others did not.  What an interesting, interesting, interesting game.
That's why people recommend it, that's what makes it fun and if nothing else, when you finish UNDERTALE you will have thoughts on it and that's why it deserves a recommendation.

Before I do a big long pros and cons list, just a quick note. This game makes you consider what you're doing as a player. When you kill someone, you as a player have murdered someone. Sure you can go back to a previous save and they'll be there, but you are now a murderer. The game knows that, and it tells you that it knows. The game works like this in other ways too, but it is something not done in any other game I know of and I believe this game is worth the purchase for this ingenious design alone.
Pros:
Incredible storyline, whether you like storylines in games or not (personally I do not) this really is a gem that you can appreciate.
Atmosphere, truly makes you feel all types of emotions through incredible soundtracks, strong characters, and powerful backgrounds.
Combat, if you enjoy bullet hell style fights then it's an added bonus, if you don't then it in no way takes away from the game experience.
Decisions, I feel like everything I do in this game means something and has a real impact on what goes on, probably because it does.
Characters, not much to say here apart from each character is wonderous, fully flushed, and thoroughly intruiging.
Cons:
Repetitive, The last hour of gameplay to me feels like the same thing over and over again, worth it for the ending but it does start to feel like lazy game design.
Repetitive, I've met this same boss like three times now... Is this a glitch?
Repetitive, Look I'm sure there's a point to this but why are you saying the same speech for like the billionth time?
Repetitive, HOLY F*CKING SH*T IF I HAVE TO WALK THROUGH THIS SAME F*CKING HALLWAY ONE MORE D*MN TIME!
This game tries so hard to be "deep" by walking you through the same places over again after revealing more information that it becomes dull and repetitive, especially in the last 1-2 hours.
All in all, incredible game. I recommend.

I've been playing Rust for about 3 years now, I started with Legacy and now I'm on the current iteration. The game has a lot of potential, however the creator of the game, Garry Newman, is an alcoholic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and literally tells his playerbase to stop playing this game. It has been in Alpha forever, with no Beta release in sight. You can spend money on skins though!
The community is pretty toxic, I have made a few friends along the way, but the majority of players are the kind that get off on griefing others. Base sabotaging, item despawning, naked killing, racist/homophobic trash talking, and just general cancerous attitudes are prevalent. You have to be in a group to get anything done, otherwise you will die from pvp or raiding. Solo players be ♥♥♥♥ed as far as Garry is concerned.
Animals, they run through walls, into boulders, into your base, and they can hit you from 15 feet away. They literally programmed the A.I. to detect when they are in a headshot crosshair and to move the opposite way. You can make a horse do the friggan two step with a bolt action rifle from a mile away. Bears and wolves somehow know to avoid running directly at you when you have a gun, but if you are a naked with a spear they will maul you from out of nowhere.
The game development is fragmented as hell, with Garry and his team seemingly ignoring most players requests and releasing whatever the hell they feel is important at the time. Weekly Dev notes include a lot of "we did this obscure computer programming to fix something that we ♥♥♥♥ed up so that we can put something we know you don't want into the game a year from now", and "we know you won't like it, but that's tough♥♥♥♥♥♥quot;. I'm talking about skins and the component system, which requires you to bang on barrels for hours. That is no exaggeration, you can spend HOURS banging barrels, just to find a scrap you need to make a certain weapon.
I've had a lot of fun with Rust and I've always hoped it would keep improving, I feel like I was the victim of a very long, cruel joke.

In the end, Undertale is a true gem in the increasingly mediocre field of Indie games populating the Steam platform. It actually even manages to stand on its own among more traditional RPGs & JRPGs with its unique characters, humor, branching story, interesting gameplay, outstanding music, and unapologetic breaking of the 4th wall (and our hearts). It’s certainly not a game for everyone, and is more likely to impress people that get a sense of nostalgia for the retro-gaming era than younger audiences with little or no personal connection to the games that Undertale lovingly emulates.
More than anything however, this game stands above any others in how it affected me on a personal level. The Normal and Pacifist paths/endings pulled at my emotions, made me laugh, brought me to seething rage, and made me cry. It brought me to love the characters that you can befriend along the journey in a way that, the mere thought of replaying the game to attempt the “Genocide” mode made me feel sick. The monsters and their underground world became more than just pixels and data. They became beloved friends in the same way characters in a great book can feel real to you… and their pain can feel like your own.

Unlike many sequels, I believe that Borderlands 2 is a faithful follow-up to the first installment. The feel of the game is etremely close to the first one, and the gameplay has a similar reflective qualities of the original. The combat remains engaging and enjoyable, and the (slightly) different classes along with those added by the many DLC options have kept it fresh, while still remaining true to the spirit of the game. Similarily, the environment of Pandora in Borderlands 2 is reminscent of its predecessor but provides the player with new areas to explore and many new enemies to combat, along with lots of the more memorable adversaries that were seen also in Borderlands. The story, too, flows well from the primary to the secondary. I loved the fact that the four classes/player characters from the first one were npcs in Borderlands two, due to the continuity and immersion that they add to the second game if you've played through the first one.
However, I suppose I do have some issues with the game. As I'm not the greatest at first person games that involve shooting (it felt wrong straight-up calling Borderlands an FPS), and as Borderlands 2 does not provide a difficulty level slider besides advancing from one playthrough to the next, I find myself having trouble not dying repeatedly  at some parts of the game, even with considerable grinding and side-questing. The other problem I've had is odd behavior of some dropped items, but I won't get into seeing as I don't want to criticize programming directly, as I know next-to-nothing about it.
Overall, Borderlands 2 is a great game, and deserves to be played by whoever is into this sort of thing. The couple problems I have had are not really anything to squak about, and the positives outweigh the negative.
Good day, Steam users.

Generally, im not a shooter type of guy but there are some exceptions to that rule. Borderlands 2 is one such exception. Rather than being a disembodied pair of arms holding a gun fighting folks that re more or less the same thing. Amusing but repetitive and such games tend to barely enough of a single player mode to say it's there. Fun for some, but not worth my dollar. Any game that wants you to spend money should provide a healthy single player experience. This it what brings me to Borderlands 2 here, having skipped the first I cannot speak for it, but 2 here Im absolutely loving. You aren't just on a map fighting racist ten year olds, you're in a large sprawling world which in a way reminds me of the old west with an untamed chaotic feel. Add to that a very colorful, and more importantly memorable cast of NPCs, an actual story, a ton of guns with a ton of effects and variations and many memorable moments and you have here a game that I would gladly buy, and buy it I did. There is a multiplayer component of course, but the game can be enjoyed solo just fine as well. Personally I recomend the GOTY edition as you get a ton of content from the get go.
Overall I recomend the game, whether you are a lone wanderer or have some friends to form a band of gun toting looters you will be in for a good time that you will have plenty to talk about.

Rust is probably one of my top few favorite games of all time. It's a survival crafting/building game filled with replayability as about every 1-2 weeks there is a new update with quite a bit of content worked into it. Every day you will meet someone new in the community of Rust, sometimes it can be quite cruel and filled with death and horror as your hard worked resources are lost to a group of men with weapons better then your own, but the next day you will meet a friendly man who feels pity for you and gladly gives you tools and invites you into his base. Rust is also a game that induces anger, and lot's of it. You will probably never play a game that gives you more of a doomed/enraged feeling then Rust. You will be inside your base crafting and hear multiple footsteps right outside your base, and then the footsteps stop and are replaced with the sound of c4 slapping onto your wall and beeping until it's inevitable explosion which will allow these people inside of your base. Though if you work hard enough you can impose this horrible dreadful feeling on others and reap the benefits. So from my review you can probably tell that Rust is best played with friends as being alone in this world is just too painstakingly hard. In the end Rust has it's ups and downs and some patches of the game are better than others, but overall I highly reccomend the game as it brings upon hours and hours of excitement and adrenaline.

In the end, Undertale is a true gem in the increasingly mediocre field of Indie games populating the Steam platform. It actually even manages to stand on its own among more traditional RPGs & JRPGs with its unique characters, humor, branching story, interesting gameplay, outstanding music, and unapologetic breaking of the 4th wall (and our hearts). It’s certainly not a game for everyone, and is more likely to impress people that get a sense of nostalgia for the retro-gaming era than younger audiences with little or no personal connection to the games that Undertale lovingly emulates.
More than anything however, this game stands above any others in how it affected me on a personal level. The Normal and Pacifist paths/endings pulled at my emotions, made me laugh, brought me to seething rage, and made me cry. It brought me to love the characters that you can befriend along the journey in a way that, the mere thought of replaying the game to attempt the “Genocide” mode made me feel sick. The monsters and their underground world became more than just pixels and data. They became beloved friends in the same way characters in a great book can feel real to you… and their pain can feel like your own.

Rust is probably one of my top few favorite games of all time. It's a survival crafting/building game filled with replayability as about every 1-2 weeks there is a new update with quite a bit of content worked into it. Every day you will meet someone new in the community of Rust, sometimes it can be quite cruel and filled with death and horror as your hard worked resources are lost to a group of men with weapons better then your own, but the next day you will meet a friendly man who feels pity for you and gladly gives you tools and invites you into his base. Rust is also a game that induces anger, and lot's of it. You will probably never play a game that gives you more of a doomed/enraged feeling then Rust. You will be inside your base crafting and hear multiple footsteps right outside your base, and then the footsteps stop and are replaced with the sound of c4 slapping onto your wall and beeping until it's inevitable explosion which will allow these people inside of your base. Though if you work hard enough you can impose this horrible dreadful feeling on others and reap the benefits. So from my review you can probably tell that Rust is best played with friends as being alone in this world is just too painstakingly hard. In the end Rust has it's ups and downs and some patches of the game are better than others, but overall I highly reccomend the game as it brings upon hours and hours of excitement and adrenaline.

Rust is a survival game created by Facepunch Studios. Inspired by games like DayZ, Minecraft and Stalker – Rust aims to create a hostile environment in which emergent gameplay can flourish. The aim of the game is to survive. To do this the player should gather resources. Hitting a tree with a rock will give you wood, hitting a rock with a rock will give you rock and ore. You can then craft a hatchet from the wood and rock, allowing you to gather faster. You can go out and hunt a variety of wildlife such as boars, chickens, rabbits, bears, wolves and deer. Once you have killed an animal you can butcher it to gather its meat and skin. You can craft a fire using wood and cook the meat inside the fire. Then you can eat. You face two major dangers in game. Rust is a multiplayer game, so there will be other players trying to survive in the same way that you are. Unfortunately for you they can find you, kill you and take your stuff. Fortunately for you – you can kill them and take their stuff. Or maybe you can make friends and help each other survive. Rust’s world is harsh – so you might need to make friends to survive. The environment is not kind. Bears and wolves will chase and kill you. Falling from a height will kill you. Being exposed to radiation for an extended period will kill you. Starving will kill you. Being cold will kill you.

Generally, im not a shooter type of guy but there are some exceptions to that rule. Borderlands 2 is one such exception. Rather than being a disembodied pair of arms holding a gun fighting folks that re more or less the same thing. Amusing but repetitive and such games tend to barely enough of a single player mode to say it's there. Fun for some, but not worth my dollar. Any game that wants you to spend money should provide a healthy single player experience. This it what brings me to Borderlands 2 here, having skipped the first I cannot speak for it, but 2 here Im absolutely loving. You aren't just on a map fighting racist ten year olds, you're in a large sprawling world which in a way reminds me of the old west with an untamed chaotic feel. Add to that a very colorful, and more importantly memorable cast of NPCs, an actual story, a ton of guns with a ton of effects and variations and many memorable moments and you have here a game that I would gladly buy, and buy it I did. There is a multiplayer component of course, but the game can be enjoyed solo just fine as well. Personally I recomend the GOTY edition as you get a ton of content from the get go.
Overall I recomend the game, whether you are a lone wanderer or have some friends to form a band of gun toting looters you will be in for a good time that you will have plenty to talk about.

I have never regret reading wikis or guides about a game so much. For so many games, "spoilers" just meant playing the game right, once. For this game though, "spoilers" truly
spoiling the game for you. I enjoyed the game immensely, but can only imagine what other experiences I could have gotten if I had only just jumped in and played the game as is, true to my beliefs...
Undertale doesn't have outstanding graphics, nor exciting combat, nor will it make you commit hundreds of hours into it. Its world is small, some of its gameplay tedious and annoying, and there's barely any character customisation options. But what Undertale is... it is an intellectual, emotional, and roller-coaster of a journey, that challenges accepted norms and leads players into re-examining themselves deeply. I will return to this game again once I've forgotten about it enough, which will be... hard.
Oh, and the soundtrack. The soundtrack is amazing.

Pretty much all my hours were spent on the legacy version of Rust. I got my 20$ worth out of it, but having the game I loved taken away and replaced by what I find to be significantly inferior does leave a bitter taste in my mouth.
Legacy Rust had its problems but would still be played to this day had you dedicated proper anti-hack support to the game and fixed some of the few outstanding bugs. It was perfect in its simplicity and people liked it for this reason. The shooting was fun and rewarding, base design wasn't overly complex but had enough to it to try and throw raiders for a loop. Raiding was fun whether the victims were online or not. There wasn't a monstrous list of items to craft, there was just enough.
The map could have also been fleshed out with generic stuff, or just slice off the 75% empty part of the island if need be to force player interaction.
New Rust has too large of a map, the item list over inflated and somehow they made the game even more of a grind than it was on Legacy. If you don't have a massive, very active group you are just going to get raided out of the game by well, a massive active group. In Legacy you could make do with 3 people who were semi active, or even just one super active person with two of his friends. The raiding in new Rust is very extreme, at least it was last time I played. You can literally demolish someone's entire base if you c4 correctly which reaffirms how super active your group needs to be in order to come back from a raid mid-wipe. In Legacy if you were raided it was a matter of replacing a few broken walls and doors as your foundations could not be destroyed, bringing down the entire structure.
Griefing in new Rust is extreme thanks to the tool cabinet system, so if you don't have your base wiped out you might just come back and not be able to build anything near it or use any of it anymore because some♥♥♥♥♥♥shoved a cabinet behind a bunch of walls that you won't be able to get to without c4 and left. They have no intention of using your base, just ensuring that you won't be able to either.
Honestly if you made the appropriate and very little amount of effort to fix up Legacy and released it you'd see a resurgence in the player base because it was quite frankly the better game, just not the supported one. I know people/devs will just say "Well more people were played new Rust than old so new must be better!" and that is simply not true. People didn't switch purely because New Rust was better. They switched because after you started development on new rust the number of hackers on Legacy surged and eventually it became impossible to continue playing. There were still boatloads of people on Legacy holding out, hoping at the very least we'd get the deserved anti-cheat that the game needed so we could continue playing it but eventually the hackers beat everyone out.
I got my 20$ worth so in that sense I am happy but can safely say this is the last early access project I ever contribute to under this development team. I understand in going into an early access things are subject to change but you very much sold people one game and then created a different one, which in my opinion is completely different. New rust and Legacy have similar concepts but are two very very different games and I paid for the latter.

Rust is a survival game created by Facepunch Studios. Inspired by games like DayZ, Minecraft and Stalker – Rust aims to create a hostile environment in which emergent gameplay can flourish. The aim of the game is to survive. To do this the player should gather resources. Hitting a tree with a rock will give you wood, hitting a rock with a rock will give you rock and ore. You can then craft a hatchet from the wood and rock, allowing you to gather faster. You can go out and hunt a variety of wildlife such as boars, chickens, rabbits, bears, wolves and deer. Once you have killed an animal you can butcher it to gather its meat and skin. You can craft a fire using wood and cook the meat inside the fire. Then you can eat. You face two major dangers in game. Rust is a multiplayer game, so there will be other players trying to survive in the same way that you are. Unfortunately for you they can find you, kill you and take your stuff. Fortunately for you – you can kill them and take their stuff. Or maybe you can make friends and help each other survive. Rust’s world is harsh – so you might need to make friends to survive. The environment is not kind. Bears and wolves will chase and kill you. Falling from a height will kill you. Being exposed to radiation for an extended period will kill you. Starving will kill you. Being cold will kill you.

TL;DR: Great game, mainly story-based. fantastic characters. Requires a lot of patience for some areas of the game. Some replay value, definitely worth the $10. Try to avoid the fanbase though.
LONG VERSION:
Undertale is an excellent game. It's charming, it's unique, and it's got a fascinating universe with likeable characters (with a few intentional exceptions). It takes a break from the traditional "these enemies are in your way. remove with extreme prejudice" approach to combat that you'll see in most turn-based RPG-ish games.
Speaking of combat, i'm not usually one for turn-based games just because you'd normally have to take at least a few hits in any fight and pray to the RNG that things go your way. Undertale does away with this by letting you score critical hits or dodge enemy attacks entirely if you've got your positioning and timing right. It's not huge, but it certainly adds character.
The difficulty of the game seems to have borrowed a bit from dark souls, especially in the later boss fights, in that they can be mercilessly difficult until you've learned all of an enemy's moves and can dodge them all reliably, at which point they can't do a single point of damage to you. Keep in mind, though, that doing such a thing can take a while. For example, it just took me four hours to finally beat the last, hardest boss, a feat that only takes about 7 minutes from start to finish.
There isn't a huge amount of story. Essentially, you are "faceless child with big head esq." who fell down a hole while out exploring one day and now you have to get out of said hole, and there's a race of nonhumans down here who would also like to get out of the hole.
Mind you, the lore of the game is intriguing and it's really the characters and settings that make the game. The locations are all distinct from each other and each carry their own atmosphere and characters to interact with.
The gameplay outside of combat is just the right amount of interesting so that combat doesn't necessarily feel like a chore (unless you make it your mission to grind every enemy in the area) and that it doesn't feel like the overworld is just a place you travel around to get to more bossfights. Progress is usually inhibited by puzzles that are just easy enough so you don't spend fifteen minutes on a single one but just hard enough that they're more than just things that slow your progress to the next area.
The game offers different story routes depending on how you approach monsters in the game. There's one good, a whole lot of neutral (that tweak a dialogue line here or there between them and that's pretty well it) and one evil. It's recommended that one play the good and evil endings at least, which are the second hardest and the hardest routes to play, respectively, but offer the best in terms of storytelling and background lore told to the player. The average game takes about 2-3 hours to finish, but will always take much longer than that unless you've had a lot of experience with japanese bullet hell-style shooters. While i didn't get a huge amount of time out of the game for what i paid, a lot of those hours were thoroughly enjoyed and i'd take them over 20 hours spent in almost any other game.
Long story short, if you've got a spare $10 ($5 on sale), pick up this game. it's well worth it.

Legacy? Thumbs up. Now? Thumbs down. The community is extremely terrible (yes another person saying it, but you have to admit, this is an online-only multiplayer survival game, the community is a big component of it). If you can't get past the crap community, bring your friends with the best aim, and/or join a PvE (or almost empty) server. Nothing fills the bloodlust of the average Rust player like seeing a naked body flail towards the ground. Lots of servers require a large team, moving to where no one else is, and becoming KoS yourself. Its a really bad way to act towards the new entrys, and if the game hadn't have had a large fanbase before the push for new Rust I'm pretty sure the community would've completely sank this game. I've had way more fun times playing Legacy (which had way less content in every way) and the players were a huge part of it. Blasting music to people, having normal conversations with others I don't group with, fighting giant KoS clans on servers, none of that is anything I can replicate anymore. If you can, good for you.
As for gameplay, again, its tough to actually get started solo unless you are very careful about what you do. Especially on servers where nights are very short. Large groups prosper, and you will have a higher chance of survival if you join a freshly wiped, populated server. That, or join a server that has low population for the moment. In my experience building a base as fast as you can is a good way to get settled, along with slowly getting supplies over time. Don't try to rush it, or you might regret it. The helicopter adds a rather strange element to the game, as everything is kind of "Mad Max-esqe" and the helicopter looks seemingly new, but its forgivable. I'm honestly surprised the arm textures are all you can see on your character considering you can hold Alt to look around, similar to DayZ, except there you can see your whole body. The animations for some things don't transition smoothly (hitting trees/rocks multiple times on your left arm, for instance). Steam ID randomizing your character is an interesting choice, certainly better than things like ARK where you can just go full retard with your player model. As for raiding, explosives are always your friend, so make sure you yourself are prepared before you try to raid someone who may be way better off than you are. I haven't been through much else in new Rust, only about 1/16th of my playtime is with it.
There are no real issues I have seen with servers, unless it was just a server owner problem, not an entire Rust problem. Joining a very high population server can be dangerous because there can be multiple people that could spawn right on top of you, along with KoS players being nearby. Again, play recently wiped, decently populated servers for an optimal experience. I also have not went into any modded servers or anything like it. I have, however, played on RP Medieval servers, and even when there is a bannable offense for KoS without RPing the situation (not anything much, you can literally just say "gimme your things" and if they don't cooperate within 1 second, fire away), people still KoS normally anyways.
The community that the devs show us seems to be a very few and far between instance of the actual Rust community. I check the community updates every once in a while, then it sparks my interest to play, then I immediately regret that decision upon remembering that the community is nowhere near what they are shown as on the website.
I'll give it proper credit, though. I have yet to see Facepunch run off with our money the way people like Jig did with The Stomping Land. Honestly considering that most Legacy Rust servers are cracked, it wouldn't even be that bad of an idea to release Legacy for free on the Rust website. It could be a deal similar to Minecraft Classic; nowhere like the game it is now, but still a free experience for those who want to really play it.

Undertale is an emotional and inspiring game that makes you feel like you are genuinely part of the world it takes place in. Its an incredibly detailed game with so many dialogue options that you can play through it several times and still not have seen all of it. Its incredibly unique from other RPGs, and it has more character depth than a lot of triple A games do. The combat system is a mix between bullet hell and turn-based games. There is little to dislike about Undertale for most people who enjoy the genre and share Toby Fox's sense of humor.
Pros:
-The best soundtrack I've heard of any game.
-A simplistic art style that is very visually appealing.
-Bad puns.
-A storyline that isn't too difficult to understand.
-3 largely different possible endings and a ton of slightly different variations of one of them.
-You feel like your decisions matter (for the most part)
-Lots of secrets and hidden easter eggs to keep people interested.
-Even the side-characters you will talk to only 2 or 3 times have fully developed personalities.
-Epic boss battles.
-Completely unique boss battles with entirely different fighting styles.
-You will find at least one character relateable.
-The music and artstyle complement the atmosphere and the gameplay.
-Some amount of replayability.
-1 of the endings provides a challenge by having a couple boss battles that are way more difficult than any others.
-Secrets hidden throughout the music.
-Reused themes throughout the music that create nostalgia.
-Should take more than a few hours to complete (depending on how detailed you are).
-Spooky scary skeletons.
-The puzzles are decent, but nothing special.
-Lots of good messages to take away.
-Every monster has a unique fighting style that fits their personality.
Cons:
-Occasionally some jokes or situations that are arguably a bit "cringeworthy".
-You cannot experience the game fully without getting at least 2 of the major endings.
-Your experience can be ruined a little bit if you're an idiot like me, and don't understand the obvious mechanics of the game's decision making, your first time through.
-Replayability will go away at some point.
-You can't fly a dragon to Jupiter.
In summary, I would recommend Undertale to anybody. Even if you don't usually play games like this or don't think you would like it, please give it a try. It is most definitely worth the amount of money it costs, as it is a game that takes hours to finish and has decent replayability to it, and you will likely walk away from Undertale feeling like you just went on an entire adventure, like you just experienced a completely different lifetime.  After all if you don't like it within the first 2 hours of playing it you can just refund it :P

Ok, Undertale is now one year old. Definitely doesn't feel like it though. I'm not really one for reviews, but I feel like if I put some effort into making a nice review for Undertale explaining all its pros and cons, it would be 8 paragraphs. Besides, there are enough of those. So, I'll cover the main points-
Undertale's story has a wonderful concept, but can be lacking in length. I highly recommend you do not spoil it for yourself if you do not know how the story goes. For most people, it's either you love the plot to death or think it's the epitome of mediocre. Personally, I love the story to death. Even though it may only span out to be 10-15 hours depending on your play style, I found the intro and plot twists very pleasing. The option to play the game in different routes is a great addition that the game cannot survive without. Pacifist ending would have to be my favorite, and if you ever play this game, I recommend you do the Pacifist run
playing it in your own style, though.
Okay, the
is
good. 101 songs composed by Toby Fox that fit all the game's moods perfectly. The genres range from 16-bit nostalgic music to orchestrated masterpieces, so there should be one perfect song for everyone. Plus, the unused songs of Undertale were released two days ago (as of the 15th of September, 2016) (you can find them on
or on
). I have way too many favorite songs from the OST, but the one that takes the cake is 'Death by Glamour'.
The Undertale community, in general, is good. The amount of amazing artwork created for the game by it's fans are truely brilliant, and many musicians have created some of the best game remixes I've heard. Most of the fans of the game, as far as I can see, are very friendly and have a genuine love for the game, as I do. The Undertale fandom on tumblr or on any other social media outlet isn't as edgy as it's made out to be. But, if you are looking for anything Undertale related created by fans, I wouldn't really recommend looking for it through Steam (some people do that?). The community page is just bad memes and stolen art. There are some original works on Steam, but there are
more original works on other sites.
I don't want to rate Undertale a score out of 10, because if I did, it would be a
biased
. Tell you what, play it yourself, and give it an honest rating. As for me, I'll stick with my 10/10. I don't know why, but I just really like this game. For an unbiased rating, I'll give it an 8.5/10

Undertale is an emotional and inspiring game that makes you feel like you are genuinely part of the world it takes place in. Its an incredibly detailed game with so many dialogue options that you can play through it several times and still not have seen all of it. Its incredibly unique from other RPGs, and it has more character depth than a lot of triple A games do. The combat system is a mix between bullet hell and turn-based games. There is little to dislike about Undertale for most people who enjoy the genre and share Toby Fox's sense of humor.
Pros:
-The best soundtrack I've heard of any game.
-A simplistic art style that is very visually appealing.
-Bad puns.
-A storyline that isn't too difficult to understand.
-3 largely different possible endings and a ton of slightly different variations of one of them.
-You feel like your decisions matter (for the most part)
-Lots of secrets and hidden easter eggs to keep people interested.
-Even the side-characters you will talk to only 2 or 3 times have fully developed personalities.
-Epic boss battles.
-Completely unique boss battles with entirely different fighting styles.
-You will find at least one character relateable.
-The music and artstyle complement the atmosphere and the gameplay.
-Some amount of replayability.
-1 of the endings provides a challenge by having a couple boss battles that are way more difficult than any others.
-Secrets hidden throughout the music.
-Reused themes throughout the music that create nostalgia.
-Should take more than a few hours to complete (depending on how detailed you are).
-Spooky scary skeletons.
-The puzzles are decent, but nothing special.
-Lots of good messages to take away.
-Every monster has a unique fighting style that fits their personality.
Cons:
-Occasionally some jokes or situations that are arguably a bit "cringeworthy".
-You cannot experience the game fully without getting at least 2 of the major endings.
-Your experience can be ruined a little bit if you're an idiot like me, and don't understand the obvious mechanics of the game's decision making, your first time through.
-Replayability will go away at some point.
-You can't fly a dragon to Jupiter.
In summary, I would recommend Undertale to anybody. Even if you don't usually play games like this or don't think you would like it, please give it a try. It is most definitely worth the amount of money it costs, as it is a game that takes hours to finish and has decent replayability to it, and you will likely walk away from Undertale feeling like you just went on an entire adventure, like you just experienced a completely different lifetime.  After all if you don't like it within the first 2 hours of playing it you can just refund it :P

First and foremost, I have enjoyed my time with this game. I bought into it when it was released as Alpha, and for the money I paid, I have had a lot of fun with my friends.

The slow down in development recently has been disheartening to say the least. It has gone through many iterations since I bought in, and most have been for the best. But active development seems to have stopped, and there do not appear to be any realistic goals to get the game into Beta at any point.
If you have friends you want to play this game with, then by all means buy it. But if you are looking for something like the DayZ Mod, this is not your game.
It's too bad, but the game has stalled in Early Access hell, and is the reason I am wary of buying into anything in Alpha. I firmly believe DayZ SA has ruined the Alpha concept for many people and that will hurt games that actually want to deliver their profuct via a viable Early Access method.

This game its the kind of game that makes you feel like a child again,  getting carried away by the characters and the world in it, making you laugh or cry.

Why DayZ will always have a place in my heart. Well for starters this game or if you got into this a lot earlier 'mod' was what set the standard for most survival games today ad infact is what a lot of other survival games aspire to be. Has this Alpha early access standalone been buggy? Yes ofcourse but I remember the mod being the very same. Has it improved much since it's relase? Well if you actually take the time to see the devs work you would see they done a lot considering what they had to work with. So all i can say is props to them. Keep in mind in terms of features are probably on the back burner till the core fundementals have been addressed and bug free. Considering they have move the game to a whole new engine which was very needed due to the out of date Dirext x version which caused a lot of rendering issues which of course effected FPS greatly. Since they moved to the infusion engine as it is called the game for me runs on everything on highest settings with a 50-60 fps with very little drops.
Zombies have been a bbig complaint also and I for one can also say they have been a nightmare prior to the .60 update. Again the zombies have gotten a lot better and don't glitch through buildings anymore but infact became a lot more smarter and more dangerous with their ability to vault and climb. Also in the near future hordes are going to be a thing making them even more dangerous.
Survival aspect is indepth with it probably only going to get more so into detail as the game progresses, people complaining over people killing them are usually the ones treating the world like a harmless 'take what you want' mentality without remembering what kind of game they are playing. Chernarus is a map big enough to play hide and seek with 500 players looking for you and you still might not get found. Water sources are easy enough to get too with lakes, wells, rain, soda and even some foods providing hydration. Food it's self is probably the only difficult aspect but if you can't find canned products in houses you can pick apple trees, hunt animals or even grow your own food through the farming system. Again the opntions are available.
Vehicles are located around the map but they are usually in need of a few parts, they can be accuired in sheds, warehouses, garages, storage units and if you have the tools you can take the parts from another vehicle you find.
Weapons and ammo can be found anywhere! You can litreally find a rifle in a back seat of a car or in a house or maybe even on top of a food stand or a deer stand.
Community it's self has a mix of individuals from friendly approchable players to the slightly nervous players with itchy fingers or outright bandits. Sometimes you got to roll the dice and make your own decisions about them but that is what makes interaction on this game so enjoyable because you never know what will happen next.
You probably heard of this game being named the running simulator and that is mostly due to the fact of the map size which some players find tedious to get around on but that is all base don personal preference. My opinion is that I can get form south to north in less than 25 minutes without gear and just live off what I come by, Honnestly the game gets a bad name for what you do in a lot of other survival games anyway, name one similar game were you don't do this...
Conclusion, this game in my opinion is probably the daddy of zombie survival games and holds some of the best memories I even had from gaming in the past 4 years I played this. Players looking for more interaction can find like minded players on communities based around these principles such as role play whitelisted servers. Intime this game will only get better and I still mised out a lot of features that I have not mentioned. You will not regret buying this game as it may be still in Alpha but investing in a game with this much potential should not be missed out on.

If I had to make a list of the best games I've ever played in my life, then Undertale would DEFINITELY BE ON THIS LIST. It's beautiful in almost every aspect, and I highly recommend it to anyone.
PROS:
-GORGEOUS soundtrack.
-Amazing plot and story. (you really need to pay attention to all the little details to fully appreciate it though), good plot twists.
-Lovable characters. (every single character in this game is different, and unique on their own way.)
-Full of secrets and easter eggs. (if you are clever, you get to see a lot of hidden dialogue and special scenes!)
-Multiple endings, choices DO matter! (REAL different endings, you can get from the happiest ending, to the most bizarre, horrible, and evil one.)
-Quite original fighting mechanic, (mixing bullet hell genre with rpg elements.)
-Full of humor, jokes and references.
-Simple graphics, but still pleasant to the eyes.
-High replay value, you'll probably play it more than at least 2 times to uncover the whole story
CONS:
-Although the graphics are not bad, there could be made some improvements. (like adding backgrounds to the fights, or colors, or some more sprites whenever enemies attack or get hit.)
-Lack of difficulty setting, (For some, this game is too hard, for others it's too easy)
-Lack of language variety. (The game's only in english, but people are working on language patches)
-The fandom (sadly, it is extremely easy to get spoilers from the internet, completely ruining the experience for new players, without mentioning some other things)
I fell in love with this game, seriously, give it a try, don't look up anything
about the story or anything, JUST PLAY IT.

I see all these reviews ♥♥♥♥♥ing about the KoS community and how the game is nothing but a cancer. This couldnt be further from the truth. It's a survival game and everyone is out to do the same thing, survive. If you're solo, don't build next door to a big clan. If you and your friend are partially geared, don't take pot shots with your SAR at a fully geared group with bolts and AK's. You have to lay low and farm bits at a time. There are still the trolls, as with any game, but they aren't that hard to deal with.
I have played Rust solo, in a small group and in a medium sized group. Rust is a fickle mistress. Some times, she will let everything go your way, other times, you'll be rage quitting 6-7 times a day.
The dev's listen to the community and try to better the game with frequent patches. In the span of a year, they've tried the blueprint system, xp system and the component system. It is still in early access and I can imagine there will be a lot more changes to come. Garry, Helk and the FP crew are active in the online Rust communities, listening and responding to what people have to say about the game.
The game itself is great. Graphics are nice, gameplay is fun and there are a lot of active servers up at all times. The modding community is pretty large and there is a lot of variance between all the modded servers.
Vanilla rust is a game that will not hold your hand. It's not a casual game. If you're constantly dying, you need to change the way you play and adapt.
10/10, would have the best (and worst) times of my life playing this game again.

TL;DR Review:
This is a fun game as it currently stands, to waste many an hour on in my opinion, but I see a lot of potential for an even better completed game and truly hope the developers have much more in store for us.
[ETA] **I don't recommend buying the game unless you are willing to play a game in development that possibly may not ever reach completion.**
That said, while I understand the frustration expressed by so many others regarding the long-standing EA status of DayZ, I've chosen not to include that as a complaint in my review and instead review the game's playability as it currently stands. From here on, I assume that readers of this review understand the general downsides to playing a game still in development.
Full Review:
I logged several hundred hours of playtime on a friend's computer (thanks for putting up with me, B!) and thoroughly enjoyed the experience. I held off purchasing the game myself for a long time because I feel the price tag is a bit high for a finished game (and by extension, far too high for an EA game.) However after a few months of playing the ARMA II mod (with Epoch) I found that, base-building aside, I enjoyed the standalone version more and so I bit the bullet and bought DayZ SA.
I've owned it for about two weeks as of this writing and have been averaging 40 hours a week of playtime. I've very much enjoyed the RP aspect and play on various private and public servers, and here is my list of pros & cons:
PROS
- immersion is unlike any other game I've played--nearly had a heart attack while hiding from several zombies and my phone rang.
- i have already made several friends on various servers and the game is even more fun when playing with others.
- the zombies/walkers/zeds/roamers are surprisingly intimidating (without being OP and thus frustrating) and i quickly found myself having to adjust my playstyle between "pew pew"ing to being more stealthy after several deaths caused by being overwhelmed by zeds drawn to my gunfire
- i enjoy the crafting and hope to see crafting expanded in the future
CONS
- without a general chat channel it is hard to interact with people
- would like to see more silent ranged weapons like the crafted bow and/or higher spawn rates of various bow and crossbow models
- as a hearing impaired individual, i am frequently murdered by people using VOIP to communicate and I would prefer not to have to wear my hearing aid when relaxing with a game
- no way to identify someone using exploits and no way to report them even if you can ID them
- in-game map appears worthless, navigation is near impossible if you are new and don't have the app iZurvive
I would personally like to see the following things brought into standalone:
- Epoch-esque base building, vehicles, traders
- GPS or other means of orientation that doesn't require an outside app or hella good memory
- serverwide chat
- ability to contact server admin in the event of hacking/duping/rule-breaking or to report glitches
- clan identities (a la World of Warcraft guilds) and ability to designate areas as some sort of shared base (a la Walking Dead's Woodbury/Terminus/Prison/Alexandria/Hilltop/Kingdom) that would allow only members of said clan to enter--or defend against other invading clans
Most importantly to me, generally I would like to see more accessibility options brought in as currently this game is nearly impossible to play if one has hearing, visual, or dexterity related disabilities. having all three myself, I get frustrated more often than I feel is necessary. Though I doubt it will happen I would be more than happy to be part of perhaps some sort of focus group to discuss accessibility options with the devs that would allow for improved gameplay for disabled persons without creating an unfair advantage.

Undertale.
The RPG where you can change the lives of thousands.
Undertale was reccommended to me by a friend from school. He told me of things like the Lesser Dog, how if you would pet it its neck would extend far off the screen, and, of course, Sans and Papyrus, the two skeleton brothers...
I soon began browsing around on its wikia page. The storyline seemed deep, the gameplay immense, and the characters as lovable as ever - So I saved up and bought it.
And I was not disappointed.
Undertale's storyline, to begin with, is so vast that no-one has completely figured it out yet. Most of it involves Gaster..
Everything you do changes the story. If you kill one person, the game remembers it the whole way through. Even if you reset. And let's not forget genocide runs, then pacifist runs. A genocide run cannot be erased with a True Reset. Only by reinstalling the game.
The characters indeed seem to have lives of their own, and respond differently to how you play. And they're the most lovable sprites you'll ever get attached to. Because there is no question about becoming attached to them.
The world itself is beautiful and carefully thought out. There isn't a crack in the wall out of place. The environment, when paired with the soundtrack, is a luscious experience. Even if it is pixels. Especially notable is the room where you have to light the path with mushrooms before you can proceed.
The endings are all sensibly put together, and makes everything you've done make sense.
The combat is unlike any other game out there. And you don't have to raise your weapon once in the entire game. You can, instead, chat with a monster. Flirt with it. Sing it a song. Strike a pose. Tell a really bad pun. And relying on your own evasive maneuvers rather than RNG is truly ingenious. Not to mention it gave Toby Fox so many different options for special attacks.
And, last but not least, the game leaves an emotional impact.
At the end of the True Pacifist run at Sans' speech, I CRIED.
Okay?
It felt so great to have even a skeleton tell you you succeeded. And the way he said it was so meaningful to me.
So, yeah.
Get this game.
Ten dollars?
This is priceless.
Toby Fox, I salute you!

In this game you play on an island where everybody is exposed and can kill or be killed by anyone at any time. There's no teams or guilds; only spoken agreements between players through vocal proximity chat. The gimmick of Rust is that everything anybody has is up for grabs. This means that if you die your entire inventory - guns, clothes, resources, etc. - can be taken by whoever killed you. Furthermore, the houses you build can be busted into and even taken over by other players which in-turn leaves you a fresh spawned man or women naked and with nothing but their trusty rock. This twist on open-world quickly produces a sense of urgency and risk in the player, spawning from a fear of loss of which makes the game both exhilarating and rewarding. Risk vs Reward is what Rust is all about; it makes you think hard about every choice you make.
Coincidentally this gimmick unintentionally provides an small insight on basic human behavior.
Since everyone has the power to kill everyone else in Rust, player interaction is incredibly stressful. TL;DR Review:
This is a fun game as it currently stands, to waste many an hour on in my opinion, but I see a lot of potential for an even better completed game and truly hope the developers have much more in store for us.
[ETA] **I don't recommend buying the game unless you are willing to play a game in development that possibly may not ever reach completion.**
That said, while I understand the frustration expressed by so many others regarding the long-standing EA status of DayZ, I've chosen not to include that as a complaint in my review and instead review the game's playability as it currently stands. From here on, I assume that readers of this review understand the general downsides to playing a game still in development.
Full Review:
I logged several hundred hours of playtime on a friend's computer (thanks for putting up with me, B!) and thoroughly enjoyed the experience. I held off purchasing the game myself for a long time because I feel the price tag is a bit high for a finished game (and by extension, far too high for an EA game.) However after a few months of playing the ARMA II mod (with Epoch) I found that, base-building aside, I enjoyed the standalone version more and so I bit the bullet and bought DayZ SA.
I've owned it for about two weeks as of this writing and have been averaging 40 hours a week of playtime. I've very much enjoyed the RP aspect and play on various private and public servers, and here is my list of pros & cons:
PROS
- immersion is unlike any other game I've played--nearly had a heart attack while hiding from several zombies and my phone rang.
- i have already made several friends on various servers and the game is even more fun when playing with others.
- the zombies/walkers/zeds/roamers are surprisingly intimidating (without being OP and thus frustrating) and i quickly found myself having to adjust my playstyle between "pew pew"ing to being more stealthy after several deaths caused by being overwhelmed by zeds drawn to my gunfire
- i enjoy the crafting and hope to see crafting expanded in the future
CONS
- without a general chat channel it is hard to interact with people
- would like to see more silent ranged weapons like the crafted bow and/or higher spawn rates of various bow and crossbow models
- as a hearing impaired individual, i am frequently murdered by people using VOIP to communicate and I would prefer not to have to wear my hearing aid when relaxing with a game
- no way to identify someone using exploits and no way to report them even if you can ID them
- in-game map appears worthless, navigation is near impossible if you are new and don't have the app iZurvive
I would personally like to see the following things brought into standalone:
- Epoch-esque base building, vehicles, traders
- GPS or other means of orientation that doesn't require an outside app or hella good memory
- serverwide chat
- ability to contact server admin in the event of hacking/duping/rule-breaking or to report glitches
- clan identities (a la World of Warcraft guilds) and ability to designate areas as some sort of shared base (a la Walking Dead's Woodbury/Terminus/Prison/Alexandria/Hilltop/Kingdom) that would allow only members of said clan to enter--or defend against other invading clans
Most importantly to me, generally I would like to see more accessibility options brought in as currently this game is nearly impossible to play if one has hearing, visual, or dexterity related disabilities. having all three myself, I get frustrated more often than I feel is necessary. Though I doubt it will happen I would be more than happy to be part of perhaps some sort of focus group to discuss accessibility options with the devs that would allow for improved gameplay for disabled persons without creating an unfair advantage.

Listen, this review can be summed up in just a few words, and if that's all you want to hear from me, just look at the conclusion and rating. But for those of you nerds who want to know a little more, keep on reading.
GAMEPLAY
You know, gameplay doesn't get much more simple than this, yet quite frankly, it can turn from an easy, walk in the park, to the most annoyingly painful experience in your life. Undertale is a cool game, because of the metaphor it seems to be based on. And that is that the choices you make in life, are what make your life, your life! Undertale is all about the choices you make, and how they impact your gameplay. You can become friends with everyone and have the happy ending you dream of, or kill everyone you come across and gET STUCK ON THE LAST BOSS, ♥♥♥♥ YOU
! (Whom I still have not beaten...) Who would have thought that this game can make you both question ethics and share some of the best laughs I've had in a while. There are so many charming and wonderful characters to befriend, as well as annoying and evil ones to kill, but in Undertale, the choice is yours.
GRAPHICS
Well, it may feel a bit underwhelming at times, but this is a very pixelated game. Now it's not painful to look at, so I wouldn't say they are bad graphics, just low resolution. But in a game like this, you'll find that it doesn't matter. Plus, that means you can run on a potato like me and be able to play!
COMMUNITY
You know, I like this game a good bit, and it will remain something I'd recommend to those who aren't too big into video games, and even sometimes those who are. But never will I understand why some people love this game as much as they do. Sometimes it just gets creepy... But yeah, not a terrible fanbase, but not a great one either. Not that it matters too much, as this game is single player.
CONCLUSION
It's a good game! Don't expect to love it, and don't expect to hate it. If you don't want to fork over ten bucks, watching a YouTuber play it is a very similar experience.
RATING
7/10; a bit underwhelming at times, yet extremely overwhelming at others.

Buried within Rust is a good concept, and an average game.  Don't get me wrong, the game play is well done, with a solid foundation, but it always leaves you wanting more and doesn't really 'deliver' on that.
Additionally, starting out in Rust is a nightmare.  The Rust community has a few helpful groups to aid you in this, and even some helpful servers for it, but for the most part you're going to encounter trolling.  Since Rust, as a concept, depends on its over all community and the feelings that it gives off this is a big knock against the project.
So, first and foremost:  Rust is not meant to be played alone.  I had some good times with some friends, but over all my experience was negative even when playing with a group.  The most interesting experience I had in the entire game was when two players attacked me and mine and we were all at a fairly similar equipment level, I lost that battle but had a blast over all since it was at least an actual fight.  That was fun as well as engaging, and I can honestly say it was the high point of my entire rust experience save for when I found a private server that was willing to help my group learn how to play.  Unfortunently by then the game had soured.
You see the rest of the game save for that one battle and the private server always had me running around desperate for equipment and getting shot at by higher geared players with nothing better to do.  Resources were impossible to get, meeting up with friends was a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ and over all this drug what would have otherwise been an exciting style of game down quickly.  Even when I found my stride in Rust and thought I was making good progress the game blindsided me.  Me and my limited number of weapons could do nothing against a helicopter.  So, with me seeing no real room for advancement I recognized that my fun with Rust was clearly at an end.  There's only so much you can do in a community oriented game that has a very negative over all sentiment, and with a difficulty level that fits the 'brick wall' description aptly.  The fun ultimately could not survive that.
That's the key point.  If you think you will enjoy the head bashing style of game then maybe this is for you.  It doesn't have the depth of Dark Souls, and doesn't have the equity of DayZ, and doesn't have a positive community over all.
For me, it's not to be, but if you can over come those issues, as I said, you will find an average game.  The developer recently asked players if he felt they got their 20 dollars worth of entertainment.  I did not, and would not recommend buying the game at full price.
Keep in mine, the game is still in development as of the time of this review, and communities can evolve.  Perhaps one day Rust will come through and become the game I wish it could be.
