Buried within Rust is a good concept, and an average game.  Don't get me wrong, the game play is well done, with a solid foundation, but it always leaves you wanting more and doesn't really 'deliver' on that.
Additionally, starting out in Rust is a nightmare.  The Rust community has a few helpful groups to aid you in this, and even some helpful servers for it, but for the most part you're going to encounter trolling.  Since Rust, as a concept, depends on its over all community and the feelings that it gives off this is a big knock against the project.
So, first and foremost:  Rust is not meant to be played alone.  I had some good times with some friends, but over all my experience was negative even when playing with a group.  The most interesting experience I had in the entire game was when two players attacked me and mine and we were all at a fairly similar equipment level, I lost that battle but had a blast over all since it was at least an actual fight.  That was fun as well as engaging, and I can honestly say it was the high point of my entire rust experience save for when I found a private server that was willing to help my group learn how to play.  Unfortunently by then the game had soured.
You see the rest of the game save for that one battle and the private server always had me running around desperate for equipment and getting shot at by higher geared players with nothing better to do.  Resources were impossible to get, meeting up with friends was a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ and over all this drug what would have otherwise been an exciting style of game down quickly.  Even when I found my stride in Rust and thought I was making good progress the game blindsided me.  Me and my limited number of weapons could do nothing against a helicopter.  So, with me seeing no real room for advancement I recognized that my fun with Rust was clearly at an end.  There's only so much you can do in a community oriented game that has a very negative over all sentiment, and with a difficulty level that fits the 'brick wall' description aptly.  The fun ultimately could not survive that.
That's the key point.  If you think you will enjoy the head bashing style of game then maybe this is for you.  It doesn't have the depth of Dark Souls, and doesn't have the equity of DayZ, and doesn't have a positive community over all.
For me, it's not to be, but if you can over come those issues, as I said, you will find an average game.  The developer recently asked players if he felt they got their 20 dollars worth of entertainment.  I did not, and would not recommend buying the game at full price.
Keep in mine, the game is still in development as of the time of this review, and communities can evolve.  Perhaps one day Rust will come through and become the game I wish it could be.

I'm going to start off by saying that rust is, in my opinion, a very good game. Even though it might not have the best optimisation around, it still is so much fun to play. If you're looking to buy the game, I would highly recommend it. And here's why:
First off, this game has so much re-playability. The difficulty curve is pretty steep, but once you start getting the hang of it it gets real fun. The great thing about it is that its always a challange, and you're always learning, from other players, and from your previous mistakes. It's a game that will take you a lot of time to master. From your aim, to raid tactics, to base building, you'll find yourself always trying out different ideas.
I also really like the PvP in rust. There is a decent number of weapons, both melee and ranged, and many ways to go into combat. I always find it to be really entertaining and at points, can get really intense.
Which takes me to the more grindy part of the game. Unless you're playing on a modded server, you're probably going to spend a lot of time hitting trees and rocks for resources. This can get quite tedious and boring sometimes if you're alone. But, as I mentioned, there are modded servers that give you increased gather rates and will make the game way less tedious.
Something else to keep in mind is the fact that solo rust might not be the thing for you. Personally, I usually play Rust with a group of friends, usually at least 4-5 people. I have played Rust Solo, and it's pretty hard, mostly when in combat situations when you get outnumbered by an enemy clan.
Last but not least are the graphics. I love the graphics rust has, but, at this point in time, it can be pretty resource intesive and does require a pretty powerful rig to run on max settings. If you have a pretty crap pc, I wouldn't recommend spending the money on it.
Overall, I would highly recommend Rust. It may be a bit grindy and slightly repetitive at times, but every time I start fresh on a new server, It's a totally different adventure.

. In Borderlands 2, you played a mercenary along with three other buddies, but this time everything's completely different. .

The book that I chose for my Summer Reading Essay is The Extraordinary Education of Nicholas Benedict, which is the final book in The Mysterious Benedict Society Series. The Extraordinary Education of Nicholas Benedict is about Nicholas Benedict who is an orphan with narcolepsy going to a new orphanage and trying to find a hidden treasure that he finds out about early in the book. Nicholas is not able to look for the treasure in the morning so he finds a way to get out of his room at night, which is locked at night because he has horrible nightmares and would scare the other children, by getting a wax mold of a skeleton key that the orphanage operator has. Nicholas also meets a friend whose name is John. Nicholas loves to read and while he is reading a book about astronomy, he comes across a note that says “Consult the Butler” and the book that was next to the book he was reading was written by Brian T. Butler, and inside the book are receipts to very expensive telescopes, which Nicholas thinks is the treasure. Nicholas is also very smart and realizes that the telescopes must have been placed in an observatory, and he sneaks outside during one of the nights and finds an overgrown pathway that he follows up a hill to the observatory. Nicholas goes inside to find the treasure but when he checks inside the observatory there’s a spot for a massive telescope but the telescope had been removed by someone. After Nicholas leaves the Observatory and is going to go back to the orphanage disappointed, he sees another overgrown pathway that after following it leads to a farm. Nicholas leaves and the next day he gets his friend John to sneak out and they go to the observatory together after Nicholas shows John the hidden passage, and they follow it to the farm. Once they get there they see a girl sitting on the edge of the cliff. Nicholas and John panic and try to get the girls attention, but she can’t hear them. After a while she realizes that she is being watched and turns around and looks frightened, and almost backs off of the cliff, Nicholas and John leave so that the girl is frightened and accidently falls off the cliff. The next day John and Nicholas go back to the observatory and think where the treasure would be in the observatory when Nicholas here’s someone in the forest coming to the observatory (which they started calling the Giant’s Head). At first Nicholas thinks it Mr. Collum, the orphanage director, but when they look to the door they see that it is the girl who was sitting on the cliff. Nicholas and John scream, and Nicholas faints. The next day the girl comes to the observatory and Nicholas starts talking to her in sign language. John asks how Nicholas knew how she was deaf and Nicholas explains how he realized that it took her a while to realize people were behind her when she was on the cliff, and when she scared them in the Giant’s Head and she didn’t flinch when they screamed. Nicholas and John talk to the girl all night and she explains that her name is Violet and that lives on the farm next to the cliff. A few days later- WAIT THIS IS UNDERTALE!!! Ahh, UnderTale… How do I begin to express my opinion on this game? Well, I suppose I could start off by saying that I honestly wasn’t “instantly hooked” on the game when I saw it for the first time. In fact, it wasn’t until very late in the game, when I had gotten the chance to see the “Broad image” of the story where I really started to enjoy it, and I am damn glad I finally did.
I know it has been said before, but UnderTale is a fantastic game, and the fact that it was mostly made by one person is mind-blowing. Toby “Radiation” Fox, you are a freaking genius! And you know what? I think this is my favourite PC-game ever.
I am going to try not to spoil anything, in case someone out there has managed to remain spoiler-free since the game’s release, but I’ll try to talk about as much as I can. Let’s start with the presentation: While most of the sprite-work in the game isn’t very impressive, the game is still pleasing to look at, especially the battle-sprites, well done animation, and the charming character-designs. The music in the game is spectacular, and even though, like with the overall game, I wasn’t originally very impressed by it, I now listen to the soundtrack every day. Tracks like "Heartache", "His Theme", "Hopes and Dreams", "SAVE the World", "Last Goodbye", and "Megalovania" are among my favourite songs in video games.
Now that I’ve talked about the presentation, I guess I should mention that the gameplay is, like the rest of the game, extraordinary. I have always loved RPGs, but even some of my favourite RPGs ever, such as EarthBound/Mother 2 tend to get repetitive, since the combat is mainly just pushing the A/L button over and over again. UnderTale takes the concept of a turn-based RPG and adds a sort of “Bullet Hell”-element, making the combat feel interesting, and way less luck-based than other RPGs. Let’s not forget one of the biggest elements in this game -- The “Mercy”-function. In UnderTale, you get the choice to kill or spare every enemy. If you decide to befriend everyone, you get one ending. If you decide to kill everyone, you get one ending. If you kill X-person, but spare Y, you get another ending, etc. Thing is, showing mercy doesn’t make the game less interesting, since every battle is a puzzle of sorts, in which you figure out how to befriend the enemy, instead of just slaughtering them. I recommend going for the “True Pacifist Ending”, but that’s the thing: that’s all up to you. The game greatly revolves around the player’s choice, and it does so way better than most triple-A titles, at least if you ask me.
And with all that out of the way, I give you: The story. I really don’t want to talk too much about this part. The story can be extremely happy at times, and completely heart-breaking at others.
The basic story goes something like this: Long ago, there was a great war between humans and monsters. After a long battle, the humans were victorious, and used a magic spell to seal the monsters deep inside Mt.Ebott. The player takes the role of a human child who has fallen into the mountain many years after the war ended. It is now your job to find your way out of the Underground, and back to where you came from. The story might seem basic, but towards the end of the game, it starts getting more complex, but that’s only the start of it. After doing several playthroughs, and looking at the smaller details scattered about, you start to realize how much more there is than what meets the eye.
I often have trouble memorizing character-names, but that was no problem with UnderTale. (Hell, if a game can make you remember to think of blue stop-signs, It can probably make you remember anything.) The characters are all unique, relatable, and all around lovable. By the end of the game I get rather emotional when I look back at all the great friends I’ve made throughout my journey.
Something else that I love is the humour. It is always on-point, and never fails to make me smile. If you like point-and-click games, I assure you that you will enjoy exploring the world of UnderTale, as there is so much to interact with.
I would especially recommend this game if you like “Mother 3” (Or similar games), since UnderTale clearly got a lot of inspiration from that game.
In order to end this off, I am going to do something unusual. I am going to quote the YouTuber JackSepticEye: “Never have I wanted to applaud a game so much in my life. That is how video games are made, man! So f****n’ good. There is almost nothing to fault the game on. It’s so awesome! You have all of these Triple-A games going out of their way, trying make
“Choice based games” that have these real big effects, and this has done it PERFECTLY.”
I couldn’t have said it better myself. “Never have I wanted to applaud a game so much in my life”.
… Well, I suppose I just wrote it. Whatever, you get the point, it was well-worded.

It's also a perfect length to play for a single-player campaign if you like the idea of collecting random drops while playing an FPS.  There's a well-deeloped story and narrative, and playing it by yourself is much more enjoyable than playing it co-op since you can actually follow along with the story instead of being distracted by teammates who may just want to rush from point to point.  Although I never played the first Borderlands game, it allowed me to jump in while slowly feeding me the backstory during the progression of the game, which left me satisfied without feeling the need to go back and play the first release.
I purchased it on a sale, but this is the one time I regret not paying full price as I think showing support with my wallet would really help the developers and publisher.  If they make a third game, I'm definitely in for a "day one" purchase!

The book that I chose for my Summer Reading Essay is The Extraordinary Education of Nicholas Benedict, which is the final book in The Mysterious Benedict Society Series. The Extraordinary Education of Nicholas Benedict is about Nicholas Benedict who is an orphan with narcolepsy going to a new orphanage and trying to find a hidden treasure that he finds out about early in the book. Nicholas is not able to look for the treasure in the morning so he finds a way to get out of his room at night, which is locked at night because he has horrible nightmares and would scare the other children, by getting a wax mold of a skeleton key that the orphanage operator has. Nicholas also meets a friend whose name is John. Nicholas loves to read and while he is reading a book about astronomy, he comes across a note that says “Consult the Butler” and the book that was next to the book he was reading was written by Brian T. Butler, and inside the book are receipts to very expensive telescopes, which Nicholas thinks is the treasure. Nicholas is also very smart and realizes that the telescopes must have been placed in an observatory, and he sneaks outside during one of the nights and finds an overgrown pathway that he follows up a hill to the observatory. Nicholas goes inside to find the treasure but when he checks inside the observatory there’s a spot for a massive telescope but the telescope had been removed by someone. After Nicholas leaves the Observatory and is going to go back to the orphanage disappointed, he sees another overgrown pathway that after following it leads to a farm. Nicholas leaves and the next day he gets his friend John to sneak out and they go to the observatory together after Nicholas shows John the hidden passage, and they follow it to the farm. Once they get there they see a girl sitting on the edge of the cliff. Nicholas and John panic and try to get the girls attention, but she can’t hear them. After a while she realizes that she is being watched and turns around and looks frightened, and almost backs off of the cliff, Nicholas and John leave so that the girl is frightened and accidently falls off the cliff. The next day John and Nicholas go back to the observatory and think where the treasure would be in the observatory when Nicholas here’s someone in the forest coming to the observatory (which they started calling the Giant’s Head). At first Nicholas thinks it Mr. Collum, the orphanage director, but when they look to the door they see that it is the girl who was sitting on the cliff. Nicholas and John scream, and Nicholas faints. The next day the girl comes to the observatory and Nicholas starts talking to her in sign language. John asks how Nicholas knew how she was deaf and Nicholas explains how he realized that it took her a while to realize people were behind her when she was on the cliff, and when she scared them in the Giant’s Head and she didn’t flinch when they screamed. Nicholas and John talk to the girl all night and she explains that her name is Violet and that lives on the farm next to the cliff. A few days later- WAIT THIS IS UNDERTALE!!! However they have out done themselves in making a game that completely invites people to be the biggest♥♥♥♥♥♥♥possible towards new players and I am sure that the comments section if the other reviews were anything to go buy will be flooded by the angry wailing of fanbois claiming I'm a noob and I don't know how to play the game blah blah blah, well you guys can ♥♥♥♥ off, no one likes you and no one especially likes a bunch of fanbois who refuse to admit that their game is broken.
For those who will actually read my review, this is a good 'game', the mechanics are excellent, I actually like the survival aspect of Rust, however I have picked up on two glaring faults that are breaking the game completely. The first one is the most obvious when you are a newbie and you first try this game. The spawn system is flat out broken, because of the way building works in this game what has happened is that especially on the small maps because the older players know exactly where newbies will spawn they actually build huge ♥♥♥♥ing walls to stop them from escaping easily and there are players on there literally sitting and waiting on rooftops for not just geared up players to come along but specifically targeting brand new players for ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles because they have nothing better to do than make people rage in the review section about this.
With this spawn system, it is therefore impossible for new players to have any chance of fighting back, I'm no pushover, I was really determined to try and take these ♥♥♥♥ers down and I did actually manage to nail a guy who had let his guard down on one of the smaller maps with a stone spear when all his buddies came rushing after me once I got through the outer edge of his base he opened by accident. However there's just no fighting it, especially when you're solo and you go in for the first time, the newbies have to have some kind of balance protection against these people, even DayZ wasn't this ♥♥♥♥ing bad and EVE Online at least had safe zones where any of the veteran players would be gunned down in a second if they tried attacking players who were just learning.
The second major flaw with this game is you gussed it, the balance of the weapons, again, this is to do with the spawn system partly, but fresh spawns cannot even go up against somebody with a bow if they're unlucky enough to be spawned next to someone like that and that actually ♥♥♥♥ing happened to me. The spawn system is so bad when I spawned on the coastline ( Which I think is mainly where you end up generally which is why players could predict where you'd end up ) I ended up getting shot at before I could even react properly just as I had come in.
This is a serious flaw not just with survival open world PVP games but open world games in general, I tried Rust because it was pretty reasonably priced but had it been something like Elite: Dangerous again I would have been pretty♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off because in the open multiplayer that game suffers from the exact same problems as well.
Games developers need to stop ignoring these glaring issues, if you offer up more private game options and community options then that would definitely fix things, maybe even allow admins to change the spawn areas and so on or randomise things more, just stuff like that. However with the way things are I am not surprised at all at the amount of raging people are doing over this game, I can't blame them and it's actually reminding me of why I'm really enjoying staying in singleplayer games generally or really well balanced shooters that don't have these issues.
If you're really intent on buying this game, I would see if you can find a nice community server to play in where there's an active admin that will boot any griefers, that's all I can really suggest if you are fed up of the griefing players right now that get off on ganking newbies.

The book that I chose for my Summer Reading Essay is The Extraordinary Education of Nicholas Benedict, which is the final book in The Mysterious Benedict Society Series. The Extraordinary Education of Nicholas Benedict is about Nicholas Benedict who is an orphan with narcolepsy going to a new orphanage and trying to find a hidden treasure that he finds out about early in the book. Nicholas is not able to look for the treasure in the morning so he finds a way to get out of his room at night, which is locked at night because he has horrible nightmares and would scare the other children, by getting a wax mold of a skeleton key that the orphanage operator has. Nicholas also meets a friend whose name is John. Nicholas loves to read and while he is reading a book about astronomy, he comes across a note that says “Consult the Butler” and the book that was next to the book he was reading was written by Brian T. Butler, and inside the book are receipts to very expensive telescopes, which Nicholas thinks is the treasure. Nicholas is also very smart and realizes that the telescopes must have been placed in an observatory, and he sneaks outside during one of the nights and finds an overgrown pathway that he follows up a hill to the observatory. Nicholas goes inside to find the treasure but when he checks inside the observatory there’s a spot for a massive telescope but the telescope had been removed by someone. After Nicholas leaves the Observatory and is going to go back to the orphanage disappointed, he sees another overgrown pathway that after following it leads to a farm. Nicholas leaves and the next day he gets his friend John to sneak out and they go to the observatory together after Nicholas shows John the hidden passage, and they follow it to the farm. Once they get there they see a girl sitting on the edge of the cliff. Nicholas and John panic and try to get the girls attention, but she can’t hear them. After a while she realizes that she is being watched and turns around and looks frightened, and almost backs off of the cliff, Nicholas and John leave so that the girl is frightened and accidently falls off the cliff. The next day John and Nicholas go back to the observatory and think where the treasure would be in the observatory when Nicholas here’s someone in the forest coming to the observatory (which they started calling the Giant’s Head). At first Nicholas thinks it Mr. Collum, the orphanage director, but when they look to the door they see that it is the girl who was sitting on the cliff. Nicholas and John scream, and Nicholas faints. The next day the girl comes to the observatory and Nicholas starts talking to her in sign language. John asks how Nicholas knew how she was deaf and Nicholas explains how he realized that it took her a while to realize people were behind her when she was on the cliff, and when she scared them in the Giant’s Head and she didn’t flinch when they screamed. Nicholas and John talk to the girl all night and she explains that her name is Violet and that lives on the farm next to the cliff. A few days later- WAIT THIS IS UNDERTALE!!! Absolutely incredible! My favourite video game! My favourite aspect of the game is the soundtrack. It is so well thought out and I find myself humming tracks such as Heartache, Megalovania and Battle against a true hero on a regular basis. The battling style is rare, entertaining and at the same time challenging. Each character has their own unique style that is relevant to their character traits. The designs of the monsters of the underground are so varied and beautiful and each one gives the story a little special something. For example the Skelebros Sans and Papyrus give the game a light-hearted and comedic feel where as characters such as Asgore add drama and emotions to the story. Even less important characters such as Naptablook, Mad Dummy and my personal favourite, Muffet add things to the gameand it just wouldn't feel the same without them. Another thing I love about the game is how the ending is different based on the choices you make throughout the run. Overall I must say that Undertale can give you a challenge, make you laugh and tug at your heart strings all at the same time. I would strongly recommend it to everyone of all ages and genders. I thoroughly enjoyed playing Undertale and despite the fact it was mostly spoiled for me by the internet, I felt multiple emotions whilst playing.

Borderlands 2 is a really good game if you love shooting people and collecting loot, especially the awesome guns. What you probably won't like though is that it's really REALLY repetitive for some people. That's one reason that people may not like this game. The other reason is that, in this game, you kind of need to grind a bit because in the later places of this game, you might find yourself getting owned. And finally, my third reason that you may not like this game is: the level difference. I'm talking about when you join a friend's game and find out you're a bit behind.
Okay so it starts normally, you're shooting enemies right? And then you notice, your shots are doing so little damage. Your reaction would be: What the ****, why is my gun useless? Yeah, that will happen. It really reeks of donkey♥♥♥♥♥♥how that works. Anyway moving on, if you can ignore all of that, this game is great.
(Like me, I like this game even though it's shooting people and collecting loot. I bought the goty edition of this game even though I already had the original just for all the dlc :D)
Characters:
The characters of this game are really well acted. I like how Handsome Jack is a kind of villain that's likeable though you still hate him. Cl4ptr4p is annoying though. I heard the C14PTR4P from the original Borderlands was much better. I honestly don't know since I haven't played much of the first game. And to be honest, I didn't really know the story of the first game since it was really vague. Tiny Tina is also an interesting character so to speak. Her backstory was really interesting too, for me.
The playable characters you can choose from are: Axton, Maya, Salvador, Zer0, Gaige, and the latest and last playable character, Krieg. I will summarize all of these characters' main abilities.
Axton is a (bisexual, lol) guy who can summon his turrets to fight alongside him (or with his friends too). You can further upgrade his ability so that when he summons his turrets they can have a shield sphere, or when you summon it, it can cause an explosion which damages the enemies near your turret. And also you can upgrade your turret's gun which makes it stronger.
Maya is a siren, who basically has an ability called phaselock which allows her to trap her opponent in an orb that makes them unable to move. You can further upgrade this so that it can cause effects like slag, or you can make it a supportive ability which you use phaselock on your friends to heal them.
Salvador is a kind of um short and plump guy who has the ability to dual wield any two weapons of your choice. Sniper and rocket launcher, check. Pistol and assault rifle, check. Smg and smg, check. Basically any weapon combo you want, it's possible.
Zer0, this guy is too awesome. He's an alien guy, who can turn invisible and slash enemies with his katana. I can't describe him much. The info about him is really vague. And yes, you heard me right, he is an alien. (Or possibly, it's heavily hinted he's an alien though.)
Gaige is girl with a mechanical arm who summons Deathtrap, a robot that she can summon to fight for her. To be honest I haven't played Gaige's char yet. So idk what she really does well in.
Krieg, now this is where it gets fun. Have you always wondered if you could play as the psycho in Borderlands? Ohhhh boy, well if yes then, this is for you. No? Well then, this is still for you. Imo he is my favorite character next to all of these char. I can't really pick my fave character because I like all of them, but Krieg is my favorite if I'm forced to pick. This guy is so awesome to play with. I recommend you get the Psych0 pack dlc if you haven't. His special ability is that you use your axe and ♥♥♥♥ people up. Yes, I mean that literally, okay maybe not but still. He is ♥♥♥♥ing awesome.
You either throw the axe at those mofos or chop the ♥♥♥♥ out of them yourself. Not only that, you can also upgrade his skill tree which makes him more awesome. Basically, you got downed? No problem man, get the ♥♥♥♥ back up and strap a bomb to yourself. Then when you explode, bam, you get revived. There's also something SUPER MEGA FOOKIN AWESOME. When you upgrade his skill tree high enough, when a time comes your health is low at a certain level, you transform into a badass psycho and..... holy ♥♥♥♥ing♥♥♥♥♥♥ get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥rekt. You can rek them like there's no tomorrow.
Sound:
Hmmm, this section is going to be short. The sound is what can I say, okay I guess for this game. There's not much music going on that makes me really want to fight. If you count the opening song though, that song is awesome. The gun sounds are pretty good. They sound great if you ask me. I'm not really a gun sound expert but it sounds fine to me. Great sound.
Visuals:
Unlike some people, I actually like the cell-shaded style of this game. It's what makes this game Borderlands. It probably wouldn't be the same if they tried to make the graphics different. The visuals for this game are really good. I like the landscape, the ice areas, lava, eridium blight. All the places in this game are well done. Props to Gearbox for making this game spectacular. Awesome visuals.
Plot:
I'm not going to say much but the plot of this game is great for me. It's a game about where you're a vault hunter who is searching for the vault in this game. And throughout the game you encounter Handsome Jack, the main villain, I already described him but basically he's a likeable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. In the beginning of the game, you are discovered by C14PTR4P who is shocked to see a vault hunter like you alive. After that you go through fights and then you reach Sanctuary. Here is where the main cast of Borderlands 1 are in this game. (Lilith, Mordecai, Brick and Roland) At this point you're going to meet the Firehawk and then rescue Roland. You basically meet all of the original cast of the first game and you work together to defeat Handsome Jack. It's a good story imo.
I would say this game is well worth your money at the 10 dollars I spent during the Steam Summer Sale. As I said, I already owned the game, but I decided to buy goty for 10 dollars which is the same price for the season pass. (Goty is the same price as the season pass, the season pass contains all the main story dlc which is in the goty. The goty edition has additional dlc like the Gaige and Krieg char pack.) So if you own the game, I would recommend you buy the goty edition if you want the dlc of the season pass. Back to the main topic, this game is well worth over 10 dollars to be honest. It's the best RPG FPS I've ever played. (Not counting Deus Ex because I consider that sci-fi) If you didn't already have this game, I would suggest you buy it. Good job Gearbox, you did a good job. I'm a bit sad about Aliens: Colonial Marines. But in this game, you've put an outstanding amount of work into it.

Ahh, UnderTale… How do I begin to express my opinion on this game? Well, I suppose I could start off by saying that I honestly wasn’t “instantly hooked” on the game when I saw it for the first time. In fact, it wasn’t until very late in the game, when I had gotten the chance to see the “Broad image” of the story where I really started to enjoy it, and I am damn glad I finally did.
I know it has been said before, but UnderTale is a fantastic game, and the fact that it was mostly made by one person is mind-blowing. Toby “Radiation” Fox, you are a freaking genius! And you know what? I think this is my favourite PC-game ever.
I am going to try not to spoil anything, in case someone out there has managed to remain spoiler-free since the game’s release, but I’ll try to talk about as much as I can. Let’s start with the presentation: While most of the sprite-work in the game isn’t very impressive, the game is still pleasing to look at, especially the battle-sprites, well done animation, and the charming character-designs. The music in the game is spectacular, and even though, like with the overall game, I wasn’t originally very impressed by it, I now listen to the soundtrack every day. Tracks like "Heartache", "His Theme", "Hopes and Dreams", "SAVE the World", "Last Goodbye", and "Megalovania" are among my favourite songs in video games.
Now that I’ve talked about the presentation, I guess I should mention that the gameplay is, like the rest of the game, extraordinary. I have always loved RPGs, but even some of my favourite RPGs ever, such as EarthBound/Mother 2 tend to get repetitive, since the combat is mainly just pushing the A/L button over and over again. UnderTale takes the concept of a turn-based RPG and adds a sort of “Bullet Hell”-element, making the combat feel interesting, and way less luck-based than other RPGs. Let’s not forget one of the biggest elements in this game -- The “Mercy”-function. In UnderTale, you get the choice to kill or spare every enemy. If you decide to befriend everyone, you get one ending. If you decide to kill everyone, you get one ending. If you kill X-person, but spare Y, you get another ending, etc. Thing is, showing mercy doesn’t make the game less interesting, since every battle is a puzzle of sorts, in which you figure out how to befriend the enemy, instead of just slaughtering them. I recommend going for the “True Pacifist Ending”, but that’s the thing: that’s all up to you. The game greatly revolves around the player’s choice, and it does so way better than most triple-A titles, at least if you ask me.
And with all that out of the way, I give you: The story. I really don’t want to talk too much about this part. The story can be extremely happy at times, and completely heart-breaking at others.
The basic story goes something like this: Long ago, there was a great war between humans and monsters. After a long battle, the humans were victorious, and used a magic spell to seal the monsters deep inside Mt.Ebott. The player takes the role of a human child who has fallen into the mountain many years after the war ended. It is now your job to find your way out of the Underground, and back to where you came from. The story might seem basic, but towards the end of the game, it starts getting more complex, but that’s only the start of it. After doing several playthroughs, and looking at the smaller details scattered about, you start to realize how much more there is than what meets the eye.
I often have trouble memorizing character-names, but that was no problem with UnderTale. (Hell, if a game can make you remember to think of blue stop-signs, It can probably make you remember anything.) The characters are all unique, relatable, and all around lovable. By the end of the game I get rather emotional when I look back at all the great friends I’ve made throughout my journey.
Something else that I love is the humour. It is always on-point, and never fails to make me smile. If you like point-and-click games, I assure you that you will enjoy exploring the world of UnderTale, as there is so much to interact with.
I would especially recommend this game if you like “Mother 3” (Or similar games), since UnderTale clearly got a lot of inspiration from that game.
In order to end this off, I am going to do something unusual. I am going to quote the YouTuber JackSepticEye: “Never have I wanted to applaud a game so much in my life. That is how video games are made, man! So f****n’ good. There is almost nothing to fault the game on. It’s so awesome! You have all of these Triple-A games going out of their way, trying make
“Choice based games” that have these real big effects, and this has done it PERFECTLY.”
I couldn’t have said it better myself. “Never have I wanted to applaud a game so much in my life”.
… Well, I suppose I just wrote it. Whatever, you get the point, it was well-worded.

Hype kills, and someone told me how they felt like Undertale should be worth $100. I kept a level head and in the end that was a hilariously wrong statement and the asking price of $10 is just fine.
It’s interesting through all the hype I saw I never once saw someone say “i love dodging white dots :D” Cus while the combat system is different, it’s the weakest part of the game. It’s either some easy gimmick fight, or intentionally hard gimmick that gets itself closer to the bullethell origin that it comes from. Personally I don’t care for bullethell so I didn’t care much for it, but I would say it was worth slogging through the dot dodging just for the gameplay payoff for the big twist boss fight reveal at the end. That is I mean it was a gameplay payoff, but the actual draw of the game is the cute quirky characters and their personal journies.
The tagline being about how you don’t need to kill anybody, well alot of RPGs already allow intentional pacifism. FO1/FO2/New Vegas have pretty funny pacifist dialogue options. So a pacifist route in an RPG isn’t new, but what’s unique to Undertale is how cute the pacifism is. All the monsters look and act cute which adds to how evil the act of killing them would be.
The main cast of characters, specifically Sans and Papyrus, have a similar cute/quirkiness of that of the Homestuck trolls, and in general the humor is similar to that of Homestuck. When you know of the history of the game it’s no surprise really, and it’s no surprise that all the Homestuck fans clobbered onto Undertale because of that.
But Undertale reminds me of a specific period of Homestuck. The points of where Homestuck started to before the trolls were introduced. This is where sure there’s the quirky characters, there’s the meta videogame humor, but there’s an underlining mystery to it all. Something was off, which was hinted at by the mayor an anarchist (this som homestuck tangent sowy but itll connect back) and the enjoyment was seeing the mystery be revealed and how that will affect the characters. Then of course the trolls were introduced and more wacky characters were added and out of like 30 characters only like 4 get a story arc, everyone else was a gimmick and thus the story went nowhere and everyone gave up on attempting to hold interest.
This is where Undertale being a singular, finished, product greatly benefits over a continuous series. All NPCs have a character arc, however small it may be, in Undertale. Not even joking. Of course the arcs change too depending on the player actions as well. But man, the True Pacifist Ending had the best story pay-offs out of the 3 other games I played.
side note: the game has minimal graphical options so no v-sync and such so the game had screen tearing whenever I walked around cus I believe the framerate is stuck to 30fps so I guess that’s a negative.

Disclaimer: This is a pretty opinionated review.
Honestly, despite how much the Fandom has destroyed this game's reputation and despite how much I distance myself from it. I still enjoyed this game.
Bear in mind to ignore the Fandom's antics and don't let it immediately spoil the game for you, sure the fandom is incredibly toxic towards critics of this game, however it's best to ignore them and for you to form your own opinion on the game (whether it be positive or negative) without encountering these folks.
Anyways allow me to cut to the chase.
Undertale is an indie RPG game made in 2015 that pays tribute/homage towards the Earthbound/MOTHER games. The game gathered quick popularity and is the story of a young boy who falls deep within the underground filled with monsters.
So what are the pros and cons?
Pros: Great gameplay, good bullet-hell esque gameplay, genocide and pacifist are both pretty challenging, different paths and endings, dogs,  interesting story and characters, occaisional good humor, dogs, tragic/redeemable villains, great soundtrack, good boss-fight, meta as hell, dogs, Yathzee (from Zero Punctuation) considered this game his game of the year, dev is a pretty cool guy.
Cons: Humor is dated for some people (kinda, it has tons of meme references which can be dated in a few years), paths are limited at times, gameplay can get boring after a while, story and dialogue is a little sappy, fanbase's behavior can spoil the game for most people.
Honestly, I enjoyed the game, though that might be due to my love for the Earthbound/MOTHER games and my willingness to play any spiritual successor to those games, even if it's something as depressing as LISA (which truth be told, I kind of prefer over Undertale, however that doesn't stop Undertale from being a good game in my eyes). I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys what I described as the pros. I know there are people that don't enjoy the game, but I definetly can see why, this isn't a game for everyone, but I still enjoyed it nonetheless.

Borderlands 2 is a really good game if you love shooting people and collecting loot, especially the awesome guns. What you probably won't like though is that it's really REALLY repetitive for some people. That's one reason that people may not like this game. The other reason is that, in this game, you kind of need to grind a bit because in the later places of this game, you might find yourself getting owned. And finally, my third reason that you may not like this game is: the level difference. I'm talking about when you join a friend's game and find out you're a bit behind.
Okay so it starts normally, you're shooting enemies right? And then you notice, your shots are doing so little damage. Your reaction would be: What the ****, why is my gun useless? Yeah, that will happen. It really reeks of donkey♥♥♥♥♥♥how that works. Anyway moving on, if you can ignore all of that, this game is great.
(Like me, I like this game even though it's shooting people and collecting loot. I bought the goty edition of this game even though I already had the original just for all the dlc :D)
Characters:
The characters of this game are really well acted. I like how Handsome Jack is a kind of villain that's likeable though you still hate him. Cl4ptr4p is annoying though. I heard the C14PTR4P from the original Borderlands was much better. I honestly don't know since I haven't played much of the first game. And to be honest, I didn't really know the story of the first game since it was really vague. Tiny Tina is also an interesting character so to speak. Her backstory was really interesting too, for me.
The playable characters you can choose from are: Axton, Maya, Salvador, Zer0, Gaige, and the latest and last playable character, Krieg. I will summarize all of these characters' main abilities.
Axton is a (bisexual, lol) guy who can summon his turrets to fight alongside him (or with his friends too). You can further upgrade his ability so that when he summons his turrets they can have a shield sphere, or when you summon it, it can cause an explosion which damages the enemies near your turret. And also you can upgrade your turret's gun which makes it stronger.
Maya is a siren, who basically has an ability called phaselock which allows her to trap her opponent in an orb that makes them unable to move. You can further upgrade this so that it can cause effects like slag, or you can make it a supportive ability which you use phaselock on your friends to heal them.
Salvador is a kind of um short and plump guy who has the ability to dual wield any two weapons of your choice. Sniper and rocket launcher, check. Pistol and assault rifle, check. Smg and smg, check. Basically any weapon combo you want, it's possible.
Zer0, this guy is too awesome. He's an alien guy, who can turn invisible and slash enemies with his katana. I can't describe him much. The info about him is really vague. And yes, you heard me right, he is an alien. (Or possibly, it's heavily hinted he's an alien though.)
Gaige is girl with a mechanical arm who summons Deathtrap, a robot that she can summon to fight for her. To be honest I haven't played Gaige's char yet. So idk what she really does well in.
Krieg, now this is where it gets fun. Have you always wondered if you could play as the psycho in Borderlands? Ohhhh boy, well if yes then, this is for you. No? Well then, this is still for you. Imo he is my favorite character next to all of these char. I can't really pick my fave character because I like all of them, but Krieg is my favorite if I'm forced to pick. This guy is so awesome to play with. I recommend you get the Psych0 pack dlc if you haven't. His special ability is that you use your axe and ♥♥♥♥ people up. Yes, I mean that literally, okay maybe not but still. He is ♥♥♥♥ing awesome.
You either throw the axe at those mofos or chop the ♥♥♥♥ out of them yourself. Not only that, you can also upgrade his skill tree which makes him more awesome. Basically, you got downed? No problem man, get the ♥♥♥♥ back up and strap a bomb to yourself. Then when you explode, bam, you get revived. There's also something SUPER MEGA FOOKIN AWESOME. When you upgrade his skill tree high enough, when a time comes your health is low at a certain level, you transform into a badass psycho and..... holy ♥♥♥♥ing♥♥♥♥♥♥ get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥rekt. You can rek them like there's no tomorrow.
Sound:
Hmmm, this section is going to be short. The sound is what can I say, okay I guess for this game. There's not much music going on that makes me really want to fight. If you count the opening song though, that song is awesome. The gun sounds are pretty good. They sound great if you ask me. I'm not really a gun sound expert but it sounds fine to me. Great sound.
Visuals:
Unlike some people, I actually like the cell-shaded style of this game. It's what makes this game Borderlands. It probably wouldn't be the same if they tried to make the graphics different. The visuals for this game are really good. I like the landscape, the ice areas, lava, eridium blight. All the places in this game are well done. Props to Gearbox for making this game spectacular. Awesome visuals.
Plot:
I'm not going to say much but the plot of this game is great for me. It's a game about where you're a vault hunter who is searching for the vault in this game. And throughout the game you encounter Handsome Jack, the main villain, I already described him but basically he's a likeable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. In the beginning of the game, you are discovered by C14PTR4P who is shocked to see a vault hunter like you alive. After that you go through fights and then you reach Sanctuary. Here is where the main cast of Borderlands 1 are in this game. (Lilith, Mordecai, Brick and Roland) At this point you're going to meet the Firehawk and then rescue Roland. You basically meet all of the original cast of the first game and you work together to defeat Handsome Jack. It's a good story imo.
I would say this game is well worth your money at the 10 dollars I spent during the Steam Summer Sale. As I said, I already owned the game, but I decided to buy goty for 10 dollars which is the same price for the season pass. (Goty is the same price as the season pass, the season pass contains all the main story dlc which is in the goty. The goty edition has additional dlc like the Gaige and Krieg char pack.) So if you own the game, I would recommend you buy the goty edition if you want the dlc of the season pass. Back to the main topic, this game is well worth over 10 dollars to be honest. It's the best RPG FPS I've ever played. (Not counting Deus Ex because I consider that sci-fi) If you didn't already have this game, I would suggest you buy it. Good job Gearbox, you did a good job. I'm a bit sad about Aliens: Colonial Marines. But in this game, you've put an outstanding amount of work into it.

Undertale takes place in the Underground, a realm where monsters, once equal to humans, were banished to after war broke out between them. The Underground is sealed from the surface world by an imperfect magic barrier, the only point of entry being at Mount Ebott.[12] A human child falls into the Underground and encounters Flowey, a sentient flower who teaches them the game's mechanics and encourages them to raise their "LV", or "LOVE", by gaining "EXP" through killing monsters.[a] When Flowey attempts to murder the human to take their soul for himself, the human is rescued by Toriel, a motherly goat-like monster, who teaches the human to solve puzzles and survive conflict in the Underground without killing. She intends to adopt the human, wanting to protect them from Asgore Dreemurr, the king of the Underground.
The human eventually leaves Toriel to search for Asgore's castle, which contains the barrier leading to the surface world. Along the way, the human encounters several monsters, including: the skeletons Sans and Papyrus, two brothers who act as sentries for the Underground; Undyne, the head of the royal guard; Alphys, the kingdom's royal scientist; and Mettaton, a robotic television host Alphys created. Some of them are fought, with the human having to choose whether to kill them or to show mercy; should the human spare them, they become friends. During their travels, the human learns the cause of the war between humans and monsters. Asriel, the son of Asgore and Toriel, befriended a human child who fell into the Underground and was adopted by Asgore and Toriel. One day, the child was fatally poisoned by some flowers. I don't know how facepunch studios have done it, because I thought easily that the worse game for PvP back in the day was EVE Online with the RPG mechanics and how much the older players griefed new players. However they have out done themselves in making a game that completely invites people to be the biggest♥♥♥♥♥♥♥possible towards new players and I am sure that the comments section if the other reviews were anything to go buy will be flooded by the angry wailing of fanbois claiming I'm a noob and I don't know how to play the game blah blah blah, well you guys can ♥♥♥♥ off, no one likes you and no one especially likes a bunch of fanbois who refuse to admit that their game is broken.
For those who will actually read my review, this is a good 'game', the mechanics are excellent, I actually like the survival aspect of Rust, however I have picked up on two glaring faults that are breaking the game completely. The first one is the most obvious when you are a newbie and you first try this game. The spawn system is flat out broken, because of the way building works in this game what has happened is that especially on the small maps because the older players know exactly where newbies will spawn they actually build huge ♥♥♥♥ing walls to stop them from escaping easily and there are players on there literally sitting and waiting on rooftops for not just geared up players to come along but specifically targeting brand new players for ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles because they have nothing better to do than make people rage in the review section about this.
With this spawn system, it is therefore impossible for new players to have any chance of fighting back, I'm no pushover, I was really determined to try and take these ♥♥♥♥ers down and I did actually manage to nail a guy who had let his guard down on one of the smaller maps with a stone spear when all his buddies came rushing after me once I got through the outer edge of his base he opened by accident. However there's just no fighting it, especially when you're solo and you go in for the first time, the newbies have to have some kind of balance protection against these people, even DayZ wasn't this ♥♥♥♥ing bad and EVE Online at least had safe zones where any of the veteran players would be gunned down in a second if they tried attacking players who were just learning.
The second major flaw with this game is you gussed it, the balance of the weapons, again, this is to do with the spawn system partly, but fresh spawns cannot even go up against somebody with a bow if they're unlucky enough to be spawned next to someone like that and that actually ♥♥♥♥ing happened to me. The spawn system is so bad when I spawned on the coastline ( Which I think is mainly where you end up generally which is why players could predict where you'd end up ) I ended up getting shot at before I could even react properly just as I had come in.
This is a serious flaw not just with survival open world PVP games but open world games in general, I tried Rust because it was pretty reasonably priced but had it been something like Elite: Dangerous again I would have been pretty♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off because in the open multiplayer that game suffers from the exact same problems as well.
Games developers need to stop ignoring these glaring issues, if you offer up more private game options and community options then that would definitely fix things, maybe even allow admins to change the spawn areas and so on or randomise things more, just stuff like that. However with the way things are I am not surprised at all at the amount of raging people are doing over this game, I can't blame them and it's actually reminding me of why I'm really enjoying staying in singleplayer games generally or really well balanced shooters that don't have these issues.
If you're really intent on buying this game, I would see if you can find a nice community server to play in where there's an active admin that will boot any griefers, that's all I can really suggest if you are fed up of the griefing players right now that get off on ganking newbies.

The game have a very deph story telling with a great cast of characters wich you just can't hate on. toby went through this games writing really well, i haven't seen such well writen characters and story in a AAA game in a long time.

this game have a 2 major ending paths you can pick. Borderlands 2 is a game that throws you in the deep end of the pool by getting you shooting up more things than you can imagine minutes after starting the story. It is recommended to play with friends for more fun and co-operation, however playing on your own is fine as the diverse characters and the funny things they have to say keeps you entertained all the way through. The leveling system is made to keep you at the right level during the game, so after 1 or 2 levels of grinding, you will not be getting much experience to level up at all, this could be a posotive or negative depending on the way you look at it. I have heard complaints of the games art style and more specifically the outlines, however this art style gives off the same vibe as the game itself, and the game was not made to be deadly serious, with you shouting commands to your friends, it was made to be fun and interesting, and that is what the art style delivers. The skill tree varies for each character, giving lots of replay value to the game to see what combinations of skills are possible to make the most powerful class possible.
The DLC for the game hae their ups and downs in some ways. The DLC's for the first time run-through are set at specific levels, which makes it hard for you to be at the right level for each of them as they vary a bit depending on your level, but only to a limitation. You can easily go over the recommended level by playing through one DLC and end up being over-powered on the the other DLC. However, these things aside as they are only really the first time run-through that it occurs on, the DLC offers new worlds to explore and hours of more interesting storyline, witty phrases, familiar faces (and some new ones) and fun to be had.
I strongly recommend this for someone looking for hours of fun with their friends, or on their own. Anyone who is skilled and wants to make a combination of skills that work together nicely in the skill tree, or fun someone just wanting to get stuck into a game.

In Rust players must survive on a procedurally genrated map by collecting resources, hunting wildlife, and crafting tools. But you're not alone, other players are also enduring the wilderness. Survive by building a shelter and arming yourself with weapons in an unforgivable environment.
Pros:
+Intricate building tools
+Procedurally generated maps (no two servers feature the same world with various environments to keep gameplay fresh)
+Extensive crafting system (from wooden spears and burlap headwraps, to pistols and Thompson machine guns, create a large catalog of items)
Cons:
-No tutorial makes learning systems difficult
-Poor optimization causes crashes
-Time consuming to play effectively
It's an incredibly fun game that's easy to pick up. The procedurally generated maps ensure that it can be fun every time the server resets. Everything from simply harvesting resources to building a base is really intuitive. The constant threat of getting raided or jumped only makes the survival aspect of the game way more fun. Well worth the 20€ on steam.

When this game was released and was receiving rave reviews, I read 'an RPG where you don't have to kill anything!' and quickly wrote the game off as the type of emotional, pseudo-intellectual BS that critics fawn over.
However, a close friend just recommended I try this - trusting her judgement, I bought it. Wow, I couldn't have been more wrong about this game. It's got so much going for it. It's hilarious and it harkens back to those old RPGs with a lot of random side stuff to do and well-hidden secrets. The game is also quite short, but has a lot of replayability for new endings and side quests.
No one told me that this game is part shoot-em-up, aswell - at least, the dodging part (not so much the shooting part). Enemies' attacks happen within a box which your 'ship' (a heart) can move about, dodging bullet spray. There is also a very Ikaruga-like mechanic in which you can dodge blue attacks while not moving and orange attacks while moving. This whole battle aspect is never brought to an insanely difficult level, it's mostly pretty casual, but it keeps combat interesting and fun. I say 'mostly' because the final battle(s) are actually pretty difficult and require some skill.
The story and field gameplay are also interesting for such a short RPG. Definitely some stuff peppered throughout about true identity, love, friendship etc. Some stuff about gender identity, which to be honest I feel is over-used nowadays in games, like everyone has suddenly turned into this progressive, gender-equality warrior. But still, it worked out in the context of Undertale, as the writing is just so good. It's funny, the characters are zany, the situations are ridiculous but never out of place.
I had a great time playing this game (I did so in one sitting). And I'm sure I will replay it soon to get the other endings.

Ok, so Undertale is a great game. I have had a great time playing it. I have run through Neutral, Pacifist, and Genocide, so, I have a lot to say. Oh, and, if you start complaining about spoilers, well, too bad. This game has been out for a year, so if you haven't played it yet, then too bad.
Ok, so this is one of the very few games where choices make a HUGE impact on the game, and not just a new dialouge from a character. I mean HUGE. If you run through the ENTIRE game, not killing a single enemy, befriend Papyrus, Undyne, and Alphys, then you will get the True Pacifist ending. If you kill even one thing, then you will be on a Neutral run. If you kill EVERYTHING, and then kill Sans at the end, then you get the True Genocide ending. Even the things you say or don't say can change the ending of this game. So, yes: Choices matter a whole lot. And this game strecthes this concpet and shoves it down our throat, wether you like it or not, a lot.
The mechanics are simple: Shift or X to close out of an option, Enter to comfirm, C to open up menu, and arrow keys to move. The attacking system is very easy to use, aswell. All you have to do is land your little line thing in the center, to the most damage. ANd, if you are running through a Pacifist run, then you don't want to kill ANYTHING. So, what you will do is use your actions options, and then once their name is yellow, spare them. However, you don't have to spare them. Whichever you choose to do, wether it be kill everything, spare everything, or kill some things and spare others, it will change the ending you will get. Because, again, choices matter.
The games story is very well thought out, and quite frequently breaks the 4th wall. The game also uses the Save mechanic as an actual important thing, instead of just being a save file. Each time you beat the game, the charcters remember that you were once here, ESPICALLY Sans and Flowey. What I mean is that, Sans and Flowey know what's going on, and they know that you can save the game, and that you have the power to reset everything if you please. The game has 3 different endings, depending on what your actions in the game are. However, if you do decide to beat the True Genocide route, which is living HELL, trust me, then your game will become corupt. This means that whichever ending you get, no matter if it's a pacifist ending, everyone still will die, for the soul of the original, evil human, Chara, will replace Frisk's soul, so everyone will still die. So, a lot of things need to happen to get each ending, and it can be very tedious work.
Overall, this is a great game. Is it the best I've ever played, no, but it is up there. I recommend this game to everybody. Oh, and, little tip, don't run through the Genocide route first, for, once you beat it, it corrupts your game. You should also, never, play, the, True Genocide route. Sans almost made me go mental.

Now to the negative... Upon opening the game, the lighting, even with my computer settings and in-game settings on the very highest possible, still very dark. Seemingly completely black and white, save for slight color hue here and there, such as green in the grass and Autumn colors in the tree blobs. The walking is glitchy, not only for myself but for several friends I made an attempt to play this game with. Trying to run up a hill, I understand for the sake of being realistic you don't go as fast, but my character went snail pace. I quite nearly was crawling like a new-born going uphill; how am I to escape anything, were there something chasing me? Which brings me to the next topic; the wildlife and zombies. The only animal I saw was a chicken. One chicken. I saw not one zombie the entire time I played for. A friend of mine, on the other hand, did see one or two. Now it's understood that hand-to-hand combat is completely undesirable, however these zombies seem to hit and then move through player-characters to their blind spots to continue attacking, making keeping up very difficult and death almost certain. Brings me to healing, if surviving said attack is successful. No bandages are given upon spawn nor could be found anywhere, so if you end up bleeding from the attack, there's nothing that can be done unless, somehow, you get lucky and stumble across something for it, which none of us could after quite a while of playing. My friend, whom came across the zombie and was hit, did get a black screen and the message saying he'd gone unconscious. Next, I want to address that from the moment the lot of us spawned in, we received messages in multiple variations of the same content- "I'm thirsty" and "I'm hungry." In all of the places searched, not one bit of sustenance could be found. Now as far as mechanics go for objects and interaction; why can't we search anything? We can't open anything- Refrigerators, cabinets, lockers, dressers, wardrobes, etc. More than half of the doors can't be opened either. Our inventory is so limited, I can't pick up but, what, 4 items? I would need a backpack in order to carry more, but alike to other things, can not find any of. There's no map, no health bar, no stamina bar. The stamina bar I mention because while running, I notice my character does get out of breath (very quickly, might I add) and slows significantly, and after resting a bit, the time it takes to get tired again seems to decrease, which is highly inconvenient given that the normal paced walking is as slow as it is.

Just as I thought I'd started to get the hang of the game, two players cornered me in a shed, forced me to wear a dress and renamed me "Tim 2.0". They then killed me.
10/10 Would Recommend

When this game was released and was receiving rave reviews, I read 'an RPG where you don't have to kill anything!' and quickly wrote the game off as the type of emotional, pseudo-intellectual BS that critics fawn over.
However, a close friend just recommended I try this - trusting her judgement, I bought it. Wow, I couldn't have been more wrong about this game. It's got so much going for it. It's hilarious and it harkens back to those old RPGs with a lot of random side stuff to do and well-hidden secrets. The game is also quite short, but has a lot of replayability for new endings and side quests.
No one told me that this game is part shoot-em-up, aswell - at least, the dodging part (not so much the shooting part). Enemies' attacks happen within a box which your 'ship' (a heart) can move about, dodging bullet spray. There is also a very Ikaruga-like mechanic in which you can dodge blue attacks while not moving and orange attacks while moving. This whole battle aspect is never brought to an insanely difficult level, it's mostly pretty casual, but it keeps combat interesting and fun. I say 'mostly' because the final battle(s) are actually pretty difficult and require some skill.
The story and field gameplay are also interesting for such a short RPG. Definitely some stuff peppered throughout about true identity, love, friendship etc. Some stuff about gender identity, which to be honest I feel is over-used nowadays in games, like everyone has suddenly turned into this progressive, gender-equality warrior. But still, it worked out in the context of Undertale, as the writing is just so good. It's funny, the characters are zany, the situations are ridiculous but never out of place.
I had a great time playing this game (I did so in one sitting). And I'm sure I will replay it soon to get the other endings.

I had no idea if I should recommend the game or not but I decided that I would because although there are some shortcomings in the game. It is a solid game that is still being worked on hard by the developers to make it better and there isn't much bad with it.
I like the base building in the game, is is fun to have little rooms and upgrade the strength of the building to try and withstand the impending doom that is some nerdy kid with c4 and an ak wanting your wood.
The animals are quite derpy, you will find a lot of them will run through rocks and external walls which is annoying, especially when it kills you but the developers are working on that so that isn't that major.
The survival aspect is nice, I personally wish that there was a single player option so that people like me can go and play the survival aspect only although for that to happen there would need to be a lot more PvE danger and harder to find resources because you can get a base and guns etc in a days worth of playing provided you don't get killed a heap by other players. Now the reason I say this is because although yes, many people view Rust as a game that is PvP and there is no other way to play it, there are many different ways to play games and I feel that having the option there would be nice. I also think this because Rust has all of the components needed for a great base survival game so it could make a great PvE and PvP survival game given the chance.
Now even though I said that I would like to see a singleplayer PvE survival Rust game. I also play PvP Rust....I mean well duh that is all that is there right now but what I mean by this is that IF there was a PvE version put in I would play both PvE and PvP because the PvP is fun, I'm just not very good at it. I find that for me when I play Rust I build a base, get resources and I play very defensively, building in such a way my base can only be attacked from one direction and I defend that direction like all hell and I will run around collecting heaps of resources to the point where I have so many guns, armour, ammo, metal, wood, high quality metal etc like just heaps of everything, more than I know what to do with. Then I defend...and no I don't mean roof camp, I don't just sit there all day waiting for some naked to run by, I go and get more stuff, I craft, make improvements to the base, help out nakeds that run by with gear etc. Oh yeah and I'm sure you have figured out by now I don't play on those 500 player servers because I would just get rekt and yeah that is what happened when I first played, I play on lower population servers that have about 50 players at the highest peak. I'm not a very good shot, I'm 3/4 deaf and fully blind (exaggeration) so I'm not good at combat in general anyway so yeah I'm more of a defender than attacker but I still have a blast crafting and building and occasionally I get to fight back the odd raid or two which is heart pumping.
The graphics and sounds are amazing in this game and immersion is fantastic with the music that plays it can put you on edge that someone is near by wanting to kill you and yeah it's great.
The ONLY thing that I have negative to say about the game that is major is the fact that you get salty people that will kill naked people, be a♥♥♥♥♥♥about killing people etc. I mean I like to kill people in Rust as much as the next person but there is no need to kill someone with a rock.....nor is there to be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ when you kill someone that does have stuff. i could write a review of this game, but so many other people have written exactly what i would say. so, i'll just leave a recipe for a breakfast omelette:
you will need:
3 eggs
a tablespoon of milk
4 bacon strips
cheese
1 potato
1/4 red onion
salt, pepper, garlic powder, cayanne pepper(a dash of each)
cooking oil
Start off by dicing your potato and onion into little bits, then dropping that into a medium skillet with some oil. cook over a med-high flame, stirring frequently so that the potatos don't burn. salt lightly. takes about 15 minutes to cook. when done, the outside should be alittle crunchy, the inside moist. onions will blacken, thats fine. remove from heat and set aside to dry in some paper towels or coffee filters.
Next, start the bacon, just plop that in a skillet and cook it for 3 minutes, flip, cook for 2 more minutes then add to your potatos.
While the potatoes are cooking, you can start to prepare your eggs. just crack all 3 into a cup, add the milk and seasonings you want. mix it up so its a uniform yellow. get a medium skillet warmed up.
THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART! the fire MUST NOT be too high or YOU WILL BURN THE OMELETTE! it needs to be a low flame. heat up the skillet, grease it with cooking SPRAY or butter, then drop in the egg mixture. if you didn't stir it enough you will see an egg yolk in your pan. If you do, just make scrambled eggs.
If you did it right, the eggs should cook slowly. As they start to become solid on the bottom of the pan(but still runny enough to move around the pan, it will be 2 layers), add a layer of cheese over HALF of the omelette(not too much, you will add more later and the grease from the cheese will RUIN the flip). add the bacon and potatos over the cheese, then add more cheese. Once the eggs are almost completly solid, take a spatulla and start to lift up the edges around the side that is empty, this will be the side you FLIP onto the other. once you can move most of the empty side, you will put the spatulla under the middle of the empty side and GENTLY slide it all the way to the middle of the omelette. then you will lift slowly and try to create a half circle by folding one half over the other. turn off the heat and transfer it to a plate.
If done right, you just made an amazing breakfast THAT WILL GET YOU LAID! Dont ever underestimate a home cooked meal. it will get you in bed with someone 99 out of 100 times.
Use this power responsibly.

Ok, so Undertale is a great game. I have had a great time playing it. I have run through Neutral, Pacifist, and Genocide, so, I have a lot to say. Oh, and, if you start complaining about spoilers, well, too bad. This game has been out for a year, so if you haven't played it yet, then too bad.
Ok, so this is one of the very few games where choices make a HUGE impact on the game, and not just a new dialouge from a character. I mean HUGE. If you run through the ENTIRE game, not killing a single enemy, befriend Papyrus, Undyne, and Alphys, then you will get the True Pacifist ending. If you kill even one thing, then you will be on a Neutral run. If you kill EVERYTHING, and then kill Sans at the end, then you get the True Genocide ending. Even the things you say or don't say can change the ending of this game. So, yes: Choices matter a whole lot. And this game strecthes this concpet and shoves it down our throat, wether you like it or not, a lot.
The mechanics are simple: Shift or X to close out of an option, Enter to comfirm, C to open up menu, and arrow keys to move. The attacking system is very easy to use, aswell. All you have to do is land your little line thing in the center, to the most damage. ANd, if you are running through a Pacifist run, then you don't want to kill ANYTHING. So, what you will do is use your actions options, and then once their name is yellow, spare them. However, you don't have to spare them. Whichever you choose to do, wether it be kill everything, spare everything, or kill some things and spare others, it will change the ending you will get. Because, again, choices matter.
The games story is very well thought out, and quite frequently breaks the 4th wall. The game also uses the Save mechanic as an actual important thing, instead of just being a save file. Each time you beat the game, the charcters remember that you were once here, ESPICALLY Sans and Flowey. What I mean is that, Sans and Flowey know what's going on, and they know that you can save the game, and that you have the power to reset everything if you please. The game has 3 different endings, depending on what your actions in the game are. However, if you do decide to beat the True Genocide route, which is living HELL, trust me, then your game will become corupt. This means that whichever ending you get, no matter if it's a pacifist ending, everyone still will die, for the soul of the original, evil human, Chara, will replace Frisk's soul, so everyone will still die. So, a lot of things need to happen to get each ending, and it can be very tedious work.
Overall, this is a great game. Is it the best I've ever played, no, but it is up there. I recommend this game to everybody. Oh, and, little tip, don't run through the Genocide route first, for, once you beat it, it corrupts your game. You should also, never, play, the, True Genocide route. Sans almost made me go mental.

You know, when people were saying this game was the best game ever made, I turned my head.
They commended everything about the characters, the story, the gameplay, etc.
So I decided to give it a try.
Needless to say, I did not enjoy this game as much as other people did. But instead of saying "lol da gaem suxxx♥♥♥♥♥u" I am going to take this in a more adult way.
Let's begin with the story:
Long ago, humans and monsters co-existed on Earth. However, over time, the humans blotted out the monsters, leaving them to only live in a hole in a mountain. One day, a boy falls into the only enterance to the monsters' sanctuary, and it is his/her goal to get out, either by negotiation or murder.
The story is quite underwhelming to me, in my opinion. It might be because I literally forgot about the story right after the intro cutscene happened, though.
Graphics:
The graphics in this game are just awful. Toby Fox was going for a retro style, but he executed it way too poorly. The only good sprites are the sprites for the cutscenes and the trees in Snowden. All of the other sprites look lazily done, as if Toby just gave up after making the cutscene and said "Screw it! I'm a month away from the release date, I need to get this out there as quickly as possible!" and just rushed everything else.
Before I go further, let me explain something. I know Undertale was inspired by the Earthbound series. However, Earthbound looks so much better than this, in my own opinion.
Anyways, continuing on...
Gameplay:
Whenever you walk around, occasionally you come across an enemy. In order to win on this one-on-one confrontation, you can either fight it, negotiate with it, or flee. Fighting or negotiating will bring you into a box while things fly at you, sort of like a bullet hell. Depending on what you do, the storyline can branch off into another storyline. Kindof neat.
However, the bullet hell sections feel really slow to me, and winning just doesn't feel right. Whenever you win, you're supposed to feel as if you have accomplished something. In Undertale, this really isn't the case. It might just be me, but I didn't find any enjoyment out of sparing the enemies or killing them. I just said "Whatever" and moved on.
Characters:
Oh god.
I'm not going to detail into the characters for spoiler reasons (and because im becoming really lazy,) but they were all either bland, annoying, or just not too memorable.
Soundtrack:
This is the only somewhat decent part of the game. The soundtrack is not good to me, not bad to me, just a little bit neat. Listen to it if you feel like it, it's pretty neat.
Now let me explain something.
If you're like a lot of people, you will realize that I am in an anti-undertale group. I would just like to say, there is a reason, which is what I am about to say.
This game alone is like a person with a double amputee. You look at that person, and you feel kind-of sorry. He's been through something, and that person isn't doing too well.
Then a person runs up to him and decapitates him, killing him.
That is the...
Fanbase:
I probably could have excused this game for being very meh. And I really wanted to, this game had a lot of potential, and didn't do too well.
But the fanbase is JUST SO AWFUL.
They are so quick to say that Undertale is the best game in the history of gaming, and are willing to silence anyone who says even the smallest criticism about the game.
And the fanart.
Let's not go into that.
CONCLUSION:
This game is not the greatest. The story is generic, the graphics suck, the gameplay gets boring, the characters aren't the best, and the fanbase is the equivalent to lobotomizing yourself with a pitchfork.
Overall, a 1/10.
Thanks for reading this giant wall of text, if you did. And if you like undertale, i'm glad you are able to enjoy something that I cannot. It's just euugh to me, and it's my own opinion.
