Graphics does perfectly match those old RPGs from the 90s, but still needs some improvements. There are a few sections in the game that are just so empty and bland. Nevertheless, the developer did a very good job of recreating the retro feel.
Excellent writing filled with interesting characters, humor and twists. Very well designed endings, your choices really do matter. Also the breaking-the-fourth-wall sequences are done well and really help with the immersion.

Cons:
The game can get boring if you play it multiple times non-stop.
It's too short!
STORY:
Long ago, two races ruled over Earth. MONSTERS and HUMANS. One day, war broke out between the two races. After a long battle, the humans were victorious. They sealed the monsters underground with a magic spell.
Many years later, a small human climbs Mt. Ebott, where the monsters had been sealed. Legends say that anyone who falls into the underground, the home of the monsters, will disappear forever, never to be seen again.
After discovering an opening leading into their underground home, the small human tripped and had fallen down. Now, you, the player, must guide the human out of the realm and back with your family and friends on the surface.
Final evaluation:
If you are living under a rock and haven't heard of this game before, do NOT watch videos about it, do NOT read anything about it (except reviews, obviously) and whatever you do, DO NOT ASK ANYONE ABOUT IT!
Play this game for yourself and get out from under that rock.

One of the best FPS you will find that isn't all about multiplayer, though that is still recommended if you want better loot and get a better experience of the game itself.
Right off the bat the four initial classes seem to be the same as the original but that is only on the surface as each character continues to level up and spend skillpoints there will be a few things that make them feel a little to alot different from the previous vault hunters. There is also another bonus this new group has over this previous and that is freely be able to use any gun and while the original did that too you got better bonuses from sticking with the recommended weapons. Combat has mostly stayed the same besides the introduction of a new element slag which when an enemy is slagged any attack besides slag does significantly more damage.
The overall story is more or less a repeat of the first game, find the vault and open it. But more than enough is done to make it not just a blatant rehash this easily comes from what many consider to be the best villian in video game history ever Handsome Jack. Quoting Angry Joe on his review he is just one of those villians you love to hate. Almost everything he says or does is pure gold on why you should kill him. Not going to spoil it as by the end of the game I had plenty of reasons to kill this guy whereas other games have just said he/she/it is evil kill them. Still the story is overall good as it adds enough to make me not feel like it was a chore to go through the story unlike Borderlands.
Now while I said combat is relatively the same that surely isn't the same for the game's weapons, shields, relics, and mods that you will be using to combat Handsome Jack's army. First they have somewhat shrunk the amount of weapon types before there were pistols and revolvers but now they are one in the same also eridian guns do not have their own category as they can be any type of gun and are referred as E-Tech guns and have their own colored text. A new addition to guns is that certain ones are thrown like a grenade to reload and the amount left in the clip dictates how powerful the explosion will be. Shields have a few new types such as having the chance to absorb ammo, drop shield refill, increase your melee damage when depleted, or amplify your attack at the cost of charges in your shield.
The worst I can say about this game is one of the DLC packs Sir Hammerlock's Big Game Hunt is not recommended on purchasing if you decide to not the get the Game of The Year edition. COFFEE & CHOCOLATE CUPS
INGREDIENTS :
- 100g good-quality dark chocolate (about 60–65% cocoa solids)
- 125g mascarpone
- 2 tbsp icing sugar 
- 4 tbsp strong espresso coffee, cooled
- 150ml double cream
To finish:
-  4 tbsp double cream 
- a little dark grated chocolate
- few amaretti biscuits, crushed
METHOD:
-Break the chocolate into small pieces and melt in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water. Stir until smooth, then remove the bowl from the heat and leave to cool.
-With a hand whisk, beat the mascarpone and icing sugar together until smooth, then whisk in the espresso and the melted chocolate.
-In another bowl, whip the double cream until soft peaks form. Fold the cream into the mocha mixture until well combined. Spoon the mousse into four cappuccino cups or ramekins and chill overnight.
-Just before serving, lightly whip the 4 tbsp double cream until thick and swirl over of the mousses. Sprinkle the grated chocolate and crushed amaretti on top and serve immediately.
-Cheers survivors ! :)

This game is incredible, in no way shape or form will you be disappointed with this game. An amazing life simulator that represents 5000 BC- 2000 AD all in one map. You start out as a caveman; naked, alone with a rock in your possesion. After countless hours of crafting and mining resources you build your homestead. You learn how to PVP and kill everyone in sight without a thought. The world is cruel so don't travel alone. At times the game can seem like a horror simulator, other players and clans will sneak attack from the bushes. Typically they have guns and you don't. But eventually after you respawn enough times, you will have your first gun and go on a killing spree. Like a mass murderer. You get a flame thrower burn down a wooden door and loot the dead bodies of your victims. Take a second to admire the world around you go home assemble an auto-turret invite people inside only to be shot into pieces. The greatest piece of Personal Computer lure ever synthesized 10/10.

I can't see a beta aproaching anytime soon meaning this game is easily years away from any type of a release canidate. I feel cheated, I bought this game in Early Access to help support the developers and now it is evident that is not where my money went. At this point it feels as though its little more than a well orchestrated cash grab by Bohemia to fund other projects or strictly for profit. I strongly suspect this game will not see a true final release or definitely not one living up to all the promises made during development.

Undertale is a game that holds a very special place in my heart. Yet somehow it seems to be hated by many on account of the horrid fanbase. Please pay no attention to them because the game itself deserves the praise it gets and any attention you could give it - why exactly, however, is hard to describe.
Undertale is a game in which you play as a child that falls into a cave. You then explore, trying to find a way out of the underground and meet a lot of friends and foes on the way.
The battle system of Undertale is unique - it does not only allow you to kill enemies, but also talk or interact with them as well as sparing them entirely once certain conditions are met (that are different for every enemy). Finding these conditions is fun and tells you more about the enemy attitudes. And you will want to know about them because Undertale lives off of it's characters.
Undertales characters are the strongest point of the game - everyone is different and a few even have secrets they don't want you to know. The strong writing makes you love them or hate them, but evokes emotions either way.
The most interesting part of Undertale, however, is the fact that essentially everything you do in the game influences the story - sparing every monster will open up different paths, dialogues and endings than killing every monster. You can also seek a middle ground which again influences the story.
Everything you do has consequences in some form and that is what makes Undertale so entertaining even across multiple playthroughs. Added to that, the amazing music that is among the best video game music to date, makes the game one of the best and most unique indie games of this decade.
Don't spoil yourself somehow - buy Undertale and play the game the way you want to - see where it leads you. Chances are, you will fall in love with it like so many people did.
Personal verdict: 10/10

One of the best FPS you will find that isn't all about multiplayer, though that is still recommended if you want better loot and get a better experience of the game itself.
Right off the bat the four initial classes seem to be the same as the original but that is only on the surface as each character continues to level up and spend skillpoints there will be a few things that make them feel a little to alot different from the previous vault hunters. There is also another bonus this new group has over this previous and that is freely be able to use any gun and while the original did that too you got better bonuses from sticking with the recommended weapons. Combat has mostly stayed the same besides the introduction of a new element slag which when an enemy is slagged any attack besides slag does significantly more damage.
The overall story is more or less a repeat of the first game, find the vault and open it. But more than enough is done to make it not just a blatant rehash this easily comes from what many consider to be the best villian in video game history ever Handsome Jack. Quoting Angry Joe on his review he is just one of those villians you love to hate. Almost everything he says or does is pure gold on why you should kill him. Not going to spoil it as by the end of the game I had plenty of reasons to kill this guy whereas other games have just said he/she/it is evil kill them. For those who have no idea what DayZ is or are interested in buying it on what you've heard, then this review is here for you. In the short of it, don't buy it. DayZ is unfortunately a fiasco hidden under the guise of being an Early Access game. It has been stuck in development hell for about 4 years now with multiple delays, lack of communication, and a growing dissent among the player base as more features are removed (i.e. the actual zombies. Yes, that's right, the game labeled with "zombies" has removed its zombies, and when they are in, they don't actually work.)
The features that are added are as such: new guns (to lose on death) new clothes (to lose on death) and a new renderer (to see improved FPS on death.) This game adds filler content in an attempt to stall the playerbase as they scramble to push something like the years-waiting renderer that finally was added. Do not expect this game to update quickly or well for months or even years more.
This would be fine if we weren't stuck in Alpha 4 years later. Now game development takes time, but the pace of DayZ shows the devs may never reach the intended vision they thought they could create.

Undertale is a fantastic game deserving of all the praise that it has received since its release. Never before have I played a game that effectively made the player feel such a variety of emotions, ranging from hilarity and excitement, and at times I almost felt myself at the border of tears (this would embarass me, but luckily none of my real life friends know about my Steam account). The gameplay provides a unique twist on turn-based combat, as reflex-based gameplay is a large part of it, and the soundtrack is spectacular and always appropriately allocated to different parts of the game, so that boss battles feel epic and bombastic, and jokes are reinforced by the cheery, calm music in the background. The characters in this game are endlessly entertaining and loveable, all with their own distinguishable personalities, such as the goofy Papyrus or the head-strong Undyne.
Choices in Undertale truly do matter, and unlike those found in Telltale's games, actually occur during combat and carry significant consequences, instead of just having some random NPC chastise you for 5 minutes. As I'm sure you're aware, you don't need to kill anyone to finish the game, but this is made difficult due to the fact that you can only gain EXP by slaying monsters, and therefore cannot gain health or level up by being a pacifist. However, due to the characters' previously mentioned likeability, you will most likely want to struggle through the game with no EXP and spare them, which is where the genius of Undertale's choice system lies. Do you kill everyone you encounter to make the game easier and more forgiving, or do you stay determined (ha ha, get it?) and keep everyone alive? This genius twist on the regular, black and white choice systems found in modern games sets this game apart from the crowd, and makes it an experience you're sure to remember.
If I haven't made it clear already, I whole-heartedly recommend this game to anyone, and I promise that it will be a purchase you won't regret. Please don't let Undertale's somewhat "overzealous" fanbase frighten you away from trying this game, and give it a shot.

At first, I was totally biased against the game, thinking that it would be just as bad as the Sonic/FNAF fandom. Until I dove into the story and lore and found myself watching a walkthrough of it on YouTube. After buying the game via humble bundle and playing it for myself (Playing and watching a game are two different things) I personally still prefer Final Fantasy but I will say that Undertale is one of those special games that sounds out much like Chrono Trigger.
My only gripes on the game is that even though you're not supposed to kill any monsters you HP never increases which would be unfortunate to those who are not used to bullet hell kinds of games. I am aware that there are some items that can increase your max health besides leveling up but it would've been nice if the only things that did grow other than EXP and LV was HP.
Another gripe is... the Genocide Run. If you're going to do it, I can't stop you, but you will regret it as it will permanently change the true ending unless you uninstall and reinstall the game.
Overall, is this game the greatest thing since sliced bread? Well I'd like to say that but no.
But does that means it's a bad game? Absoluetly not. If you're curious on the story or lore of this game is trailing behind, pick up a copy. It will mean a lot to Toby Fox who was inspired from EarthBound.

:

:

　• Understanding the game’s plot requires commitment. If you are not ready for that commitment, the game will leave you with a bitter taste. But if you are willing to push through that, the game will reward you immensely.

You get so much more out of the game by discovering it on your own.

I haven’t sank the hours Into this like I have Fallout or Pokemon, but from listening to SOME song from this soundtrack every day since I beat it, to finding some new information about it every few days that adds new depths to the story, to the fandom which has some amazing animations and music, I have probably spent more time in this universe than any other RPG to date.
Each play though brought out different emotions for me, and I have to give FULL credit to Toby Fox for playing me like a fiddle the entire way through. They have an amazing grasp on predicting player behavior, and doing something as little as hiding an Easter egg, to as big as basing when you discover plot elements. He completely understands how gamers WORK, and I can say that the more video games you play, the more enjoyment you will get from this as it often will play with tropes.
One of the biggest things I have to praise it for is it’s morality system. Fallout as an example.. most of the time it’s a slider.. bad and good. Here it’s a lot more fluid. You killed an enemy? They won’t be an npc further along. Decisions matter, they take effect, and whether you are merciful or cruel WILL change how you experience the game.  I’m often reminded of why the Joker is such a great villain against Batman. It’s because he doesn’t do evil, he destroys what good even is. This game has a similar feeling. We all want to label ourselves as good people, that we wouldn’t do anything horrible weather for fun or curiosity, but this game asks “Is that really true?”
Personally, mercy made me laugh, made great friends, and the FEELS, oh my god! Cruelty made me feel evil and despicable. Not that my character was horrible, but that I myself as a person was bad. I couldn’t finish my third time because of this, because it would involve betraying everyone I had those good times with. And I’m currently at the state of being torn between finishing the game, or respecting these great friends you made. It’s a constant temptation to “finish the game”
Overall, if you let it, this game will get it’s hooks into you, and you will finally understand why you see all those animations of a child with a knife fighting a skeleton, what it represents, and why this is easily the best game of this year, even possibly deserving of all time. I can wholeheartedly say this is THE game I wish I could experience for the first time all over again, hands down.

Undertale is a fantastic game deserving of all the praise that it has received since its release. Never before have I played a game that effectively made the player feel such a variety of emotions, ranging from hilarity and excitement, and at times I almost felt myself at the border of tears (this would embarass me, but luckily none of my real life friends know about my Steam account). The gameplay provides a unique twist on turn-based combat, as reflex-based gameplay is a large part of it, and the soundtrack is spectacular and always appropriately allocated to different parts of the game, so that boss battles feel epic and bombastic, and jokes are reinforced by the cheery, calm music in the background. The characters in this game are endlessly entertaining and loveable, all with their own distinguishable personalities, such as the goofy Papyrus or the head-strong Undyne.
Choices in Undertale truly do matter, and unlike those found in Telltale's games, actually occur during combat and carry significant consequences, instead of just having some random NPC chastise you for 5 minutes. As I'm sure you're aware, you don't need to kill anyone to finish the game, but this is made difficult due to the fact that you can only gain EXP by slaying monsters, and therefore cannot gain health or level up by being a pacifist. However, due to the characters' previously mentioned likeability, you will most likely want to struggle through the game with no EXP and spare them, which is where the genius of Undertale's choice system lies. Do you kill everyone you encounter to make the game easier and more forgiving, or do you stay determined (ha ha, get it?) and keep everyone alive? This genius twist on the regular, black and white choice systems found in modern games sets this game apart from the crowd, and makes it an experience you're sure to remember.
If I haven't made it clear already, I whole-heartedly recommend this game to anyone, and I promise that it will be a purchase you won't regret. Please don't let Undertale's somewhat "overzealous" fanbase frighten you away from trying this game, and give it a shot.

Dayz has been stuck in the development Hell for THREE years. I understand that a game can have bugs, but the level that this game is at is unbelieveable. One example is that there was a SIX month period with zero zombies spawning and the animal ai was nonexistant (in my playing) for instance. I came upon a deer who was eating grass, I shoot and the deer despawned I found another deer it wasn't reacting to me standing inches away I hit it with an ax (makes ax hit noise) deer despawns.
What could be done to get it out of this Hell? Simple STOP adding new content and fix the bugs, issuses, complaints, and server issues you have now before you attempt to pile more on top of that. Because the more you toss on to a broken game the more broken it's going to be.

-The worlds largest deathmatch game

What makes a masterpiece “masterpiece”?
It may look like a simple question, but an actual answer isn't. We can list a lot of important things, but if we take multiple games considered a masterpiece, look at them one after another and remove from the list of “important things” things not applicable to at least one of these games we may end up with nothing. Isn't it strange? But it's only natural! There is no recipe for a masterpiece.
I'll only tell you one thing if you consider taking on this journey. Every your choice matter and it affects entire game world. Will you be merciful or cruel? It's completely up to you, but prepare for being judged.
Occasionally in my reviews I make a list of pros and cons to emphasize good sides and warn about the bad ones. However, in case of Undertale I can't find even one thing to list in a 'cons' part. At first, I thought to list at least lack of Steam “achievements” there, but then I realized that achievements often force us to do something we wouldn't normally think of doing. They divert us from things we would normally do. Usually it's fine, but not in case when you have to be true to yourself.
BTW, Tem got messed up a bit but still came to greet you.

Borderlands 2 is a pretty interesting take on FPS in this age of Call of Duty and Battlefield, and unique and quirky experience that I find myself coming back to just fun.  It operates a lot like the Diablo series, a vast open world with several different environments, random loot with rarity generated at fixed chances, and bosses that range from being simple and easy to those that truly epic.
While I have found it easy to have fun with the game on my own; the game world is charming and hilarious, though at time in a fairly vulgar sort of way, and the gameplay is quite fluid and easy to grasp, the place where it clearly excels is in the multiplayer aspect; nothing is more fun than getting a group of 4 together and then embarking on an epic (and typically silly) adventure in a world where everything wants to kill you, and you are more than willing to return the favor.
It should be noted that the game does have several bugs and glitches which do impact gameplay, but so far none that I have come across actually negatively affect gameplay; quite the opposite, most actually make the game far more enjoyable (and typically hilarious).
All and all, it is a very fun game, and with the price having come down from its initial released somewhat, it is well worth the money to pick up, though having friends to play it with should be a key factor in determining if it is right for you.

What makes a masterpiece “masterpiece”?
It may look like a simple question, but an actual answer isn't. We can list a lot of important things, but if we take multiple games considered a masterpiece, look at them one after another and remove from the list of “important things” things not applicable to at least one of these games we may end up with nothing. Isn't it strange? But it's only natural! There is no recipe for a masterpiece.
I'll only tell you one thing if you consider taking on this journey. Every your choice matter and it affects entire game world. Will you be merciful or cruel? It's completely up to you, but prepare for being judged.
Occasionally in my reviews I make a list of pros and cons to emphasize good sides and warn about the bad ones. However, in case of Undertale I can't find even one thing to list in a 'cons' part. At first, I thought to list at least lack of Steam “achievements” there, but then I realized that achievements often force us to do something we wouldn't normally think of doing. They divert us from things we would normally do. Usually it's fine, but not in case when you have to be true to yourself.
BTW, Tem got messed up a bit but still came to greet you.

The community.
Now, don't get me wrong. There are some great players I've met. But the number of great players who will help out and form alliances or who just follow simple rules are few compared to the number of people who get on just for the joy of utterly destroying everything on one server then hopping on the next server and repeating.
I don't get a lot of time to play games and my playtime is limited to Friday nights and Saturdays, and sometimes that is even iffy. Pretty decent hardcore survival game, with a decided slant on 'Dog Eat dog'. I do quite like the variety of weaponry, but find it really hard - to - near impossible to play solo...the only way I was finally able to get ahead was join up with someone, and even then we both only established a base with the MASSIVE help of two nice fellas (now neighbours). Which brings me to a main LIKE of Rust, group anarchist behaviour. I have read of many that discount this game because they find peeps only wanna smack down everyone they see, but I find, at least on the server I play, that that is not always true. I have spoken with quite a few of my neighbours, all good behaviour and good will so far...yes I have been jacked and molested and griefed, but what do you expect? All in all, looking forward to expanding the base and gaining the upper hand when faced with threats.

It's a great concept and a good game at heart. That said... The fact that you are either forced into forming a group with people you don't know who might stab you in the back at any moment to withstand established geared clans, coordinate with a good group of friends to survive for the same reason or be forced into hosting a server to play single player or just with friends but then lose any potential element of random enemies forces an extremely hostile, angsty and toxic barrier to entry. Especially for new players. Newly spawned with nothing on you? Doesn't matter, you're a target on sight. Just trying to learn the game? Doesn't matter, target on sight. I wanna love the game so much but I've seen so many people get screwed and rage quit and then I've bucketed so many hours on multiple servers myself just to have it all torn away by some random person with no potential to recover. Perhaps I'll try again later on, but for now, I'll try other survival games with a tad more reward/thrive sense to them.

This game is brilliant. There's no other way of putting it. This game is fun in single player, and super-fun in co-op.
Gameplay:
- There is nothing more satisfying in perhaps any other game than seeing a stream of CRITICAL damage indicators streaming off a psycopath/midget/fat person/robot's head.
- The variety in guns, grenade mods and shields is unprecedented. In co-op, you'll constantly be comparing your gear to that of your friends, trying out their weapons, trading weapons. All of the gun types are fun to use - especially revolvers. I swear they're magical or something...
- The game is a well-made hybrid of FPS and RPG. You can give your character (one of 4 classes in the base game, with 2 more in the GOTY edition) abilities and level them up, enabling you to use better weapons, grenade mods and shield.
Story:
- Ridiculous humour that works - that about sums it up. You'll encounter crazy situations and missions, but you'll just accept it.
- There's an awful lot of it. The main story missions don't often feel recycled, presenting you with different challenges every time. There's plenty of voice acting in both the main campaign and side quests, whcih is impressive considering the volume of these.
- There are a fair few unexpected plot twists, but it usually doesn't feel dragged out.
- Handsome Jack is both formidable and funny. He's a truly worthy nemesis.
- Claptrap makes you want to kill him within 20 seconds of meeting him. I've yet to hear a voice on par with how annoying Claptrap's is.
Graphics and Sound:
- If you crank the settings up, this game looks pretty nice. The cartoony style means it also runs well on lower-end PCs without looking muddy.
- If you have an NVIDIA card, you're in for a treat. There are cloth and liquid PhysX, and you can cut the cloth with bullets. Debris flies off the environment and bounces off things. It makes hectic situations look awesome.
- Gun sounds and voice acting are great, everything else is generally OK, not too special.
- I've had a couple of unexpected slowdowns and 2-second freezes. This shouldn't happen on my PC really, but I suspect it's PhysX related. I keep PhysX on Medium or High, though, because it's great.
Multiplayer:
- The game has 2-4 player co-op multiplayer. All missions work in both single-player and co-op, with enemy volume and health scaling to keep difficulty constant.
- You can start duels for loot with your fellow players, in the event of disagreement.
- Pretty seamless. Invite players to your game from the main menu, and they drop into your world with all your mission progression.
- I'd advise that everyone has a different class, otherwise you'll all die at the same time and respawn back at a checkpoint, which gets annoying.
- For best experience, everyone in your co-op session should be within about a 10-level range of each other, or the underlevelled character will need reviving constantly.
Summary:
This game should be compulsory. My life is complete, now that I can shoot midgets with shotguns and find cool loot in portaloos. My advice: buy GOTY - you'll want all the Borderlands you can get.

This game is brilliant. There's no other way of putting it. This game is fun in single player, and super-fun in co-op.
Gameplay:
- There is nothing more satisfying in perhaps any other game than seeing a stream of CRITICAL damage indicators streaming off a psycopath/midget/fat person/robot's head.
- The variety in guns, grenade mods and shields is unprecedented. In co-op, you'll constantly be comparing your gear to that of your friends, trying out their weapons, trading weapons. All of the gun types are fun to use - especially revolvers. I swear they're magical or something...
- The game is a well-made hybrid of FPS and RPG. You can give your character (one of 4 classes in the base game, with 2 more in the GOTY edition) abilities and level them up, enabling you to use better weapons, grenade mods and shield.
Story:
- Ridiculous humour that works - that about sums it up. You'll encounter crazy situations and missions, but you'll just accept it.
- There's an awful lot of it. The main story missions don't often feel recycled, presenting you with different challenges every time. There's plenty of voice acting in both the main campaign and side quests, whcih is impressive considering the volume of these.
- There are a fair few unexpected plot twists, but it usually doesn't feel dragged out.
- Handsome Jack is both formidable and funny. He's a truly worthy nemesis.
- Claptrap makes you want to kill him within 20 seconds of meeting him. I've yet to hear a voice on par with how annoying Claptrap's is.
Graphics and Sound:
- If you crank the settings up, this game looks pretty nice. The cartoony style means it also runs well on lower-end PCs without looking muddy.
- If you have an NVIDIA card, you're in for a treat. There are cloth and liquid PhysX, and you can cut the cloth with bullets. Debris flies off the environment and bounces off things. It makes hectic situations look awesome.
- Gun sounds and voice acting are great, everything else is generally OK, not too special.
- I've had a couple of unexpected slowdowns and 2-second freezes. This shouldn't happen on my PC really, but I suspect it's PhysX related. I keep PhysX on Medium or High, though, because it's great.
Multiplayer:
- The game has 2-4 player co-op multiplayer. All missions work in both single-player and co-op, with enemy volume and health scaling to keep difficulty constant.
- You can start duels for loot with your fellow players, in the event of disagreement.
- Pretty seamless. Invite players to your game from the main menu, and they drop into your world with all your mission progression.
- I'd advise that everyone has a different class, otherwise you'll all die at the same time and respawn back at a checkpoint, which gets annoying.
- For best experience, everyone in your co-op session should be within about a 10-level range of each other, or the underlevelled character will need reviving constantly.
Summary:
This game should be compulsory. My life is complete, now that I can shoot midgets with shotguns and find cool loot in portaloos. My advice: buy GOTY - you'll want all the Borderlands you can get.

Right.... Imma try to make an ACTUAL review instead of fanboying the heck out. Ahem...
Story/Plot: 9/10
The plot of Undertale follows multiple routes based on morality, like a less crappy Shadow the Hedgehog. The pacifist route, the main story, follows Frisk, a fallen human, as he/she explores the vast Underground and tries to find a way out. Simple enough? Sorta. The story likes to break to fourth wall, and I have a soft spot for when media does that. I guess that's why I pray to Deadpool every night. From remembering what you did in a previous playtrough, to acting like save files are a different continuity. It also has a nice switch in moods throught the story, but I'll get to that later. The only thing that doesn't make this a ten is even though you're STILL amazed on your second or third playthrough, I've played the pacifist route 10 times, and it can get boring knowing literally almost everything about the game. The genocide route follows right after Frisk fell, to where Chara, the first human to fall before Frisk, posesses them to get revenge. It's quite self explanitory, just kill everything. However, if the misery of killing characters you likely just befiended in the pacifist route wasn't enough, you have to face one of the hardest bosses in gaming. It IS slightly satisfying to beat it at last, but let's face it, everyone who did that route and beat it still has nightmares to this day.
Characters: 8.5/10
The chracters in this game are some of the most memorable in RPG history. And compared to gmaes like Final Fantasy and Kingdom Hearts, that says alot. They range from Papyrus and Sans, the funny and quirky, to Undyne and Asgore, the serious and battle-ready, to Flowey the Flower, the demonic antagonist we all feel bad for after beating the game. The only reason this is an 8.5 is because sometimes characters like Undyne can be a bit... Too crazy. I mean, for Christ's sake, she burns her house down trying to make noodles! What I really like about the normal enemies is that they're not just grind fodder. They have personalities and character traits too.
Mood: 11/10
Hop onto the Feels Train! Choo-choo! Throught Undertale, the feel of the game constantly changes, which I like. It's one of the only games in the world that makes me actually cry. From the goofy mood of Snowdin Town, to the peaceful feel of Waterfall, to the I-don't-even-know-what of Hotland. Then there are the sad parts, which are honestly the best. The Chara and Asriel story, the Asriel fight, and the Memory statue are good examples. I don't care how much of a big boy you feel like, you WILL cry at this game like killjoys at The Black Parade. I even nominated this game for the "I'm not crying, I just got something in my eye" award.
Gameplay: 8.5/10
The gameplay has the normal elements you would see in a bullet-hell RPG. You can fight (Note: NEVER USE EVER IF YOU WANT TO ACTUALLY BEAT THE GAME!), Act, use an item, or Spare, the most useful tool in the game. In certain boss fights, however, the entire genre of the game can change. It could be a platformer one second, then the next it's a topdown shooter! This type of diversity really makes the game good. However, there's no fast way to travel besides a boat you don't have access to until two thirds into the game. Not to mention, like the story, it can get really boring after many many many playthroughs, like a song after you've heard it several million times.
Soundtrack: Infinity/10
Speaking of songs, Undertale has the greatest soundtrack ever, which explains why it costs as much as the game itself. With over 100 tunes on the track, you'll be jamming out to Megalovania, Bergentruckung, and Hopes and Dreams, while crying to His theme and the Undertale main theme. From the jazzy Death by Glamour, to the intense Spear of Justice, You'll be listening to all the songs over and over and over.
Overall: 10/10
While the fandom is questionable, and the graphics look like an NES game, the characters, emotion, story, and replayablity are superb, and I've gone far enough to lable it as my favorite game of all time. Good on ya, Toby Fox, good on ya. Godspeed in the future, my friend. I really reccomend you buy this game at once. Sell your dog, sell your bed, sell your freaking house, just buy this game. You will not regret it.

Right.... Imma try to make an ACTUAL review instead of fanboying the heck out. Ahem...
Story/Plot: 9/10
The plot of Undertale follows multiple routes based on morality, like a less crappy Shadow the Hedgehog. The pacifist route, the main story, follows Frisk, a fallen human, as he/she explores the vast Underground and tries to find a way out. Simple enough? Sorta. The story likes to break to fourth wall, and I have a soft spot for when media does that. I guess that's why I pray to Deadpool every night. From remembering what you did in a previous playtrough, to acting like save files are a different continuity. It also has a nice switch in moods throught the story, but I'll get to that later. The only thing that doesn't make this a ten is even though you're STILL amazed on your second or third playthrough, I've played the pacifist route 10 times, and it can get boring knowing literally almost everything about the game. The genocide route follows right after Frisk fell, to where Chara, the first human to fall before Frisk, posesses them to get revenge. It's quite self explanitory, just kill everything. However, if the misery of killing characters you likely just befiended in the pacifist route wasn't enough, you have to face one of the hardest bosses in gaming. It IS slightly satisfying to beat it at last, but let's face it, everyone who did that route and beat it still has nightmares to this day.
Characters: 8.5/10
The chracters in this game are some of the most memorable in RPG history. And compared to gmaes like Final Fantasy and Kingdom Hearts, that says alot. They range from Papyrus and Sans, the funny and quirky, to Undyne and Asgore, the serious and battle-ready, to Flowey the Flower, the demonic antagonist we all feel bad for after beating the game. The only reason this is an 8.5 is because sometimes characters like Undyne can be a bit... Too crazy. I mean, for Christ's sake, she burns her house down trying to make noodles! What I really like about the normal enemies is that they're not just grind fodder. They have personalities and character traits too.
Mood: 11/10
Hop onto the Feels Train! Choo-choo! Throught Undertale, the feel of the game constantly changes, which I like. It's one of the only games in the world that makes me actually cry. From the goofy mood of Snowdin Town, to the peaceful feel of Waterfall, to the I-don't-even-know-what of Hotland. Then there are the sad parts, which are honestly the best. The Chara and Asriel story, the Asriel fight, and the Memory statue are good examples. I don't care how much of a big boy you feel like, you WILL cry at this game like killjoys at The Black Parade. I even nominated this game for the "I'm not crying, I just got something in my eye" award.
Gameplay: 8.5/10
The gameplay has the normal elements you would see in a bullet-hell RPG. You can fight (Note: NEVER USE EVER IF YOU WANT TO ACTUALLY BEAT THE GAME!), Act, use an item, or Spare, the most useful tool in the game. In certain boss fights, however, the entire genre of the game can change. It could be a platformer one second, then the next it's a topdown shooter! This type of diversity really makes the game good. However, there's no fast way to travel besides a boat you don't have access to until two thirds into the game. Not to mention, like the story, it can get really boring after many many many playthroughs, like a song after you've heard it several million times.
Soundtrack: Infinity/10
Speaking of songs, Undertale has the greatest soundtrack ever, which explains why it costs as much as the game itself. With over 100 tunes on the track, you'll be jamming out to Megalovania, Bergentruckung, and Hopes and Dreams, while crying to His theme and the Undertale main theme. From the jazzy Death by Glamour, to the intense Spear of Justice, You'll be listening to all the songs over and over and over.
Overall: 10/10
While the fandom is questionable, and the graphics look like an NES game, the characters, emotion, story, and replayablity are superb, and I've gone far enough to lable it as my favorite game of all time. Good on ya, Toby Fox, good on ya. Godspeed in the future, my friend. I really reccomend you buy this game at once. Sell your dog, sell your bed, sell your freaking house, just buy this game. You will not regret it.

I could write a whole bunch of nonsense about how much potential this game has/had, but that wouldn't provide you with any useful information on whether to even consider purchasing this game or not. So I'm just going to tell you the plain truth about why this game is a huge disappointment for me and will be for you. I have 470+ hours in this game. Trust me.
The screenshots look promising. Decent graphics, interesting environment. But when you launch the game and get to the main menu (IF you get to the main menu), an astonishingly long waiting time awaits you if you decide to load up the servers. It took my €1800 gaming PC roughly five minutes to load 300 servers. Your game will almost completely freeze when it's loading servers. The Filter system to find servers to your preferences is worthless. You can't select "Only show non-password servers", there is no option to only search for 3rd person servers and there is no option to search for "Only Private/Public hives".
Finally found a server that looks good? Join in, spend about five minutes waiting for your PC to get it's ♥♥♥♥ together while you're looking at a grey, blocky environment at literally 1 FPS. Bonus points awarded if you get hit (and get killed) by a zombie you can't see coming at 1 FPS.
When luck is on your side, your FPS will rise to a steady 20. Your goal then is to find food since your character is always hungry when he spawns. The thirst will kick in about 10 minutes later. I don't know what on earth they did to the loot spawning system, but finding food is impossible. If you do manage to find any food at all, it will be canned. This requires a can opener to open. Which are rare. All due to the horrendous loot spawning system.
I could go on and on about how hard it is to find pretty much anything in this game, but I will spare you from that.
The UI is confusing and broken. The primary use of Rags for example is to bandage yourself up. Yet if you right click a rag, the first option is NOT to bandage yourself. The option to actually bandage yourself isn't called "Bandage", but rather: "Use". And trust me: you'll be bleeding loads of times because actually hitting a zombie with say, an axe, is extremely difficult. That shouldn't be the case.
There is a hot bar which - you guessed it - only works half the time. Want it to work? Mash some buttons and hope for the best. There's a good chance your character will simply put the weapon away again right after you equip it. Not to mention there is an even bigger chance the weapon disappears. Just like that. Add a chance of dropping dead by falling a few inches or walking up stairs to that and you've got a recipe for a disastrous game. Imagine spending hours upon hours to get geared up just a little bit, only to drop dead for walking up stairs. It's absurd.
The controls are confusing. The game consists 99% out of running, yet running is a mission on it's own due to plain annoying running mechanics. The whole game feels clunky.
I wouldn't play this game if I got paid to play it. It's been almost three years since they released the Alpha for this. (Released. Not "started development") so it's way too late for me to get some sort of a refund.
There is simply too much broken in this game to contain in one review. Even to just remember.
Please don't buy this game. For two reasons. Save yourself a headache and don't fund developers like this.

I could write a whole bunch of nonsense about how much potential this game has/had, but that wouldn't provide you with any useful information on whether to even consider purchasing this game or not. So I'm just going to tell you the plain truth about why this game is a huge disappointment for me and will be for you. I have 470+ hours in this game. Trust me.
The screenshots look promising. Decent graphics, interesting environment. But when you launch the game and get to the main menu (IF you get to the main menu), an astonishingly long waiting time awaits you if you decide to load up the servers. It took my €1800 gaming PC roughly five minutes to load 300 servers. Your game will almost completely freeze when it's loading servers. The Filter system to find servers to your preferences is worthless. You can't select "Only show non-password servers", there is no option to only search for 3rd person servers and there is no option to search for "Only Private/Public hives".
Finally found a server that looks good? Join in, spend about five minutes waiting for your PC to get it's ♥♥♥♥ together while you're looking at a grey, blocky environment at literally 1 FPS. Bonus points awarded if you get hit (and get killed) by a zombie you can't see coming at 1 FPS.
When luck is on your side, your FPS will rise to a steady 20. Your goal then is to find food since your character is always hungry when he spawns. The thirst will kick in about 10 minutes later. I don't know what on earth they did to the loot spawning system, but finding food is impossible. If you do manage to find any food at all, it will be canned. This requires a can opener to open. Which are rare. All due to the horrendous loot spawning system.
I could go on and on about how hard it is to find pretty much anything in this game, but I will spare you from that.
The UI is confusing and broken. The primary use of Rags for example is to bandage yourself up. Yet if you right click a rag, the first option is NOT to bandage yourself. The option to actually bandage yourself isn't called "Bandage", but rather: "Use". And trust me: you'll be bleeding loads of times because actually hitting a zombie with say, an axe, is extremely difficult. That shouldn't be the case.
There is a hot bar which - you guessed it - only works half the time. Want it to work? Mash some buttons and hope for the best. There's a good chance your character will simply put the weapon away again right after you equip it. Not to mention there is an even bigger chance the weapon disappears. Just like that. Add a chance of dropping dead by falling a few inches or walking up stairs to that and you've got a recipe for a disastrous game. Imagine spending hours upon hours to get geared up just a little bit, only to drop dead for walking up stairs. It's absurd.
The controls are confusing. The game consists 99% out of running, yet running is a mission on it's own due to plain annoying running mechanics. The whole game feels clunky.
I wouldn't play this game if I got paid to play it. It's been almost three years since they released the Alpha for this. (Released. Not "started development") so it's way too late for me to get some sort of a refund.
There is simply too much broken in this game to contain in one review. Even to just remember.
Please don't buy this game. For two reasons. Save yourself a headache and don't fund developers like this.

Upon further information being presented to me about Undertale, I decided to write a completely new review. Here it is.
Undertale is a pretty decent game with good dialogue, an interesting take on RPG combat, and a good soundtrack. However, it is marred by several design flaws and some technical errors that ruined my experience.
You can get all the way through the game attempting a True Pacifist ending, and still not get it. Why? Because you didn't backtrack. There is no indication that you need to backtrack to a certain someone's house before fighting the final boss. As a direct result, on my first playthrough, I was fooled into thinking that the neutral ending was the Pacifist ending because the game never presented any information to me suggesting that I was missing something.
Similarly, the lack of direction caused me to make a run-altering error in my first playthrough, because I was getting no feedback on what my actions were doing. This occurred during the
fight. I tried using various Act commands, but none of them seemed to be doing anything. So, I tried lowering the boss' healthbar to a sliver. And then I got the boss to half health. Whoops, I suddenly did 10x damage for no evident reason. "Congratulations, you have to start over!"
Let's move on to the neutral ending. Even if you never kill any of the game's bosses, very few of them show more than one character trait, because they barely have any screen time, UNLESS you do the Pacifist route backtracking, which, again, there is no indication for.
Moving on to technical errors, the Genocide route simply didn't work for me. There is a certain number of enemies that you need to kill in a certain area, which I tried doing, but in the first area, the last enemy never appeared, even after I spent a goodly portion of time running around trying to make it appear.
Lastly, the final boss is a joke. The fight is designed to look impossible, but it's incredibly easy, due to how long it takes to die in that fight. What happened to the challenge?
If I hadn't actively avoided information about this game before I played it, I might have enjoyed it. But because I didn't spoil it for myself, I missed out on important information that isn't provided inside the game, causing a very unrewarding experience that was not worth the six dollars I spent on it.

Rust is a refreshing take on the Survival game genre.
I've only had the opportunity to experience the game so far with a couple of friends, and although I know that there is a lot more to enjoy about the game in servers that are more populated the fact that I've enjoyed myself nonetheless has really impacted the way I feel about the game.
I remember hearing about Rust years ago when there were still zombies and the game was graphically still at it's beginning stages.  I've never been a huge fan of zombie survival games, and was pleasantly surprised that they were removed from the game before I had a chance to actually play it.  I feel that the lack of zombies really brings out a realistic touch to Rust that many other games in the survival genre seem to lack. TL;DR: Now, I usually don't write reviews, but this game deserved it. See the hours I spent on this game? That's how much replayability it has. Of course, Undertale has its flaws and isn't perfect in any way, but it's a memorable game and is worth the ten dollars.
Long Review:
This game is simply amazing. As I said before, it is not perfect in any way, but it's very well thought out. This game is special, it really is, and I believe you should experience it for yourself. I'll try not to spoil too much of the game.
Combat:
This game is like any other bullet-hell, you try not to get hit by bullets. However, the bullet-hell system is very interesting and unique.In the game, you have a SOUL. This SOUL is what you use to play the bullet-hell sequences. There's multiple colors, green, blue, purple, etc. Red is your main color. Now, this "color" system may just seem like a customizable design chocie for you, but it really isn't. Each soul has different play styles, like the green soul for example. It uses a shield-based system instead of the classic dodging bullets that appear on screen.
Story:
The story in this game is so simple at first glance, but if you dig deep enough, it's heart-warming. Hell, you don't even have to kill anyone in this game if you wanted to go all goody-two-shoes. When you first get into the game, you play as a human, a child who has fallen down Mount Ebott. As the story progresses, you meet a lot of lovable characters that you'll inevitable be attatched to. Not to mention, there are plenty of easter eggs around that are very well hidden. However, you should listen to the tutoriel's advice. (Don't worry, I know I spelled tutorial wrong.)
Characters:
There is so much variety I can't even begin to explain. Every "monster" is different in its own way, and they all have unique personalities. Of course, like any other RPGs, there are bosses in this game as well, but these bosses are special, as you can actually communicate to them. The monsters you meet in this game are lovable, to say the least, and they are all charming in their own way.
Soundtrack:
Ah, the topic I've been waiting to talk about. Overall, the soundtrack is absolute gold. There's even songs that play during songs, it's amazing how well they were put together! I love each and every song in this game's OST, it's just that wonderful. The songs fit very well to the scenarios and boss fights that you'll get to in the game, and it's just beautiful.
Overall:
Undertale is a charming game in its own way, and it's well worth the ten dollars. Seriously, for a game this amazing, I can't believe it's this cheap. The characters are well thought out, the story is pretty interesting, the combat has the right amount of difficulty, and the humor in this game is just great. You as the character encounter a lot of bumps along the way, but despite everything, it's still you. Toby Fox, you annoying dog, you did a wonderful job of making such a wonderful game.

Undertale is a great game. Its dodging-based combat minigames especially rely on that concept. Boss battles consistently subverted my expectations, even after I thought I’d figured everything out, but even run-of-the-mill random encounters are closely intertwined with storytelling and worldbuilding. Every enemy has a unique personality expressed both through combat and non-combative options. In my pacifist run I ended up talking to a lot of monsters, giving out hugs, and even (and especially) flirting with them to avoid killing them. In order to spare a monster that wanted to flirt but didn’t want to admit it, I had to “get close but not too close.” That option changed the rules of combat so that I had to narrowly dodge incoming projectiles… until the monster blushed so much that it stopped fighting.“
Undertale has to be a game, and that’s the key to its brilliance.
There are tons of jokes that appeal to internet nerds, and I often felt like Undertale was talking directly to me, like it knew what I was thinking. An anime-loving character’s “selfie,” for example, is actually a picture of a garbage can with pink sparkle filters over it (and speaking from experience, this is very accurate). I especially love Undertale’s humor when it has something to say, however subtle. I entered a snail race (called Thundersnail) and was told to press Z repeatedly to encourage my snail to win. I spammed Z until she burst into flames, and the Thundersnail organizer told me that “all that pressure to succeed really got to her.” It was, like many of Undertale’s one-off jokes, extremely relatable — and knowing and predicting its audience is one of Undertale’s biggest strengths.
Monsters Are People Too
Undertale’s writing is consistently funny, but it can also be touching. Small, semi-hidden notes and dialogue enrich the world and build on an already compelling story of humanity and morality. A favorite was a series of “echo flowers” in a beautiful, ethereal hallway that repeated snippets of an overhead conversation. A monster didn’t want to share her greatest wish — that one day she would climb the mountain that traps all the monsters underground and look out at the world — for fear of being laughed at, and although her friend promised they wouldn’t, the friend ended up laughing anyway. It was silly, until the last flower repeated: “Sorry, it’s just funny… That’s my wish too.”
Exploring Waterfall in Undertale
Exploring Waterfall in Undertale
02:41
Experiencing the depth of the monsters’ hopes and dreams is crucial to Undertale’s exploration of morality, personhood, and conflict. Different monsters talk about each other in front of you, so once I met them I got to discover who they actually were, as opposed to what their reputations suggested. Most of the main characters are also very well developed with consistent personalities across different dialogue and story routes. It made it hard for me to summon the aggression to attack any of them — and that’s precisely the point. When I was trying to go for a more violent run, fighting monsters I’d once flirted with made Undertale’s message about humanity hit even harder.
Determination
Some fights can be frustrating or even tedious, however, at least at first. In a violent playthrough, I had to grind quite a bit to meet certain story requirements and grew tired of it after a while. Fighting enemy after enemy replaced the puzzles in the peaceful runs, however, and the tradeoff felt very balanced and ultimately meaningful to the story. I also found myself trudging back through areas I had already cleared just so I could beat a boss or get an item, and while it was absolutely worth it in the end, I wasn't terribly excited to do it. At one point I had run out of gold and needed to buy healing items, and the only shop that would buy items off of me was about a 10 minute walk away. (The other shopkeepers don't buy items because they don't want your trash.)
Undertale's Ties to Anime Fandom - IGN Anime Club
Undertale's Ties to Anime Fandom - IGN Anime Club

That said, I don't regret any of the extra time I spent walking around, because I got to find things like Thundersnail and the echo flowers. It's the little details that make Undertale so special, and I wanted to see them all. Every one of them feels deliberate — long sections of dialogue at the beginning and certain fights can be slow, but they are necessary for establishing the characters in a way that only games can do. In a different run, underwhelming boss battles turn mournful because of what one-hit KOs imply in the world. It was Undertale's ongoing, well-woven theme of determination that kept me playing and replaying.
Even though the art isn't always pretty — it's often ugly, even — Undertale is an incredibly expressive game from start to finish, making up for visual limitations with excellent music and charming animations. It's also gender- and sexuality-inclusive in a very real, noticeable way. Every small detail reveals an intimate understanding of its audience, and that is essential to what makes Undertale’s commentary on personhood so effective.
The Verdict
It's hard to express just how much I adore Undertale without spoiling anything significant, but that's what I love about it. It tells its story in such a dynamic way, and with such a great understanding of the RPG player’s mindset, that it couldn’t have been told in any other way. It's a masterfully crafted experience that I won't forget any time soon.  IGN Logo

This indie game has become a legend of sorts. With a dedicated fanbase to match, and packed with enough content, lore, addictiveness and all the bits that assemble an extraordinary video game, Undertale will be remembered throughout the ages.
Now, before we begin, what is Undertale? Well simply, it’s the story of a lost human child, who finds herself trapped in an underground world, and she must find a way out. Kind of sets up the basis for a fairly modern RPG setting, right? But it accomplishes so much more than a simple “Enter da dungeon, kill da mobs, acquire increasingly powerful loot, encounter even stronger bosses, and save the day” game. Your avatar is a little girl. She’s not some badass knight in spiked armour, wielding a sword/axe/spear/staff, but if she gets violent, which the game allows you to do, things go down a dark, spiralling path that may be discomforting at its most. In short, Undertale is a colossal triumph, because not only is it brilliant, funny, and engaging, but it also demonstrates how unique and amazing indie games can be. That’s not to say that the bigger game companies today aren’t talented enough to make their own heavy-hitters (here’s looking at you, Bethesda and Telltale Games).
Anyway, let’s get down to business:
Story-wise, Undertale stars the human girl, trapped in the underworld, trying to find a way to the surface. As her journey progresses, we come across and entire ensemble of colorful, funny and memorable characters. There’s the mommy-goat figure, named Toriel, who wishes to take in the human child as her own, there’s the hilarious skeleton brothers, Sans and Papyrus, with their cartoony hijnks and skeleton-related puns that ought to tickle your funny bone, there’s the cool Undyne, with her grand plans of capturing a human, and many more. The main antagonistic force opposing the human child is a small flower named Flowey, who attempts to kill her from the very start! This is achieved with little “love pellets”, which are in reality, bullets that narrow the player’s health to one! Luckily, Toriel saves us in the nick of time and shoots a fireball right into the aforementioned flower’s face, effectively sending him flying away.
You’ll notice that it’s not just the aforementioned batch of characters, but also every single foe in the game, each with their own ambitions and personalities. In a way, they are no different from us humans; they just want to live and enjoy life. This further encourages the option to spare the monsters, which evokes positive reactions from other NPCs.
Now, gameplay is essentially a giant bullet-hell fest. During most sequences, you are enclosed in a small box, where your avatar is turned into a heart, which represents your soul. In order to win, you must dodge every projectile sent your way. This isn’t necessarily easy, and living up to its name as a bullet hell title, that small box is filled with deadly objects that will chip away at your health if you are not careful to dodge them. There are certain patterns to each attack, and you must memorise them carefully. Once you get the hang of it, the gameplay is extremely addictive and fast-paced
The graphics of Undertale retain a pixilated format, equivalent to those of old Nintendo games. Some will point out that the graphics aren’t up to par with the rest of the game, but I digress. The pixilated graphics perfectly suit Undertale, making it stand out from other games that use the same art style.
The soundtrack…oh god, the soundtrack...it’s beyond anything you’ve heard before. Whether you are walking through the woods, or a monster village, or a field of snow poffs, or a cave illuminated with glowing mushrooms, the soundtrack sets the mood and adds an atmosphere of beauty to an already enthralling adventure. During the comedic events of the game, the music becomes silly and flamboyant, to the point where you have little else to do but chuckle. The music is a key feature of Undertale, and makes you want to stand up and cheer, because it is THAT damn good, and sets an example of how amazing game soundtracks can be.
One more thing about Undertale is its ability to be funny. The humor often dabbles in the realms of the internet, and twists long-dead memes into fresh and original jokes, one-liners, and puns. Especially bone-related puns, and there are a ton of funny bones within Undertale’s body, packed with comedic calcium. From an annoying mutt that prevents you from acquiring a legendary fruit by taking up your inventory space, to the mischievous antics of the skeleton twins Papyrus and Sans, you will find few other games that will make you spit out your spaghetti with laughter then this game.
To wrap up this review, would I recommend this game? Well, would a mouse patiently wait for a slice of cheese that has become incrusted within a purple crystal? Would a sea-dwelling onion beg you to notice him? Would that dog playing poker lose, even when it’s playing by itself?! If all of those fill you up with determination, than yes! I highly recommend this game! Anyway, I can sit here and talk about this game’s greatness, but that’s absolutely nothing compared to when you, yourself, play it. You will simply have to buy it and taste the epicness that is Undertale.
And remember, no matter how you look at it…
Or whatever you make of it…
It’s still a snow poff.

I decided to go back and give this game a more serious review, because it really deserves it.
I ended up getting this game in November (around Thanksgiving) of last year, and ever since I've still enjoyed it to this day. Undertale is a game that revolves around a "choice" system, and the choices you make end up varying the game's ending. As you might have heard, there's 3 main endings - a neutral run, a pacifist run and a genocide run. It follows a sort of puzzle RPG styles while also having a bullet hell style mechanic for combat, which I ended up enjoying. Figuring out how to spare certain characters was a good part of the game for me and it was pretty interesting. Of course, the plot is incredibly well-written. At the surface, it isn't anything too special, but going deep into it (especially when you do the Pacifist/Genocide runs), there's a lot of twists and turns throughout the game that I won't spoil to keep it's integrity. With the different runs and endings of the game combined with the fun puzzle RPG/bullet hell gameplay, I was able to go back to this game plenty of times since getting it, and to be quite frank I don't regret it. While there are games I still enjoy going back to and playing, this is probably the first that's ever had a real impact on me and given me something to follow.
Sure, the fanbase can be pretty trashy and the game's pretty much everywhere at this point, but if you don't let that spoil the experience for you, then I can easily recommend picking this one up. It's an easy 10/10 from me, with the only real complaint I have being the visuals.
P.S. Alphys is love, Alphys is life.

Sure there are huge zerg style clans that can easily ruin your day but what do you expect from a game like Rust? Being a solo player like myself can be especially frustrating at times but with a little bit of brainpower and effort you will soon have yourself set up to defend yourself well enough against attackers. As far as optimization goes, there is some work to be done there but I myself have a average rig and on good settings im running at around 50-60 fps wich isn't too bad. Most of the negative reviews I've read just seem like salty kids who got raided one too many times. It would be nice to see some more PVE content but that isnt too much of a downfall for me as I really do enjoy playing but I would also like to see some more variety with regards to clothes and armor as they are quite limited.  I am currently playing solo on a vanilla server with a population of around 250 players online at a time, it has taken me two days to set up a metal base, with huge walls around and I have managed to defend myself against groups of up to 5 people at a time without much hassel. All in all I would reccomend this game as it is loads of fun but if you are a keyboard samurai and dont like having to start fresh a few times before you become comfortable in the game, then I suggest you give this a skip and try something like the Sims instead.

If you have played any game of the MOTHER series, then you will enjoy Undertale. Its quirky, turn-based, has great forms of replayability, and it has a great plot. However, it does have a few flaws. It recreates things that originated from MOTHER, and it actually outright COPIED something from MOTHER, that being Venus' voice for the song "Ghost Fight (I think its called)" and "Dummy!" He probably did get rights, and it may be cool that she's in there, but he still flat out ripped it from MOTHER 2/EarthBound.
First things first: The Protagonist. He suffers from "Silent Protagonism," like the main characters of MOTHER. He also has a striped shirt and jeans, like the main characters of MOTHER. He also has a blank expression on his face, like the main characters of MOTHER. This isn't a bad thing, but it isn't original, and again, not being original isn't a bad thing.
Secondly: The Humor. The humor in Undertale is easily defined as "quirky," like MOTHER's, but MOTHER's humor is more child friendly and more 90's-ish while Undertale is more classified as teen humor and GenZ-ish, considering the game made a smoking refrence and has anime and social media refrences. But its still quirky.
Thirdly: It breaks the 4th wall. I won't spoil TOO much of the story, but there is a character named sans (no capitalization) who knows how many times you have died in a certain type of "mode." There is another character named Flowey who knows he's in a game and says that there is "someone who is too cowardly to take this path, and that certain someone is watching us right now." This is obviously hinting YouTube.
Fourthly: The Music. The music is a mixture of catchy, dark, funny, and serious, and has a similar soundfont to that of a SNES, the same console that EarthBound was on. The charactaristics can also apply to the MOTHER series, considering it has serious, yet funny moments, like Undertale. The song names are even refrences to MOTHER songs. "Battle against a true hero" got its name from Earthbound/MOTHER 2's battle themes. Example: "Battle Against a Weird Opponent" "Battle Against a Mobile Opponent." "Megalovania" was first created by Toby in an EarthBound Halloween Hack, and was recreated in 2 games: "MOTHER: Cognitive Dissonance" and "Homestuck." Undertale's Megalovania is the 4th Megalovania used in a game, and I can garuntee you, it won't be the last.
Being a Fuzzy Pickler (MOTHER fan), I love Undertale, and it really got the recognition it deserves. It's just that it's TOO popular, and I think you know why, and some things in it aren't completely original, but they're still great. Undertale gets my rating of a 7/10. I love this game, and if you don't, thats fine, just don't go batshit crazy about it if you hate it.

An unprecedented emotional experience.
The game has a pretty unique relationship with what is known as the “forth wall”, not just making jokes with it, but even making game mechanics and plot points with it in baffling ways. Every trope relating to RPGs and anything that frequently goes with them is brought up at some point. The uniquely strange writing does a great job at making the player laugh. The game also messes with your head a lot. The neutral ending boss made it feel like the game was playing ME.
Assuming you're doing a True Pacifist run, Undertale is about finding humanity in unexpected places. The themes of the story are timeless, can be appreciated by all ages, and are well-executed. I know that gushing about this game has become a bit of a cliché, but I went into it skeptical that it could be any good and came out feeling that this was the greatest work of art of the century. There are just no words anyone can type that do it justice.
Play it without spoilers. Play it by yourself. Play it without any sort of expectations... in spite of my review.

When you hear people discussing undertale its either one of two things, how the game is overrated or the game is the best thing ever. While I dont think that Undertale is the best thing ever, I do think that all the praise the game gets is well deserved. It has such an amazing cast of characters, they're all 3 dimensional characters (not literally) and unique. Even the characters who are not main characters are great and memorable such as Temmie, the royal guards and etc. Undertale is unique because it gives you a choice that not many other games give you, they allow you to kill or spare enemies. Now if you think you're going to play this game like any normal rpg and you're just going to go on a killing spree, then good luck! The game is so well written that you will most likely fall in love with the characters upon meeting them and if you still decide that you're going to kill them, the game will make you feel bad for doing that. I've only done Neutral and pacifist runs of the game because I wouldn't be able to live with myself if I killed any character in the game. Moving on to the music in the game, all the music is great and is perfectly implemented into the game. The music convey's perfectly what the creators of the game want you to feel at all times. Whether it's the cheerfully but odd music at the Temmie village to show you how elated the Temmie's are or if its the hard hitting, energetic NGAHHH! theme that plays when fighting Undyne to show you how passionate she is. Anyways enough of my rambling I really enjoyed this game it has loads of replayability. If you enjoy games with great stories and characters do yourself a favor and pick this game up!

NOTE: DayZ is an EARLY ACCESS open world survival game. This game is NOT for casual players! You will lose everything you've worked for in the blink of an eye. You will get fustrated. You will be annoyed. You will get upset at times. You will encounter bugs. If this game doesn't sound like your type, please do not consider buying this game. If you are still interested in DayZ, please continue reading.

DayZ is an open world survival game. You spawn on the south coast of a large map (225 km) named Chernarus. Your objective is to gear up and survive. All the loot is up north, and it's a long walk. Running up north can take 30 minutes to an hour depending on how fast you are and how many times you stop to eat/drink/loot. Knowlage of the map is vital. Study the map. learn most of the spawn points and town names. This will help you get to where you need to go. Knowlage of weapon ammo types is also vital. If you are not familiar with a gun or ammo you find, the DayZ Wiki is your best friend. There are tons of other things you need to know before playing DayZ, but I want to keep things somewhat brief.

By now you've probably read some other reviews on DayZ. Here are a few common criticisms:
"walking simulator 2017"
yes, the game is a walking sim. The devs do plan to add more vehicles in the future.
"early access simulator"  "early access alpha for 4 years LOL"
yes, the game has been in Alpha for 4 years. The development is slow. The DayZ team is not that big. On the bright side, the latest patch (.62) is the last Alpha patch :)
"So many bugs"
Yes, the game is very buggy. there are more bugs than before with every patch and they are there for months before they are ever fixed. most bugs ruin the gameplay. You can see players from miles away because their face is black, and you die from walking off a 2 inch step.
"no loot"
Lol. I find loot all over the place. You just have to get off the coast. You also have to look in the right spots. Some items will be hidden.
"everyone is salty and kills on sight"
DayZ rule #1: Trust no one. Not even your friends. always have your weapon ready in case something happens.

The game does have a few upsides. The gameplay is fun. The graphics are neat. The map is neat. ect. DayZ is a very thrilling game. This game can be very scary. This game can go from 0 to 100 in less than 1 second. imagine sitting back in your chair half awake holding down shift and W and you hear a loud snap and a bullet fly past your head. This game gets your heart pumping faster than any game. The game can be very rewarding. Landing a perfect shot is very rewarding. I have not played any other game that has gameplay this thrilling and rewarding. And that would be a reason to buy this game.
but at the current state of the game, I can't recommend this. I want to recommend this game. I want you to experince the same thrill and exitment as I did in this game. This was one of my favorite games on steam and I love this game. The bugs ruin the experince. The development is painfuly slow. It may not be worth $35 to you. If you do give this game a shot, don't run around as a fresh spawn and say "this game sucks" 20 minutes later. Play in the boots of a geared player and get in some good firefights. You may not win and you may get upset, but thats all part of it.
Thank you for taking your time to read this and I hope this helps!
