If you have played any game of the MOTHER series, then you will enjoy Undertale. Its quirky, turn-based, has great forms of replayability, and it has a great plot. However, it does have a few flaws. It recreates things that originated from MOTHER, and it actually outright COPIED something from MOTHER, that being Venus' voice for the song "Ghost Fight (I think its called)" and "Dummy!" He probably did get rights, and it may be cool that she's in there, but he still flat out ripped it from MOTHER 2/EarthBound.
First things first: The Protagonist. He suffers from "Silent Protagonism," like the main characters of MOTHER. He also has a striped shirt and jeans, like the main characters of MOTHER. He also has a blank expression on his face, like the main characters of MOTHER. This isn't a bad thing, but it isn't original, and again, not being original isn't a bad thing.
Secondly: The Humor. The humor in Undertale is easily defined as "quirky," like MOTHER's, but MOTHER's humor is more child friendly and more 90's-ish while Undertale is more classified as teen humor and GenZ-ish, considering the game made a smoking refrence and has anime and social media refrences. But its still quirky.
Thirdly: It breaks the 4th wall. I won't spoil TOO much of the story, but there is a character named sans (no capitalization) who knows how many times you have died in a certain type of "mode." There is another character named Flowey who knows he's in a game and says that there is "someone who is too cowardly to take this path, and that certain someone is watching us right now." This is obviously hinting YouTube.
Fourthly: The Music. The music is a mixture of catchy, dark, funny, and serious, and has a similar soundfont to that of a SNES, the same console that EarthBound was on. The charactaristics can also apply to the MOTHER series, considering it has serious, yet funny moments, like Undertale. The song names are even refrences to MOTHER songs. "Battle against a true hero" got its name from Earthbound/MOTHER 2's battle themes. Example: "Battle Against a Weird Opponent" "Battle Against a Mobile Opponent." "Megalovania" was first created by Toby in an EarthBound Halloween Hack, and was recreated in 2 games: "MOTHER: Cognitive Dissonance" and "Homestuck." Undertale's Megalovania is the 4th Megalovania used in a game, and I can garuntee you, it won't be the last.
Being a Fuzzy Pickler (MOTHER fan), I love Undertale, and it really got the recognition it deserves. It's just that it's TOO popular, and I think you know why, and some things in it aren't completely original, but they're still great. Undertale gets my rating of a 7/10. I love this game, and if you don't, thats fine, just don't go batshit crazy about it if you hate it.

An unprecedented emotional experience.
The game has a pretty unique relationship with what is known as the “forth wall”, not just making jokes with it, but even making game mechanics and plot points with it in baffling ways. Every trope relating to RPGs and anything that frequently goes with them is brought up at some point. The uniquely strange writing does a great job at making the player laugh. The game also messes with your head a lot. The neutral ending boss made it feel like the game was playing ME.
Assuming you're doing a True Pacifist run, Undertale is about finding humanity in unexpected places. The themes of the story are timeless, can be appreciated by all ages, and are well-executed. I know that gushing about this game has become a bit of a cliché, but I went into it skeptical that it could be any good and came out feeling that this was the greatest work of art of the century. There are just no words anyone can type that do it justice.
Play it without spoilers. Play it by yourself. Play it without any sort of expectations... in spite of my review.

So...what to write about "Undertale" that others haven't?
It has been an iconic game for almost an year now, every (PC) gamer seems to have played it. But okay, I still want to try to review it a bit without spoil readers too much.
If you don't know: You are a human child falling down to the underground world of monsters. Because humans and monsters are enemies you have to find a way out. There are also friendly monsters who search no fight but others do. So YOU can fight them but also choose peaceful ways out of combats. What will you do?
"Undertale" is a RPG game which means that you move your character through this world while making decisions in fights against monsters. Depending on your choices you gain or lose certain points and gold. Also there's a life meter and a couple of saving spots throughout the game (you can't save whenever and wherever you want). You will wander through several areas of this world like the ruins, snowdin (a village covered in snow) and hotlands.
Does this game work as an RPG? Absolutely. I'm not a RPG expert but I was totally drawn into this 8-bit fantasy world that looked simple at the beginning but got quickly more and more entertaining and exciting. The fights were fun to me because it's more than just "fight the enemy until he/she dies and you can move on". Also the enemies' attacks get quite absurd here and there which also provides a good portion of fun.
I loved the settings as well as the characters that will cross the human's way. They can be hillarious, mysterious and/or intimidating but either way: it shouldn't be hard for the player to connect with them. They're likeable, creative and I guess they're highly responsible for the success of "Undertale". And I can see why.
But how about the main character, the human? The human seems to have very little character. In fact it's not even quite sure what gender the human has (I say girl but it might as well be a boy). But I feel it's okay since you can project your own thinking and reactions onto it, like a blanc canvas.
The controls are a piece of cake. Use a few keys to move the character around into four directions, select options (during fights, purchases...), make a selection. With the control key you bring up your inventory.
The graphics are quite simple for a good portion of the game. But simple does not necessarily mean ugly. And sometimes they surprise you with extra beautiful animation, details or character designs. That's cool.
The music is very beautiful and the game has already made me buying the soundtrack. They support the atmosphere here and there perfectly. The sound is like you know it from typical 8-bit games: rather minimalistic, on the other hand there also lies some potential for jokes like whatever "voices" are chosen for the characters in dialogues.
There are no achievements in the game but trading cards.
And "Undertale" has great replay value, at least so you can find out how the story goes whenever you kill or spare characters.
"Undertale" is truly a gorgeous game and one of the best I've played so far AT LEAST via Steam. Even if you are not a big RPG fan, you still may want to check it out and dive into this story of monsters, the underworld and two awesome skeleton brothers throwing puns and banterings at each other while offering you a dating battle and/or cold spaghetti.

First thing's first.
It's Alpha, yes.  It's been in Alpha for like two years.  But in those two years I've loved this game, it's been my favorite for quite a while (next to the ARMA series).
If you don't want to deal with bugs and missing features, and a few placeholders.   Don't buy this game.
Evidenced by my (albeit short) 326.2 hrs on record (as of the date this review was written) this game is fun.  If I could manage to play it for more than 10 days worth of hours, so can you.  There are some people with thousands of hours on this!
Why do I love this game, you may ask?
"With all the Kill On Sight players and OP zombies it's terrible!"
I love this game because of the danger.
You'll be salty when you die, like I was today when I lost my M4 to another guy who had a .22
But you're not salty when your adrenaline goes away.
It's a stressful game and it's the best IMO, you always look over your shoulder for somebody when you hear a footstep, you always crawl to avoid being seen by people or zombies alike.  And running through a town on a full server is always stressful, hiding from a sniper's projectile is more fun than it sounds.
Yes, while you can die from being shot easily, or be knocked out by that noob who spawned in five minutes ago, or be ripped up by a zombie in ten seconds, it adds to the fun in more ways than you can imagine.  It adds realism and sometimes you can have fun watching that♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥be torn apart by his hostage who only has a sharpened stone as a weapon.  Even if you have no time to fight back, death isn't the end.  It just feels like it is.  You worked so hard to find all that loot, but maybe you didn't deserve it if you couldn't defend it?
Or maybe you really should start over before it gets so boring?
Finding all that again and getting a heartwarming feeling again and again just makes the game feel so good.
The ability to be detained adds a value that is beyond cool.  I'll come back to that point in a second.
The fact that there is no set backstory and no one job your character had before the apocalypse adds so much replayability that you might get lost in making a backstory in your head while you look for a can opener.  The roleplay that you can do in this makes it even better of a game.
My friends and I roleplayed as a squad of U.S Marines, and if we encountered a player we stopped him and handcuffed him.  We interviewed him and searched his bag but we didn't steal anything.  We were doing our job and we took any "Government Banned Items" from anybody.  The fact that you can just do things like cuff a man to torture him or do your "job" is cool.  The prison island can make for good RP sessions, and a DayZ nation server can be great, with police officers, farmers, marketers, and even a military.  Trust me when I say this...
DayZ is glitchy, it's an Alpha, and it can be very stressful.
But it's worth the $34.99 you'd pay for it.  There's no end to the gameplay and if you play with friends you'll have an amazing time with them.  Roleplay as paramedics and help those in need, roleplay as the military evacuating people or giving them supplies, roleplay as a cop protecting the helpless.
Or don't roleplay at all and shoot to kill.
This is a game that's worth the support.
You could buy it now or wait for it to be finished (whenever that'll be).

The one and only Undertale. Fanart of it has filled entire pages, usernames have changed to "Sans", and a lot of hype has gone around.
Because of that, Undertale has recieved a lot of hate. I have seen the blind fans, the spammed fanart, and, unfortunately, some...content.
But what I want you to do is to forget the hype. forget the worse parts of the community, and just look at the game. Remember that this store page has only three things involved: You, Steam, and the game.
Undertale is an odd and fascinating RPG with less of a focus on equipment and inventory and more on story and personality. The whole point of the game is that you don't NEED to kill every enemy, nor do you have to spare them. When you kill an enemy, it will make an impact. The story will change and characters will act accordingly. The combat system is unique too. Rather than the usual "my attack stat is this and my defence is this", attacking requires, and depends on timing. Defence is more unique, as you have to avoid attacks on your "soul", a heart in a box. Every enemy type has a unique attack, and defending yourself from it is a minigame.
The game has a lot of charm and personality. It has VERY odd humor. This includes things like a bake sale run by spiders and dogs appearing where you might not expect them too. The enmies are just the same; there's an enemy that takes a lot of pride in it's hat, and that's just the start of it.
It's goofy at some parts, dark at others, and thrilling at some too. Very rarely have I killed or done something to a character in a video game and felt this emotional about it. The fact that you don't have to, and that characters react, definitely makes you think about who you are and your choices.
NOTE: As of 8/20/2016, I have played my brother's copy of this game, so it was marked as recieved for free. I do believe this game is worth full price, as it's replayable and fun. However, I'm busy, stingy, and have several games I haven't even played yet. That being said if/when i do buy this game, I may or may not be able to mention that i no longer was playing the game for free.

How do I explain this game? Its like trying to describe a sunset to the blind. There's no *real* way reading any review or explanation could give you the exact feeling playing this game gives you. But I'll try to give you an idea.
When I first saw the trailer and heard of it I skipped past it a bunch. Sure I heard it was a good game, but it was some wierd 16bit thing. I'd rather play GTAV right?
Boy was I wrong.
So it comes on sale and I grab it out of sheer curiosity. Man was I in for a treat. The game itself is mechanically simple. You avoid enemy attacks with your red heart as enemies shoot varying behaving projectiles at you and then fire back by either using the "fight" option or the "act" option.
Its how the game handles the aftermath that makes it special. Kill a monster? It remembers that. Regret it and reload the game? The game remembers that too. You grow attached to these underground dwelling monsters, from the silly innocent Papyrus to the brave Undyne. I'm going to avoid spoilers as to how these characters develop but suffice it to say that they are all unique, likeable, and everyone is going to have their favorite. No monster down here in the underground is easily classified under evil or good. They all have stories. They all have reasons for the way they are.
The graphics aren't anything special but they don't *need* to be. This is a game about a story. This is a game where you can write
story. Do you want to be the angel that saves the monsters, or the demon that destroys them? Do you want to crown someone king? Or do you wish to make no friends and simply leave this underground place.
All that can be done. By your choices. By your actions.
Don't take my word for it. I know you've been skipping past this game awhile. Maybe you keep seeing it in your front page and go "Ugh! I already know about this game!"
Do yourself a favor. Buy it. Its worth every dollar spent and you'll remember this game for the rest of your life.

The development team is a joke. This game was released on Steam on December 16, 2013 as an early access alpha. Three years later and no progress is being made. Dean Hall joined up with Bohemia Interactive to make a cash grab of a game without the intention of it ever being finished and then once they made their money, he left the development team and abandoned the game.
Let's get into the cons of the game. I will list things randomly but everything makes perfect sense and I gathered this information through playing the game first hand.
I look at the updates every now and then just to shake my head because they hardly ever work on the important stuff. The performance of the game is not great, even on high end computers. Loot spawns are TERRIBLE. Good luck finding anything other than a pistol near the cost. And if you get lucky and do find one, you won't have a magazine or any bullets. You are forced into going up north into the Northwest Airfield to find loot where half the time a group is camping waiting to rek you. The time it takes to run up north is about 20-30 minutes. So basically during the first hour of you playing, this game is a running simulator. When you do finally get fully geared up after an hour of playing, prepare for half your gear to get ruined and become obsolete once you are shot by another player, if you survive. The servers restart every few hours without warning so if you had a vehicle, say goodbye to it. Grenades don't work properly. You press G to toss them and they get stuck in mid air right in front of you most of the time. You can't talk on side chat with the whole server to find out where the action is at. Plenty more to be said, just read other reviews and you will come across ones similar to this one.
This game compares nothing to the DayZ mod. It was a lot better and more fun to play than this half completed game. You had a variety of maps to play, way better loot spawns, properly working vehicles that spawn around the map reasonably, smoother interaction with your player and items, and the list goes on.
I would only recommend this game in it's current state to people that are looking for a PVP survival sandbox game with a lot of time on their hands to roam around the map and the patience to loot up 100 houses/tents to get prepared for the apocalypse.

Community: Overall the community is complete♥♥♥♥♥♥ I found myself being killed countless times by large clans fully geared, despite the fact that I was a naked. Quite possibly one of the most well-written games I've ever played. Worth every moment of your time and then some. Art isn't the best but it doesn't matter because the design (and everything else, especially the music) is phenomenal. Mindblowing experience that I've not only played through 4 times myself, but also watched 4 other people play through the entire thing as well. It's just that good.

(Disclaimer: Most of the time I have on this game was in offline mode)So, a little bit of backstory. I'd heard amazing things about it, heard that it was the next Earthbound, etc. I watched some videos, listened to some music(most notably Megalovania), and wanted it so badly. I got some gift cards for my birthday(which neatly overlaps with the Steam Summer Sale) and thought,"Oh, what the hell, I'll get it and play it." I loaded it, played a bit of the opening sequence, got bored, quit. I came back to it later and played more(I am currently up to the point where you fight Papyrus for the first time) and I loved it. I love this game. The music is amazing, the spritework is 11/10, and the gameplay is similar to Earthbound.
PROS
--------
* Great spritework
* Messes with video game stereotypes(the tutorial literally holds your hand for most of it!)
* Earthbound-like overworld
* Music is amazing chiptunes
* Annoying dog
* Done all by one guy with help from friends
CONS
--------
* If you kill one enemy(can happen by rushing through menus) you will get switched to a Neutral run if doing a pacifist run
* Naming your character Frisk will trigger "Hard mode" which is really just the opening bit with Flowey then the Annoying Dog comes in and(essentially) say "That's all, folks!" and ends the run
NEUTRAL(no not the in-game Neutral run)
--------
* Will make you feel feels you probably haven't felt before from a game
Who I reccomend this game to:
* Gamers who long for the good old days of the SNES and Earthbound
* Those who like classic RPGs
* People who want to see what exactly what you can do with gaming
Who I do NOT reccomend this game to:
* Those who only like games like CoD and Halo and things like that
* Little kids(There are some mature themes, nothing terrible or anything, but stuff like when characters die they die forever so DON'T LET YOUR 5-YEAR-OLD PLAY THIS, I'd say those around 10-11+ are OK to play it)
FINAL VERDICT:
----------------
Fantastic, 11/10

(Disclaimer: Most of the time I have on this game was in offline mode)So, a little bit of backstory. I'd heard amazing things about it, heard that it was the next Earthbound, etc. I watched some videos, listened to some music(most notably Megalovania), and wanted it so badly. I got some gift cards for my birthday(which neatly overlaps with the Steam Summer Sale) and thought,"Oh, what the hell, I'll get it and play it." I loaded it, played a bit of the opening sequence, got bored, quit. I came back to it later and played more(I am currently up to the point where you fight Papyrus for the first time) and I loved it. I love this game. The music is amazing, the spritework is 11/10, and the gameplay is similar to Earthbound.
PROS
--------
* Great spritework
* Messes with video game stereotypes(the tutorial literally holds your hand for most of it!)
* Earthbound-like overworld
* Music is amazing chiptunes
* Annoying dog
* Done all by one guy with help from friends
CONS
--------
* If you kill one enemy(can happen by rushing through menus) you will get switched to a Neutral run if doing a pacifist run
* Naming your character Frisk will trigger "Hard mode" which is really just the opening bit with Flowey then the Annoying Dog comes in and(essentially) say "That's all, folks!" and ends the run
NEUTRAL(no not the in-game Neutral run)
--------
* Will make you feel feels you probably haven't felt before from a game
Who I reccomend this game to:
* Gamers who long for the good old days of the SNES and Earthbound
* Those who like classic RPGs
* People who want to see what exactly what you can do with gaming
Who I do NOT reccomend this game to:
* Those who only like games like CoD and Halo and things like that
* Little kids(There are some mature themes, nothing terrible or anything, but stuff like when characters die they die forever so DON'T LET YOUR 5-YEAR-OLD PLAY THIS, I'd say those around 10-11+ are OK to play it)
FINAL VERDICT:
----------------
Fantastic, 11/10

The game's aesthetics are wonderful;  the developers and voice-acting directors really took their time to make this game look and sound astonishing. Even after having played the main storyline countless times on several different platforms, I never tire of the characters who all really invite me into their inbred, overweight, militaristic, brutal, Hispanic, addicted, loud, suave, evil, pimping--but mostly loving and caring--family.  Not to mention the attractive (for a video game!) female characters... Maya, Lilith, Captain Scarlett, Guardian Angel, and Ellie (to save the best for last).  I cannot recommend this game more highly.  Please buy it, for your own sake.  I can't wait for the new Borderlands game coming out in 2014.

Undertale tells the same story many different ways, with an emphasis on the concept of humanity. Each time you play through, do it differently and more details/facts of the "whole" story are revealed to you. Play by killing monsters selectively, entirely, or not at all; it's up to you and drastically affects your experience and the storyline information that's revealed. Once you play through all three main ending types, you will fully understand the plot as complicated, hilarious, tragic, heartwarming and terrifying as it is.
Never has a game impacted me on such a lasting, emotional level as Undertale has. From the dancing visual typography, perfectly fitting soundtrack, and incredible overall sound design, everything you interact with is greatly emphasized by audio. The characters and enemies have depth and are unforgettable. My interactions and repeated playthroughs revealed so much about what I originally thought were very superficial characters. Tobyfox made the characters really feel like people, who live a certain way for a certain reason, and in some cases unable to help themselves for their actions based on their past and surroundings.
There's so much in Undertale to see, experience, reveal and enjoy; I had no expectations going in, but I was thrilled with what I found. This game deserves the innumerable amount of positive reviews it has received. I highly recommend it.

for a long time i was really hesitant or disgusted by the idea of playing this game and wasn't sure why, but i think now after 30 hours of playing and plenty of restarts to take everything in, I can say why with clarity.
BL2 is a good core game, an arcadey type moon gravity shooter with great responsiveness and plenty of variation to engage different forms of play. As a game itself I'd recommend it to anyone who enjoys shooting games without aim assist, because shooting things in the eyeballs for critical hits is really fun. It makes up for anything else you'd be bothered by, like massive levels where you have to hold W to get around, or writing that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥ at best and out-right embarassing to hear at worst.
That's basically my review. Next I'm going to explain the reason why I never wanted to play it and why it was sort of a bad in-joke to play this among friends. This has no weight to my recommendation at all, but it feels good to realize why I never liked this game wholeheartedly.
The problem I had with it was the writing. The writing is bad, like, edgy 9th grader creative writing assignment bad.
By "bad" I don't completely mean "badly written;" it also has to do with pacing. Like one minute you got a quirky clearly-fictional character talking some offensive kind of jive to be funny, then spin around 180 degrees within 2 sentences and hamfistedly♥♥♥♥♥♥out plot or character development, like they took the REALLY BROAD assumption that you gave a♥♥♥♥♥♥about the lore of their game by that point to enjoy it. They assume that hearing "bonerfart" 20 times will make you more pliable to hear about how this shoddily thrown-together indiana jones gentleman scholar character lost his arm and leg, or how he's interacted with other characters in the main hub while you're out having fun shooting things and finding items.
Imagine if Diablo were to explain to you the nuanced backstory of every single ♥♥♥♥ing character you buy items from, or get quests from, because you picked the sidequest to make sure you're the proper level to continue the story when you're done.
Borderlands 2 is excellent at pacing, making sure that doing all the side stuff per area will leave you decently raised in level to handle the next challenge in the game, but when you do these side things, the game seems to think you're going out of your way for it, that you care, even if you're just doing it to level. They'll prattle these long ♥♥♥♥ing life stories at you, because it's a chance to keep making jokes and make the characters feel more memorable, whether you want them to be or not.
All of this isn't helped by the fact that no writing in the game was coordinated, at all. The voice actors for Handsome Jack and Clap-Trap, for example, both affirmed that they were just given stupid lines to read and read them all in a sitting, then the assets were thrown everywhere into the game. The creative directors, people who should be front and center reviewing all of the stuff that was written, didn't know about most of the jokes that went in, the famous diamond horse in the first level being a prime example of something they didn't plan that was added in by one of the dozens of non-social writers who all worked on their own, trying to make their personal additions to the game "as funny as possible."
Why am I mentioning all this? Because it really did set the tone of the game. It's schizophrenic. You're making stupid jokes about rabbit butts one minute and talking about That ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Who Killed My Parents the literal next. It doesn't sit well, and is insultingly dumb for something that's praised for a story and writing so totally good that Telltale is picking it up for a point-and-click adventure on par with The Walking Dead and friends.
Then again, The Walking Dead outside of the video games is sort of a♥♥♥♥♥♥heap of bad writing, so it might be worth something salvageable if Telltale does their personal spin on the game's world.
If you want to laugh your♥♥♥♥♥off, play this game.

I bought this game about a week after it came out, after seeing a thread about it on a subreddit. Going in, I didn't have very high expectations, and I imagined it to be just another low-quality RPG to make a quick buck off of some naieve gamers. In the end, it became one of my favorite games that I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing. While other games may have acheivements or special endings if you finish the game without killing any enemies,
is the only game that I've seen make pacifism actually feel rewarding, instead of a chore. This is also aided by the writing of the game, as it makes each enemy, large or small, feel as fleshed out as the main character of your standard JRPG. The soundtrack of the game soars far above what you would expect from a RPG, and it helps to give each area, character, and cutscene its own distict feel. Even 10 or so months after its release, I still regularly listen to the OST.
---------------------------------------------------
In the end, it is a superb game that sends a message far better than any other "story driven" game I've recently played. Some may complain about how it has a low-quality fanbase, but in my opinion it's the actual game that matters, not what demographic likes it. It's only about 10 hours, but what it lacks in length it completely makes up for it with its story, soundtrack, and pretty much every other aspect of the game. All I recommend is that you go in knowing as little as possible.

I just spent almost eight hours in game and i ll try to sum up my impressions and describe, how was my first day in game.
When i started the game i was quite disappointed there is no such thing as "official" server and you have to play on server somebody has rented from someone and obey his rules. This was first let down as somebody who justs charged me money for his game provide just a client and no servers to play on.
However i mangaded to found server with decent ping(under 50)and was more than half full with players. I was fortunate as there were like 20 servers with ping below 100 and like 18 of them were completely empty, so if you live in not as dense populated area and with not so great internet connection it might happen you just bought yourself boring single player game.
Lets move on to the gameplay:
I spawned somewhere near the coast, i was quite lucky as i quickly found Makarov pistol with two bullets in its magazine, damaged kitchen knife and hoodie so i actualy had pocket to my Makarov in to. While leaving the village i noticed there is another addition to my survival kit, left in a Lada vehicle wreck. A plastic bottle full of water! Great, im not thirsty anymore and as i dont have any more space in my pockets im leaving first village in excitement whit pet bottle in my hands.
Im traveling by the road even i know its not smartest idea, but i would love to meet just anyone to see how player interactions works.
After some time i arrived to trainyard of town called Elektrozavodsk(glad school days finaly payed off as im fortunate to have ability to read cyrillic). My heart started pumping as i spotted first zombie wandering around the tracks. In nearby house i was lucky enought to find crowbar and as it provided me with bit of slef confidence i returned to the place where i met my first zombie and dispatched it off this world in Gordon Freeman style. This was my second disappointment with the game as even ping was great combat felt sluggish and unresponsive. I mean cmon! Its 2016 and melee combat feels like in Ultima Online 20yrs ago, played through dial up internet connection?
After my first combat experience i started scavenging nearby houses, finaly found bag! I was quite excited about it as it was childs briefcase, red one with ladybug on it, exactly the same like my classmate had back on the elementary school:-) Found some food, canteen, gun holster, rifle with no ammo and other supplies. I spent about hour doing this  and decided to leave the town as there was more and more zombies arnoud.
I followed the tracks west and after about hour of walking i arrived to the city of Chernogorsk, my visit was going the same way like in case of Elektrozavodsk and it started to getting bit repetetive and boring as i still did not met anyone. Spent another hour sweeping houses desperate to find bigger backpack(still no luck), and after that i conitnued west, by the tracks.
Tada! Met first person! Some guy, probably scared by my makarov and huge fireaxe in my hands he was mumbling something in french crawling in the corner of the room i cought him in with his hands up. I tought great, there are actual people around i waved to him and continued my journey west.
Sweeped throguh some small airfield and finaly found more ammo for my Makarov in nearby village(still no luck with bigger bag). This was quite encouraging and i decided to head up north as i heard northern areas should be more populated with players.
During my journey i become quite bored, but after some time i spotted quite big town ahead of me, when i got closer i found out its name is Zelenogorsk and it was swarming with zombies. I was foolish enought to shoot at them with my Makarov as i finaly wanted to test how shooting feels and thought i can put few zombies down with it as around 50 spare bullets in my childs brief case gave me more confidence.
It was bad idea as sound lured more of them running in my direction at a speed of Usain Bolt. I started running for my life, ran through few buildings, closing the doors behind me i managed to escape.
That was first 7 hours of the game for me and its a hard decision how to rate this game as there is no "mixed feelings" button. From technical side of thing the game is terrible, ui is still the same like in Operation Flashpoint, no official servers, and game is just as responsive as Ultima Online was two decades ago.
Map is huge and while that is great its not detailed enought for a survival game as scavenging through empty houses is no longer fun after couple of hours. Also map is too big for the number of players server can support and meeting one person in almost 8 hours of gameplay on almost full server is tragic.
Shame is that i dont see the point in further development of the game as without drastic changes likes scaling the map down or increasing the player limit servers can handle, the game will always feel the same.
Sorry, but i just cant recommend the game to anyone, as it offers you nothing you cant do on your own in real world. Want to save money spent on Day Z just to test it out? Take a backpack, stuff it with some basic supplies and leave your home on friday and walk straight out of the town and keep direction for two days, as soon as you ll leave the city you live in you ll have almost same experience like playing Day Z minus zombies(hopefuly).

If you get bored, try some class you wouldn't normally touch.  Each one really brings something different to the game.  There's a lot of replay value for this game, along with new DLCs that came out over time.  The multiplayer system is great and fun, I've experienced no issues.
The new story, graphics, and characters make this a great sequel.

I've heard a lot of good things about this game since the release so I decided to finally buy this when it went on sale. The game turned out to be even better than I thought. The plot twists, the humor, the depth of story, the emotional rollercoaster. This game touched me like no game had ever touched before. I'd like to share my experience with you.
There might be some potential, light, spoilers i guess:
At my first playthrough I decided that I'm going to be "the good guy", as I usually do in games. I've heard some things about this game but I didn't know the basic mechanics or story, so more or less I was clueless as to what should I expect. I've tried my best to not kill anyone to get the good ending. Unfortunately, I was not able to figure out how to spare some of the creatures/bosses. I wondered how this will all end and kinda expected "meh" result. I was so sucked up in the game I finished it in one go. After defeating the king I've met my
from the beginning of the game. First time my game "crashed" I was like '-what? I was just about to finish the game, come on !'. Then I launched the game again and I was like 'Oh ok. Nice one'. After finishing the game
tells me that if I want to see the real good ending I have to kill no one.
Ok, I can do that.
Next run, I can do this, I can spare everyone. After a little consulting with uncle google I know how to spare all the bosses(I'm horrible, I know).
And I did it. I was so thrilled that I'll see the good ending. I get to the king, defeat him and...
again. Motherf...
Turns out not only I have to spare everyone, I have to be friends with all of them. What?
I was mad at this game. I decided to kill everyone this time. I knew there was a different ending if you do that.
So I killed everyone I've encountered. Usually I wouldn't care either way since it's quite common to do so in most of the games but here... it was somehow hard. And those dialogs... I felt like the scum of the Earth with every kill. I was sad when I was about to finish the game. And after defeating the king once again...
shows up and the game ends with a neutral ending again. Turns out I didn't kill enough.
I didn't think I'll have it in me to try again and kill more after crying like 5 times during this run. But I really wanted to see other endings, so I decided to try doing the Pacifist route again.
This time I had it. I knew what I needed to do to get the right ending. I wanted to rush through the game since I saw everything 3 times already. Or so I thought. This path shows you a little more about the lore. And with every second it was getting darker. I was spooked a little at first but I continued. The I was spooked a little more but I was still going forward. The fact that I was playing at night wasn't helping. Finally I've reached the final boss and after defeating him I was satisfied. I've finally reached the good ending!

A nice idea, but even after years of development it seems the development priorities are all wrong.
Don't get me wrong, I'm a big fan of Facepunch and I think maybe in a few more years, Rust will amount to something. As Rust stands today, much the same as it did several years ago, a game where you fight with the engine more than you'll fight against anything else.
Play Rust for a few hours and a majority of your experiences will involve being killed by wall-ghosting bears, unsolveable hunger or thirst, or if that doesn't get you, another player will kill you  with no options for recourse. A large majority of gameplay (probably >80%) of a casual player not playing in a large group/clan is spent gathering resources and dying, restarting, and gathering resources again. Rust is designed to award players already doing well, which means within a few hours after a server wipe your odds of having fun start to decrease over time. It's entirely posslbe to frequently have a Rust gameplay session where you do nothing but spawn, gather resources for a half hour, and then be killed by a bear hiding inside of a tree or a player with a gun within a mile radius.
I'm sure Rust is fun for the groups that play together for an advantage and end up building bases and attacking others, but for anyone else Rust is generally going to be more frustrating than fun.
- Broken game mechanics and functionality (such as significantly physics-defying animals) that have existed as problems for years, with seemly no fix in the future
- Poor performance, even on a higher high end PC. As Rust is still technically early access, I suppose this is acceptable.
- Hackers and optional advantages (turning off graphics features like shadows and increasing monitor gamma gives players an advantage, and not doing so puts you at a major disadvantage)
- A crafting system that's actually pretty well made, but you'll likely die before you can see most of it. Most of your time in Rust will be spent at the very bottom of it.
- A seemingly engineered anti-social environment (unless you've agreed to meet up with a friend in advance, anyone else will immediately kill you - because that's always the best decision in Rust)
To be completely fair here, I like Rust. I think it has a lot of great ideas and great depth to it, and at rare moments it can appear fun. As of right now though, Rust leaves me hoping for a different game entirely, one that just incorporates some of the ideas of Rust and drops all of the problems Rust seems to create for itself. On it's own, Rust isn't fun - unless you have a group or just want a running around naked simulator.
Will Rust be better in the future? It's really impossible to say, but if you look at their progress from when they started to now and extrapolate out a few years, I'd say it gets better, but never really becomes a game that anyone besides the more hardcore Rust players really get to enjoy.

I was struggling with the decision to recommend this game, or not..on the one side, I've had brilliant moments and memories in this game, really good ones, and then on the other hand when I think back, those moments and memories are over shadowed by frustration and anger.
Now I know this game is in early access, but for how long now..? The optimisation is ok, I get 30/40ish frames on my GTX760 GPU with low/medium settings. A lot of things has changed throughout the games development, but my frustrations stay the same. Except for some broken game mechanics, like melee combat for example or things disappearing from my inventory/the ground, and except for the occasional hacker, my biggest gripe with this game is the loneliness...this may be the fact that I have to play on EU servers due to living in South Africa, but still..I feel there is waaaay to many servers, and people are too spread out accross them all.
Whenever I play the game, I am alone, I meet someone, even after I show/say I am friendly, they kill me, I spawn, I am alone. The few times I managed to group up with a few peeps, I had a good time but then still, you walk/run around for hours and hours and maaaaybe see one or two other players. When you die, it takes a very very long time to get back to your friends.
I actually got my brother to buy this game as well, but meeting up and playing together is such a huge chore that we gave up. Hello reader, if you are like me, you want a solid and professional review about a game that will help you decide if you want it or not. If you are not like me and do not want a serious review, please stop reading now.
Now, to start this review I would like to first say that, this game is either very fun and awesome, or boring. Depending on the player, DayZ is a fun and interesting game that you could spend hours and hours playing, or it can be a boring waste of money to others. One easy way to tell if you are the kind of player to like this game is just a few simple questions you have to ask yourself.
One is, "Can I spend a long period of time of this game for possibly a bad ending where I get shot by a sniper"
"Am I mature enough to take this game seriously?"
And "Do I have the patience to try and try again?"
If you said yes to these questions, congratulations, you are some of the players to like and understand this game!
Now, time to get to game review itself.
Dayz... It's a huge game in my opinion, a big world and so many items, so in my opinion, you guys should cut the devs some slack. Dayz is also not quite sure what kind of game it is, and that may be a good thing, so you can play your way and not how the game says it should be played, like other games I have seen.
Now on to what people say about Dayz. To this day I have never seen a hacker, ever. On high and low population servers, I have never. Also, it is true that this game is five times and fun and enjoyable with a friend, but you can make friends in game, or just plain old play by yourself and have a good time. It's your story, you are free to write it.
My overall opinion of this game is.. 8/10
The only reasons this game is not 10/10 is that it can be grindy at some times and boring at others, but still a very good game.
Thank you for reading, and good luck survivors!

At the actual state of the game I would not recommend people to buy the game, here are some reasons.
First of all I follow the game since day 1 and I can clearly say that the game had a lot of good changes through its development time but there is still a lot to do. The game had major updates such as the engine one that refreshed the game, graphically only (from my point of view).
The game has greatly evolved but some of the most annoying bugs that are in the game from the start never got fixed, for example dying from walking in stairs, running inside/outside houses.
Also last update blocked some duplication method and some hacks / cheats, that is great but some others bugs came in (For example gun sounds not playing when other players shoots, you understand the problem in pvp, you can't figure out from where people shoot on you) some cars bug that despawn randomly after a server restart and the lac of optimization that limit synchronization on full  servers, wont blame the game for that, can be material issues on servers too...
All of those things let me came to a question: Am I still having fun playing the game? Well the answer is not clear in my mind, but I would more likely say no. I did like the game in the past, I had lot of fun playing it but in the current state it is barely playable. So I wont recommend people to buy the game NOW, wait t'ill the game is better, more stable and optimized (sync issues) and polished of course.
Also want to mention that devs are doing updates not frequently, 0.60 took 6 months (understandable for an engine reworking) and others are kinda random to me, around 2 to 4 months.
Will edit this evaluation in the future, if needed, I hope It get better...

Undertale is one of the best games almost short enough to play in a single sitting I have ever had the pleasure of experiencing. The graphical decisions were a bit off-putting at first, but in the end I think it is the perfect fit for what the game is. The soundtrack is phenomenal, bringing out the mood of the scenarios and environments perfectly. Speaking of, the environment design, while seeming a bit bare-bones at first, is very well done and leaves much room for artistic interpretation--especially the mysterious beauty of Waterfall., which is by far my favorite area. The characters are quirky, unique, interesting and lovable, with very distinct personalities. Goat mom is best mom :P
I even made a butterscotch-cinnamon pie because of this game, and it's actually
good.
Also, dogs. Dogs are always good.
Hitting a more somber note here; I discovered Undertale at a very low point in my life, and I was going down fast. (cue "Don't Give Up" playing in the background)  I cried on multiple occasions throughout my adventures in the Underground, and not for reasons you might think. There were several moments that, while they would likely not affect someone more emotionally stable than I, had me in tears because they struck a chord with me. If you've already played the game, you likely know what I'm talking about. This game did not singlehandedly solve my emotional problems, but it did help me--and I'm sure many others--understand the true meaning of determination: No matter how bleak your circumstances may seem, there is always a reason to stick it out. There will always be people who will care about you, protect you, and help you on your journey, wherever your destination may be. If you are lost and confused and feel empty, you will always,
, have friends to turn to--even if you've gotten to the point where you're an angry ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ attacking everyone you once loved because you've forgotten how to love
. That is what is so beautiful about this game--we have taken what is essentially one man's creation and expanded upon it in unforeseen, beautiful ways and created a loving community where everyone will always have a home.
Wow, tangent, sorry. But it's true. This game wouldn't be nearly as loved as it it without such an amazing fanbase built upon one simple principle: Determination.

DISCLAIMER
Before you read this review, please grant this one request: read the whole thing. If you cannot do that, than please just read the last two paragraphs. I am not trying to take away any joy you find in this game, I am just stating how I feel. Thank you for reading this.
REVIEW

This game is alright at best in my opinion, but what has happened to it saddens me.
Firstly, I must applaud the creators, for what has been produced by such a small team is quite impressive. In addition, this game's premise is creative and the art style, though pixelated, pontificates the great effort put into the game.
With that said, this game has some issues in terms of character personalities and plot lines.
I oft begin with the plot. It is rather rudimentary in terms of the protagonist's goal, to leave the underground. However, in the first moments of the game, the player is introduced to a morality system of sorts (the aforementioned "premise"), which is interesting yet leads to all players thinking that they MUST take the high moral road. This is problematic, as it leads to a one minded way of thinking that stifles the game's intellectual creativity. Ergo, if you go into this game as biased player (meaning someone has told you something about the game) or an emotionally sensitive player, you will fall into the standard demographic of players. As I observe some of the other reviews, I see that there are some people who agree with this notion.
Now, I believe the best way to address the character flaws is to describe my experience with the game. I bought this game around late September early October 2015, and I had heard nothing about this game whatsoever besides the name itself. I will save my breath and tell you this, I am dry, sardonic, misanthropic, and cynical, so I got what many would call "The Genocide Ending" on my first playthrough. Yes, I was under the impression that the introductory statements about sparing creatures was supposed to be sarcastic, and that the player was supposed to act ironically and kill everything like in what the public would call "A Standard RPG". Consequently, once I defeated the final boss of that ending, I never launched the game afterwards for awhile. Hence, I was under the impression that game was supposed to have a dark or "Edgey" ending and that I did what I could. Of course later I realised that there were more endings and I began to experiment a bit more.
You may be thinking two things:
"You must of been biased, nobody would get THAT ending on their first time."
or
"Wow, you are a really terrible person."
However, whatever you may have thought, I feel that I ought to justify why I got such an ending. As I previously mentioned, I was nonplussed by the level of seriousness in the early stages of the game. Therefore, I failed to take the message seriously. Secondly, and this is where the character flaws come into play, I hated every single character in this game. "Hated" is a bit of an understatement as well, I would much rather say that I LOATHED EVERY ONE OF THEM WITH EVERY GRAM OF WILL THAT I HAVE. Now I know that such a statement is an opinion, but come on, they have such archetypal personalities. Let's see: every motherly figure ever, check; deceptive antihero framed to be the villain with a tortured backstory, check; secret villain who is only revealed later on, check; the most annoying, insufferable, childish, idiotic, excuse for a character with a 5 year-old's sense of humor, GIGANTIC CHECK. There are more archetypes, but I tire of listing them. In addition, there is a segment of the game where, right after you are introduced to a character, they interupt you multiple times immediately making a slightly impatient person hate them. Oh, and that character who I demonstrated a sever disliking to, happens to be the centre of comedy in most of the game.
While I am already on the topic, the comedy in this game is meant for two demographics, young children (and/or people with an immature sense of humor) and internet dwellers. I hate both of those demographics, and I am not alone. Henceforth, when you get people wincing and sighing at the humor in this game, they most likely find the humor appauling.
There is one more thing however, the saddest thing of all, that I must address. The primary creator of this game, Toby Fox, made this game and did not expect the insane spreading and popularity that ensued. He, like all creators, had an idea, and he wanted to share his idea. The fact the he gained revenue and popularity was great, initially. However, it slowly spiraled downward destroying the reputation of the game. That is why I delayed writing this review. I unsure if complaining so intensly about a game made by mostly one person, but I finally decided to do it. The greatest tragedy of this game, is that anyone who actually enjoyed this game will not be remembered. The people on the internet have ruined this game, and what they have done will never be undone. Toby Fox will not be remembered as the guy who made a poignant game which touched many, but the idiot who spawned another cancerous and disgusting fandom. This is unfair to him, because all he wanted to do was share his idea. Had this game been released around the time that Earthbound, a game that inspired this one, it probably would not have been ruined, due to the fact that less social media existed. You want to know why this game is bad to so many? You want to know why so many people hate this game?
People. YOU people. I do not fully hate this game, but because of all you people this game will be scrutinized, torn apart, and destroyed. It will be left and remembered as a game of the times, which all future generations will laugh at. If you asked me after I finished my first playthrough, I would have reluctantly reccomended this game, but now, I cannot bring myself to recommend this game.

You'll meet a top tier hero type character who'll give you the clothes off your back, and then five minutes later meet a cannibal who will cut off your legs and eat you. That's just how that world works, and I like how this game presents it to you. The map is huge (Bigger than games like Grand Theft Auto V, and maybe Rust.) Loot is pretty balanced. And since the game's on the Arma engines, there's a lot of realism. Everything makes sense, from handmade splints to camouflage actually working effectively, to hunting to fishing to farming.
You just survive.
This game isn't without flaws, but for early access, I'd say the price is GENEROUS.

First impressions though this game is in Early access its got good graphics it runs smoothly, day and night cycle  is really good. You can really see some beautifully sunsets and sunrises. The crafting system is simple and easy to use you can place down a structure fairly quickly.
Its a good solid survival game, So why not recommend it?
Where this game takes a down turn is the multiplayer only side of things. I have played survival games such as Savage lands, Space engineers and Medieval engineers. Which each have single player options. Now i know that multiplayer is where these games each excel as well as Rust.
But the issues that Rust MP servers have is that as a new player to a server you are so far behind every other player, that the moment you meet another player you are heavily outgunned you probably have a hatchet while they have sniper rifles or other modern weaponry. Now its understandable that the people who have been playing sometime will have a decided edge on newbies, but these 'advanced' players tend to be♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ They will kill a player who poses no threat to them and i have experienced no form of working together with newbies to build a community. Because these 'advanced' players band together and don't give newbies a chance to actually enjoy the game.
In other multiplayer games these people tend to be called griefers, but its the norm in Rust.
Some may say that my short play time is not really adequate enough to really enjoy the game. This may well be so, but this short play time is because I spend a max of 1hr in a server because with in that time i will have been killed and my resources stolen before i have a chance to get established.
By all means this game is a beautiful FPS survival game, it just has a tremendously unforgiving community on the servers.This is why i would not recommend this game.

I don't know what to say about this game, so here is a recipe for pancakes,
Ingredients:
4tbsp plain flour (about 100g)
1 large free range egg
½ pint semi-skimmed milk + water (about 300ml - ¾ milk ¼ water)
Pinch of salt
Butter for frying
How to make pancakes:
Sieve the flour and salt into a large bowl and make a well in the mixture.
Break in the egg and stir to make a breadcrumby mix.
In a jug add 1/3 of a pint of milk and top up with water to make 1/2 a pint (200ml milk, 100ml water) - this makes a lovely light batter.
Add the milk and the water mix bit by bit, beating constantly to avoid lumps.
Tip:*If you have a food processor just throw all the ingredients in and zap until smooth!
Pop a large frying pan over a medium heat.
Add a large knob of butter (roughly 50g) and melt.
Pour the excess butter into a small bowl and reserve it for later.
Using a ladle pour a spoonful of the pancake batter into the hot pan and swirl to get a full covering - cook for about 1 min each side (it's ready when it's easy to flip over).
Serve immediately with sugar and lemon or other exciting toppings. We love cheese and Marmite for an extra British twist! Delicious!!

Rust is a good and my favourite survival game.
Graphics are decent. There are a lot of servers, and there is voice chat, so you can easily communicate with other players.
The game is still bugged, for example animals can penetrate through objects.
After the first log on a server, first you have to collect some wood and stone and craft necessary tools like hatchet and axe. After that, you can build your first base. Bases can be made of wood, stone and they can be even armoured. At the beginning, you will probably use weapons like bow, crossbow, spear which you can easily acquire but there are also weapons which are difficult to get, like for example AK47. Weapons can be used against other players and also on animals. Some animals will run away from you, but animals like bears and wolves will try to kill you. A lot of players will try to kill you as well, so be careful. There are a lot of hoodies, jackets, pants and other attires. There are also attires that will make you stronger, like vests, helmets, etc. In the game there are rad towns and in them there are barrels and crates. In barrels and crates you can find different weapons, tools and food. Every now and then your character needs to eat and drink. You can eat meat from animals or for instance chocolates and bars which you can find in mentioned above barrels and crates.
Overall
Rust is the best survival game I have ever played. It's still bugged, but I recommend it nonetheless. Especially if you have friends that you can play with.

So how do you review a game like Rust? It's difficult, there are a great many things to consider before you can decide which direction your thumb will point. Such as:
Community;
Pitiful at best. I mean, seriously, the community is quite possibly the worst in the history of online gaming, on par even with CS:GO and that is saying something. Reasons for that, in my opinion, are the Russians. Russians, Russians, Toxic AF Russians. They hide in bushes, trees and rocks. They hide in your stash, in your pocket, in your walls and in your freaking hard-drive. They be anywhere and everywhere. Oh, and they have just had, or are about to have, sexual intercourse with your mother. And your sister. Probably your brother, your father and your pooch too. In fact, no orifice is safe from these sexual deviants. It is no coincidence that both CS:GO and Rust have the worst communities around, they both contain a frighteningly large Russian player base.
Gameplay;
Great fun, generally speaking. Building mechanics are solid and if you are prepared to donate time and effort in to building your base, you can build something nigh on impossible to penetrate - unless you encounter a hacker of course, but all games of this nature contain hackers and it would be unfair of me to downvote a game due to the many hackers who frequent it, the devs do their best to remove them. The animals in game (wolves, deer, bears and chickens) are utterly dull, lifeless and generic creatures that bring very little to the positive side of the game. So, basically you gather and gather and gather some more until ur fingers go numb, you then build your base of operations, before standing back and admiring it for an extended period of time, then you go raid some poor unfortunare soul of their hard earned resources, and/or get raided yourself. Rince and repeat. Rust in a nutshell.
PvP:
The PvP aspect is great fun. Fairly balanced, generally speaking, I've had some great shootouts during my time in the game. Shooting Russians is always fun. Get's boring rather fast, though. At the end of the day raiding another players base, although loads of fun if they're online, can get rather repetitive after a while. Basically you spend resources to make C4/rockets in order to gain entry to a player owned house/base, only to steal their resources (sulfur mainly) to cover the cost of the resources you spent to raid their base. Welcome to the PvP cycle of Rust. Raiding is also 99% offline and unless they kill you during the raid there is no way to find out who did it.
PvE:
No PvE content to speak, and for a lot of people this means that the game will run dry rather fast. The game is crying out for PvE content in some form or another. Yes there are a few towns scattered across the map and for the most part they are well designed, but aside from the odd loot crate that you may be lucky enough to find, there is very little else to do there as there are no zombies/mutants or mobs of any kind to deal with. So basically you just head in to a town and loot as many crates as you can find, that is assuming the rooftop campers who control the town  (mainly large clans who dominate the server) don't Kalashnikov/Bolt-Action you to death first. So even the very little PvE content that the game contains is ruined by the KoS player base/Russians who know no better. Word to the devs: add more PvE content as your game is drastically lacking in comparison to Ark. Bigtime. Sort it out or lose the survival race.
Getting bored now so I'll cut off here. Decent game but severely limited with regards to depth and a distinct lack of PvE content. Fun for a while but gets boring rather fast. Worst of all is the community, though. Truly is terrible. Thus I cannot recommend.

I've been playing DayZ for years, right from the mod before standalone was even announced. The game is definitely not perfect, but I do believe the negativity around it is becoming unjustified and over-the-top. Standalone has been in development for a ridiculously long time, and it's frustrating but it doesn't bother me because we still get updates. It may still be classed as alpha, but to everyone who complains about that fact: What would a name change to "beta" actually do? The game is still being updated and improved upon but if it was beta then you know... It would just be a different name.
The actual gameplay is immersive and genuinely captures a feeling of suspense, from the slowly intensifying hunger as you scramble to find food to the heart-wrenching feeling as you get hit by a rifle round from the opposite building. Every situation is tense in DayZ but equally, once you pass the tension, you are rewarded either by continued survival, a potential new friend or, if whoever you are fighting won't stand down, some nice, shiny new gear. The only unfortunate downside is that helping people is a really risky action because some wont hesitate to stab you in the back, while others will return the favour if you meet again down the line. People are, by default, hostile towards you as they believe you will be hostile to them. It doesn't take much to change their mind and stop them potentially shooting you instantly.
The new development team is far better than the old team which many reviews are based off. Rocket was an awful lead, his roadmap for a single year ended up taking two to actually do half of, while the new team has managed to put together much of the roadmap in a few months. Updates are roughly once a month and are relatively substantial, the last update introduced an entirely new engine that has doubled my FPS in game on high settings. New gear and equipment is added frequently, and contrary to other reviews, I've found that weapons that are useable are becoming rarer rather than more common.
To sum up, here are some pros and cons of the new era of DayZ:
Pros:
-Heavily updated engine that has doubled performance from old updates.
-Diverse range of loot, from improvised weapons forged from sticks to military rifles salvaged from crash sites.
-Fantastic, huge game map that is riddled with opportunities.
-Deep satisfaction when you finally aquire an item you have been after for a while.
-Highly tense moments, be it when you suffer from disease or when you are engaged in combat.
-Zombies have been largely fixed since the last updates.
Cons:
-Potentially hostile community in the sense that you are more likely to be shot than helped.
-A range of bugs. None of them are TOO game-breaking but they can be incredibly frustrating when you are geared up and get flung out of a window.
-Rather small selection of vehicles right now.
-Loot spawning can be frustrating and unbalanced, with a plethora of clothing spawning yet no actual loot of value.
Neutral:
-Has spent a while in Early Access. Not sure how this changes the quality to some people as it is just a simple title.
Overall, I do recommend this game if you are willing to immerse yourself in it and power through any issues.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding Chocolate-Caramel Cream Pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
All-purpose flour, for surface
Chocolate pie crust
1/2 cup sugar
1/4 cup cornstarch
3/4 teaspoon salt
2 1/2 cups whole milk
4 ounces bittersweet chocolate (preferably 61 to 70 percent cacao), finely chopped
4 large egg yolks
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
2 cups Whipped cream
2 tablespoons caramel
1 thick block bittersweet chocolate, room temperature, for garnish
Directions
1.
On a lightly floured work surface, roll pate sucree to 1/8-inch thickness. Fit into a 9-inch pie dish. Trim edges, leaving a 1-inch overhang. Tuck overhang under dough so edges are flush with rim, and crimp edges. Lightly prick bottom of dough with a fork. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
2.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Line dough with parchment, and fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake until edges begin to look dry, 20 to 22 minutes. Carefully remove weights and parchment. Bake until crust is darker around edges and bottom looks dry, 10 to 12 minutes. Let cool completely on a wire rack. (Chocolate crust can be stored overnight.)
3.
Whisk together sugar, cornstarch, and salt in a small bowl. Heat milk and chocolate in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until chocolate melts.
4.
Whisk 1 cup hot milk mixture into sugar mixture until smooth. Whisk milk-sugar mixture into the remaining milk mixture in the saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until bubbling and thick, 4 to 5 minutes total (about 2 minutes after it comes to a boil).
5.
Whisk yolks in a medium bowl until combined. Pour in milk mixture in a slow, steady stream, whisking until completely incorporated. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it just begins to bubble, 1 to 2 minutes.
6.
Remove from heat, and stir in vanilla. Let custard cool in saucepan on a wire rack, whisking occasionally, for about 10 minutes.
7.
Pour custard into chocolate crust. Press plastic wrap directly on surface of custard. Refrigerate until custard filling is chilled and firm, at least 4 hours (or overnight).
8.
Gently fold caramel into whipped cream, then spread the caramel whipped cream over pie. Using a vegetable peeler, scrape chocolate block at a 45-degree angle to make a small mound of shavings, and sprinkle over whipped cream. Serve immediately, or refrigerate and serve within 2 hours.
Tip
The caramel mixture must be very cold before the whipped cream is folded in. Otherwise, the whipped cream will collapse.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding Chocolate-Caramel Cream Pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
All-purpose flour, for surface
Chocolate pie crust
1/2 cup sugar
1/4 cup cornstarch
3/4 teaspoon salt
2 1/2 cups whole milk
4 ounces bittersweet chocolate (preferably 61 to 70 percent cacao), finely chopped
4 large egg yolks
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
2 cups Whipped cream
2 tablespoons caramel
1 thick block bittersweet chocolate, room temperature, for garnish
Directions
1.
On a lightly floured work surface, roll pate sucree to 1/8-inch thickness. Fit into a 9-inch pie dish. Trim edges, leaving a 1-inch overhang. Tuck overhang under dough so edges are flush with rim, and crimp edges. Lightly prick bottom of dough with a fork. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
2.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Line dough with parchment, and fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake until edges begin to look dry, 20 to 22 minutes. Carefully remove weights and parchment. Bake until crust is darker around edges and bottom looks dry, 10 to 12 minutes. Let cool completely on a wire rack. (Chocolate crust can be stored overnight.)
3.
Whisk together sugar, cornstarch, and salt in a small bowl. Heat milk and chocolate in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until chocolate melts.
4.
Whisk 1 cup hot milk mixture into sugar mixture until smooth. Whisk milk-sugar mixture into the remaining milk mixture in the saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until bubbling and thick, 4 to 5 minutes total (about 2 minutes after it comes to a boil).
5.
Whisk yolks in a medium bowl until combined. Pour in milk mixture in a slow, steady stream, whisking until completely incorporated. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it just begins to bubble, 1 to 2 minutes.
6.
Remove from heat, and stir in vanilla. Let custard cool in saucepan on a wire rack, whisking occasionally, for about 10 minutes.
7.
Pour custard into chocolate crust. Press plastic wrap directly on surface of custard. Refrigerate until custard filling is chilled and firm, at least 4 hours (or overnight).
8.
Gently fold caramel into whipped cream, then spread the caramel whipped cream over pie. Using a vegetable peeler, scrape chocolate block at a 45-degree angle to make a small mound of shavings, and sprinkle over whipped cream. Serve immediately, or refrigerate and serve within 2 hours.
Tip
The caramel mixture must be very cold before the whipped cream is folded in. Otherwise, the whipped cream will collapse.

FOR PEOPLE THAT ARE CONSIDERING OF PURCHASING THIS GAME IN ITS ALPHA STAGE:
I recommend this game, but it depends on you, the player, to decide whether or not if it is your cup of tea. If you're like me, some one who has never touched the Mod or even any Arma games, your experience might be a bit more learning than success more than half of the time. Now about the game, for your (in)convenience, I will lay out the facts and opinions of the games below in the order of pro then con:
Pros:
1. Longer learning curve (might be con), but when you are used to the complicated control, it gives you an advantage over new players or people that are not controlling efficiently.
2. There are opportunities where you will feel really rewarding: eliminating threats, finding rare items, curing your illness, or even just meeting up with your friends (will be addressed again down below).
3. A fact: the developers have been through the developments of Arma 2 Day mod, meaning that they are really one of the oldest and most innovative developers (duh, the "zombie survival game rush" started after the popularity explosion caused by the Dayz mod).
4. (Also a indecisive one) the realism in this game is quite complicated. The process of just dragging and reloading guns manually is entertaining me so far but it may vary depends on individuals.
5. The sense of concern. You're going to be truely worried every time a red bar (negative bodily condition) appears and especially when it's lethal, and that's exactly what people tend to find in survival and horror games, and again the feeling of accomplishment goes through your body when you find the drink, food, or medicine in time and save yourself.
6. Rarity of weapons. For truely rare weapons, they are not common to find, but the game is giving a chance for any starters to find pistols randomly over the towns and car trunks.
7. The adrenaline pumps when get into a fight, and thinking that you might loose your gear, afraid to move an inch and stay prone the whole time. One fight will simply get you hooked to the game once you experience it.
8. Dynamics. Weathers, day and night, varied by the server, are increasing the details of the game bit by bit, creating a series of dynamic game experience.
9. Alpha. Being a part of an alpha game development is to help the developers make the game better, despite the cons I present you below, there's chances that our dev will work hard to change and make this game a better experience. Patience should be the way to go.
I believe I can continue this pros list further more, but let's move on to cons for now.
Cons:
1. The map. The map of Churnarus is absolutely ginormous and there's really not that many chance of you seeing any action in low populated servers or just not at the hottest place at the hottest time (combat usually happens in big cities). Plus a lot of communication is needed when you are trying to meet up with your friends. (Side note: learning the map gains advantage but it takes a long time).
2. Player interactions. If you are not on designated role play servers, you are more likely to "standalone" and have to face enemies instead of interesting roleplay moments. It is common that in survival game communities, players are not always friendly and helpful, unless he's... Your friend.
3. Controls. I have mentioned before that this game has a lot of movement and controls inherited from Arma, and it's most reasonable to stay that way. (Easter egg: f11 when you have a usable weapon to attempt suicide) Of course it takes time to master the skills of movements and combat. The first time I enter this game, all I did was tweaking the configurations and controls before I actually stepped into actual gameplay.
4. Graphics. I list it in the cons not because the graphics are horrible, but the graphics that we need is not as amusing. By that I mean this game is a PC killer (funny how they are trying to import it on PS4), and for a normal to high spec computer to run smoothly, you gotta take it to the lowest possible (for me to have over 80 fps in order to record smoothly) and that is not pleasant. Plus I really hope the dev import some of the "amazing" Arma3 engine graphics onto Dayz Standalone since it's using the same engine.
5. Engine. Arma engines are notoriously being known for bugs and graphics card graveyards; it's not the most efficient engine they can use, but it is not going horrible so far (still, ew... Arma engine).
6. Rage. Combats are exciting in this game, but when you're the victim of anything (they're about to add wolf in 0.61 !!!), you are going to be upset for losing whatever you've been working on for the last hour, maybe. And that is not the best feeling in the world.
7. Building and crafting. In most zombie survival games ( even Arma 2 mod), you're able to build yourself a comfortable little shack or a tiny hut, but sadly you're not going to be able to build in Dayz standalone. But eventually, natural servers without player built stuff would actually be pretty convenient since it would have things like spawn trapping or trolling buildings.
8. Glitches. I've probably mentioned a bit of glitch while mentioning the Arma engine, but this game has been in alpha for 3 years and devs should be concerned about some significant glitches that appeared from day 1 like item duping, space management, and zombies! Seeing zombies a tracking you through walls is pretty game breaking and heart breaking.
9. Modability. The Arma2 mod started out as an extremely elastic and modable piece of content, unlike Standalone, it has much more weapons and vehicles like machine guns and helicopters that some might say will be overpowered but it should be fun as an option to explore on different servers.
10. Cost. Finally it brings us to the topic of money, currently is August 2nd 2016 and without any sales event, Dayz is selling at a price of $34.99 USD just like Arma3, a military simulator game with advanced graphics mods. I believe they should make the price for Dayz a bit lower for more people to enjoy Dayz at the price it deserves (around $19.99 USD - $24.99 USD).
