So how do you review a game like Rust? It's difficult, there are a great many things to consider before you can decide which direction your thumb will point. Such as:
Community;
Pitiful at best. I mean, seriously, the community is quite possibly the worst in the history of online gaming, on par even with CS:GO and that is saying something. Reasons for that, in my opinion, are the Russians. Russians, Russians, Toxic AF Russians. They hide in bushes, trees and rocks. They hide in your stash, in your pocket, in your walls and in your freaking hard-drive. They be anywhere and everywhere. Oh, and they have just had, or are about to have, sexual intercourse with your mother. And your sister. Probably your brother, your father and your pooch too. In fact, no orifice is safe from these sexual deviants. It is no coincidence that both CS:GO and Rust have the worst communities around, they both contain a frighteningly large Russian player base.
Gameplay;
Great fun, generally speaking. Building mechanics are solid and if you are prepared to donate time and effort in to building your base, you can build something nigh on impossible to penetrate - unless you encounter a hacker of course, but all games of this nature contain hackers and it would be unfair of me to downvote a game due to the many hackers who frequent it, the devs do their best to remove them. The animals in game (wolves, deer, bears and chickens) are utterly dull, lifeless and generic creatures that bring very little to the positive side of the game. So, basically you gather and gather and gather some more until ur fingers go numb, you then build your base of operations, before standing back and admiring it for an extended period of time, then you go raid some poor unfortunare soul of their hard earned resources, and/or get raided yourself. Rince and repeat. Rust in a nutshell.
PvP:
The PvP aspect is great fun. Fairly balanced, generally speaking, I've had some great shootouts during my time in the game. Shooting Russians is always fun. Get's boring rather fast, though. At the end of the day raiding another players base, although loads of fun if they're online, can get rather repetitive after a while. Basically you spend resources to make C4/rockets in order to gain entry to a player owned house/base, only to steal their resources (sulfur mainly) to cover the cost of the resources you spent to raid their base. Welcome to the PvP cycle of Rust. Raiding is also 99% offline and unless they kill you during the raid there is no way to find out who did it.
PvE:
No PvE content to speak, and for a lot of people this means that the game will run dry rather fast. The game is crying out for PvE content in some form or another. Yes there are a few towns scattered across the map and for the most part they are well designed, but aside from the odd loot crate that you may be lucky enough to find, there is very little else to do there as there are no zombies/mutants or mobs of any kind to deal with. So basically you just head in to a town and loot as many crates as you can find, that is assuming the rooftop campers who control the town  (mainly large clans who dominate the server) don't Kalashnikov/Bolt-Action you to death first. So even the very little PvE content that the game contains is ruined by the KoS player base/Russians who know no better. Word to the devs: add more PvE content as your game is drastically lacking in comparison to Ark. Bigtime. Sort it out or lose the survival race.
Getting bored now so I'll cut off here. Decent game but severely limited with regards to depth and a distinct lack of PvE content. Fun for a while but gets boring rather fast. Worst of all is the community, though. Truly is terrible. Thus I cannot recommend.

Where to start ?
Well, Undertale is by far one of my most favorite games, of all time xD
When I first bought it, I was semi doubtful seeing as the graphics were a bit... retro and I wasn't used to that xD I had also never played RPGs before and this was my first one. Of course I jumped in without even watching any videos or anything because I wanted to figure it out for myself. Well, not understanding the mechanics I accidentally killed one of my most favorite characters and felt the need to reset the ENTIRE game, just for that character. That's one of the many things that makes this game special, you feel as if YOU yourself are actually in game, and you can't help but feel for the characters. Another thing that surprised me is that Flowey The Flower, actually remembers your past progress (unless it's a True Reset) and as soon as I came out of the ruins he had said that I had reset because I had killed her and felt bad. It had made me literally almost♥♥♥♥♥♥my pants because I've never played a game where it remembers your past progress xD (Even if its only that one character).
Now,it's an amazing and (maybe if life changing ? for me a little :/) game. The characters were really well thought and I loved their individual and unique personalities. The soundtrack, AMAZING. I can't get through a single day without listening to it over and over, or even humming it. Really well done. Had me in the feels a lot, not many games do that to me. I also loved the little surprises like Temmie Village ^_^ This game also had me laughing a LOT, which is awesome. The story was deep, and not what I expected, AMAZING job with this.
With every GREAT game comes cons. There is only one Con in my opinion, and that is the fan base. Yes, lots of people have made complaints and even avoided the GAME itself because of the toxic fan base. BUT PLEASE REMEMBER that this is with ALL games, and with Undertale it happens to be slightly worse than usual, but this doesn't NOT, I repeat, DOES NOT mean that you shouldn't play the game. With the fan base comes terrible roleplay that is just sad to even porn.(SERIOUSLY ? This is a HEARTFELT and heartwarming game. What kind of SICK people would make porn out of such an AMAZING game ?) This is the only con IN MY OPINION  yet it has nothing to do with the game itself, but people who are completely obsessed and mindless. BUT not ALL of the fan base is toxic, there's still some parts where you'll find heartwarming fan art from people which I find really nice.
OVERALL
===========
Really great game. Not what I had expected (In a REALLY good way xD). Amazing story and the message was really heartwarming. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.  Be weary of toxic fan base, but please don't judge the game because of this. Well done Toby Fox !

This game is a well rounded game.
Yes it does have its issues and bugs but i feel currently the game is in a good place for both old and new players and ill list why.
i have played about 1350 hours within thi game.
i have played solo, in gorups of 2-3, in group of 5-6, all the way up to groups of 20+
This game has a place for every group size and thoe complaining about clans dominating solos, you are on the wrong server
the reason people have a bad experience is because they choose to place themselves in a server which does not match their playing style.
solos decide to play on the biggest server in the oceanic region rustralasia then complain when the big 20+ member clans ruin them
if you want to tart playing the game please do not rush into these servers you are legit putting yourself up for failure.
there are MANY MANY modded and vanilla servers that contain longer wipe cycles AND lower pop caps.
There has always been complains about the system implemented for crafting.
originally the system was simply
you found a blueprint in a barrel (IF YOU WERE LUCKY) researching blueprints cost a fortune
THEN
You collected Blueprint fragments from barrels and you had to luck out for the blueprint you wanted, this caused large groups to roam the rad towns where barrels pawned, solos and small group complained as they couldn't easily get access to these blueprints. researching was improved though and became more cot efficient.
THEN
Blueprint system was removed. XP system was brought in, where you would farm and grind for experience and eventually level and unlock the levels for the item you wanted. This was again an issue for less frequent players as it took many hours of grinding just to unlock a gun for protection. researching was modified to give item fragments for temp use.
NOW
they have removed XP because it was too grindy, they have removed researching items. EVERYTHING IS UNLOCKED FOR EVERYONE!. the current system is the COMPONENT system
the component system is very straight forward in my opinion
it requires you to break open barrels and open boxes which are now spread all over the map
in these barrels you collect components such as rope or gears or tarp or gun bodies.
having access to craft every item make it MUCH more friendly to newer players.
it is as simple as search the item needed, find what is required, get the items, craft it.
This system allows for players of greater experience and hours to feel a fresh game play style
while giving new players a straight forward way to learn the game.
the game occasionally has lag issues, part of these are due to the unity engine causing some memory leaks.
though fixes are common and released weekly.
having a great GPU and CPU only contributes so much to performance.
for me a HDD upgrade to an SSD was the by far the biggest improvement to performance and consistent play without lag spikes.
Graphics features can be disabled which highly hinder the fps of the game. these features are honestly not needed for the game to look great, but actually make it harder to play e.g. motion blur
animal issues include bears being able to go through foundations ONLY when they are extremely low foundations.
to recap.
- new players: play on smaller pop servers which will help you learn the basics without being wrecked by larger groups present on larger servers.
- the game is suited for solos, small groups and big groups, if you place yourself in the right server
(that's your choice to be around these players)
- There are servers of multiple pop caps, and different length wipes (this is good)
- the current crafting system is GOOD, it allows for straight forward learning of whats needed to craft (everyone i honestly on an even playing field)
- Graphics fps issues are occasionally present as are bugs, as it is AN ALPHA.
- Graphics can be lowered to improve FPS without actually affecting game play.
- Biggest issue for FPS is OFTEN RAM AND HDD (recommended 16GB RAM and SSD (HUGE IMPROVEMENT))
- build smart, animals will not be able to kill you.
i hope this overview i useful, the game has a place for every player and group, you just have to be reasonable about your expectation when joining specific servers, that's up to you not the server

This is, by far, the BEST single player game I have ever played in all of my life.
Undertale, a game in which you actually do decide your fate by the very actions you take. Who will you be? Will you be the Peace loving friend who wouldn't harm a soul? Would you be the psychotic knife-wielding maniac determined to kill all the things? Will you be an explorer looking for treasure? Will you be the seeker of Justice, killing those who deserve it and sparing those who don't? This game lets your personality emerge in pure form. Whereas most other game I could kill mercilessly with no consequences and feel no shame, this game makes your personality emerge in the form of your very conscience.
One of the reasons that makes this game unique is that every last fightable enemy has a unique personality, so that if you kill, it feels like actually ending a life, whereas killing in other games is 'just another enemy'. I would reccomend this game to anyone, as it helped me understand more of who i am.

Game mechanics/controls:
So you see, map and movement wise, Undertale is your standard rpg. you move around and do some puzzles,basic stuff right?,The interaction button being z, the exit button being X, and the Inventory button being C,.the only real complaint i have is not moving with wasd , but this can be overlooked as a minor nitpick. Boom, you've just encountered the first mechanic taken from other rpgs, RANDOM ENCOUNTERS .However random encounters are not annoying in this game, in fact, a big chunk of the game is the memories you make that time when you fought that one stubborn enemy.At first glance , the Fight screen is standard, a first person earthbound-esque menu , facing the enemy, but wait , theres two options you don't understand, Act and Mercy, Act is your simple actions menu, Talk to the enemy, flirt with the enemy, taunt the enemy, challenge the enemy.During attacks by the enemy, you move a heart around the screen , this is your soul, if they hit it with their attacks ,you take damage ....and than theres mercy.A key feature in Undertale is the ability to spare enemies , once certain act based conditions are met, you may spare an enemy ,If you are the kind of experienced player i was, at first you thought nothing of this , killing everyone and farming...and than this happens
*But nobody came
Ah yes, the sort of creepy moment in the game , where a battle starts... and nothing happens, you just get that sore reminder that "You KILLED them .You truly are a terrible person" No turning back now, you cant reset, and you cant bring them back, so , you have to take on a boss... its boring, the games bosses are boring in the Genocide run, you kill them all in one hit.

Every once in a while a game comes around that is for actual gamers.  Rust is one of those games.
Rust is the ONLY survival game on Steam that is barebones and won't treat you like a simpleton. The game has it's share of babies playing no different than any other MP game, the difference in Rust is the devlopers won't bend the knee for their kind and ruin the game at the expense of the core gamer.  Rust is as barebones/hardcore as you, the gamer, would want your survival exprience to be.  When you die, it's going to be 100% your fault 99% of the time.  The game will not hold your hand.  As a gamer, you need to be self-sufficient and mindful of your actions.  Common sense goes a long way in surviving a game like Rust.  There's no gimmicky progression systems or item-based mechanics.  You can do anything from the start, so long as you can get the recources to make it.  There's no "progression wall" in your way.  Rust is as good as it gets for the survival genre.  No one else comes close, the rest that tried ended up pandering to alternative gamers.

What started out as a bright new future for one of my favourite mods of all time has slowly shown to be one of the lesser impressive early access games to date. Having played the game in interavals since it was put on Steam, I feel like almost nothing has been done. Sure, we got some more props, weapons and a higher framerate, but what else? What about the glaring issues of interaction with objects? The netcode? A rewamped player controller that's way too late to fix the clunky madness that is every ARMA game and its relatives.
While the development time for larger games usually exceed 4-6+ years from scratch, I just don't feel like we've come far enough to say DayZ will still have a playerbase when it's actually done. Considering what we've gotten so far, and compare that to other games that have been built from scratch, as opposed to DayZ already having a map, loads of assets and functions from the in-house engine and its games, it's rather embarrasing that games like Playerunknown's Battlegrounds and H1Z1 are moving faster ahead with more polished games than DayZ.
Please, prove me wrong, Bohemia. I want to love DayZ again, but at this rate, I'll be retired and suffering from dementia before we reach full release.

After 941 hours and several patches ( I have been playing since patch .55 ) it is safe to say that Dayz is dead.
Dayz promised something unique. A zombie survival game where players focused on surviving not only the AI but the loot system as well as other players. Not withstanding the COD fanboys who think any first person game with a gun requires you to expend bullets in a meaningless hail of pointless pvp, the game had serious potential. Gamers longing for a post apocolyptic survival game found a home in Dayz. One of the few games at the time of its release where weeks if not months of looting and surviving could be wiped away with a bad encounter with a bandit, the environment, or a zombie.
Despite all its promise Dayz could not gain traction on the development side. Players spent $30 for an Alpha game in the hopes of something more. In fits and sputters developers would hint at new content, bug fixes, and changes to the game to make it more playable and move the ball towards to endzone. But alas all these promises were empty. Each new patch brought about a fraction of the promised changes and content, fixed some bugs while creating new ones. The only thing consistent about the development team seems to be their endless partying and tweets at social events parading across europe. My $30 well spent I guess. To be fair 941 hours, I got my moneys worth.
DayZ is the game that could have been, but it will be nothing more. Forever an Alpha, and if by some miracle Brian Hicks runs out of booze money you might actually see a beta, but I wouldn't hold my breath.

Saying I love this game is an understatement. I could play this game and never tire of it, and it's that kind of endless re-playability that makes Borderlands 2 one of the best buying decisions you'll ever make. A word of warning though: make sure you have at least one friend to play it with. Multiplayer is what truly makes this game worth playing every single day. Sure, playing the campaigns solo is fun and satisfying on its own, but with a friend (or friends) the game takes on a whole new dimension of enjoyment.
I love every bit of dialogue in this game, the writing is spot-on hilarious, and even emotionally touching at times. And the weapons....oh, the weapons~    Searching for rare, legendary or otherwise badass weaponry is a reason to play in and of itself. It seems the possibilites in this world are truly endless. It's an action FPS on the outside, sure, but I love just how much of an adventure RPG-element there is at the heart of the game in terms of style and character skill development. You care about the characters plights, as well as the story itself. Borderlands 2 really has its own personality, and you can immerse yourself completely in this crazy world.
Another thing to mention is the DLC. There are plenty of extra missions to choose from, and it only adds to the replay value. In fact, you're much better off just buying the Game of the Year edition since it includes a lot of them.  Since I mentioned RPG's earlier, I will specifically suggest Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep as my favorite of all the DLC missions. If you enjoy Magic the Gathering, Final Fantasy, Dungeons and Dragons or anything like it---you will experience a nerdgasm with this one.

I highly reccomend this game if you've somehow not been spoiled, and even if you have it's worth giving a try.

Despite all the issues, it is STILL the MOST REALISTIC zombie game out there. You want a game that's actually about SURVIVAL and EXPLORATION in an OPEN WORLD with RP elements, then this game is the one.
Unlike zombie games like:
- Dead Island (Action)
- Dead Rising (Action)
- Resident Evil (Action/Survival horror)
- Red Dead Redemption Zombie Nightmare (Action)
- Dead Space (Action/Survival horror)
- CoD Zombies (Action)
- Left 4 Dead (Action)
- Dying Light (Action)
- The Evil Within (Survival horror)
- State of Decay (Action)
- TWD Survival Instinct (Action/Survival horror)
etc.
DayZ actually takes a REALISTIC apporach to the zombie apocalypse.
There are no special infected, no giant boss zombies, no mutants, no zombies using guns, etc.
I am NOT saying any of those game series are bad, Resident Evil is actually one of my favorite game series of all time, but the games lack REALISM
The ONLY other games that compare, in the SLIGHTEST, to DayZ is "H1Z1" and "7 Days to Die", and even those games dont compare well to the REALISM that is in DayZ.
There are a lot of problems in this game from hackers, glitches, bugs, etc. and as you can guess, all the players will kill you on sight. There are no friendly players in DayZ.
In DayZ you have a whole country to explore. The problem here is it takes a LONG time to get from 1 place to another. You will spend possibly HOURS running before you actually get somewhere, so its pretty much best to just camp in/near 1 large city.
Now in other games you might get that right? In Dead Island you get a whole island, in Dead Rising you get a whole City, but like I said in DayZ you get a whole COUNTRY. Not only that but areas are not spearated like they are in other games. There are no loading screens  or boundaries to the exploration. I would even argue that DayZ has the largest map in gaming history. The map is HUGE.
In DayZ you have to worry about:
- your body temperature
- starvation
- hydration
- infection
- sickness
- fractures and broken bones
- blood loss, you have a blood type so you can do blood transfusions with certain players if they have the same as you
And you can do things such as:
- cook food
- set up a camp to house your items and for your group to live at
- customize your character
- scavange for food, weapons, medical supplies, etc.
- craft and customize your weapons by finding weapon attachments
- PvP
- PvE
etc.
Until another game comes out, that does a better job than DayZ, I have to recommend this game.
I recommend this game to those, who are like me, who are looking for a zombie game that is OPEN WORLD and REALISTIC, and focuses on RP and EXPLORATION.
This game is for people who are NOT looking for an open world sandbox zombie game to do as you please like some kind of zombie killer BA.
It's a shame that this game doesn't recieve much updates and the devs keep dissapointing everyone who has supported this game. But it still holds as the most REALISTIC zombie game as of now.

There's a major problem with DayZ that, if it doesn't get fixed, will kill the game indefinately. Fluidity. The engine for the game is so bad, that it lacks the realism in the motions of what my character is doing. It makes the player feel as if they're not supposed to be in the world they are in, which is a huge problem. The reason why games like 7 Days to Die is good is because the game feels quick, with my character doing the motions as soon as I tell them to, not a few seconds later. However, in DayZ, the character moves from one animation to the other so slowly, it's almost funny.
One of the few games that I would want a refund for. Do Not Buy, unless the game becomes free.

Well... it's been 2.5 years. Bought this game on launch hopeful for the most realistic and advanced standalone zombie game to date. Since then there have been competitors, most notably H1Z1, who have made tons of progress.
Day Z simply seems to be dragging itself along as if crippled, after making tens of millions of dollars. They made progress for a bit at the beginning, but updates are now very small and add little to nothing more in terms of advancing the mechanics of the game, polishing/optimizing the graphics, or even fixing glitches that have been around since launch (zombies phasing through walls anybody?)
I play it on occasion every month or so, but see that little to nothing has changed. I will continue to do so until the game has officially been released, and if they have redeemed themselves then maybe, just maybe, I will give this game a positive review.

Saying I love this game is an understatement. I could play this game and never tire of it, and it's that kind of endless re-playability that makes Borderlands 2 one of the best buying decisions you'll ever make. A word of warning though: make sure you have at least one friend to play it with. Multiplayer is what truly makes this game worth playing every single day. Sure, playing the campaigns solo is fun and satisfying on its own, but with a friend (or friends) the game takes on a whole new dimension of enjoyment.
I love every bit of dialogue in this game, the writing is spot-on hilarious, and even emotionally touching at times. And the weapons....oh, the weapons~    Searching for rare, legendary or otherwise badass weaponry is a reason to play in and of itself. It seems the possibilites in this world are truly endless. It's an action FPS on the outside, sure, but I love just how much of an adventure RPG-element there is at the heart of the game in terms of style and character skill development. You care about the characters plights, as well as the story itself. Borderlands 2 really has its own personality, and you can immerse yourself completely in this crazy world.
Another thing to mention is the DLC. There are plenty of extra missions to choose from, and it only adds to the replay value. In fact, you're much better off just buying the Game of the Year edition since it includes a lot of them.  Since I mentioned RPG's earlier, I will specifically suggest Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep as my favorite of all the DLC missions. If you enjoy Magic the Gathering, Final Fantasy, Dungeons and Dragons or anything like it---you will experience a nerdgasm with this one.

Undertale is a game that has been on my list of "Games to Play" ever since I started hearing about it. Not only from what I heard of its unique take on the RPG-genre, but also because monsters were a centerpiece in its story. And as somebody who loves monsters in just about every medium they appear in, I had to see how the game handled them.
A few weeks ago I happen to see the game on sale so I decide to buy it to cross one more game off my list. And when I sit down to actually play the game, I am abosolutely blown away. Story, characterization, and a stunning soundtrack all come together to create one the greatest gaming experiences I've had in years. The game turns the RPG-genre on its head by making the formula of killing monsters to increase your character's level and power entirely optional. Which on its own doesn't sound like much, but the ramifications for choosing to kill or not to kill are great, and both consequences create an emotionally moving story.
Undertale is one of the very few cases where it is a game that is deserving of all the praise it receives. I think it is a game that should be experienced by everyone, at least once. It is not for everyone (and perhaps it resonates so strongly with me because I'm emotional and sentimental) but it offers a unique journey, and maybe you'll learn something on that journey.
Undertale has reignited my passion for storytelling again, perhaps it can do something similar for you.

Undertale is a game that has been on my list of "Games to Play" ever since I started hearing about it. Not only from what I heard of its unique take on the RPG-genre, but also because monsters were a centerpiece in its story. And as somebody who loves monsters in just about every medium they appear in, I had to see how the game handled them.
A few weeks ago I happen to see the game on sale so I decide to buy it to cross one more game off my list. And when I sit down to actually play the game, I am abosolutely blown away. Story, characterization, and a stunning soundtrack all come together to create one the greatest gaming experiences I've had in years. The game turns the RPG-genre on its head by making the formula of killing monsters to increase your character's level and power entirely optional. Which on its own doesn't sound like much, but the ramifications for choosing to kill or not to kill are great, and both consequences create an emotionally moving story.
Undertale is one of the very few cases where it is a game that is deserving of all the praise it receives. I think it is a game that should be experienced by everyone, at least once. It is not for everyone (and perhaps it resonates so strongly with me because I'm emotional and sentimental) but it offers a unique journey, and maybe you'll learn something on that journey.
Undertale has reignited my passion for storytelling again, perhaps it can do something similar for you.

Mixed bag of emotions...
Best way to explain DayZ. I have been playing since DayZ Mod back in 2013/14 and before that all I really played was survival open sandbox games. When the standalone came out I was super excited and super let down all at the same time. The game was not ready to be released what so ever and was super buggy. Hacks were rampant and trolls were a many, however now a days (.60) the game is starting to turn around. There is still much work to be done and the dev team has to make some attempts to curb some of the trolling players.
If you are looking for a serious, gritty, survival based game... well this just isn't it. The game lacks any sort of serious need to find food, water or shelter. Food and water are literally everywhere, you also need a TON of it to make yourself full and not thirsty. It leaves you feeling more like an insatiable force roaving the land devouring everything in site, rather than someone just trying to live.
As for shelter, you don't need it... at all. Rain is rare and doesn't really cause much discomfort beyond (I am soaked). Night time, well most servers reset just before it gets dark so who cares.
Then there is the KoS. Kill on sight isn't a bad aspect of the game, BUT it would be nice if developers didn't encourage it by only updating the game with more weapons and weapon sounds. Maybe add barricading, base building, and struction building. Work more on the survival aspect of the game than just the PvP aspect. Make zombies more of a threat so that people can't just shoot without any major reprecussions. Fire a gun, get swamped by zombies?
Anyway, if you want a super realsitic survival game, this isn't it.
Want a game that has a large map and has a few zombies but is still counter strike, play DayZ.
That being said I still love the game, I just wish it could be more than what it is.

First of all I'll start by saying this game is AMAZING! DayZ is the PERFECT survival game, your playstyle options are wide and you can either choose being a hunter which kills animals / other survivors to survive or you can choose to fix up a car and explore the entire extremely large map! You can even help grow yourself some vegetables in a small garden. Thanks to the last patches, the wind can affect trees and some new environment sounds have been added, which changes from place to place around the map. For example - You'll hear birds chirping when you're deep in the woods and you'll hear the wind blows when on a hill. These changes makes Dayz also LOOK realistic! I play this game since 2014 and I have to say this game progressed amazingly. It was pretty slow though but this is the point! The creators want us to tell them what we want to add to DayZ so it will be the best! Every comment, every bug report, every recommendation, these helped this game become what it is today! As of June 2017 the BETA version is about to be released! In my opinion, this game called "EARLY ACCESS" only because the creators are still add more and more to the game. They finished fixing things ( pretty much :'D ). All they do now is adding more cool stuff to the game to make it even greater!
The only main problem this game has is not the game itself, but the COMMUNITY!
I do my best to play as a friendly guy and I am REALLY looking for some interaction. As of recent times, it's pretty much IMPOSSIBLE to find friendly people. Every guy that I met and had a gun with bullets just shot me without even thinking twice. Most of the times I was unarmed anyways but people don't care about it, they just want to have the feeling that they killed someone. The way you can get the best interactions is joining a Roleplay whitelisted community. To do that you have to be above the age of 15 (Most of the times... Some communities accept every age and some accept only 18+ and even 21+ everything depends). If you are already about 15 and you're looking for some interaction like me, you have to walk through a pretty long proccess of applications and interviews... I got to a point that I've had enough, I decided to QUIT THIS GAME until the community will be fixed. Unfortunately, this isn't something that a few computer programs can fix...
This is why I am writing this post, if you think about buying this game, I would highly recommend doing so and I would even more reccommend playing it in a "HERO" play style. You don't have to be friendly all the time and even you don't you can still use some callouts like "put your hands up or you're dead". This game's future is up to YOU! Please choose the correct way to play it, not only for your enjoyment but everyone's...

Bought this game on August 1, 2014.
Here's my Opinion so far: (TL;DR Scroll down)
At first, game was buggy and had extremely low frame rates on my gaming PC, but even then, i lowered the graphics and game was kinda OK.

TL;DR
Buy it, game is so much fun, but don't play it by yourself. If you're new to the game look for a High Loot server and have fun. :)

Even as I've played other great games, Undertale is still remains my favorite.
And not just because it filled the angry lesbian fish warrior-shaped hole in my heart I didn't even know I had. Or because it filled the "adorable weeb bi dinosaur scientist" hole. Or filled the "adorable romance between fish warrior and a weeb dino" hole. Those were all very important holes that this game filled though.
Undertale is great because all of the characters are loveable and wonderful and flawed, even the minor ones. Undertale is great because it genuinely made me care about these characters and want to save them, and made me feel so awful when I killed them I had to restart immediately. Because it offers a huge world that you can almost endlessly explore, with fun dialogue options every which way. Because it has a great soundtrack and a sprawling complex story. Because it makes you think about your choices and feel the impact of them.
The game gets in your head and makes it almost impossible to be disconnected from the story you're in. It makes you rethink how you play games and how games work. It takes full advantage of the immersiveness of gaming, the control the player has and messes with your head. It cleverly subverts expectation and weaves mechanics like saving, repeated dialogue and resets into the story in inventive, awesome and sometimes hilarious ways.
Gameplay, story, visuals, music, characters, replayability, great humor- this game has it all. A thousand thumbs up. Play it, be good to your goat mom and enjoy the pie. Or become a monster who deserves to burn in hell. Whichever you're cool with.

This game. There is not enough I can say about this game. It made me laugh, cry, think, feel, dream, hope, and love. It broke my heart and put it back together again. Rarely do I ever finish adventure games or rpgs. I often find that games can't hold my attention for longer than 10 minutes, but this game kept me enthralled and entranced long after I had reached the end. And I honestly believe that playing this has made me a bit of a better person and gamer.
The writing for this game is amazing. It takes a lot of work to fully develop so many characters in what is essentially a game that has 5-6 hours of content (if you are rushing through it). I started playing one night with my little brother sitting on a couch beside me, and almost immediately we both fell deeply in love with these small pixels on the screen. I know, crazy right, but this game is so amazingly well made that these little character who aren't real start to become so amazingly vivid and full of life. The game had a fraction of the funds most AAA games have to work with, and it had me more emotionally invested within the first few minutes than any other game I have played before. This game is an amazing display of what characters in games can be if developers are willing to put heart into them, instead of trying to squeeze money out of them.
And the music. God is the soundtrack beautiful. I have been listening to the songs since the game came out in 2015 (its 2016 when I wrote this). Every song fits so graciously into the background and builds on to this world that is so graphically unimpressive that it is more captivating than anything I've seen in 2015 or 2016. And yes, the graphics aren't that impressive. It's an rpg. But the graphics fit it well too, in a way that I doubt better or realistic graphics would have. Even with such simplistic graphics, you can tell that tons of work and love went into creating them.
AAA game devs could learn a thing or two from this game. While everyone is so intensely set on making choices a huge thing in games, Undertale fits it in without making it this all-important game changing mechanic and without making it overwhelming. And yes, your choices do matter (looking at you Telltale), and this game will make you think on your feet about what it is you want to do and what kind of person you want to be. You literally change the world you are in with your decisions, which gives me hope that maybe bigger game devs will see this and actually start making good games again.
There is no one way to play this game. Of course, there are a vast number of "endings." This game is deeply aware of what you do and remembers things you've done that you might try to jump back to an old save to remedy. (Don't kill the Goat Mom for the love of god.) It really is worthwhile to play the game several times, if you can manage to do so (you'll understand when you play). It's super meta. And if you get to a difficult part of the game, I'm sure determination will see you through.
This game is so charming, and funny, and beautifully made that I can't give it enough praise. It came to me at a time when I was sick of video games and sick of the redundency they throw at you. It reminds you what it is to play games and fall in love with them, in an age where games are racing just to have the best graphics. It reminds you that you do matter, no matter how small or insignificant you think you are; that with enough determination you can do anything you set your heart to. Thanks Toby and the Undertale team, for making me love playing again, and for reminding me to keep holding on to my hopes and dreams.

==========
--->> DayZ Standalone - DirectX 11 - REQUIRED NOW <<---
==========
Are you REALLY running DX11 - Read on and I'll tell you how to know for sure.
The recent update (6.0) now requires you to have a graphics card that runs DirectX v11
Most older cards will not and even if you were able to run the game before you may not be able to run it now.
(I have 1300+ hours but can't play anymore unless I buy a new GPU)
I would like to offer information that I hope will help prevent some stress.
The game requirements do clearly say DX11 is required - and at first glance most players will see DX11 when they look at their "System"
Even my "System" says: "DirectX Version: DirectX 11"
Although this is right it is wrong ...
Let me explain - you're looking in the wrong place at the wrong version
I had the same problem - my pc said I was running DX11 but in reality I had 10.1
The CORRECT place to look for the version of DirectX you need is:
On the DISPLAY Tab in the DirectX Diagnostic Tool
On the Right side you will see "DDI Version:" 10.1 (or whatever you have)
(Mine says 10.1 - which is why I can't run dayz anymore)
==========
To access the DirectX Diagnostic Tool:
1) Click Start, and then click Run
(depending on your version of windows you may use a different path to search your pc)
2) Type dxdiag in the search box and press enter to launch the DirectX Diagnostic Tool
3) When the DirectX Diagnostic Tool opens it will be on the "System" tab so JUST NOTE the version of DirectX that is displayed on the DirectX Version line at the bottom
(THIS IS NOT THE CORRECT TAB)
4) Now click on the "Display" Tab at the top and look on the right side under the word:
-Drivers-
_________
"DDI Version:" 10.1 (or whatever you have) (again mine says 10.1 so I can't play)
==========
This is the actual location of the DirectX version you need to run DayZ Standalone.
It MUST say version 11 here or you will NOT be able to run the game.
When you are finished checking your DX version click exit.

Sooo... Undertale, this may be one of my first serious reviews so let's go with it:
History:
I just got to say this, it doesn't have a history, yeah sure you get some background at the beginning, but most of the game is just the "stuff that happens" while the character travels around the underworld, not much to say, I would have loved a little more instead of "plot happening" right at the end of any route in the game.
Gameplay:
The concept of the gameplay was nice, but at the end I feel bored by it, most fights will go "Do an action to be able to spare an enemy", I really tought you will be actually talking or convincing the enemies into being friendly, but no, any enemy has a set pattern of actions to do in order to spare them, it got bored and I felt I was in any other RPG, just doing the same to every enemy.
Graphics:
Not complaining about it, cute a nice graphics, that's it.
Music:
One of the best parts of the game, some really nice music that gets really well in either the fight or the place you are, just really good music.
Final opinion:
The game in the end is really good, some nice music, good quality, nice graphics, but it has flaws, lack of a more defined and progressive history really upsets me, repetitive combat made me feel like I was playing any other RPG, some characters are good, but it really depends on how you are, because you will love some but you'll hate some, It's a masterpice? No, but it's a really good and nice crafted game.

Rust is the kind of game you love to hate.
I love it because Rust itself is a good game, the idea behind it is awesome and its potential is huge.
BUT (there's always a but. And a butt) the community is rather toxic and the game is poorly optimised.
All public servers are "ruled" by big clans, so competing with them if you're a solo player is next to impossible. Also, rust gets reeeaaaaally boring after a while if you're a solo player, and being "successful" in rust by yourself is a nightmare. Only once did I manage by myself to make a base so strong that it never got raided all the way in an entire month, but it was tedious, boring and not really worth the time invested in it.
Play Rust with your friends however, and the whole game experience changes. You probably still won't be able to compete with the established clans on public servers, but tons of fun are guaranteed nonetheless.
PRO:
- loads of fun if you've got a group of friends to play it with
-Has the potential of being the best survival multiplayer game on the market
CON
-Extremely poorly optimised
-Gets either boring or frustrating after a while when playing by yourself
-New Exp system sucks
-Early Development since it's launch in 2013, we do get regular updates but nothing gamechanging for the past 6 months in the way of optimising
-Did i mention that it is EXTREMELY POORLY OPTIMISED?
-Oh and optimisation sucks.
-Also, i hate the bears.
TL;DR
If it's on sale, and your pc can run it, then buy the game. 10 bucks is a decent price for a couple dozens of hours of fun.

Or you can be a murderous villian and kill everything you encounter. I also love how depending on which run you do, different storylines open up. When doing a Neutral Run, you begin to learn that the characters and really sweet and nice under everything, and that they all have personailtys. For example, Undyne at first seems to be a bad person by continuesly trying to kill you. But it turns out that she is a good guy trying to save her own kind. I also like like how each battle is fleshed out. It's either you can kill them, or flirt your way away from a Tsunderplane. The amount of choice in the game is amazing.
One of my favourate things to do was the inclusing of a secret 3rd mode called the Genocide Route. When killing enough monsters in the first part of the game, you activate this route and the music gets drery and dark, as if something bad is afoot. The more you kill the more you distane yourself. I also like how by the time your adventure is nearly over, one character stands in your way. Sans has a lot of backstory that we simply don't know yet. All we know is that he and Papyrus appeared in town one day and that Snowdin got more "interesting" since. We know Sans has the abillity to bend time and space as he usaully uses "shortcuts" to go to places. He is also seen to appear in two places at once in the forests of Snowdin. In the Genocide Route, you learn that even though Sans is a lazy character, he is very powerful, only beaten down by one flaw. His 1 Attack and 1 Defence. Only one hit will take him down. But the 4th wall helps him as he is able to dodge the attacks, making the battle difficult if its your first time going through it.

Why am I putting this much effort into a review for Undertale when I could simply just write “Buy It.” and call it a day? I’m not quite sure. Reviews praising the game are a dime a dozen, and rightfully so.
I played Undertale back in early 2016 for the first time. I bought it due to it’s reception although I knew little to nothing about it at the time . This however worked in my favour as I had no idea what was coming or to expect.
Spurred on by the clunky, comical trailer and the reception my first few hours of playing the game were magical. I don’t wish to spoil the game though and I avidly suggest trying to avoid the big spoilers. As soon as you boot the game up you’re presented with a little backstory, explaining the premise of the game. After naming your character and falling down a hole into some ruins you start the game, soon coming across your first character, Flowey the Flower.
It's worth mentioning that the combat is hilariously entertaining. I've never really played any bullet-hell games, only segments in games where it crops up but Undertale's various twists on it will leave you chuckling and asking for more. Plus it'll keep you guessing as to what the game has up it's sleeve...
Flowey is extremely helpful when starting the game, giving you all the tutorial shtick you’d come to expect. His happy-go-lucky demeanour is certainly easy on the soul when you begin.
Soon after you’re finished with Flowey you’re attacked by a vicious rabid goat, just kidding. Tutorial the Goat greets you and makes your life hell for the next 10-20 minutes, literally holding your hand around segments of the ruins which act as a rather boring tutorial. Like any decent game it is necessary though in getting to grips with the basics. Monsters are strewn throughout the ruins which you’ll frequently come into contact with. Some advice: Be careful how you choose to “interact” in combat.
Like my father always told me,
Except I made that up.
After the tutorials done the kind goat lady brings you into her humble abode. You eventually ask her how do you leave the ruins, she dodges the question. You follow her after she says she’s got something to do and she reveals she’s going to destroy the ruin’s exit unless you can prove to her you’re strong enough to survive in the outside world and without her care. After you “prove” you can (forgive me for being vague, avoid spoilers where I can) you exit the ruins and enter Snowdin Forest.
You are soon acquainted with the skeleton brothers Sans and Papyrus and oh lord you’re in for a treat. The two are hilarious and act as the comic relief (more so Papyrus) throughout the game. After you encounter them you venture through the snowy woodland, bumping into yet more creatures, conversing with Sans and best of all, being tested by The Great Papyrus in an array of convoluted puzzles. The atmosphere through the woods is really peaceful and somewhat beautiful. The puzzles are, well, easy, simple and don’t really function as challenges but that’s the point. You laugh at Papyrus’ failed attempts to capture you, playing along with each scenario as you can’t help but love and feel a ‘lil sorry him for it. Eventually you reach the end of Snowdin Forrest and the gauntlet of deadly terror where papyrus obliterates you.
Just kidding.
After that you get to Snowdin Town and have a poke around before you’re soon met with one of the greatest boss battles I have ever witnessed (If you can even call it a “battle”). Soon you meet Undyne, a character who has been mentioned once or twice by Papyrus. The Heavily Armoured Knight doesn’t seem too friendly towards you and as you go through the games third area waterfall you must progress whilst surviving various encounters with Undyne.
Hopefully by this point I’ve at least got you interest in buying the damn thing. I don’t want to go any further. Instead from this point onward I’ll talk about some of the other things Undertale has going for it.
If it’s not the great writing and characters that make this game great then it’s the music. I’m going to take a page out of videogamedunkey’s book and say that the music is the crowning achievement of this game. There are so many different, quality songs and melodies that will resonate with you throughout your adventure. You’ll feel pumped, sad, happy, amused to name a few of the emotions Undertale will bring on with its superb story and symphonic score. Toby Fox really outdid himself. Kudos to him.
The game also has 3 unique endings: The neutral, the true pacifist and the genocide (imagine the last one dripping with blood). My recommendation is to go through the game blind without knowing how to achieve each ending. Look up a guide after the first time you beat the game if you feel so inclined. S'what I did.
No. There simply aren’t enough bone jokes (that was sarcasm for all the foetuses typing angrily on their laptops whilst floating around in their mothers wombs).
To further illustrate my point this isn't my first review of Undertale on Steam. My original one was negative and I slammed the game for obscene reasons. I was being sarcastic of course.
Thank you for reading and I hope I could be of help.

Before I begin my review, here's my rating for this game:
9001 / 10 (That awesome!)
I initially bought this game for the PS3 because I'd heard  it was indescribably awesome and from the moment I installed it I was hooked. I even managed to get my casual gaming girlfriend to play it with me and she loved it so much, she kept dragging me away from my studies and other duties so we could play, and hell, I let her! This game has tons of replay value and add the fact that you can form a group of up to 4 friends to raid bosses or just visit any random corner of the map and kill everything in it (except NPCs), its awesome. Even if you're not good at FPSs, this game is very casual-friendly. Long story short, I ended up buying the Steam version with a couple of friends so we could play online whenever we wanted without having to pass the controller around.
There are four initial classes (2 more in DLC) and, if you want, you can make a squad made up of the same class if that's what all your friends chose (there are a lot of sniper fanatics out there). The story's hilarious, the game steps up the difficulty depending on how many people are in the adventure and their overall levels, there's tons and tons of weapon types, weapon mods, class mods, shields all of which affect how much damage your character can soak up, how much it can dish out and even how it looks. Even when the story's over, the difficulty doesn't let up and it even has New Game + mode where you restart your adventure but keep all your guns, loot and level (and you can restart as many times as you want!).
And don't worry about thinking if you pick the sniper class you'll always have to play with a sniper in hand; NO! Any and all playable characters can use any and all weapon types. What makes the classes different is their special abilities which can be (sort of) customized by spending skill points when you level up.
If you think your character's going to look too bland compared to all the other Siren, Gunzerker, Assassin, and Soldier classes out there, don't fret. You can make your character unique by customizing its head and body by finding rare items when you beat tough enemies. To make the deal sweeter, the guys at Gearbox have a facebook group where they post what they call "Shift Key Codes" which once entered in the game, your character are rewarded with Golden Keys which open a special treasure chest which always spawn really rare loot depending on your level.
If you're considering buying this game, just stop thinking about it and just click the buy button dude(ette). Even in single player the game is awesome.
TL;DR
Game's awesome. Great replay value. Hilarious, challenging and fun story. Seamless drop-in-out multiplayer where you can join a friend or vice-versa. Awesome RPG elements and easy to pick up and play FPS gameplay with a comedic albeit sometimes silly yet creative world. Oh, and the DLC just adds to an already awesome game. Just get it!

What a burst of creativity and fun this game was!  An absolute gem.  If you grew up on old school RPG's, first off, you NEED to play this game.  It's a love letter to the RPG, yet simultaneously a brilliant critique as well.  If you like pixel art, play this game.  I'm not a huge fan, but there were several scenes were even I was like wow, that looks great!  If you like a great score variating between 8 bit and orchestral elements, play this game.  If you like a great, emotionally investing story, play this game.
The gameplay is seemingly simple, but as the game progresses, well... you'll see.  The story in this text-only game has a surprising depth, incorporating well crafted doses of humor, sadness, romance, and even eerieness.  I can't believe a game with no voice actors made me tear up, but this one did it.  Player choice also has a strong impact on the story, there are literally dozens of ending variations.
Undertale:  Great story, high replay value, fantastic score, offbeat yet hilarious humor, memorable characters...

It's a love letter to the RPG, yet simultaneously a brilliant critique as well.  If you like pixel art, play this game.  I'm not a huge fan, but there were several scenes were even I was like wow, that looks great!  If you like a great score variating between 8 bit and orchestral elements, play this game.  If you like a great, emotionally investing story, play this game.
The gameplay is seemingly simple, but as the game progresses, well... you'll see.  The story in this text-only game has a surprising depth, incorporating well crafted doses of humor, sadness, romance, and even eerieness.  I can't believe a game with no voice actors made me tear up, but this one did it.  Player choice also has a strong impact on the story, there are literally dozens of ending variations.
Undertale:  Great story, high replay value, fantastic score, offbeat yet hilarious humor, memorable characters...

I remember when I played in the legacy days and why I quite. Right before Rust got put onto the new version, it was horribly toxic and full of hackers on my servers.
People would use notepad++, turn off doors, walls, whatever, sleeping bag through a door they couldn't see, kill themselves, and repeat until they got to loot. One person could destroy everything in a night, two people could take an inventory of your best doodoo and destroy the rest. Eventually the only way to get past this was a few things.
Put barriers everywhere, hackers have to now turn off an extra thing in order to kill you, or destroy it. also fill the entire floor with boxes so they have to detroy it to sleeping bag through. also spikes everywhere possible so they can't fly through.
Also a glitch where you could stack an infinite amount of stairs on one block so you could spend hours destroying a few hundred stairs/ramps that were put on one block.
Also every server with any players was abolutely filled with hackers.
I remember a community that was only mostly KOS, where you could join massive groups, and you could trade with people and only be murdered some of the time. And even then, its a hunt. You track that group down and they know they're being hunted. They need to fortify or always be moving loot and hoping to not get killed on transport missions.
But, the community is now somehow more KOS, and while I'm not entirely sure if the hacker issue is as bad as before, but if it still is, you need to ask what it is worth. This game has been in development for years and the biggest thing I can say is now it looks prettier.
I wouldn't be surprised if people can still turn off doors and walls with some exploit or another, or some hack, and just destroy literally every box in your house. It was happening for a long time in many different ways in legacy, and don't be surprised if it's still happening in the current, but for all I know it isn't.
I was in one of the largest groups on a large public server, and there were amazing, all-nighter raids, trading missions, having to do espionage and get door codes from a guy and pretend to join his clan to be able to have an easier time on raiding missions.
It was awesome.
But the only way to have the truly awesome experiences in Rust are to play every or almost everyday, and join a massive group.
So if you want to play, wait for a sale, and commit a summer to it, and then never touch it again.

I have never been part of a gaming community that is more active and enjoyable then that of Rust. Of course, I'm speaking in terms of a large scale, as certain individuals can be a little undesirable. The devs have been releasing updates for this game every week, for almost 3 years, working hard until this game is at the point of perfection. It has been an honor playing this game for a long time, watching the game evolve as time passes.
Enough about the community, let's move on to the gameplay. As a new player, it can be very difficult to get a hold of yourself and get started into becoming an avid Rust player. Unfortunately, many people enjoy KOS'ing and much more of the sort. I recommend getting into a clan or a small group of players willing to teach new players so that you can get your foot on the pedal and start driving your way into the world that is Rust. I was quite lucky, having a few friends to help me enjoy Rust a little more.
TL;DR. Great community, but friends may be needed to enjoy the full potential of this game.

An RPG where you don't have to kill anyone. That's what UNDERTALE is. The words 'don't kill anyone' may seem pretty boring but that's not the case with this game. It's gameplay is, in my opinion, one of the most unique yet spectacular ones I've ever seen or heard of. Talk your way through each fight or slaughter everyone in your path. Most people would pick the latter but the consequences of doing so can be collateral. The storyline of the game revolves around your actions. Killing everyone would cause you to go down the genocide path in the story. Sparing everyone generates the pacifist route. A mix of both causes the neutral route. The game is a game that wants to instill a new perspective into each player. A perspective in where every single action results in something favorable or unfavorable depending on the action. I can't say more about this unique perspective this game presents as it would be a spoiler. UNDERTALE's soundtrack is also amazing in so many levels. As an original soundtrack, it sets the overall feel of the whole story. The graphics in the game are unique in its own way. It's neither detailed nor realistic yet it, in my opinion, is perfect for the game. Every character is beautiful and detailed in terms of background and personality. UNDERTALE also tends to be pretty random at moments which is one of the reasons why it's pretty special. It tends to become humorous at times of sadness and despair. The fandom of UNDERTALE can be pretty unnecessarily 'intense' at moments which can be a problem sometimes. Overall, UNDERTALE is a great game in almost every aspect and I also recommend that every gamer who play any games with murder or choices in it play this game. It can change your whole ideal on video games. It breaks the fourth wall over and over again. It makes comments about how gamers think, people watching youtube videos instead of gaming, and etc..
TL;DR- Go buy this game. It's good.

This is my second review of rust as the game continues to change.
Now take this review with a grain of salt, as everyone who plays rust and is part of the community will have heard a lot of this before.
First off we need to look at how rust started. When "legacy" was first launched it was an in browser game pushing the envelope. It had many of the same features as rust today and in some places even more. This was my favorite game at the time (and still is) but lately things have progressed in a different direction. Some of the reasons I loved how rust was, the hyper realism the pve, and a good balance of resources meaning kos was a lot less prevalent. When it came to pvp you where hopeless without a gun and every player had a different weapon off choice with mods.
It seems like rust has been following a trend set by cry baby preteens who shouldn't be playing mature rated games any way.
I see all to often people eating 8 bullets and running into a bush never to be seen again. And as always there is the constant threat of the rag to riches hero who can some how pierce solid metal with a stick and kill you in one hit.
Sure the graphics look hella good, but we need some form over function. At least before when they where artistic and cartoony, people could still reach a playable fps with out building a pc specific for rust.
In my opinion garry needs to come back to rust, take helk off the job and reinstate his dream.
I don't want to play rust the rp fairytale.
It would be inspiring to see them make some of the goals set out in the road map. But additions to the game that don't turn immediate profit seem to have gone to the back burner for skins.
In a game that is all about pvp and base raiding/building it would be nice to see the introduction of new building mechanics and structures as well as craft able in game items other then guns and armor. Like the old temporary shack. As it is, you farm for a day. Make the same base you always do, then roam around looking for a group smaller then yours to kill and loot.
I miss the days of rage induced from some one out gunning me In a fair pvp battle while at the same time, sick of getting geared up just to find  six door campers with  sticks waiting for me and the very expensive gun I spent a day farming to make.
Rust is the very definition of the alpha disclaimer. It has changed immensely and will continue to do so. Do not get used to anything.
To sum things up, if you know what rust is and you think you'll like it after watching all the recent coverage and exposure, then yes buy it! It's better than you could imagine. But if your waiting for rust to be how you remember from previous versions... keep waiting

An RPG where you don't have to kill anyone. That's what UNDERTALE is. The words 'don't kill anyone' may seem pretty boring but that's not the case with this game. It's gameplay is, in my opinion, one of the most unique yet spectacular ones I've ever seen or heard of. Talk your way through each fight or slaughter everyone in your path. Most people would pick the latter but the consequences of doing so can be collateral. The storyline of the game revolves around your actions. Killing everyone would cause you to go down the genocide path in the story. Sparing everyone generates the pacifist route. A mix of both causes the neutral route. The game is a game that wants to instill a new perspective into each player. A perspective in where every single action results in something favorable or unfavorable depending on the action. I can't say more about this unique perspective this game presents as it would be a spoiler. UNDERTALE's soundtrack is also amazing in so many levels. As an original soundtrack, it sets the overall feel of the whole story. The graphics in the game are unique in its own way. It's neither detailed nor realistic yet it, in my opinion, is perfect for the game. Every character is beautiful and detailed in terms of background and personality. UNDERTALE also tends to be pretty random at moments which is one of the reasons why it's pretty special. It tends to become humorous at times of sadness and despair. The fandom of UNDERTALE can be pretty unnecessarily 'intense' at moments which can be a problem sometimes. Overall, UNDERTALE is a great game in almost every aspect and I also recommend that every gamer who play any games with murder or choices in it play this game. It can change your whole ideal on video games. It breaks the fourth wall over and over again. It makes comments about how gamers think, people watching youtube videos instead of gaming, and etc..
TL;DR- Go buy this game. It's good.

This is my second review of rust as the game continues to change.
Now take this review with a grain of salt, as everyone who plays rust and is part of the community will have heard a lot of this before.
First off we need to look at how rust started. When "legacy" was first launched it was an in browser game pushing the envelope. It had many of the same features as rust today and in some places even more. This was my favorite game at the time (and still is) but lately things have progressed in a different direction. Some of the reasons I loved how rust was, the hyper realism the pve, and a good balance of resources meaning kos was a lot less prevalent. When it came to pvp you where hopeless without a gun and every player had a different weapon off choice with mods.
It seems like rust has been following a trend set by cry baby preteens who shouldn't be playing mature rated games any way.
I see all to often people eating 8 bullets and running into a bush never to be seen again. And as always there is the constant threat of the rag to riches hero who can some how pierce solid metal with a stick and kill you in one hit.
Sure the graphics look hella good, but we need some form over function. At least before when they where artistic and cartoony, people could still reach a playable fps with out building a pc specific for rust.
In my opinion garry needs to come back to rust, take helk off the job and reinstate his dream.
I don't want to play rust the rp fairytale.
It would be inspiring to see them make some of the goals set out in the road map. But additions to the game that don't turn immediate profit seem to have gone to the back burner for skins.
In a game that is all about pvp and base raiding/building it would be nice to see the introduction of new building mechanics and structures as well as craft able in game items other then guns and armor. Like the old temporary shack. As it is, you farm for a day. Make the same base you always do, then roam around looking for a group smaller then yours to kill and loot.
I miss the days of rage induced from some one out gunning me In a fair pvp battle while at the same time, sick of getting geared up just to find  six door campers with  sticks waiting for me and the very expensive gun I spent a day farming to make.
Rust is the very definition of the alpha disclaimer. It has changed immensely and will continue to do so. Do not get used to anything.
To sum things up, if you know what rust is and you think you'll like it after watching all the recent coverage and exposure, then yes buy it! It's better than you could imagine. But if your waiting for rust to be how you remember from previous versions... keep waiting

This is not a "survival" game.. This game is a FPS shooter with building and crafting.. But more on the FPS side..
You can watch twitch to get an idea of the game...
The game in vanilla form.? Well just leave that to groups, clans and more than 2 people playing at one time..
The balancing the devs are doing is more to control groups/clans.. ( rightfully so )
I have to say, this is a really great game and the new era of "FPS games"..
The old days of spawn, die, spawn, die, rinse and repeat have hit a peak in terms of popularity. ( CSGO, COD, BF etc... )
This game is the newer slower type of FPS game.. Build a base to protect and help protect you while you learn to run around like a crazy maniac stealing and killing.. ( 2 of the worst things in real life, ironic it's what this game is about )
For first time players.. Do your self a favor and go strait to modded servers.. This way you can get a feel for all of the items in game.. If you do go into the "vanilla" servers. You will rage quit and want to never play again.. You have been warned.
Devs have tried to make this game suited for solo players but it just don't work and makes the groups/clans only get stronger..
Vanilla is for veterans and groups/clans...
Modded is the communities way of "balancing" the game for solo players.. It works quite well really...
I am an older gamer, I was playing CS 1.0 back in 2000-2002 so my "clans" have all grown up.. Also having a full time career makes being in a "group/clan" not feesable...
I have found alot of love in this game from the modded community.. And thankfully so.. I enjoy the game so much more than the wasted time on vanilla.. I do recommend this game, it is one of the best games I have played..
Just don't go onto the "Official" servers unless you have 2 or more other people to play with..

This is my first review and will probably not be my last.
Because I have played this game for a while with several groups of friends, I have had a good time. However, had I not been a girl who was easily welcomed in by most groups (lol, let's be honest, it definitely made a difference)... this game probably would have gotten very boring very quickly.
I have a love-hate relationship with many aspects of the game, and I think the veteran community allows the developers to continue to fail them time and time again. By the time this game is fully released (if ever) it will be graphically, functionally and conceptually behind other games of it's time (it already is and it's still in alpha).
There are some amazingly fun people who play this game and there are so many opportunities to really enjoy yourself and have some good laughs along with heart pounding immersive action, but once you're a fan and have so many hours, you kind of become filled with resentment because this game could be so much more, but over time the community has suffered and the developers have moved at a pace which should warrant refunds.
Don't get me wrong, I love looting and going on nomad adventures up north. Sometimes I pitch a tent and hunt wild game and sit by a fire.... just to soak in the atmosphere. And sometimes I play with groups in PvP action that makes my heart pound. And sometimes I pretend to be an evil genius doctor who gives bad blood tranfusions and feeds people the meat of their comrades.... But the amount of times I've spent hours getting loot and meeting up with my friends, only to fall through the roof of a house and drop dead instantly, or get repeatedly hunted down by a hacker or get shot on site as a freshie by people who don't understand that fun player interaction is what makes or breaks a game like this... all that makes me (and everyone else I know) quit this game for months at a time.
Honestly, I don't know if it's fair to say I don't reccomend this game. I'd love to see the community grow and flourish so that when I play I have a great experience, but I haven't seen that happening in so long. I also will continue to play this game for reasons I don't truly understand. And I definitely don't want to doom this game to failure because I have had such high hopes for so long. But I honestly just don't know where it's headed.
So for now:
Buy the game if you have the extra money and don't mind being extremely disapointed (depending on your experience). Don't buy the game if you're looking for your next big adventure/PvP experience (you'd be better suited for Arma III or something similar).

I have had the game for a while and have been addicted to the game..
The game is a great game but I think the community and the developers are like a teenagers.
Don't know what they hell they want..
This is not a "survival" game.. This game is a FPS shooter with building and crafting.. But more on the FPS side..
You can watch twitch to get an idea of the game...
The game in vanilla form.? Well just leave that to groups, clans and more than 2 people playing at one time..
The balancing the devs are doing is more to control groups/clans.. ( rightfully so )
I have to say, this is a really great game and the new era of "FPS games"..
The old days of spawn, die, spawn, die, rinse and repeat have hit a peak in terms of popularity. ( CSGO, COD, BF etc... )
This game is the newer slower type of FPS game.. Build a base to protect and help protect you while you learn to run around like a crazy maniac stealing and killing.. ( 2 of the worst things in real life, ironic it's what this game is about )
For first time players.. Do your self a favor and go strait to modded servers.. This way you can get a feel for all of the items in game.. If you do go into the "vanilla" servers. You will rage quit and want to never play again.. You have been warned.
Devs have tried to make this game suited for solo players but it just don't work and makes the groups/clans only get stronger..
Vanilla is for veterans and groups/clans...
Modded is the communities way of "balancing" the game for solo players.. It works quite well really...
I am an older gamer, I was playing CS 1.0 back in 2000-2002 so my "clans" have all grown up.. Also having a full time career makes being in a "group/clan" not feesable...
I have found alot of love in this game from the modded community.. And thankfully so.. I enjoy the game so much more than the wasted time on vanilla.. I do recommend this game, it is one of the best games I have played..
Just don't go onto the "Official" servers unless you have 2 or more other people to play with..

I rarely use the phrase "instant classic" because classic implies that it stands the test of time. Yet Undertale is a game that I feel we should have gotten earlier so it makes sense. A lite RPG that stands out mostly by its humor and combat (or lack thereof) it's a short game on purpose as it's designed for multiple playthroughs. Memorable characters, a soundtrack full of earworms, and a fantastic story that doesn't get in your way are among the highlights. However, even a game like this has its pitfalls. A mostly linear map means you won't get lost often, but it also sacrifices some of the exploration that makes some RPGs fun. While puzzles break up the action, they may be frustrating enough to look up tutorials which may accidentally spoil the game for some.
Length: 4-10 hours per playthrough.
Should you buy this: Absolutely. Even if it's just to say "hey I've played this", Undertale is a game that everyone should play at least once.
Worth: $10 is a good price, but I recommend waiting for a sale if you're still on the fence.

While the community of the game is a bit "questionable" at times, the game itself is an amazing experience. I grew up never really likeing RPG style games like Final Fantasy or other titles, as they always get the same grinding boring experience into killing everything in sight. I do watch my brothers from time to time as it seemed intertaining, but he knew what he was doing and where to go, what level he has to be and what weapon he has to get to defeat the monsters. It really revolved around the idea that RPG's=GRINDING and that's really a sad truth for many, many RPG games out there that fall under this formula.
Undertale however, was different.
After watching videos (as I didn't care much for spoilers as everybody spoils everything in front of me anyway), I was interested in the game. It had the idea of RPG's of killing and gaining EXP, Saving, Bosses, A story, (optional) sidequests and things of the sort.
Then it hit me right at the beginning: You didn't need to kill anyone.
Unlike a game like Final Fantasy or Kingdom Hearts, you MUST grind and slay monsters to level up and become more powerful in the game, but Undertale pulls it off and it shows that you DON'T have to follow that rule as every monster in some way can be spared and you can go on your marry way.
Of course, the game also has a cast of funny quirky characters, to characters that are name after the two most (in)famous fonts in history: PAPYRUS and comic SANS. To a fish that wants to kill you. To Robots wanting to be a star, and even to a couple that had lost a child, the game tells you that they are not just some pixels on a screen, or a monster, or anything, but they're just as human as you and me. With feelings, a life, wants, needs, and best of all: friends.
Even the UNUSED content has sparked a community within the Undertale community, from monsters, to whole new game, to even downright animations and lore written as if these never to be seen bits of data are just as part of the game as if they ARE in the game. It's what makes a good community too.
Now that has been said about Undertale, now beware, beware of the man who speaks in hands. ;)

A well made 8-bit soundtrack that helps drive tension and carries weight exceptionally on the more dramatic scenes of the game. An fresh and interesting turn-based combat system that requires percision and focus, whether you are fighting to bring down your enemy or just dodging their blows to defuse the situation carefully. All of your choices matter in this adventure, so be careful how you go about every situation. A deceptively vivid and wonderful pixel art style that shows a lot of detail and nails the carefree and child-like vision of this curious world. If you haven't played it yet, you're missing out on a wonderful and truly marvelous adventure that can move even the hardest and coldest of stone hearts.
And if Toby, Temmie, or anyone who worked on this game sees this, thank you for such an awesome ride.

After i would leave a town, i would run with the few pieces of gear i had managed to scavenge to the next, through the mountains and forests, ever mindful that i may be minutes from death. At this time the servers generally had a very limited number of players, and so interaction with someone even at a dangerous place like Balota airstrip may not even occur. Still, the ambiance and sounds and lighting gave me a sense of being alone in a desperate world, and although hindered by glitches and performance issues, this game still gives that. Be it the loneliness of crossing the mountains or going through forests, or the sheer terror of seeing two other survivors behind you shortly followed by gunshots. This game gives a unique experience to the zombie apocolypse genre, and players must understand this going into this game.
This game will forever be an early access game.
