I rarely use the phrase "instant classic" because classic implies that it stands the test of time. Yet Undertale is a game that I feel we should have gotten earlier so it makes sense. A lite RPG that stands out mostly by its humor and combat (or lack thereof) it's a short game on purpose as it's designed for multiple playthroughs. Memorable characters, a soundtrack full of earworms, and a fantastic story that doesn't get in your way are among the highlights. However, even a game like this has its pitfalls. A mostly linear map means you won't get lost often, but it also sacrifices some of the exploration that makes some RPGs fun. While puzzles break up the action, they may be frustrating enough to look up tutorials which may accidentally spoil the game for some.
Length: 4-10 hours per playthrough.
Should you buy this: Absolutely. Even if it's just to say "hey I've played this", Undertale is a game that everyone should play at least once.
Worth: $10 is a good price, but I recommend waiting for a sale if you're still on the fence.

While the community of the game is a bit "questionable" at times, the game itself is an amazing experience. I grew up never really likeing RPG style games like Final Fantasy or other titles, as they always get the same grinding boring experience into killing everything in sight. I do watch my brothers from time to time as it seemed intertaining, but he knew what he was doing and where to go, what level he has to be and what weapon he has to get to defeat the monsters. It really revolved around the idea that RPG's=GRINDING and that's really a sad truth for many, many RPG games out there that fall under this formula.
Undertale however, was different.
After watching videos (as I didn't care much for spoilers as everybody spoils everything in front of me anyway), I was interested in the game. It had the idea of RPG's of killing and gaining EXP, Saving, Bosses, A story, (optional) sidequests and things of the sort.
Then it hit me right at the beginning: You didn't need to kill anyone.
Unlike a game like Final Fantasy or Kingdom Hearts, you MUST grind and slay monsters to level up and become more powerful in the game, but Undertale pulls it off and it shows that you DON'T have to follow that rule as every monster in some way can be spared and you can go on your marry way.
Of course, the game also has a cast of funny quirky characters, to characters that are name after the two most (in)famous fonts in history: PAPYRUS and comic SANS. To a fish that wants to kill you. To Robots wanting to be a star, and even to a couple that had lost a child, the game tells you that they are not just some pixels on a screen, or a monster, or anything, but they're just as human as you and me. With feelings, a life, wants, needs, and best of all: friends.
Even the UNUSED content has sparked a community within the Undertale community, from monsters, to whole new game, to even downright animations and lore written as if these never to be seen bits of data are just as part of the game as if they ARE in the game. It's what makes a good community too.
Now that has been said about Undertale, now beware, beware of the man who speaks in hands. ;)

It's astounding how some of the exact same issues from over a year ago are still in this game. I can't believe it.
Recent big update DID make it look good. That's about it. Yes, there were tons of "improvements" made, but none that make the game any less "DayZ", when referring to the issues associated with the title. Zombies can still hit you through walls and from lower levels, they don't even need to be facing in your direction, BUT they HAVE been made faster and more agile, able to leap walls. So you have that awesome combination, always great. Melee is still terrible, REALLY BAD. Items are so britle, and items STILL get frozen or randomly disappear without notice. Manually chambering weapons is....well, that's just an amazing feature, isn't it? Goes well with the incredibly frustrating loading process for the weapons that's implemented already. Balance for this game is searching hours for 40 rounds of ammo, total, for two different primary weapons and then not being able to carry two primary weapons, unless willing to deal with an additional level of frustration, with having to drop and pickup your second weapon repeatedly. Don't worry, the weapons are sturdy, supressors last a whole 15 shots before being ruined. Got hit once? Guess it's time to destroy every item you own. OH! Want to walk over this rounded pile of trash, well I'm just going to glitch you out and hold your right here, right in the open.

Don't get me wrong, I've had good shootouts, funny moments and all that good stuff, but I mean....c'mon man. It's obvious by now that the development of DayZ, in particular, is a bit slower than it should be for a game that has had so much support, including financially.
I don't even know what to say about this to someone interested in buying it. Maybe? I guess. It still gets updates, but the issues you'll experience have always been there and seems that they'll always be there. It's a unique experience, but one that can be had on so many other games, where some of the things in the game just seem dated and unpolished now. No longer inovative. Imagine DayZ as if they were Apple after just releasing the iPod, it was groundbreaking and new. The issue is, where Apple went on to create and grow and polish their product(s), with DayZ, it seems the instant success dumbed down the need to progress the title, with new and creative features and more polished gameplay, instead it basically just stayed the same for a long while, then updates trickled out that seemed out of touch with what the games real issues were. It's since had a graphics overhall and some minor changes, like the inventory, but even though it looks and works differently, it still has the same issues (i.e. lag when dragging items). I can't get my head around how they can basically recreate something, but still have it work just as poorly, in the same exact way.
I say, get this when on sale. Get this expecting rampant scripting from♥♥♥♥♥♥head 15 year olds. Prepare to be stream sniped if streaming. Prepare to spend an entire day "looting" to realize most of your time was spent desperately searching for one bottle or can at a time to survive. Then, right when you get a gun and a handfull of bullets, you get shot by some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ camping in a tree from 500m away. Get this expecting all of your gear randomly disappearing when restarting the game to fix a bug, leaving you  in your underwear with just the base of your weapon and no ammo. Oh, and expect to drive a vehicle, while manually shifting as if it were a motorcycle transmission (1 down neutral/2 up 1st), to have a door shot off completely with 3 rounds. Not like you spent an hour searching for parts to rebuild it. Don't worry, if you do manage to gear up and creep around to take in the new beautiful graphics, there are a bunch of try-hards out there with their settings set to low for visual advantage basically rendering any graphics updates pointless since you have to turn them off to keep any type of even playing field.

I've been playing DayZ for 3 years now and I'm one of the Veterans of the game so here's my review (if you don't have time to read just scroll to the bottom for pros and cons):
At first, DayZ seemed like the next generation of gaming. A game where you have the option to kill, but you don't always have to. it was more about interacting with players. Talking to them, handcuffing them, saving them, robbing them, torturing them and many other things. DayZ represented the true face of a Zombie Apocalypse world. They would add lots of new stuff including natural ways to find food or clothes and etc. You could hunt, you could pick fruit, you could plant seeds and grow them and many other things. There were a lot of things you could craft. But this all didn't happen in 1 week. It took 2 years. After that the developers lost their idea of what DayZ was supposed to become. They started adding worthless loot and changing the gameplay from rpg to action. Now it wasn't clothes that were being added or bugs that were getting fixed, it was weapons. Only weapons, lots of weapons. To the point where you could never worry of not having a weapon to kill someone. Slowly, DayZ changed to the game it is today. A game that anyone who even glances at you will fire a bullet towards you if they can. All those Youtube videos of people getting handcuffed or messed with got replaced by videos of PVP Battles. So now, all the new players are small minded people who came from Counter-Strike or Call of Duty, which means the only thing they know how to do is kill other players. This isn't the DayZ we've been waiting for for 3 years. This is crap! For the last 2 years 80% of us players have had the most horrible graphics. After 2 years they've nearly but not fully fixed that. Until a few months ago I still had the will to play for a new experience, but that will is now dead because of all the bullets I've taken to the head. I have to say this one: There are items that have been made from the first day and still not usable after 3 years. You call that developing?
A players will to play will last long, but not long enough to see this game fully released.
Here are the pros and cons:
Pros:
Next generation open world rpg game.
Lots of players from different countries.
Lots of servers.
Cons:
Longest Early access game in the history of games.
Has a big but slow and worthless developer team with a big lack of leadership.
More bugs than you can imagine. Even for a game that has been in development for 3 years.

The latest update did manage to weed out a lot of the framerate issues, but a lot of work needs to be done. I understood when I bought it that it was not a finished game, but when you decide to back a game, especially one that has a larger purchase price as this one does, you kinda hope it would grow and improve a little. Not a whole lot has changed since 2013. Certain features have gotten more polished, but simple things like broken zombie AI have never been fully fixed.
Now, for those who want a gritty survival experience and have cash to throw away, this is probably what you are looking for. I've played a lot of other survival games and most are very comical at the least. If there is one thing Dayz is shooting for, its a more realistic zombie survival experience. Are they there yet? Not really, but compared to H1Z1, this is hands down the winner in my opinion. I still really hope they implement more vehicles and more features, but am very skeptical. I do still give it a thumbs up however, because there is nothing else like it really in my opinion. I just wish the player community wasn't so scummy. I don't like bullet storm gameplay. It's just not my thing, and I'm not very good at it.
But I like an RPG stuffed with good mechanics, a well-crafted difficulty curve, even better characters, entertaining conversation and touching moments. I laughed or aww'd a lot. Everything you can do, everyone you can talk to, everything you can go back to at the end, and a few hidden things...
Worth the occasional frustration of being terrible at bullet storms.
Stay determined. You'll be alright.
Why?
This is a beautifully-crafted exercise in dissatisfaction. With a bipolar difficulty curve that purposely does nothing to prepare you for what few encounters aren't dull and unsatisfying, characters who deride your choices or cower at your approach, certain bosses that are just beastly hard with no warm-up, a firm narrative keeps you harshly aware of the moral low ground you tread upon and the righteousness of the enemies you battle.
You...
...you begin to take a grim, masochistic satisfaction in watching yourself slaughtered, again and again, as you struggle to learn the few fights that are actually challenging. You come to love the sound of your SOUL shattering into the winds. As the innocent scatter before your path and lie in a trail of blood and mangled limbs behind you, you know you deserve it when you die again and again at the hands of the
heroes of this story.
Because you are, truly and unequivocally, the villain. And when you finally win, your reward...
... is heartbreak, along with a sharp reminder of just what kind of morally-bankrupt, murdering, backstabbing, inhuman
you are.
What did you expect out of a gameplay path known as
Well-crafted mechanics meet well-crafted characters and story to build a great experience. And it does things other games won't... like punish
for making evil choices.
Be good, okay? Or you're gonna have a bad time.
And you might like that.

As pretty much having 1,000 hours in this game. I feel like I should give it some kind of review.
I started liking this game in late 2013 when legacy rust was a thing. The game almost instantly clicked for me. The game also taught me two things: People are bad and Hammerspace is real. The word "Friendly" is something that echoed in my mind... as well as a 12 gauge buckshot as they pulled out a shotgun and... well... you get the picture. The point is, legacy rust really connected with me and its something that i'll never forget.
A year or so after I started playing, they started working on rust 2.0. At first I was really excited about it.. I mean think about it - Water that doesn't kill you? NICE! A better set of code to improve from? NICE! Removing a lot of really awful bugs that was caused by said code? REALLY NICE! That excitment quickly turned to dissapointment. Update after update, I lost that feeling I had for this wonderful game. I mean, at times I would still play... just not too serious. Slowly over time, I grew to dislike this game. The straw that finally broke the camel's back was the XP system. It turned Rust, The open world survival game, into a game that makes me feel like i'm playing Runescape. Grind xp so you can have fun. Plus, if you're not in a clan of 3+ when playing vanilla... Don't expect to have fun for the first 2-3 days. The xp rates are awful.
I think what i'm trying to say is - Rust was a great game... WAS. Now its very washed up (so to say) and hard for me to find enjoyment in. I hate to leave a negative review on a game I put so much time in but... It had to be done.

I have played this game for a while now, and I can honestly tell you that it has some of the most basic quests ever. Literally every quest consists of either picking up a certain number of something, or killing an enemy. Many of the quests are extremely similar and the game relies on the loot and humor to be entertaining. The levels are much more varied compared to the original borderlands however, with snow and lava and stuff. If you get a good weapon, have fun not being able to use it in a few levels, because gearbox decided that weapons should become useless after 3 levels, and you can also expect not to get any more than 1 or 2 legendary weapons if you don't farm bosses. The game also gets really repetitive when you are doing the story mode over and over again to try to get to ultimate vault hunter mode, it really is annoying. All in all I would give this game a 8/10 as it stands right now because it has provided me with hour upon hour of fun that I couldn't have got anywhere else.  I can see the game reaching 10/10 though if the developers continue on the path that they are taking and I don't see them straying any time soon.

I'll admit I wasn't really on board with this game at first, mostly because of the fanbase and such. But when I saw a discount over the weekend, my curiosity got the best of me, and I bought it. Now... I was very surprised for the emotional journey about to unfold before me.
Undertale is one of the strangest, most unique games I have ever played. Though pretty short, it still entertains you in its own unique way. Though the graphics might not be...appealing at times, the inspiring story behind it makes it all up. Surprisingly, this game makes every character likable—even the random encounter characters. I might have also gotten a bit teary-eyed when I was battling the main antagonist of the game. I don't think I'll have the courage to do a Genocide run anytime soon, not after I just finished the True Pacifist route.
The music...heck, the music is amazing! It ties the game together well. Just from the music alone, you can feel the various emotions in the game. Personally, my favorite has to be "ASGORE"...but that's just me.
The battles can be a bit frustrating at times (Mettaton EX is a pain in the neck for me), and I don't think people who are in this mostly for the gameplay will really enjoy it.
However, I will definetely recommend this game to someone who is in it for the story; an amazing, strange, and surprisngly touching must-play experience.

Early Alpha 8/10 - Flawed but fun
Current Alpha 3/10 - Flawed, made to focus on the flaws.
TL:DR: The people is what made the game fun. Devs are only focusing on single player and making it harder to have strange encounters and fun adventures with other people, because its harder to encounter people.
The main aspect which has been missed by the devlopment team is "Is the game fun to play?" and when they are fixing, changing and implementing new stuff, they have not been considering the reason people play the game.
For me, playing Day Z was all about the people that I encountered and the adventures that came from it. I enjoyed playing solo and fearing for my life and also playing with my friends to do something new and crazy.
In the early stages of the game, I encountered gangs of cannibals that chased me with pitchforks and knives. I encountered morgan freeman, who tricked me into drinking bleach (he said charcoal tabs would save me), who then gave a tear jerking eulogy as he stood over my uncouncious body as I died. I even got "arrested" by a fully armed group who forced me to bare knuckle fight other "bambi's" and the victor would earn freedom.
The community and the people are what made the game fun and enjoyable.
The current game has lost the enjoyment I used to get from playing. The developers have gone on a tangent which focused on "surviving" and put more focus into PVE stuff for the 5% of people who enjoy going out alone and surviving in the wilderness (which I am not bashing)
However with the new patches, new locations, new guns, new loot economy, even more new guns, zombie changes, new fishing poles, new bows, chickens etc. They have forgotten that people enjoyed interacting with eachother more than the actual game itself. The game was always flawed as it is alpha, but the direction that Day Z is heading is a single player survival game.
Gone are the good old days when the coast was packed with people and fun times. When the crazies were all excited to play because of;
Frankie On Pc
Syndicate Gaming
Mr Moon
Now, it is very rare to encounter people as they are spread across the extremely large map and the only hotspots are now the big pvp areas which take a long time to reach. I have no problem with the game being in alpha and having its flaws. However, I understand why people are upset. This game is very fun. The whole plot is based around an alien vault that is being controlled by the leader of the company Hyperion. This game is a loot and shoot kind of game. Though you don't need to play the first borderlands to understand Bl2, I would also play through BL1 to tie up certain loose ends. (Plus, you'll get a special edition head for your characters for playing it, and it's lots of fun.) One thing to mention is that if you're a casual player than I would not reccomend buying the Lvl 61 and 72 upgrade packs. This makes almost every gun in the game virtually useless and you'll die within seconds without very specific guns and sheilds. Playing the game as a level 50 is very satisfying. Once you beat the game and you're max level I would reccomend start farming good weapons. (Farming is to kill a certain boss that drops a specific item over and over until you get the gun you want. Overall, the game alone is very fun. By buying the GOTY edition, you are getting the lvl 61 upgrade pack so if you want the challenge of level 61 or 71, get the GOTY. If you want to be a casual player though, I would spend the extra money to buy the DLCs seperately without the 61 upgrade. If you're going to buy everything seperately, I would reccomend the following DLCs:
.Captian Scarlet and her Pirate's Booty
.Tiny Tina's assault on Dragon Keep
.Mr. Torgue's Campaign of Carnage
.Krieg Character Pack ( If you want to be a melee or explosive based character)
Those were my personal favorite DLCs, feel free to buy the others if you want though. Overall, Borderlands 2 is a great game. With many different characters and weapon builds to choose from, each playthrough is very unique. Overall, I would give it a 9/10. If it's on sale, don't hesitate to buy it. If not, still go for it. You will not be disappionted.

Early Alpha 8/10 - Flawed but fun
Current Alpha 3/10 - Flawed, made to focus on the flaws.
TL:DR: The people is what made the game fun. Devs are only focusing on single player and making it harder to have strange encounters and fun adventures with other people, because its harder to encounter people.
The main aspect which has been missed by the devlopment team is "Is the game fun to play?" and when they are fixing, changing and implementing new stuff, they have not been considering the reason people play the game.
For me, playing Day Z was all about the people that I encountered and the adventures that came from it. I enjoyed playing solo and fearing for my life and also playing with my friends to do something new and crazy.
In the early stages of the game, I encountered gangs of cannibals that chased me with pitchforks and knives. I encountered morgan freeman, who tricked me into drinking bleach (he said charcoal tabs would save me), who then gave a tear jerking eulogy as he stood over my uncouncious body as I died. I even got "arrested" by a fully armed group who forced me to bare knuckle fight other "bambi's" and the victor would earn freedom.
The community and the people are what made the game fun and enjoyable.
The current game has lost the enjoyment I used to get from playing. The developers have gone on a tangent which focused on "surviving" and put more focus into PVE stuff for the 5% of people who enjoy going out alone and surviving in the wilderness (which I am not bashing)
However with the new patches, new locations, new guns, new loot economy, even more new guns, zombie changes, new fishing poles, new bows, chickens etc. They have forgotten that people enjoyed interacting with eachother more than the actual game itself. The game was always flawed as it is alpha, but the direction that Day Z is heading is a single player survival game.
Gone are the good old days when the coast was packed with people and fun times. When the crazies were all excited to play because of;
Frankie On Pc
Syndicate Gaming
Mr Moon
Now, it is very rare to encounter people as they are spread across the extremely large map and the only hotspots are now the big pvp areas which take a long time to reach. I have no problem with the game being in alpha and having its flaws. However, I understand why people are upset. They spend 2-3 hours playing a game and barely encountering anyone, so they have to focus on the game itself, which is inherintly flawed, so obviously they will get upset.
On the upside - The huge FPS improvement is great and things look to be improving of recent. I hope this game goes back to its roots and remembers what made it fun initially.

No, I am not one of the ultra fans of UNDERTALE. I changed my picture to Papyrus' spaghetti-
derived face because I wanted to make a joke on the Internet, surprising as it may be.

When I had to fight Goat Mom, as she was now known to me, I thought 'No biggie. I just have a stick. No WAY I can kill ultra-goat of flames.' How wrong I was. I had just befriended a goat lady who was excited tobe a parent again. And then I murdered her.
And I stumbled into Snowdin, checking everything for loot. And I seemed to have discovered an easter egg. Won't say here, but it's next to the Ruins door. And a big stick that snapped for 'no reason.'
Either way, I won't spoil the entire game.

It's been almost a year since Undertale's release, and initially I didn't really care for it, I didn't even have a steam account. But a friend ended up buying the game for me months ago, so I finally got a steam account and gave it a shot.
And gosh darn it, I loved it. The amazingly done old styled videogame music, characters who all overturned initial expectations and fell in love with, and an endearing battle system whose mechanics all tied in with the in-game universe and story. The tagline is appropriately along the lines of 'a friendly RPG where no one has to die', and combat is a mix up of RPG tropes and bullet-hell. You get to choose the overall fate of the underground by your choices to fight or show mercy, as you learn more about the world, characters, and circumstances around you. I'm glad I got to play through without any spoilers, because many parts leave you feeling like you emotionally got hit by a truck. And lets just say the replay value can be very interesting.
Only con is that I can't erase it from my mind to play it for the first time again.
After almost a year, the soundtrack's still on my mind as well as the impact the game had on me. If you haven't been blasted wth practically every spoiler of the game yet, give Undertale a shot. If not, enjoy the soundtrack, it's godly if you enjoyed SNES era videogame music.

Undertale was a game gifted to me by my significant other, and, having not heard anything online about it, I was genuinely intrigued by the story it could possibly possess, and was excited to play it. . I was so distraught about

TL;DR: This game has incredible story, good characters, and will make you cry and laugh no matter what you do. So thank you, Toby, for the great game and the great memories, laughs, and tears  it's provided me with.

There was a perception one time that RPGs were not for PC. Then there were games like Diablo and such that proved that they could work. Next, there are JRPG style games, which computers are not really known for. Enter Undertale. An original turn-based RPG that defies any sort of expectations you would have for typical JRPG games like Final Fantasy. Undertale was made by one guy (largely) and for a game that was made with that approach it's quite impressive in what it achieves.
You begin your adventue in a underground full of monsters and all sorts of varied creatures. While that sounds simple enough, the story becomes deep through progression. But what I like about the story is that it doesn't assault you with needless exposition unlike other games which seemingly build a philosophy around it. Undertale can balance comedy with darkness which is an amazing feat in of itself really. The characters are charming and hilarious, but they all have their own unique personality and insecurities. And depending on which route you choose (genocide/neutral/true-pacifist), a little more is revealed of each character. Undertale is the exact definition of interactive story-telling. And its story and characters are presented in ways that is only unique to Undertale. The pacing is also very consistant. It's an experience that's unforgettable.
The gameplay is very interesting and extremely enjoyable. It's like a normal, basic turn-based RPG, but it contains two features that make it different.
- You have the option to spare any foe you come across. This affects the story (especially as it's a requirement for the true ending) by varying how other characters interact with you. You can have a mixture of killing enemies/sparing enemies in just one playthrough. Or you can kill/spare everyone.
- Undertale has something called "bullet hell" where you have to dodge projectiles. Different enemies have different attacks if you don't dodge you lose HP, it's as simple as that. Good thing is that when I first played Undertale I never found the game impossibly difficult.
The gameplay is a real treat.
Undertale has the best ost I have ever heard. I don't know how to describe it, just type in on YouTube "Undertale OST", it's fantastic and each track fits their respective scenes so well.
All in all, here are the pros and cons:
- Gameplay is amazing
- Story is emotional and well written
- Characters are funny and awesome
- Best soundtrack
- I like the 16-bit look (reminds me of the SNES JRPGs)
- Seriously I really like that soundtrack
- Did I mention the soundtrack?
- Quite cheap
- Where's Undertale 2?
10/10 - Great game.

What a great game honestly. I hated it at first because all it gave me was anxiety and huge amounts of stress in fear of being held up, sniped, or killed by zombies. Luckily I had a friend hold my hand all the way through and I'm able to experience the game in full. It is a resource heavy game but my god is it beautiful. One complaint though is that the rain tanks my FPS real hard. A lot of the players in this game have a "kill on sight" mentality, and I don't blame them. In a game in where there is almost no HUD I would be afraid of players, and I still am. The mechanics in this game are fantastic. The game is still glichy, (some advantagous) but a most the time its fine. The guns have realistic zeroing so you can hit a target 800m out, there is bullet drop and guns sound different depending on the round. Some loot is really hard to come by sadly, a Smersh vest and backpack is about as rare as a gold ingot sitting on your desk when you wake up in the morning. Zombies are sometimes glitchy, and they have pretty good aggro mechanics. You can sneak up on them and kill them quickly, or you can accidentally shoot your gun and all the townsfolk want to come to meet you (trust me, not fun, I've been there). Navigation in this game is honestly pretty challenging. Luckily there is an online map that gives you pretty good reference points. Unfortunately since this game is set in Russia, all the road signs and town names are in cyrillic. Sadly not every body speaks Russian, so you just need to get familiar with what combination of funny looking, backwords English letters/numbers make up the name of a town for example, if it looks like a 3, followed by the sign for pi, and then a lowercase "e". You probably arrived in Elektro, and if you run into a sign that looks like "4eph" its probably Cherno. Both of those are violent towns. I don't recommend staying for long. The status affects are decent, hunger, thirst, bleeding, wet and sick affect you in their own way. Hunger and thirst tends to kill you if you are dehydrated. Not sure what sickness really does to you as when I drank of bleach some guy decided to end my life earlier than Id liked it too. Being wet makes you cool down and get cold really quickly, which can lead to death. You can also overheat and die too. There are cars in the game, and if you get run over you better have a splint to fix your legs you cripple. On top of that your shoes will be ruined and somehow you can die from your legs being sore. Since its in alpha, most of the problems will be fixed but this is a pretty solid game for what it is now.

Personally I've played a lot of undertale (as you can see with my 84 hours) Edit: 96 hours Edit2: 117 hours Edit3: 145 hours (I have way too much time on my hands). 4 whole days.. It's the best story game I've ever played. I haven't played a lot of mainstream storyline games (except undertale) but I still think it will be up there. I understand why some people might not like the game and why people like me can appreciate it. I can relate to quite a few characters meaning I care for them and I get attached to them. When I did the genocide route I knew it would be tough and I wouldn't like it. But I seriously lost it at Papyrus and Sans. I just got frustrated at Undyne and I couldn't care for her any longer. That was before I started Sans' battle. Oh god... I spent so long on Sans' battle. I'm not gonna lie it took me a long time. Unlike Undyne's battle I wasn't just happy to win I was sad that I killed him. Then I also went on to do a no hit of Sans' battle (which took me even longer, like a LOT longer). When I sat down and thought about my no hit run I realised something, it was actually kind of depressing. It's not just monsters last hope but humans too. If Sans lost then the universe was literally destroyed, and for Frisk/Chara to just completely dunk on him is kinda embaressing for the world. Not a single hit? It's kinda messed up if you think about it.
The pacifist run was truly something. While then jokes were very meme based (anime etc.) I still think they'll last a while because I'm pretty sure anime is still going strong. I found the comedy of the pacifist run very light hearted (A bit too lighthearted, no one can deny that the fanbase is just... ugh) if the comedy was a little more mature then I doubt the fanbase would be full of 10 year olds downvoting any person with an opinion slightly against undertale. I personally like listening to criticism as long as it's not just "THIS GAME'S FOR LITTLE BABY KIDS" and it's something a developer could actually use to make their game better. I believe that the storyline was very hooking (for me anyway, some people found it boring which I can understand) and that it was a nice game to follow with and it gently eased you into it. Obviously the game is quite short (unless you're me and you spend 84 hours on the game finding every other option when I could be doing something productive with my life) but Toby wanted the game to be short enough so that it could feel like a movie but still have the interactivity of a game, which I loved.
For Toby Fox to create this game all by himself (with the help of one other person do some of the sprites) storyline, (most) animation (I understand it's 8-bit), characters and the incredible soundtrack in 2 and a half years is simply incredible. By the way if you've made it here then congratulations, you're not lazy enough to give up halfway through. I know a few game developers that could learn a thing or two from him. Toby is very talented.
Don't forget that it's not just pacifist and genocide, you have all the different neutral endings which Toby planned for. The massive change of atmosphere between the genocide and pacifist route is gobsmacking. In the pacifist route you play as a cheerful kid that goes through puzzles and japes with 2 loveable skeletons. While in the genocide route, you play as a heartless monster that goes out of their way to kill every monster in an area, walking straight through anything close to fun or happy.
In conclusion I would highly reccomend this game to anyone from 12 upwards (Has anyone else seen that old guy that plays Undertale? It's god damn hilarious). This game truly is incredible but I don't think it's the best game ever. Yes it actually won that on a PUBLIC vote poll. The only bad thing about the game is the fanbase. It's just disgusting how they treat it.
Edit: I forgot to mention how Toby planned for EVERYTHING. He knew someone would have to just go and kill every single monster, and he knew that someone would try to go back to undyne's house as she was chasing them. There's no flaws in the game, just the fanbase. Like seriously I hate the fanbase.

so let's start the review:
i started playing the game on a recommendation from my two of my friends recently and started playing on a kinda small server with them (usually around 20/200 are on at most whenever i log on), there's a pretty large clan that is pretty dominating on it, we built a good base so were able to hold them off after they do a good chunk of damage when they attack. the building is fun and the game can be pretty enjoyable once you get things going.
however, when going to a larger server the people on are almost all toxic, KOS is way too common and you'd get killed even if you're naked with nothing but the rock and torch. not saying everyones toxic, just today i helped out a guy and he gave me so much good stuff in return. the balance of the game is pretty bad honestly with people already being fully armored and player hunting and securing supply drops in a clan within a day of a wipe, you can build a base and then come on the next day to find that your dead, bed gone and base grieved if your unlucky, naked and with nothing left if you are.
not sure how the xp system was or the BP system was but they sound a whole lot more balanced than how the game currently is. aside from that bears glitching throught your walls into your base and killing you has gotta be fixed cause that can get frustrating quick. the live, die, repeat within a 10 minute span cycle due to a bad community while it can't be completely removed is a big problem.
At it's current state the game is good but can be better. solo players better steer clear of this game, because unless you join a clan or have friends it's gonna take you alot longer than it's worth to actually just feel safe enough to log off, even only for an hour or two or being afraid to leave your house at the mere sight of another player.
im not not the best at reviewing but my current verdict on the game is that it's not worth it. the gameplay and constant player KOS mindset will make you feel that the game is getting stale quite quickly and from what i've found so far is that there are other games of the same genre on steam that can be just as enjoyable if not more for those who don't like how the game is so far or are discouraged from buying it due to the current state of it but are looking for a good way to enjoy a few hours without being frustrated or paranoid that something will happen when you're gone.
p.s in case someone with with something like 6k hours (and i've met a few) comes and tells me that i don't know♥♥♥♥♥♥about how to enjoy it or you gotta sink a hundred more hours into it before getting good or something, NO, im not gonna do that. i like playing games to relax from the stress of the day or to stave off my boredom, i'll be starting university soon and for the proffession im aiming for i won't have time nor the inclination to do that. this is a new account so and i tend to hop between consoles so while it may not show i've played alot of mmo's, rpgs, first person and third person games to pass the time and can honestly say i don't feel as much enjoyment or accomplishment playing this game compared to others. that is my honest opinion. i'll sink more hours in this game to try and change my opinion on it but unless there's a drastic change i don't think i'll be playing it once the end of the month hits.
